================================================================================
TECHSARA SOLUTIONS - SALESFORCE ORG KNOWLEDGE BASE (OBJECTS & FIELDS)
================================================================================

WHAT THIS FILE IS
-----------------
This file is a plain-English knowledge base of every object and field in the
Techsara Solutions Salesforce org (preprod sandbox). It is written for an AI
agent so it can answer questions about the org: what each object is for, how it
is used in the business, which objects connect to it, and what every field
means in real business terms (not just its data type).

HOW TO READ THIS FILE
---------------------
- Each object gets one big section, separated by a line of "=" characters.
- Inside each object section:
    1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS        - purpose and a short description
    2. KIND OF OBJECT             - custom/standard, parent/child, sharing, size
    3. RECORD TYPES               - the flavors of the object (if any)
    4. HOW IT IS USED (PROCESS)   - the real business workflow, step by step
    5. CONNECTED OBJECTS          - every relationship and what it means
    6. BUSINESS RULES             - validation rules users hit while saving
    7. AUTOMATION                 - flows, triggers, scheduled jobs on it
    8. FIELDS                     - every field, grouped by purpose, explained
    9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT         - actual record counts from the preprod org
- Field entries look like:  Field_API_Name__c (Field Label) [Type]
  followed by an indented explanation of what the field is used for, who or
  what fills it in (a user, a flow, an integration), and its picklist values
  where relevant.
- If something could not be fully confirmed from the org, it is marked
  "(not fully documented - verify with team)" instead of guessing.

ORG OVERVIEW (READ THIS FIRST)
------------------------------
Techsara Solutions runs a RECRUITMENT + CANDIDATE-TRAINING/ONBOARDING platform
on Salesforce. The key concepts every answer depends on:

- A CANDIDATE IS A PERSON ACCOUNT. The standard Account object (with Person
  Accounts enabled) is the spine of the whole org. Candidate = Person Account;
  client/vendor companies = business Accounts. Almost every custom object hangs
  off Account through a Candidate__c / Client_Account__c / Account__c lookup.

- EMPLOYEES HAVE THEIR OWN OBJECT. Recruiter__c (label "Employee") is a custom
  object representing Techsara's internal staff (recruiters, support persons,
  trainers, managers). It is separate from the Salesforce User object. Most
  "who works on this" lookups point to Recruiter__c, not User.

- TWO RECRUITING PIPELINES EXIST SIDE BY SIDE:
  1) B2B STAFFING: a client/vendor sends an open job requirement
     (Job_Requirement__c) -> recruiters submit candidates against it
     (Job_Submission__c) -> interviews are scheduled (Interview__c) -> offer /
     placement -> Onboarding__c.
  2) CANDIDATE MARKETING ("bench marketing"): Techsara markets a candidate into
     the open job market. A Marketing__c record tracks the engagement, daily
     Application__c records log the job applications made for the candidate,
     and when an outside company responds, an Interview__c is scheduled.
  The same Interview__c object serves both pipelines (see its record types).

- INTERNAL vs EXTERNAL INTERVIEWS ARE DIFFERENT OBJECTS. Interview__c is the
  candidate interviewing with an OUTSIDE company (a client or a market
  employer). Internal_Interview__c is Techsara internally screening/assessing
  a candidate (template-driven, AI question generation, Hire/NoHire decision).
  Do not confuse them - and note that Interview_Evaluation__c belongs to
  Internal_Interview__c, NOT to Interview__c, despite its name.

- TRAINING/LMS LAYER: Program__c -> Program_Version__c -> Cohort__c curriculum;
  Candidate_Training__c enrolls a candidate; Session__c is the generic
  scheduled-meeting object (Zoom/Google Calendar backed) used for training and
  many other meeting types; Deliverable__c tracks candidate work products.

- INTEGRATIONS: Google Calendar (interview/session invites), Zoom (meetings +
  recording management in S3), Slack (team notifications for almost every
  important event), AWS API Gateway/Lambda (the external AI assignment/scoring
  engine called "COMPASS"), OpenAI, QuickBooks (billing).

- PORTALS: employees work mainly through the "AIC Portal" (an Experience Cloud
  community), candidates through candidate portals with custom token auth.

PART 1: THE CORE - PEOPLE & COMPANIES

================================================================================
OBJECT: Account  (Label: "Account" / a candidate is a "Person Account")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Account is THE HUB of the entire org. Person Accounts are enabled, and the
object carries three completely different kinds of records at once:

  a) A CANDIDATE - a Person Account. This is what ~75% of all Account records
     are. A candidate is created by converting a website Lead (the Convert
     button runs Lead_Conversion_Flow -> Apex LeadConversionHandler ->
     Database.convertLead) and from then on the Person Account is the
     candidate's master profile: identity, visa/work authorization, skills,
     education, job preferences, marketing credentials, training plan and
     payment terms, DocuSign agreement data, and interview statistics.
     Almost every custom object in the org hangs off it through a
     Candidate__c lookup (Marketing, Applications, Interviews, Onboarding,
     Training, Invoices, Background Checks, Resumes, Sessions...).

  b) An INTERNAL EMPLOYEE's portal identity - a Person Account with the
     "Recruiter" person record type (~23% of records). Techsara employees
     are modeled on the custom Recruiter__c ("Employee") object, but to give
     an employee a Customer Community Plus login on the AIC Portal they also
     need a Person Account + Contact. These employee Person Accounts are
     created by the Create_Recruiter_Contact / Provision_Employee_Portal_User
     flows and linked back via Recruiter__c.Recruiter_Contact__c.

  c) A BUSINESS ACCOUNT - a client, vendor, or implementation partner
     company (B2B Client / Vendor record types, ~1% of records). These carry
     the client-relationship fields (Client Status, Client Type, Payment
     Terms, Default Submission Email, Account Manager) used by the B2B
     staffing pipeline (Job_Requirement__c / Job_Submission__c).

Because one object serves three personas, most fields only make sense for one
flavor - the field groups in part 8 say which flavor each group belongs to.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- STANDARD object with Person Accounts enabled, heavily customized:
  192 fields total, of which 148 are custom - the second-largest field count
  in the org after Interview__c.
- Org-Wide Default sharing: Public Read/Write (the role-hierarchy redesign
  plans to tighten this; the client has also ruled that no one may edit the
  candidate Account going forward - see the security design docs).
- Owned records: normal ownership model (OwnerId). NOTE: 378 of 1,013
  accounts are owned by INACTIVE users - a known cleanup item in the
  role-hierarchy project ("375 inactive-owned Accounts to reassign").
- 1 validation rule, 15 list views, 5 Lightning record pages (which page a
  user sees depends on record type + app + profile):
  Candidate_Record_Page1 (Person Account = candidate; the main page),
  B2B_Client_Account_Record_Page, Vendor_Account_Record_Page,
  RecruiterRecord_Page, Account_Record_Page_Three_Column.
- Scale: 1,013 records in preprod (Aug 2024 - Aug 2026).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES (4 in the source snapshot; 6 active in the live org)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The metadata snapshot holds 4 business-account record types; the live org
additionally reports 2 person-type record types (person record types were not
retrieved into the source folder):

- "Person Account" (developer name: PersonAccount, person type) - THE
  CANDIDATE record type. 765 records (75.5%). Every converted Lead becomes
  one of these; the Candidate Record Page's candidate-only components are
  gated on RecordType.DeveloperName = PersonAccount.
- "Recruiter" (Recruiter, person type) - an internal EMPLOYEE's Person
  Account, used only to give the employee a portal login (Contact + user).
  237 records (23.4%). Created by Create_Recruiter_Contact /
  Provision_Employee_Portal_User; do not confuse with the candidate type.
- "B2B Client" (B2B_Client) - "Select this option to create an account for
  B2B client company." 7 records; all currently Client_Type = Direct Client.
- "Vendor / Implementation Partner" (Vendor_Implementation_Partner) -
  "Select this option for vendor, implementation partner, or middle-layer
  partner relationships." 0 records so far (Vendor__c is the object actually
  used for proxy-support vendors; this RT is for B2B-supply-chain companies).
- "Recruiters(Do Not Use)" (Recruiters_Do_Not_Use) - description literally
  says "Do not use this option to create an account." A deprecated business
  record type kept active but empty (0 records). The person-type "Recruiter"
  RT replaced it.
- "Master" - 4 legacy business records carry no record type.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - A CANDIDATE IS BORN FROM A LEAD. A website/marketing Lead is worked
  on the Lead page; clicking Convert runs Lead_Conversion_Flow. The flow
  first calls Apex LeadConversionHandler in check-duplicate mode (same email
  OR phone against existing Person Accounts), lets the user pick/merge, then
  converts. The new Person Account lands on the Candidate Record Page. The
  flow copies the intake answers onto the account (visa status, niche,
  relocation readiness, referrals, communication rating, training schedule,
  contact numbers, address, declarations...).

STEP 2 - ONBOARDING KICKS OFF AUTOMATICALLY. On creation of a candidate
  account, Create_Onboarding_from_Account_1 creates the child Onboarding__c
  record (copying ~20 profile fields), emails the candidate, and posts to
  Slack. As the candidate fills the onboarding form, the reverse flow
  Update_Candidate_Information_from_Onboarding writes ~30 profile fields
  BACK onto the Account (DOB, SSN last 4, work authorization, preferences,
  marketing email, passport, plan/amounts...). The DS_* DocuSign block is
  maintained for the service-agreement / ACH paperwork sent via DocuSign.

STEP 3 - TRAINING & PLAN. The candidate buys a Plan (Career Accelerator for
  ~95% of those with a plan), pays an Upfront Amount, and goes through the
  training layer (Candidate_Training__c, Session__c). Invoices are raised
  straight from the account via the Send Invoice button (QuickBooks
  integration stamps QB_Customer_ID__c on first use).

STEP 4 - MARKETING & INTERVIEWS. A Marketing__c engagement is opened (Create
  Marketing button). Marketing flows keep the account in sync: the assigned
  recruiter, the Application Start Date (when active marketing began), and
  Candidate_Status__c itself all mirror the Marketing record. Daily
  Application__c records log job applications; Interview__c records (master-
  detail children) accumulate under the account, feeding the rollup counters
  and the Expected_No_of_Interviews__c pacing formula. The nightly
  AccountSchedulerJob Slack-alerts recruiters about Active candidates with
  no interview for 30/45/60 days (stamping Last_Alert_Sent__c).

STEP 5 - STATUS LIFECYCLE. Candidate_Status__c walks In Progress -> Active
  -> (Hold / Paused) -> Placed / Closed / Terminate / Resigned. Any change
  away from Active requires a >=50-character reason (the one validation
  rule); every change is chattered on the record by
  Candidate_Status_Change_Log. Pause_or_Stop_Marketing and
  Onboarding_record_Inactive are the screen flows that move the status with
  proper notifications. A non-Active status also shows a warning banner on
  the record page.

STEP 6 - PLACEMENT / B2B. When B2B submissions happen, the candidate must
  have Resume_Ready__c and Active_for_B2B_Submission__c checked. Client
  companies live as B2B Client business accounts, carrying the Account
  Manager, payment terms, and submission email defaults that flow onto
  Job_Requirement__c records.

PARALLEL TRACK - EMPLOYEE PORTAL IDENTITY. HR runs the
  Provision_Employee_Portal_User flow (or Create_Recruiter_Contact) from an
  Employee (Recruiter__c) record: it creates a "Recruiter"-record-type
  Person Account (name, email, Slack user id), links it via
  Recruiter_Contact__c, and enables a portal user on it. Offboarding
  deactivates it (Employee_Offboarding flow).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM ACCOUNT TO OTHER OBJECTS:
- User (Account_Manager__c): the AM owning a CLIENT relationship (business
  accounts only) - defaulted onto Job Requirements created for the client.
- Recruiter__c (Assigned_Recruiter__c): the Techsara recruiter working this
  candidate - kept in sync from the Marketing record. 65% populated.
- Account (Candidate_Referral__c, self-lookup): the existing candidate who
  referred this one (21% populated - referrals are a real channel).
- Vendor__c (Default_Vendor__c): default proxy-support vendor for the
  candidate (1 record - effectively unused).
- Internal_Interview__c (Internal_Interview__c): pointer to a candidate's
  internal screening interview (0 populated - unused in practice).

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT ACCOUNT (children):
- Interview__c.Candidate__c (MASTER-DETAIL) - all external interviews of the
  candidate. The only master-detail child; interviews inherit the account's
  sharing. Also Interview__c.Client_Account__c (lookup) for B2B interviews.
- Marketing__c.Candidate__c - marketing engagements (bench marketing).
- Application__c.Candidate__c - daily job-application logs.
- Job_Submission__c.Candidate__c - B2B submissions of this candidate.
- Job_Requirement__c.Client_Account__c - the CLIENT side: job reqs raised by
  a business account.
- Onboarding__c.Account__c - the onboarding record(s), auto-created at
  candidate creation.
- Candidate_Training__c.Candidate__c - training enrollments.
- Session__c.Candidate__c and Session_Attendee__c.Candidate__c - meetings
  and attendance.
- Internal_Interview__c.Candidate__c - internal screening interviews.
- Education_History__c.Candidate__c - structured education rows (the
  College_Name_1-5 flat fields on Account are the legacy version of this).
- Resume__c.Candidate__c - resume versions.
- Background_Check__c.Candidate__c - post-offer verification.
- Invoice__c.Candidate__c - QuickBooks-integrated invoices.
- Pre_Enrolment_Request__c.Candidate__c - pre-enrollment requests.
- Candidate_Portal_Credential__c.Candidate__c - the custom candidate-portal
  login credentials (token auth, not standard users).
- Recruiter__c.Recruiter_Contact__c - the Employee record pointing at its
  portal Person Account (the "Recruiter" record type flavor).
- AI_Assignment_Logs__c.Candidate_Interview_Change__c - AI assignment audit
  rows referencing the candidate.
- Account.Candidate_Referral__c - other candidates referred by this one.
- Case - standard cases via AccountId/PersonContact (support tickets).
- Contact - every business account has Contacts; a Person Account owns its
  hidden PersonContact.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Candidate_Status_Change_Reason_Required (active): when Candidate_Status__c
  CHANGES to anything other than "Active", the user must type a genuinely
  NEW Candidate_Status_Change_Reason__c of at least 50 characters. Changing
  to Active is exempt, and the rule does not fire on record creation. Error
  shown on the reason field: "Please enter a status change reason of at
  least 50 characters." This is the audit backbone of the status lifecycle -
  the reason is then posted to Chatter by the status-change-log flow.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOWS ON ACCOUNT (active):
- Create_Onboarding_from_Account_1 (after save, create, record-type gated):
  creates the child Onboarding__c copying ~20 profile fields, sends the new-
  candidate email, posts Slack (via HttpCalloutGeneric).
- Candidate_Status_Change_Log (after save, when Candidate_Status__c changes):
  posts a rich-text Chatter entry - with the reason section when the new
  status is not Active. (Its doc references a companion before-save flow
  Candidate_Status_Reason_Clear_On_Status_Change to clear the old reason,
  but that flow is not present in this org snapshot - verify with team.)

FLOWS ON OTHER OBJECTS THAT WRITE ACCOUNT (active):
- Lead_Conversion_Flow (screen, Lead Convert button): creates/updates the
  Person Account through Apex LeadConversionHandler, mapping ~30 intake
  fields; de-dupes on email OR phone against existing Person Accounts.
- Candidate_Status_Update_when_marketing_status_Updated (Marketing__c
  update): mirrors the Marketing status onto Candidate_Status__c and copies
  hold/pause reasons into Reason_for_Hold__c.
- Marketing_Update_Application_Start_Date_on_Candidate (Marketing__c
  update): stamps Application_Start_Date__c when marketing goes active.
- Marketing_Update_Assigned_Recruiter_on_Candidate (Marketing__c update):
  syncs Assigned_Recruiter__c from the Marketing record.
- Update_Candidate_Information_from_Onboarding (Onboarding__c update):
  writes ~30 candidate profile fields from the onboarding form back onto
  the Account (everything except the two encrypted password fields).
- Onboarding_record_Inactive (screen, Onboarding "Pause" button): sets
  Candidate_Status__c + Reason_for_Hold__c.
- Pause_or_Stop_Marketing (screen): sets Candidate_Status__c and sends
  pause/stop emails + Slack alerts.
- QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks_For_Account (screen, "Send Invoice"
  button): creates/finds the QuickBooks customer (stamping
  QB_Customer_ID__c and address parts), creates the Invoice__c, emails it.
- Create_Recruiter_Contact / Provision_Employee_Portal_User /
  Employee_Offboarding (screen flows, HR feature): create / disable the
  employee "Recruiter"-record-type Person Account for portal login.
- Draft (NOT live): Update_Total_Interviews_on_Candidate - would maintain
  Total_Interviews__c from interviews; it has never run (field is empty).

SCHEDULED APEX:
- AccountSchedulerJob (Schedulable): nightly. (1) For every Active
  candidate, checks days since the last interview (or since Application
  Start Date if no interview): at 30/45/60 days with a 15-day repeat
  throttle it Slack-alerts the assigned recruiter (+ senior recruiter) and
  emails the team, stamping Last_Alert_Sent__c. (2) Posts a daily Slack
  table of today's supported interviews.

APEX THAT READS/WRITES ACCOUNT (main classes):
- LeadConversionHandler - the @InvocableMethod convert/dedupe utility (see
  above); also creates Contacts on business accounts for B2B leads.
- AuthService / CandidatePortalController / PortalUserAdminRest - candidate
  and employee portal auth resolve the Person Account.
- CandidateContext / DashboardService / AWSTrainingIntegration - read
  candidate data for the portal dashboard and the AWS training/AI engine.
- SlackCalloutHelper - Slack messaging used by the account alerts.
- MicrobatchSelfRegController / self-registration classes - can create
  Person Accounts from community self-signup.

QUICK ACTIONS / BUTTONS ON THE RECORD PAGES:
- Create Interview -> Interview_Create_Reschedule_Flow. NOTE: despite the
  name this creates an INTERNAL_INTERVIEW__c (internal screening), not an
  Interview__c.
- Create Marketing -> Create_Marketing_from_Candidate (guards against a
  duplicate open engagement).
- Send Invoice -> QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks_For_Account (candidate
  page).
- Initiate Payment Plan -> Initiate_Payment_Plan; Record Offer Letter
  Payment -> Create_Invoice_Payment (B2B/vendor pages).
- Child Account (create related account), Close Case / New Child Case /
  New Case, Login to Portal as User, Enable Portal/Customer User (grant the
  Person Account an Experience Cloud login), Mass Change Owner, Call.
- Embedded on the candidate page: Candidate_Status_Banner_Flow (warning
  banner when status is not Active; flow version currently marked Obsolete
  in the snapshot) and Attached_Resume_To_Lead (Resume tab).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 148 custom + key standard, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: KEY STANDARD FIELDS USED -----------------------------------------

Name / FirstName / LastName [Name]
    For Person Accounts the name splits into FirstName/LastName (plus
    Salutation); for business accounts it is the company name. Required.
PersonEmail [Email]
    THE candidate email (98% populated) - the identity key the lead-convert
    dedupe and the portals match on.
Phone / PersonMobilePhone / PersonHomePhone / PersonOtherPhone [Phone]
    Standard phone fields; Phone is the working number (75% populated).
OwnerId (Owner) [Lookup -> User]
    Record owner. Shown read-only on the candidate page. 378 records are
    owned by inactive users - a pending cleanup in the security redesign.
RecordTypeId [Lookup -> RecordType]
    Which of the six flavors this record is (read-only on the page).
IsPersonAccount [Checkbox, system]
    TRUE for candidate/employee person records (1,002 of 1,013).
ParentId [Hierarchy]
    Standard account hierarchy - used with the "Child Account" action for
    business accounts.
Industry [Picklist, standard]
    The candidate's target industry (read-only on the candidate page;
    copied to/from Onboarding). Standard values.
AccountSource / PersonLeadSource / Rating / Type / Ownership [Picklists]
    Standard classification fields, lightly used; AccountSource carries the
    marketing channel values (LinkedIn, Website, Referral types...).
BillingAddress / ShippingAddress / PersonMailingAddress / PersonOtherAddress
    Standard compound addresses; BillingAddress is copied onto Onboarding.
Description / PersonBirthdate / PersonTitle / PersonDepartment / Website /
NumberOfEmployees / AnnualRevenue / Fax / Sic / SicDesc / Site / Tier /
TickerSymbol / Jigsaw / AccountNumber / PersonAssistantName /
PersonAssistantPhone / PersonDoNotCall / PersonHasOptedOutOfEmail /
PersonHasOptedOutOfFax / PersonGenderIdentity / PersonPronouns /
PersonLastCURequestDate / PersonLastCUUpdateDate / IsCustomerPortal /
SourceSystemIdentifier
    Present but not meaningfully used by Techsara processes; the custom
    fields below carry the real data (e.g. Date_of_Birth__c is used instead
    of PersonBirthdate).

--- GROUP B: CANDIDATE LIFECYCLE, TEAM & PACING -------------------------------

Candidate_Status__c (Candidate Status) [Picklist]
    THE candidate lifecycle field: In Progress | Active | Hold | Paused |
    Placed | Terminate | Closed | Resigned. Set by users and by the
    marketing-sync flow (Marketing status changes mirror here) and the
    Pause/Stop and Onboarding-Inactive screen flows. Changing it away from
    Active requires a 50+ char reason (validation rule) and every change is
    posted to Chatter. Formula copies of it appear on Interview__c and
    other children. Live data (candidates only): Active 299, Closed 258,
    Hold 183, Terminate 16, Placed 7, In Progress 2. (Employee "Recruiter"
    person accounts are also stamped Active - 235 of them.)

Candidate_Status_Change_Reason__c (Candidate Status Change Reason)
[LongTextArea]
    WHY the status changed - typed by the user, enforced >=50 chars for any
    non-Active change, then chattered by Candidate_Status_Change_Log. The
    flow docs reference a before-save flow that clears it on each change so
    the rule sees a fresh reason (flow not in this snapshot - verify).

Reason_for_Hold__c (Reason for Hold) [LongTextArea]
    Reason the candidate is on Hold/Paused - written by the marketing-status
    sync flow (copying the Marketing record's hold/pause reasons) and by the
    Onboarding_record_Inactive screen flow.

Assigned_Recruiter__c (Assigned Recruiter) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    The Techsara recruiter (Employee record, NOT a User) working this
    candidate. Auto-synced from the Marketing engagement by
    Marketing_Update_Assigned_Recruiter_on_Candidate. The nightly
    AccountSchedulerJob alert @-mentions this recruiter (and their senior)
    on Slack. 65% populated.

Candidate_Owner_Name__c (Candidate Owner Name) [Formula, Text]
    Owner.FirstName + Owner.LastName - a plain-text owner name for reports
    and for copying onto Onboarding at creation.

Candidate_Referral__c (Candidate Referral) [Lookup -> Account]
    Self-lookup to the candidate who REFERRED this one. Set during lead
    conversion when the intake says "referred by an existing candidate".
    21% populated - referrals are a significant channel.

Employee_Referral__c (Employee Referral) [Text]
    Free-text name of the Techsara employee who referred the candidate
    (intake answer copied by the lead-conversion flow).

Acquaintances_Using_Our_Services__c (Acquaintances Using Our Services)
[Text]
    Intake answer: names of friends/acquaintances already using Techsara -
    a referral-mining question from the lead form.

Application_Start_Date__c (Application Start Date) [Date]
    The day active marketing (daily job applications) STARTED for this
    candidate - stamped by Marketing_Update_Application_Start_Date_on_
    Candidate when the Marketing status goes active. Anchor for the pacing
    math below and for the nightly stale-candidate alert. 66% populated.

Days_since_application_started__c (Days since application started)
[Formula, Number]
    TODAY() - Application_Start_Date__c. How long the candidate has been in
    active marketing.

Expected_No_of_Interviews__c (Expected No of Interviews) [Formula, Number]
    The pacing target: 5 interviews within the first 15 days of marketing,
    then +10 for every further 30 days. Compared against the interview
    rollups in reports to spot under-performing engagements.

Last_Alert_Sent__c (Last Alert Sent) [Date]
    When the nightly AccountSchedulerJob last sent the "no interview
    scheduled" Slack/email alert for this candidate - the job uses it as a
    15-day throttle so the same alert is not repeated daily. System-written
    (30% of records have one - the alert fires a lot).

Internal_Interview__c (Internal Interview) [Lookup -> Internal_Interview__c]
    Pointer to a candidate's internal screening interview. Never populated
    in practice (0 records) - the reverse lookup from
    Internal_Interview__c.Candidate__c is what is actually used.

--- GROUP C: IDENTITY & PERSONAL DETAILS (CANDIDATE) --------------------------

Middle_Name__c (Middle Name) [Text]
    Candidate's middle name (standard person name has no middle-name slot
    the org uses; also feeds the DocuSign DS_ block).

Date_of_Birth__c (Date of Birth) [Date]
    Candidate DOB - synced from the Onboarding form; read-only on the
    candidate page for everyone. Sensitive - FLS-restricted. 42% populated.
    (Used instead of the standard PersonBirthdate.)

Date_of_Arrival__c (Date of Arrival) [Date]
    When the candidate arrived in the US (most candidates are international
    students on OPT). Synced from the Onboarding form.

Last_4_digits_of_SSN__c (Last 4 digits of SSN) [Number(4,0)]
    Last four SSN digits for background-check / I-9 style verification.
    Synced from the Onboarding form. Sensitive - check FLS before exposing.

Passport_Number__c (Passport Number) [Text]
    Passport number, again for verification paperwork. Synced from the
    Onboarding form; copied onto Onboarding at creation. Sensitive.

Secondary_Email__c (Secondary Email) [Email]
    Backup personal email (PersonEmail is primary). Copied to Onboarding.

Secondary_Phone__c (Secondary Phone) [Text]
    Backup phone number. Copied to Onboarding.

Contact_Number_Calling__c (Contact Number Calling) [Phone]
Contact_Number_WhatsApp__c (Contact Number WhatsApp) [Phone]
    The number to CALL vs the number on WHATSAPP (candidates often keep an
    Indian WhatsApp number and a US calling number). Captured at lead
    conversion; WhatsApp number is copied to Onboarding.

Email_replica__c (Email_replica) [Formula, Text]
    Formula copy of PersonEmail - exists so automation/reports that cannot
    read PersonEmail directly (or need a text type) can use it.

Slack_User_Id__c (Slack User Id) [Text, unique, external ID]
    The person's Slack member ID. Populated on EMPLOYEE Person Accounts
    (the "Recruiter" record type flavor) by Create_Recruiter_Contact /
    Provision_Employee_Portal_User so Slack automations can @-mention them.
    137 populated - roughly the active employee roster, not candidates.

--- GROUP D: ADDRESSES --------------------------------------------------------

Current_Address__c (Current Address) [Address compound]
    The candidate's current US address - the primary address field, written
    at lead conversion, edited on the page, and pushed to QuickBooks as the
    customer billing address by the Send Invoice flow.

Home_Address__c (Home Address) [Address compound]
    Home-country / permanent address (distinct from the current US one).

Address_Line_1__c / Address_Line_2__c (Address Line 1/2) [Text]
Zip_Code__c (Zip Code) [Text]
    Legacy flat address parts predating the compound Current_Address__c.
    Kept for old records and form mappings.

Complete_Address__c (Complete Address) [Formula, Text]
    Concatenates the Current_Address__c parts (street, city, state, zip)
    into one display line for reports/emails.

Current_State_in_USA__c (Current State in USA) [Picklist]
    US state the candidate currently lives in - full 50-state picklist
    (note "Indiana," has a stray comma in its value). Used for filtering
    candidates by location/timezone.

--- GROUP G: SKILLS, EXPERIENCE & JOB PREFERENCES -----------------------------

Technology__c (Technology) [Picklist]

    Manager, AI/ML Engineer, Business Analyst, Data Engineer, DevOps,
    Financial Analyst, Full Stack Developer, Java Developer, and ~15 more).
    Synced from Onboarding. 89% populated; AI/ML Engineer is the biggest
    single track (164), and legacy near-duplicate values exist in data
    ("Ai/ML", "Java Full Stack" vs "Java Full Stack Developer").

    Newer, coarser niche classification: AI ML Engineer | Python
    Developer/Engineer | Java Fullstack Developer/Engineer | Product/
    Project Manager | Marketing Manager | Finance Analyst | Other. Written

    Technology__c is still the field with real coverage.

Preferred_Job_Positions__c (Preferred Job Positions) [Text]
Preferred_Job_Locations__c (Preferred Job Locations) [Text]

Preferred_Locations__c (Preferred Locations) [TextArea]
    Comma-separated preferred work locations ("New Jersey, New York, Texas"

Preferred_Tech_stack_If_Applicable__c (Preferred Tech stack (If
Applicable)) [Text]
    Tech stack the candidate prefers to be marketed on (e.g. "React +

Open_to_relocate__c (Open to relocate) [Checkbox]

Job_Seeking_Intensity__c (Job Seeking Intensity) [Number(1,0)]

Communication_Skills_Rating__c (Communication Skills Rating) [Number(1,0)]

Salary_Expectations__c (Salary Expectations) [Text]
    Free-text salary expectation ("120k", "60/hr C2C") - synced from

Current_Rate_Expectation__c (Current Rate Expectation) [Currency(18,0)]
    Numeric rate expectation: hourly for contractors, annual for full-time

Interview_Support__c (Interview Support) [Checkbox]

--- GROUP J: TRAINING PLAN & CANDIDATE COMMERCIALS ----------------------------
Candidates PAY Techsara for the career program - these fields are the
candidate-side commercial terms (distinct from Group L's client terms).

Plan__c (Plan) [Picklist]
    The program tier purchased: Career Launcher | Career Accelerator |
    Premium / Fastrack | Ultimate Career Architect. Set at onboarding
    (synced from the form). 71% populated; Career Accelerator dominates
    (691 of 722). Read by the invoicing/payment-plan flows.

Upfront_Amount__c (Upfront Amount) [Currency(18,2)]
    The upfront fee paid at enrollment (67% populated). Copied to/from
    Onboarding; input to the payment-plan flow.

Offer_letter_amount__c (Offer letter amount) [Currency(18,2)]
    The fee due when the candidate receives an offer letter (the success
    fee). 67% populated; the Record Offer Letter Payment action invoices
    it.

Salary__c (Salary %) [Percent(14,2)]
    Percentage-of-salary component of the agreement (e.g. X% of first-year
    salary). 70% populated. Copied to/from Onboarding.

January_Kicker_Rate__c (January Kicker Rate) [Percent(18,2)]
    An additional "kicker" percentage applied from January (a promotional /
    seasonal pricing term). Rarely used (not fully documented - verify with
    team).

Joining_Date__c (Joining Date) [Date]
    Date the candidate joined the program (or their placement start date -
    usage varies; verify with team).

Preferred_Training_Schedule_EST__c (Preferred Training Schedule EST)
[Picklist]
    Which daily training slot the candidate wants, quoted in EST:
    9:30-11:30 AM | 11:30 AM-1:30 PM | 2:30-4:30 PM | 4:30-6:30 PM.
    Captured at lead conversion; read when assigning training cohorts.

Service_Agreement_Sent__c (Service Agreement Sent?) [Checkbox]
    The service agreement went out (DocuSign). 49 checked. Set by the
    agreement-sending process on the Onboarding side.

QB_Customer_ID__c (QB Customer ID) [Text, external ID]
    The QuickBooks customer id for this account - stamped by the Send
    Invoice flow the first time an invoice is pushed (it searches QB,
    creates the customer if needed, saves the id for reuse). 21 populated.

--- GROUP K: DOCUSIGN AGREEMENT BLOCK (DS_*) ----------------------------------
Twenty fields that feed DocuSign document generation for the service
agreement and ACH (bank auto-debit) authorization. They duplicate identity
data on purpose: the agreement must carry EXACTLY what the candidate typed,
frozen from their legal documents, independent of later profile edits.
Maintained on the candidate page's "DocuSign Candidate Information" section
and via the Send_ACH_and_Promissory flow. Bank/ID fields are sensitive -
check field-level security before exposing.

DS_First_Name__c / DS_Middle_Name__c / DS_Last_Name__c (DS First/Middle/
Last Name) [Text]
    Legal name exactly as it must appear on the agreement.

DS_Person_Email__c (DS Person Email) [Email]
DS_Person_Phone__c (DS Person Phone) [Phone]
    Contact details to print on the agreement / route the envelope to.

DS_Date_Of_Birth__c (DS Date Of Birth) [Date]
    DOB as on the legal ID.

DS_Address_Line_1__c / DS_Address_Line_2__c / DS_City__c /
DS_State_Province__c / DS_ZIP_Postal_Code__c (DS Address block)
[Text / Picklist (global "State" value set) / Text]
    Legal address for the agreement.

DS_Bank_Name__c (DS Bank Name) [Text]
DS_Account_Type__c (DS Account Type) [Picklist: Checking | Savings]
    Bank details for the ACH auto-debit authorization.

DS_ACH_Identification_Type__c (DS ACH Identification Type) [Picklist:
Passport | Driver's License | State Id]
DS_ACH_Identification_Number__c (DS ACH Identification Number) [Text]
DS_ACH_Issuing_Authority__c (DS ACH Issuing Authority) [Text]
    The ID document presented for the ACH authorization: type, number, and
    who issued it.

DS_Service_Identification_Type__c (DS Service Identification Type)
[Picklist: Passport | Driver's License | State Id]
DS_Service_Identification_Number__c (DS Service Identification Number)
[Text]
DS_Service_Issuing_Authority__c (DS Service Issuing Authority) [Text]
    Same ID triplet for the SERVICE agreement document.

DS_Today_Date__c (DS Today Date) [Formula, Text]
    Today's date formatted MM/DD/YYYY - merged into the generated document
    as the signing date.

--- GROUP L: CLIENT / VENDOR (BUSINESS ACCOUNT) FIELDS ------------------------
Only meaningful on B2B Client / Vendor business accounts (11 records).

Client_Status__c (Client Status) [Picklist]
    Relationship state: Prospect | Active | On Hold | Inactive. Help text:
    Active = sending requirements; On Hold = temporarily paused; Inactive =
    no longer working; Prospect = new unqualified. Currently empty on all
    business accounts (the B2B practice is brand new).

Client_Type__c (Client Type) [Picklist]
    What kind of company: Direct Client (hiring directly) | Vendor
    (staffing vendor) | Implementation Partner (tech implementation
    company) | MSP (Managed Service Provider) | Other. All 7 typed
    accounts are "Direct Client" today. Also written by the B2B branch of
    the lead-conversion flow.

Payment_Terms__c (Payment Terms) [Picklist]
    Agreed invoice terms with the client: Net 15 | Net 30 | Net 45 |
    Net 60. Help text: Net 30 is standard, confirm with Finance before
    changing.

Default_Submission_Email__c (Default Submission Email) [Email]
    Where candidate submissions are emailed for this client (hiring manager
    or vendor coordinator, per help text). Read by the B2B submission flow.

Confidential_Client__c (Confidential Client) [Checkbox]
    Client asked for confidentiality: when checked, the client name must
    NOT appear on website job postings regardless of other settings (help
    text). Read by the job-posting/website process.

Account_Manager__c (Account Manager) [Lookup -> User]
    The internal AM who owns this CLIENT relationship - defaulted onto
    every Job Requirement created for the client (help text), from where it
    cascades to submissions and interviews. 1 populated so far.

--- GROUP M: INTERVIEW & APPLICATION COUNTERS ---------------------------------
Five are real ROLLUP SUMMARY fields (system-computed from the Interview__c
master-detail); six are plain number fields that nothing currently fills.

Total_no_of_Interviews_Initial_calls__c (Total no. of Interviews & Initial
calls) [Rollup Summary, COUNT]
    Count of ALL child Interview__c records regardless of type - the
    candidate's grand total of interviews + initial calls.

Total_Number_of_Interview__c (Total Number of Interviews) [Rollup Summary,
COUNT filtered]
    Count of child interviews with record type "Interview" only (real
    interviews, excluding initial calls). This is the live counter shown in
    the page's Interviews Summary section and compared against
    Expected_No_of_Interviews__c.

Total_Number_of_Initial_Calls__c (Total Number of Initial Calls) [Rollup
Summary, COUNT filtered]
    Count of child interviews with record type "Initial Call".

Interviews_Ghosted__c (Interviews Ghosted) [Rollup Summary, COUNT filtered]
    Count of "Interview"-type children whose STATUS is Ghosted - how often
    companies went silent on this candidate.

Interviews_Rejected__c (Interviews Rejected) [Rollup Summary, COUNT
filtered]
    Count of "Interview"-type children whose STATUS is Rejected.

Total_Interviews__c (Total Interviews) [Number]
    Plain number meant to be maintained by the
    Update_Total_Interviews_on_Candidate flow - but that flow is DRAFT, so
    the field is empty on every record. Use the rollups instead.

Total_Number_of_Interviews__c (Total Number of Interviews) [Number]
    Older manual counter with the same label as the rollup above; empty on
    every record. Legacy - ignore.

Total_Number_of_Applications__c (Total Number of Applications) [Number]
    Intended count of job applications made for the candidate; only 6
    records have a value. The real application counts live on
    Application__c / Marketing__c.

Total_Training_Sessions__c (Total Training Sessions) [Number(5,0)]
    Intended training-session counter; empty on all records (session
    attendance is tracked on Session_Attendee__c instead).

Total_Internal_Interviews_Excl_Intake__c (Total Internal Interviews Excl
Intake) [Number(5,0)]
    Intended count of internal screening interviews excluding the intake
    call; empty on all records.

Latest_Internal_Interview_Date__c (Latest Internal Interview Date)
[DateTime]
    Intended stamp of the most recent internal interview; empty on all
    records.

--- GROUP N: NOTES & FREE-FORM CONTENT ----------------------------------------

9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 1,013. Created 2024-08-06 to 2026-08-07.
- Flavors: Person Account (candidates) 765 (75.5%) | Recruiter (employee
  portal identities, also person accounts) 237 (23.4%) | B2B Client 7 |
  no record type (Master) 4 | Vendor / Implementation Partner 0 |
  Recruiters(Do Not Use) 0. IsPersonAccount: true 1,002 / false 11.
- Candidate status (PersonAccount RT only): Active 299 | Closed 258 |
  Hold 183 | Terminate 16 | Placed 7 | In Progress 2. (Employee "Recruiter"
  records: Active 235, Closed 2.) Only 7 Placed - the funnel's endpoint is
  rare; Closed + Hold together outnumber Active.
- Ownership: 378 records (37%) owned by INACTIVE users - the reassignment
  backlog called out in the security redesign docs.
- Work authorization: OPT 572 | (blank) 364 | USC 22 | H1B 19 | Green Card
  14 | H4 11 | CPT 6 | Other 5. Current_Visa_Status__c is only 9%
  populated - Work_Authorization__c is the maintained field.
- Plan: Career Accelerator 691 | (blank) 291 | Career Launcher 18 |
  Premium / Fastrack 10 | Ultimate Career Architect 3.
- Technology (candidates, top): AI/ML Engineer 164 | (blank) 116 |
  Financial Analyst 55 | Software Engineer 43 | Full Stack Developer 42 |
  Product Manager 41 | Data Engineer 29 (plus legacy near-duplicates like
  "Ai/ML"). Niche__c populated on only 111 records.
- Population of key fields: PersonEmail 98% | Phone 75% | Plan 71% |
  Salary % 70% | Upfront / Offer amounts 67% | Application Start Date 66% |
  Assigned Recruiter 65% | Work Authorization 64% | Marketing Email 51% |
  DOB 42% | Open to relocate 42% checked | Last Alert Sent 30% |
  YoE 24% | Candidate Referral 21% | LinkedIn URL 18% | Slack User Id 137
  (employees) | Comm. Skills Rating 97 | QB Customer ID 21.
- Effectively unused (as of this snapshot): all six plain-number counters
  in Group M (0-6 records), Internal_Interview__c lookup (0),
  Acknowledgement_Declaration__c (0), Default_Vendor__c (1),
  Account_Manager__c (1), Previously_Engaged_with_Other_Consultanc__c (1),
  Active_CPT__c / Currently_Employed__c / Sponsorship_Required (3 each),
  Resume_Ready__c / Active_for_B2B_Submission__c (3 each - B2B is new),
  Interview_Support__c (5), Client_Status__c (empty on all clients).
- Key takeaway for answering questions: "Account" almost always means a
  CANDIDATE Person Account; remember the 237 employee "Recruiter" person
  accounts exist purely for portal logins (do not count them as
  candidates), and the business-account side is tiny (11 records) because
  the B2B client practice is just starting.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Contact  (Label: "Contact")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The standard Salesforce Contact object - a person attached to an Account. In
THIS org it plays two very different roles, and knowing which one you are
looking at matters for almost every question:

  a) PERSON-ACCOUNT SHADOW CONTACTS (98% of records). Because candidates and
     employees are Person Accounts, every Person Account automatically owns a
     hidden Contact record behind the scenes. Users never open these directly -
     they work on the Account - but the platform NEEDS them: a portal login
     (User record) must point at a Contact, so every one of the 233 community
     users in the org hangs off one of these person contacts.
  b) B2B CLIENT/VENDOR CONTACTS (24 records). Real business contacts - the
     people at a Techsara B2B client or vendor company (hiring managers, HR
     coordinators, vendor managers). This flavor is brand new, built for the
     B2B staffing pipeline: 4 custom fields decide who at the client receives
     candidate-submission emails. Like the rest of the B2B path, it is
     designed-but-barely-used so far.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- STANDARD object with 4 custom fields (35 fields tracked in source overall).
- Sharing is "Controlled By Parent": whoever can see the Account can see its
  contacts. Contacts still carry their own OwnerId for contacts saved without
  an account ("private" contacts).
- 1 record type, 0 validation rules, 8 list views (5 of them from the Zoom
  "ZVC" managed package), 3 web links (Google Maps / Google Search standard
  buttons + the Zoom package's "Add To Webinar").
- Scale: 1,026 records in preprod - but only 24 are real business contacts;
  1,002 are the automatic shadow contacts of Person Accounts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES (1)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- "B2B Client/Vendor Contacts" (developer name: B2B_Client_Vendor_Contacts),
  active. Intended for people at B2B client and vendor companies; it scopes
  the picklists (Contact_Role__c, LeadSource, salutations, etc.) for that use.
  IN PRACTICE NO RECORD USES IT YET - all 24 business contacts were created
  with no record type, and person-account shadow contacts never get a Contact
  record type (their record type lives on the Account). Treat it as part of
  the newly built B2B layer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PERSON-ACCOUNT SIDE (automatic, invisible):
  - Creating a candidate or employee Person Account auto-creates the shadow
    Contact. Nobody edits it; it exists so the platform can hang things off
    it - most importantly PORTAL LOGINS: an AIC Portal (Customer Community
    Plus) User record is "enabled" on this contact. All 233 portal users in
    preprod point at a person contact.
  - The interview-creation screen flows (Interview_Creation, _V2,
    B2B_Create_Interview_from_Submission) use this chain in reverse: they take
    the running portal User, read User.ContactId, and resolve through the
    Contact/Person Account to the Recruiter__c ("Employee") record - that is
    how a flow knows WHICH EMPLOYEE is the person currently logged in.
  - The "Create Contact" quick action on Recruiter__c (screen flow
    Create_Recruiter_Contact) is part of this wiring: despite the name it
    creates a PERSON ACCOUNT for the employee (which brings the shadow contact
    with it) and links it back to the Recruiter record - the precondition for
    giving that employee a portal login.

B2B SIDE (manual + lead conversion):
  - When a B2B lead (a client company inquiry) is converted, the
    Lead_Conversion_Flow decides whether a contact with that email already
    exists on the client Account ("Check_Existing_Contact"); if not, it calls
    the Apex LeadConversionHandler action, which creates the Contact on the
    (existing or newly created) business Account, copying FirstName, LastName,
    Email, Phone (into MobilePhone) and Title from the lead, with a
    duplicate-safe insert.
  - Client contacts are then meant to be referenced from
    Job_Requirement__c.Client_Contact__c ("who at the client owns this job
    req" - 3 records linked so far) and to drive submission-email routing via
    the custom fields (Contact_Role__c, Primary_Submission_Contact__c,
    Receives_Submission_Emails__c, Submission_Notes__c). None of those four
    fields is populated on any record yet - the email-routing process is
    designed but not live.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Account (via AccountId): the company (business contact) or the Person
  Account (shadow contact). Sharing is inherited from here. Only 9 of the 24
  business contacts are attached to an Account - the other 15 are unattached
  "private" contacts visible only to their owner.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT CONTACT:
- User (ContactId): the portal login enabled on this contact. Every community
  user (233 in preprod) points at a person contact. This is THE reason the
  shadow contacts matter.
- Job_Requirement__c (Client_Contact__c, Lookup): the client-side contact
  person for a B2B job requirement (3 records populated).
- AccountContactRelation (ContactId): the standard junction letting one
  contact relate to several accounts (see its own section - only auto-created
  rows exist).
- Contact itself (ReportsToId): optional manager-of-this-contact link inside
  the client org chart (unused in data).

EXPLICIT NON-RELATIONSHIPS (common confusions):
- Candidate-facing objects (Interview__c, Marketing__c, Onboarding__c ...) do
  NOT look up Contact - they look up Account (the Person Account). If you are
  hunting for "the candidate", go to Account, not Contact.
- Recruiter__c links to the employee's Person ACCOUNT
  (Recruiter_Contact__c -> Account), not to the Contact record, despite that
  field's "Employee Contact" label.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Contact has no validation rules in this org - data quality on the B2B
contacts relies on the (still unused) record type and on duplicate rules
handled during lead conversion.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- NO record-triggered flows and no Apex trigger run ON Contact.
- Flows that TOUCH it as a lookup:
    * Lead_Conversion_Flow: dedupe check ("is there already a contact with
      this email on that account?") + the two LeadConversionHandler Apex
      actions that CREATE the contact on an existing / new client account.
    * Interview_Creation / Interview_Creation_V2 /
      B2B_Create_Interview_from_Submission: read the running portal user's
      ContactId to resolve the logged-in employee (no writes).
- Apex: LeadConversionHandler.createContactForAccount is the only code that
  inserts Contacts (B2B lead conversion, duplicate-safe insert).
- Quick actions / buttons: the standard "NewContact" create action appears on
  many objects' related lists (Job Submission, Onboarding, Invoice, Session,
  etc. layouts); Recruiter__c's "Create Contact" button launches the
  Create_Recruiter_Contact flow (which actually creates a Person Account -
  see part 4). Web links: Google Maps / Google Search (standard), ZVC "Add To
  Webinar" (Zoom managed package - not part of the recruiting process).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 35, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: IDENTITY & CLASSIFICATION ---------------------------------------

Name (Name) [Standard Name: Salutation + First + Last]
    The person's name. Salutation values: Dr. | Mr. | Mrs. | Ms. | Mx. |
    Prof. For shadow contacts it mirrors the Person Account's name; for B2B
    contacts it is entered manually or copied from the converted lead.

Title (Title) [Text]
    Job title at the client company (e.g. "VP Engineering"). Copied from the
    lead at conversion or typed by the user. Populated on only 2 of 24
    business contacts.

TitleType (Title Type) [Picklist]
    Standard Salesforce-added classification of the title into a seniority
    band (CEO, VP, Director...). Never used in this org.

Department (Department) [Text]
    Free-text department of the person at their company. Unused in practice.

DepartmentGroup (Department Group) [Picklist]
    Standard Salesforce-added normalized department category (companion to
    TitleType). Never used in this org.

Birthdate (Birthdate) [Date]
    Standard birthday field. Not part of any Techsara process; the Zoom
    package ships a "Birthdays This Month" list view over it, unused.

GenderIdentity (Gender Identity) [Picklist]
    Standard optional self-identification: Female | Male | Nonbinary |
    Not Listed | I choose not to disclose. Not used in this org.

Pronouns (Pronouns) [Picklist]
    Standard optional pronouns: He/Him | He/They | She/Her | She/They |
    They/Them | Not Listed. Not used in this org.

Description (Description) [LongTextArea]
    Free-form notes about the person. Manual entry; rarely used.

--- GROUP B: LINKS (ACCOUNT, OWNER, HIERARCHY) -------------------------------

AccountId (Account Name) [Lookup -> Account]
    The company this person belongs to - or, for shadow contacts, the Person
    Account itself (system-managed, do not touch). Only 9 of 24 business
    contacts have it; the 15 without are private contacts only their owner
    can see. Sharing of the contact follows this account.

OwnerId (Owner) [Lookup -> User]
    The internal user who owns the contact record. Defaults to the creator.
    Matters mainly for the 15 account-less contacts (owner-only visibility).

ReportsToId (Reports To) [Lookup -> Contact]
    Optional link to the contact's manager, for mapping the client's org
    chart. Never populated in this org.

--- GROUP C: CONTACT DETAILS (PHONE, EMAIL, ADDRESS) -------------------------

Email (Email) [Email]
    The person's email - the key dedupe field: lead conversion only creates a
    new contact if no contact with this email exists on the target account,
    and the planned submission-email routing sends to it. 18 of 24 business
    contacts have one.

Phone (Business Phone) [Phone]
    Main phone number (17 of 24 populated).

MobilePhone (Mobile Phone) [Phone]
    Mobile number. The lead-conversion Apex writes the LEAD's Phone into
    MobilePhone (not into Phone) when it creates the contact. 3 of 24.

HomePhone (Home Phone) [Phone]
OtherPhone (Other Phone) [Phone]
Fax (Fax) [Phone]
    Standard extra phone/fax fields. All unused in this org.

AssistantName (Assistant's Name) [Text]
AssistantPhone (Asst. Phone) [Phone]
    Standard assistant contact fields. Unused.

MailingAddress (Mailing Address) [Address compound]
    Standard mailing address (street/city/state/zip/country). Manual entry;
    essentially unused - addresses live on the Account side in this org.

OtherAddress (Other Address) [Address compound]
    Second standard address block. Unused.

--- GROUP D: SOURCE, MARKETING & COMPLIANCE FLAGS ----------------------------

LeadSource (Lead Source) [Picklist]
    Where this person came from: Advertisement | Customer Event | Customer
    Referral | Employee Referral | External Referral | Facebook | Google
    AdWords | Instagram | LinkedIn | Other | Partner | Purchased List |
    Trade Show | Webinar | Website. Would be inherited from the converted
    lead; not actively reported on.

ContactSource (Contact Source) [Picklist]
    Standard Salesforce-added "how was this contact captured" system
    picklist. Never used here.

BuyerAttributes (Buyer Attributes) [Multi-select Picklist]
    Standard buying-role tags: BusinessUser | Buyer | Champion |
    DecisionMaker | Detractor | Evaluator | ExecutiveSponsor |
    TechnicalExpert. Overlaps with the custom Contact_Role__c; the org built
    its own field instead - this standard one is unused.

DoNotCall (Do Not Call) [Checkbox]
HasOptedOutOfEmail (Email Opt Out) [Checkbox]
HasOptedOutOfFax (Fax Opt Out) [Checkbox]
    Standard compliance opt-out flags. Manual entry; no automation reads
    them in this org (candidate communications run off Account, not
    Contact).

Jigsaw (Data.com Key) [Text]
LastCURequestDate (Last Stay-in-Touch Request Date) [DateTime]
LastCUUpdateDate (Last Stay-in-Touch Save Date) [DateTime]
    Legacy Data.com / Stay-in-Touch system fields from retired Salesforce
    features. Always empty; ignore.

--- GROUP E: B2B SUBMISSION ROUTING (THE 4 CUSTOM FIELDS) --------------------
All four were built for the B2B pipeline: "when we submit a candidate to this
client, who gets the email and how". ALL FOUR ARE EMPTY ON EVERY RECORD so
far - the process is designed but not yet live.

Contact_Role__c (Contact Role) [Picklist]
    The role this person plays in the client's hiring process: Hiring Manager
    (the decision maker) | HR (HR coordinator) | Vendor Manager (vendor-side
    coordinator) | Technical Panel | Recruiter | Finance | Other. Manual
    entry. Meant to determine who receives candidate submissions and
    interview communications. 0% populated.

Primary_Submission_Contact__c (Primary Submission Contact) [Checkbox]
    Marks THE main recipient of candidate-profile submission emails for this
    client. Business rule (from help text, not enforced by code): only ONE
    contact per client account should be checked. 0% populated.

Receives_Submission_Emails__c (Receives Submission Emails) [Checkbox]
    Marks additional CC recipients of submission emails - multiple contacts
    per client may be checked, in addition to the primary above. 0% populated.

Submission_Notes__c (Submission Notes) [LongTextArea]
    Client-specific instructions for submitting candidates to THIS person -
    e.g. "always send the application as PDF", "include LinkedIn URL", "do
    not mention rate". Manual entry; read by the (future) submission
    process. Unused so far.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 1,026 (created Aug 2024 - Aug 2026).
- Split: 1,002 (98%) are Person Account shadow contacts; only 24 are real
  business contacts.
- Of the 24 business contacts: 18 have Email, 17 Phone, 3 MobilePhone,
  2 Title; only 9 are attached to an Account (15 are private/account-less);
  0 use the B2B record type.
- The 4 custom fields (Contact_Role__c, Primary_Submission_Contact__c,
  Receives_Submission_Emails__c, Submission_Notes__c) are populated on
  0 records - the submission-routing design is not yet in use.
- 233 portal Users point at contacts, and every single one points at a
  PERSON contact (0 business contacts back a login).
- Job_Requirement__c.Client_Contact__c links to a contact on 3 records.
- Key takeaway: for candidate questions ignore Contact and use Account; for
  B2B client-people questions this object is the place, but the data and the
  routing fields are still nearly empty.

================================================================================
OBJECT: AccountContactRelation  (Label: "Account Contact Relationship")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The standard Salesforce junction object that lets ONE Contact be related to
MANY Accounts (beyond the single AccountId on the contact itself). Salesforce
auto-creates a "direct" row whenever a contact is attached to an account;
extra "indirect" rows can be added by hand to say "this person also works
with that other company".

In THIS org it is essentially dormant plumbing: only the 9 auto-created
direct rows exist (one per business contact that has an account), nobody has
ever created an indirect relationship, and the single custom field added to
it (Relationship_Strength__c - grading how strong the relationship with a
client contact is) has never been filled in. It exists because the platform
creates it, plus one custom field someone prepared for future client
relationship management.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- STANDARD junction object between Account and Contact; 8 fields tracked in
  source, 1 custom.
- No record types, no validation rules, no list views, no page-layout
  customization worth noting.
- Access follows the related Account and Contact (a junction has no own
  sharing model).
- Scale: 9 records in preprod - all auto-created direct relations.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every relationship row is the same shape.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - AUTOMATIC CREATION. The moment a Contact gets an AccountId (e.g. the
  lead-conversion Apex creates a client contact on a client account),
  Salesforce silently inserts a direct AccountContactRelation row for that
  pair. That is where all 9 existing rows came from - no user created any of
  them deliberately.

STEP 2 - (NOT HAPPENING YET) MULTI-COMPANY RELATIONSHIPS. The intended future
  use: when the same hiring manager or vendor coordinator works with several
  client companies, add indirect rows so one contact shows under multiple
  accounts, and grade each relationship via Relationship_Strength__c
  (Strong / Neutral / Weak) to know which client relationships are solid.
  No indirect row and no strength value exists yet.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Account (via AccountId): the company side of the pair. In practice a B2B
  client/vendor business account.
- Contact (via ContactId): the person side. In practice one of the 24 B2B
  business contacts (person-account shadow contacts do NOT get relation rows;
  only 9 rows exist - matching the 9 account-attached business contacts).
- Nothing else in the org references AccountContactRelation - no custom
  object, flow, Apex class, report the team relies on, or quick action.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. No validation rules exist on this object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. No flow, Apex trigger, quick action, or scheduled job touches
AccountContactRelation in this org. The only "automation" is the platform
itself auto-creating the direct row when a contact is linked to an account.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 8, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE PAIR --------------------------------------------------------

AccountId (Account) [Lookup -> Account]
    The account side of the relationship. Set by the platform for direct
    rows; would be picked manually for indirect ones. Immutable after
    creation.

ContactId (Contact) [Lookup -> Contact]
    The contact side of the relationship. Same creation rules as above.

--- GROUP B: RELATIONSHIP LIFECYCLE ------------------------------------------

IsDirect (Direct) [Checkbox, system]
    TRUE when this row mirrors the contact's own AccountId (the "home"
    relationship Salesforce created automatically). All 9 rows in preprod
    are direct.

IsActive (Active) [Checkbox]
    Whether the relationship is currently in force. Deactivating (instead of
    deleting) keeps history when a person leaves a company. All 9 rows are
    active.

StartDate (Start Date) [Date]
EndDate (End Date) [Date]
    Optional validity window of the relationship (when the person started /
    stopped being associated with the account). Manual entry; never used
    here.

--- GROUP C: CLASSIFICATION --------------------------------------------------

Roles (Roles) [Multi-select Picklist]
    Standard field for the person's role(s) at that specific account
    (business user, decision maker, etc.). Never populated in this org -
    the team's role field is Contact.Contact_Role__c instead.

Relationship_Strength__c (Relationship Strength) [Picklist] (custom)
    The one custom field: how strong Techsara's relationship with this
    contact at this account is - Strong | Neutral | Weak. Intended for
    client-relationship management on the B2B side (who do we have a warm
    line to?). Manual entry; populated on 0 of 9 records so far.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 9 (created Aug 2024 - Aug 2026), matching the 9 business
  contacts that are attached to an account.
- All 9 are IsDirect = true and IsActive = true - i.e. purely the automatic
  rows; no indirect (multi-company) relationship has ever been created.
- Relationship_Strength__c: empty on all 9. Roles: empty on all 9.
- Key takeaway: this object currently answers no business question; if asked
  about client-people roles/strength, note the fields exist but hold no data
  yet.

================================================================================
OBJECT: User  (Label: "User")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The standard Salesforce User object - a LOGIN IDENTITY: username, password,
profile (license + baseline permissions), role (sharing position) and locale.
Everyone and everything that authenticates to the org is a User: internal
staff, the ~130 employees who log in through the AIC Portal community,
Experience-site guest users, and system/integration users.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS MOST IN THIS ORG: User is NOT the employee
record. Recruiter__c (label "Employee") is the HR/staffing profile of a
Techsara staff member - department, manager chain, skills, Slack id,
incentives. User is only "the account that logs in". Most "who works on
this?" lookups across the org point at Recruiter__c; User appears mainly in
audit fields ("who clicked this button"), owner fields, and platform wiring.
An employee typically has BOTH: a Recruiter__c record (the profile) and a
User record (the login), joined via Recruiter__c.Recruiter_User__c and via
the employee's Person Account.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- STANDARD object; 50 fields tracked in source, 5 custom: 1 hand-built
  (Slack_User_Id__c) and 4 from the DocuSign eSignature managed package
  (dfsle__ namespace).
- Org-wide default for User sharing is Read (users can see each other).
- No record types, no validation rules. 4 list views (incl. "AIC Portal
  Users" - all users on the AIC Portal profile), 1 field set
  (PersonalInfo_EPIM - a field-masking set for Einstein privacy tooling),
  1 compact layout.
- Scale: 302 user records in preprod (Aug 2024 - Jul 2026); 168 active,
  134 deactivated (users are never deleted in Salesforce, only deactivated).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. User does not support record types; the "flavors" of user are carried
by UserType/license and Profile instead (see part 4).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE USER POPULATIONS (by license/UserType, live data):
  - EXTERNAL PORTAL STAFF - 233 records (128 active), UserType
    "PowerCustomerSuccess" = CUSTOMER COMMUNITY PLUS license, profile
    "AIC Portal". This is how MOST staff work: they log into the AIC Portal
    Experience site, not the internal Salesforce app. Each of these logins is
    enabled on the employee's own PERSON ACCOUNT - every portal user's
    ContactId points at a person contact (see the Contact section). Their
    record access is held down by sharing/OWD, not the profile.
  - INTERNAL USERS - 57 records (30 active), UserType "Standard" = full
    Salesforce license: the Bench Marketing team (20 active, IP-restricted
    profile), 5 System Administrators, and a handful of integration/legacy
    logins (API-only integration profiles, Read Only, etc.).
  - GUEST USERS - 6 (5 active): the unauthenticated visitor identity of each
    Experience site (Candidate Portal, Talent Hub, AIC Portal site,
    Techsara Candidate Hub, QuickBooks webhook site).
  - SYSTEM USERS - 4 Automated Process users + 1 Cloud Integration user +
    1 inactive Chatter-only user. Platform-owned; ignore for business
    questions.

PROVISIONING A NEW EMPLOYEE LOGIN (the HR portal-user lifecycle):
  - HR runs the "Provision Employee Portal User" screen flow (with
    Reset_Employee_Portal_Password and Employee_Offboarding as siblings; all
    three Active in this snapshot). Because HR themselves are external
    Customer Community Plus users who cannot Manage Users, the flows call the
    PortalUserAdminAction Apex, which calls the PortalUserAdminRest
    @RestResource over the "Admin_Identity" named credential - the code then
    runs AS a System Administrator (the connected app's run-as user) to:
    reassign the person account to an internal owner, create the Customer
    Community Plus login on the person contact, reset a password, or
    deactivate a login when someone leaves.
  - (Older/standard path: the Communities*/Lightning* self-register
    controllers exist for community self-registration but the HR-driven flow
    above is the built process for employees.)

ROLES & THE SECURITY REDESIGN: 273 of 302 users have a UserRoleId - portal
  users automatically get a per-account community role, internal users sit in
  the 14-role internal hierarchy. The org's ACTIVE PROJECT is the
  role-hierarchy/security redesign: segmenting data department/team-wise via
  role hierarchy + record ownership, with all portal users on Customer
  Community Plus (see docs/security intake and the Role Hierarchy Blueprint).
  User.UserRoleId is where that design lands physically.

DAY-TO-DAY: users appear as record owners (OwnerId on every ownable object),
  in CreatedById/LastModifiedById audit stamps, in "who initiated this AI
  run" audit lookups on Interview__c / AI_Assignment_Logs__c, and as the
  Account_Manager__c on the B2B objects. Slack notifications @-mention
  people via Slack_User_Id__c.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LINKS FROM USER:
- Contact (ContactId): the contact the portal login is enabled on - in this
  org ALWAYS a Person Account contact (233 of 233). Empty for internal users.
- Profile (ProfileId): license + baseline permissions. Active users: AIC
  Portal 128, Bench Marketing 20, System Administrator 5, the rest are
  guest/integration profiles (1-2 each).
- UserRole (UserRoleId): position in the sharing hierarchy (internal role or
  auto-created portal account role). 273 of 302 populated.
- User (ManagerId, DelegatedApproverId): standard manager / approval-delegate
  links. ManagerId is empty on ALL users - the real manager chain lives on
  Recruiter__c (Assigned_Sr_Recruiter__c etc.), not here.

KEY OBJECTS THAT POINT AT USER (beyond OwnerId/CreatedById everywhere):
- Recruiter__c (Recruiter_User__c): THE bridge from the Employee profile to
  its login (44 employees linked so far). RecruiterHierarchyService walks
  Recruiter__c, not the User table, to compute the staff hierarchy.
- Account (Account_Manager__c), Job_Requirement__c / Job_Submission__c
  (Account_Manager__c, Submitted_By__c): the B2B account-manager fields.
- Interview__c (Account_Manager__c, User_Initiated_By__c,
  Reassignment_Initiated_By__c) and AI_Assignment_Logs__c (7 audit lookups:
  who ran the nightly scheduler, manual runs, reassignment / reshuffle /
  rollback / preferred-support-person actions, last support person): the AI
  (COMPASS) assignment audit trail.
- Training: Candidate_Training__c (Assigned_Trainer_User__c,
  Candidate_Owner__c), CandidateTrainingStep__c (Assigned_Trainer_User__c),
  Cohort__c (Lead_Trainer__c), Deliverable__c (Approved_By__c,
  Submitted_By__c).
- Interview_Participant__c (User__c): internal attendee identity on an
  interview roster.
- Zoom recording compliance: Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c (User__c,
  Opened_By__c), Zoom_Recording_User_Folder_Map__c (User__c, Granted_By__c) -
  who may see / did open which recording folder.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. No validation rules exist on User; integrity is enforced by the
platform (unique Username, license limits) and the provisioning Apex.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- NO record-triggered flow or trigger runs ON User in this org.
- FLOWS READ IT (8 per the reverse map, all lookups, no writes): the
  interview-creation flows (Interview_Creation / _V2 /
  B2B_Create_Interview_from_Submission) fetch the running user's ContactId /
  IsPortalEnabled to resolve which Employee is logged in;
  Interview_support_person_Assign, Interview_Send_for_Approval,
  Job_Requirement_Set_Defaults_On_Create,
  B2b_job_requirement_updated_notification_flow and
  Onboarding_Alert_after_Service_Agreement_signed look up users for
  defaults/notification addressing.
- APEX THAT WRITES USER: PortalUserAdminRest (called via PortalUserAdminAction
  from the HR flows over the Admin_Identity named credential) creates the
  Customer Community Plus login, resets passwords, and deactivates users -
  running as an admin because HR are external users. The standard
  self-registration controllers (CommunitiesSelfRegController,
  LightningSelfRegisterController, MicrobatchSelfRegController,
  SiteRegisterController) can also create community users.
- APEX THAT READS USER: SlackCalloutHelper queries User.Slack_User_Id__c to
  @-mention support people in the CC list of Slack messages;
  ZoomRecording* classes check the running user for recording access.
- The planned permission-set auto-assign flow for new employees (specced in
  Components_needs/create_list.docs) will act on the User/permission-set
  layer when built.

- Total user records: 302 (created Aug 2024 - Jul 2026); 168 active /

  (128 active) | full Salesforce ("Standard") 57 (30 active) | Guest 6
  (5 active site guests) | Automated Process 4 | Cloud Integration 1 |
  Chatter-only 1 (inactive).

  runs through the portal) | Bench Marketing 20 | System Administrator 5 |
  system/no-profile 5 | integration & guest profiles 1-2 each.

  contacts back a login.

  FederationIdentifier on 0 (no SSO).
- Slack_User_Id__c on 217 (72%). DocuSign-provisioned users: 3.
