================================================================================
OBJECT: Vendor__c  (Label: "Vendor")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Vendor__c is the DIRECTORY OF INTERVIEW-SUPPORT ("PROXY") PROVIDERS - the
people and agencies who join a candidate's interview call to help the
candidate through it. On the Interview record the lookup to this object is
labeled "Proxy Support", so users mostly know these records as "proxies",
not "vendors". Two flavors live in the same object:
  a) EXTERNAL vendors: outside agencies and the individual proxy persons who
     work under them (the person record points at the agency record through
     Vendor_Parent__c).
  b) IN-HOUSE proxies: Techsara's own people acting as proxy support,
     flagged with In_House_Proxy__c and addressed on Slack through their
     Slack user id.
It is a tiny reference master (5 custom fields) with no automation of its
own - all the action happens on Interview__c, which reads this directory
when a proxy is assigned to an interview.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Interviewing / interview-support domain.
- Standalone object with its own owner. Org-wide sharing is Public
  Read/Write internally; external (portal) sharing default is Read.
- Self-referencing: Vendor_Parent__c builds a two-level agency -> person
  hierarchy inside the same object.
- 5 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Name is a plain text field labeled "Vendor Name".
- Record page: Vendor_Record_Page FlexiPage (no custom buttons on it).
- Scale: 0 records in preprod - the directory is EMPTY in this sandbox
  (see part 9). The object is real and load-bearing in the process, but its
  rows did not survive into this environment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every vendor/proxy record has the same shape; the In_House_Proxy__c
checkbox (not a record type) separates the two business flavors.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - MAINTAINING THE DIRECTORY. Vendor records are created and edited by
  hand (standard New button). No flow, quick action, or integration creates
  or updates them. An agency gets one record; each individual proxy person
  under it gets a child record pointing at the agency via Vendor (Parent).
  In-house proxies get In_House_Proxy__c checked plus their Slack user id.

STEP 2 - ASSIGNMENT TO AN INTERVIEW. When an employee has raised an
  interview support request (Interview__c.Request_Raised__c) and the support
  team decides a proxy will help, they set the interview's "Proxy Support"
  lookup (Interview__c.Vendor__c) to a record from this directory. The Apex
  InterviewTriggerHandler reacts: it auto-advances the interview's Approve
  Stage to "Assigned", and SlackCalloutHelper posts a "Request has been
  approved" message to the support Slack channel. In that message the "Proxy
  Name" line is built from this object: an in-house proxy is @-mentioned via
  Slack_User_Id_c__c; an external one appears as plain text; when the proxy
  has a parent vendor, the parent agency's name is appended in parentheses.

STEP 3 - DAILY DIGEST. The scheduled Apex job AccountSchedulerJob posts an
  "Interview Schedule Summary" table to Slack every day listing today's
  interviews where support is being provided, with "Parent Vendor" and
  "Vendor Name" columns read from this object.

STEP 4 - CANDIDATE DEFAULT (DESIGNED, NOT LIVE). Account.Default_Vendor__c
  can store a candidate's usual proxy; the Draft screen flow "Interview:
  Approval of Support Request" was built to use it when approving a support
  request, but that flow is not active and its button is not on any page.

AFTERWARDS: whether the supported interview succeeded is tracked back on the
Interview record (Advanced to Next Round?, Vendor Feedback, Interview
Support provided?), not on the Vendor record - this object stays a static
directory.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELF:
- Vendor__c (via Vendor_Parent__c, lookup): the parent vendor agency of an
  individual proxy person. Deleting the parent blanks the child's link
  (no cascade).

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT VENDOR:
- Interview__c.Vendor__c (lookup, label "Proxy Support"): which proxy
  supports that interview. Setting it fires the Approve-Stage/Slack Apex
  described above. 38 interviews carry a value in preprod (but the ids no
  longer resolve - see part 9).
- Account.Default_Vendor__c (lookup, label "Default Vendor", relationship
  "CandidateVendor"): the candidate's usual proxy. 1 record populated;
  only the Draft approval flow was designed to read it.

No other object references Vendor__c, and it has no child objects besides
its own self-hierarchy.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. There are no validation rules on Vendor__c - any combination of
fields saves.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Nothing runs ON Vendor__c itself - no record-triggered flows, no triggers,
no quick actions. It is a hand-maintained directory. The automation that
READS it lives elsewhere:
- InterviewTriggerHandler (Apex, on Interview__c): before update, when the
  interview's Vendor lookup is newly set, auto-sets Approve_Stage__c to
  "Assigned"; after update it calls SlackCalloutHelper.
- SlackCalloutHelper (Apex): builds the support-approval Slack message using
  Vendor name, In_House_Proxy__c, Slack_User_Id_c__c and the parent
  vendor's name.
- AccountSchedulerJob (scheduled Apex): daily Slack summary table of
  today's supported interviews with Parent Vendor / Vendor Name columns.
- Interview_Approval_of_Support_Request (screen flow, DRAFT - not live):
  would set the interview's proxy from the candidate's Default Vendor.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (5 custom + the standard Name)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: IDENTITY & CONTACT ----------------------------------------------

Name (Vendor Name) [Text, standard name field]
    The vendor's or proxy person's display name. For agency records this is
    the agency name; for individual proxies it is the person's name. Shown
    as "Vendor Name" / "Proxy Name" in Slack messages and the daily
    interview summary table. Entered manually.

Email__c (Email) [Email]
    The vendor's email address (field description: "Vendor's Email"). Manual
    entry; used by the team for contacting the provider - no automation or
    template reads it. Population unknown (no records in preprod).

Phone__c (Phone) [Phone]
    The vendor's phone number (description: "Vendor's Phone Number").
    Manual entry, contact-info only; nothing automated reads it.

--- GROUP B: CLASSIFICATION & HIERARCHY --------------------------------------

In_House_Proxy__c (In House Proxy) [Checkbox]
    TRUE = this proxy is a Techsara-internal person acting as interview
    support, not an outside vendor. Set manually when the record is created.
    Read by SlackCalloutHelper: in-house proxies are @-mentioned in the
    support-approval Slack message (using Slack_User_Id_c__c) so the person
    is pinged directly; external vendors are shown as plain text only.

Vendor_Parent__c (Vendor (Parent)) [Lookup -> Vendor__c]
    Links an individual proxy person to the vendor AGENCY they belong to
    (self-lookup, child relationship name "vendors"). Read by both the
    Slack approval message and the daily summary, which show the person AND
    the agency ("Proxy Name (Agency Name)" / separate "Parent Vendor"
    column) so ops always knows which agency a proxy came from. Deleting
    the agency record blanks this link on its people.

--- GROUP C: SLACK INTEGRATION -----------------------------------------------

Slack_User_Id_c__c (Slack User Id) [Text, 255]
    The proxy's Slack member id (e.g. "U0123ABCD"), used to build the
    "<@id>" mention in the support-approval Slack message for IN-HOUSE
    proxies. Entered manually by an admin who copies it from Slack. Note
    the odd API name ending in "_c__c" - a naming slip when the field was
    created; the label is simply "Slack User Id". Same pattern as
    Recruiter__c.Slack_User_Id__c and User.Slack_User_Id__c used elsewhere.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 0 - and nothing in the recycle bin either. The vendor
  directory is EMPTY in this sandbox.
- Despite that, 38 Interview__c records and 1 Account still hold Vendor
  lookup ids that no longer resolve to any record (Vendor__r.Name comes
  back blank) - dangling references left over from rows that existed when
  those interviews were created. The directory presumably has real rows in
  production, or the rows were purged after the sandbox copy - verify with
  team before relying on vendor data in preprod.
- Consequence: every field population stat is 0 here; the field meanings
  above are established from metadata descriptions and the Apex code that
  consumes them, not from data.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Company__c  (Label: "Company")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Company__c is the MASTER LIST OF OUTSIDE COMPANIES candidates interview
with (the object description says exactly that: "Master list of companies
used in Interview records"). One record = one employer in the open job
market ("Google", "Walmart", a startup...). It exists to replace the old
free-text company name on Interview__c with a real record, so that:
  a) every interview at the same employer links to the SAME company record
     (dedupe, per-company reporting, "how many interviews at X this month");
  b) market intelligence can be stored once per company - its Tier, the
     derived Interview Difficulty, and how many rounds it typically runs.
Do not confuse it with: Account (Techsara's own B2B clients/vendors are
business Accounts), or the legacy Interview__c.Company__c TEXT field (the
old free-text name this object replaced - the current link field on
Interview is company_new__c).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Interviewing / market-intelligence domain.
- Standalone object with its own owner; org-wide sharing Public Read/Write
  (internal and external). Field history tracking is enabled on the object.
- 4 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Name is plain text labeled "Company Name" - and it is actively rewritten
  by a normalization flow on every save (see part 7).
- Record pages: two FlexiPages exist (Company_Record_Page and
  Company_Record_Page1); Company_Record_Page1 is the active View override.
- Scale: 8,101 records in preprod, all created between Apr 2026 and Aug
  2026 - the master list is a recent build, largely backfilled from
  historical interview company names.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. All companies are one flavor; Tier__c is the classification field.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATION. Two paths:
  - On the fly during interview scheduling: the Interview_Creation_V2 screen
    flow (the marketing-path "create interview" wizard) looks the company up
    by name and, if it does not exist yet, CREATES the Company__c record
    right there (name + website) before linking the new interview to it.
    (The older Interview_Creation flow did the same but is Obsolete.)
  - Bulk backfill: the record creation dates (Apr-Aug 2026) show the list
    was mass-built recently, most likely from the historical free-text
    company names on ~10k interviews.

STEP 2 - NAME NORMALIZATION ON EVERY SAVE. The active record-triggered flow
  Normalize_Company_Name_on_Save rewrites the Name before any create or
  update: it uppercases the name, trims it, and strips corporate suffixes
  and filler words in four passes - US forms (INC, LLC, CORP, LTD, LP...),
  India forms (PVT LTD, PRIVATE LIMITED, OPC, HUF, "(INDIA)"...), Europe
  forms (GMBH, SARL, BV, AG, OY, SPA...), and generic words (TECHNOLOGIES,
  SOLUTIONS, SERVICES, GROUP, LABS, CONSULTING...). "Acme Solutions Pvt.
  Ltd." and "ACME INC" both save as "ACME", so duplicate spellings converge
  on one canonical record. Side effect to know: company names in this org
  are stored UPPERCASED and shortened.

STEP 3 - ENRICHMENT (MOSTLY STILL TO DO). Users can classify the company
  with Tier__c; the Interview_Difficulty__c formula instantly derives how
  hard its interviews are expected to be, and Typical_Rounds__c records how
  many rounds its process usually has. In practice this intelligence layer
  is barely curated yet (see part 9) - a bulk default put ~86% of companies
  in the top tier, and Typical Rounds is filled on only 8 records.

STEP 4 - CONSUMPTION. Interview__c.company_new__c (label "Company") points
  here on 98% of all interviews - this is the normal "which company is the
  candidate interviewing with" field for the marketing pipeline. The
  interview's Company_Name__c formula displays this record's name, and the
  interview dedupe keys (candidate + company + month) rely on everyone
  linking to the same company record. Two more references exist but are
  essentially unused so far: Job_Requirement__c.Client_Company__c (B2B
  requirement's client as a market company - 1 record) and
  Lead.Company_Name__c (11 records).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OBJECTS THAT POINT AT COMPANY (it has no outbound links of its own):
- Interview__c.company_new__c (lookup, label "Company"): the main consumer -
  which market employer the candidate interviews with. Populated on 9,818
  of 9,991 interviews (98%).
- Job_Requirement__c.Client_Company__c (lookup): ties a B2B job requirement
  to a company from this master list. Only 1 record so far - the B2B path
  normally uses the Account object for its clients instead.
- Lead.Company_Name__c (lookup): links a website lead to a company record
  (e.g. current employer / target company). 11 leads populated - marginal.

NON-RELATIONSHIP to keep straight: Interview__c.Company__c is a legacy TEXT
field (a name string), not a lookup to this object, and the Apex classes
that mention "Company__c" (GoogleCalendarAPI, SlackCalloutHelper,
InterviewRoundNumberBackfill) all read that text field - NO Apex touches
this Company__c object; it is flow-managed only.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Nothing blocks saving a company; even Name duplicates are prevented
only softly, by the normalization flow making variants converge.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOW (active):
- Normalize_Company_Name_on_Save (before save, create + update): the name
  cleaner described in part 4 - uppercase, trim, strip US/India/Europe
  corporate suffixes and generic filler words. Runs on EVERY save, so even
  a manual rename gets re-normalized.

CREATED BY (flows on other objects):
- Interview_Creation_V2 (active screen flow, marketing interview wizard):
  looks up the company by name and creates the Company__c record (Name +
  Company Website) when no match exists.
- Interview_Creation (screen flow, OBSOLETE): the older version of the
  same wizard, also able to create companies. Superseded by V2.

No Apex, no triggers, no quick actions, no scheduled jobs touch this
object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 4, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: IDENTITY ---------------------------------------------------------

Name (Company Name) [Text, standard name field]
    The canonical company name. Entered by the recruiter (or the interview
    wizard) but then rewritten by Normalize_Company_Name_on_Save: stored
    UPPERCASE with corporate suffixes and filler words stripped, so all
    spellings of one employer collapse into one record. This is what the
    interview's Company_Name__c formula displays.

Company_Website__c (Company Website) [Url]
    The company's official website URL. Field description: "used as a
    unique identifier to distinguish company records" - i.e. the intended
    tiebreaker when two different companies normalize to a similar name.
    Written by the Interview_Creation_V2 wizard when it creates a company.
    CAVEAT: this field exists in the metadata source but was NOT queryable
    in the live preprod org at snapshot time (the API user cannot see it -
    it is either not yet deployed or lacks field-level security), so its
    real population is unknown (not fully documented - verify with team).

--- GROUP B: MARKET INTELLIGENCE ---------------------------------------------

Tier__c (Tier) [Picklist, restricted]
    Classifies the employer by type/size (description: "Categorizes the
    company by type/size"). Values and their meaning:
      FAANG / Top Product    - top-tier product companies (Google, Meta...)
      Product Company        - other product-led software companies
      Startup                - early-stage companies
      Services / Consulting  - IT services and consulting firms
      Mid-Market             - mid-size companies
      Enterprise             - large non-FAANG enterprises
      Other                  - anything else
    Manual entry; the only thing that reads it is the difficulty formula
    below. Data reality: 86% of records sit at "FAANG / Top Product" and
    14% are blank - clearly a bulk-load default, not curated tiering, so
    treat Tier-based reporting with caution for now.

Interview_Difficulty__c (Interview Difficulty) [Formula, Text]
    Derived difficulty rating of this company's interviews, computed purely
    from Tier__c (description: "Calculated difficulty rating based on
    company Tier"): FAANG / Top Product -> "Very Hard"; Product Company ->
    "Hard"; Startup -> "Medium-Hard"; Services / Consulting -> "Medium";
    Mid-Market -> "Medium"; Enterprise -> "Hard"; no tier -> "Not Set".
    Intended to help recruiters and the support team gauge prep intensity;
    while Tier data is a bulk default the output is mostly "Very Hard".

Typical_Rounds__c (Typical Rounds) [Number(2,0)]
    Average number of interview rounds this company's process runs (help
    text: "Average number of interview rounds for this company"). Manual
    knowledge capture so schedulers can tell a candidate "expect ~4
    rounds". Filled on only 8 of 8,101 records - the knowledge base is
    just starting to be built.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 8,101. All created 2026-04-24 to 2026-08-07 - the master
  list is ~4 months old (backfilled), even though interviews go back to
  Jul 2024.
- Tier distribution: FAANG / Top Product 6,939 (85.7%) | blank 1,154
  (14.2%) | Product Company 4 | Startup 3 | Services / Consulting 1 |
  Mid-Market, Enterprise, Other: 0. The extreme FAANG skew is a bulk-load
  default - real tier curation has touched only ~8 records.
- Typical_Rounds__c: populated on 8 records only.
- Company_Website__c: not queryable in the live org (see field note) -
  population unknown.
- Usage: linked from 9,818 interviews (98% of all interviews), 1 job
  requirement, 11 leads.
- Key takeaway: the object's linking job (one record per employer, hooked
  to nearly every interview) is fully in production; its market-
  intelligence job (Tier / difficulty / rounds) is built but not yet
  genuinely populated.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Niche__c  (Label: "Niche")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Niche__c is the master list of SKILL/ROLE TRACKS ("niches") Techsara works
candidates in - e.g. "Java Full Stack", "AI ML Engineer", "Product
Manager". A niche is the unit the INTERNAL screening machinery is organized
around: internal interviews assess a candidate FOR a niche, the question
bank is mapped to niches (via the Niche_Question__c junction), resumes are
tagged with the niche they target, and the hire decision records which
niche the candidate was hired into. It is a tiny two-field reference master
(plus the name) maintained by the training/interviewing admins.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the INTERNAL interviewing / assessment domain
  (the Internal_Interview__c cluster - NOT the external Interview__c side).
- Standalone object with its own owner; org-wide sharing Public Read/Write
  (internal and external). Field history tracking enabled.
- 2 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Name is plain text (label "Niche  Name" - with a stray double space).
- The list view carries a custom "New Niche" button that launches the
  Add_Niche_Flow screen flow (the guided way to add a niche).
- Scale: 10 records in preprod - a deliberately short, curated list.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. All niches are one flavor; Domain_Type__c (Tech / Non Tech) is the
only classification.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - AN ADMIN ADDS A NICHE. Via the "New Niche" list-view button ->
  Add_Niche_Flow (a 2-screen flow that captures Name, Domain Type and the
  Is Active flag and creates the record). All 10 existing niches were
  created in one batch on 2026-05-27 - the catalog was seeded once.

STEP 2 - THE QUESTION POOL IS BUILT. The Bulk_Add_Questions_Flow screen
  flow lets an admin pick a niche and mass-create interview questions
  (Question_Bank__c rows) together with the Niche_Question__c junction rows
  that map each question to the niche. Result: every niche owns a pool of
  questions (currently 105-215 per niche).

STEP 3 - INTERNAL SCREENING RUNS PER NICHE. When Techsara internally
  screens a candidate, the Internal_Interview__c record carries a Niche__c
  lookup ("which track are we assessing this candidate for"). The
  Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview screen flow reads the niche (and its
  Domain_Type__c) to drive section/question selection - pulling from the
  niche's question pool and/or generating AI questions from the resume -
  and at the end the Hired_Niche__c lookup on the internal interview
  records which niche the Hire decision applies to. The View Interview Log
  flow shows the niche when reviewing past internal interviews.

STEP 4 - RESUMES AND TEMPLATES ARE TAGGED. Resume__c.Niche__c tags which
  track a resume version targets, and Template__c.Niche__c ties an internal-
  interview template to its niche (template-driven interviews).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CHILD:
- Niche_Question__c (MASTER-DETAIL child, junction to Question_Bank__c):
  the niche's question pool - one row per question mapped to this niche.
  1,160 mappings across the 10 niches (see that object's section).

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT NICHE (lookups):
- Internal_Interview__c.Niche__c: the track the candidate is being assessed
  for (86 of 302 internal interviews populated).
- Internal_Interview__c.Hired_Niche__c: the track the candidate was
  actually hired into when the decision was Hire (12 populated).
- Resume__c.Niche__c: the track this resume version targets (8 of 17).
- Template__c.Niche__c: the niche an internal-interview template belongs to
  (1 of 1).
- Question_Bank__c.Niche__c and Section__c.Niche__c: single-niche lookups
  that exist in the metadata source but were NOT queryable in the live
  preprod org at snapshot time - likely superseded by the Niche_Question__c
  junction (a question can serve many niches) or awaiting deploy/field-
  level security (not fully documented - verify with team).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Nothing prevents duplicate or inactive-but-referenced niches; the
short curated list is managed by convention.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No record-triggered flows, triggers, or scheduled jobs run ON Niche__c.
The flows that CREATE or READ it:
- Add_Niche_Flow (active screen flow, launched by the "New Niche" list-view
  button): creates a niche with Name, Domain_Type__c, Is_Active__c.
- Bulk_Add_Questions_Flow (active screen flow): looks a niche up, then
  mass-creates Question_Bank__c questions and their Niche_Question__c
  mappings under it.
- Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview (active screen flow): reads the
  niche and its Domain_Type__c while conducting an internal interview
  (question selection, AI question generation path).
- View_Interview_Log_Flow (active screen flow): reads the niche when
  displaying a candidate's internal-interview history.
No Apex touches the Niche__c object (DashboardService's "Niche__c"
references are a same-named field on the training-requirement side, not
this object).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 2, plus the standard Name)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: IDENTITY & CLASSIFICATION ---------------------------------------

Name (Niche  Name) [Text, standard name field]
    The niche's name - a skill/role track like "Java Full Stack" or
    "Product Analyst". Entered via the Add Niche flow. Displayed everywhere
    a niche is referenced (internal interviews, resumes, question pools).

Domain_Type__c (Domain Type) [Picklist, restricted]
    Whether the track is technical: Tech | Non Tech. Set at creation via
    the Add Niche flow. Read by the Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview
    flow (interview sections are themselves Tech/Non Tech typed, so the
    niche's domain steers which sections/questions apply). Current data:
    8 Tech, 2 Non Tech (Product Manager, Product Analyst).

--- GROUP B: LIFECYCLE -------------------------------------------------------

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox, default false]
    Whether the niche is currently offered/usable. Set on creation by the
    Add Niche flow (its screen asks for it - the metadata default is
    false). Shown in search results and the list view as the on/off
    signal; retiring a niche means unchecking this rather than deleting
    (deletion would cascade-delete its Niche_Question__c pool). All 10
    current niches are active.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 10, ALL created in a single batch on 2026-05-27, all with
  Is_Active__c = true.
- Domain split: Tech 8 (AI ML Engineer, Front End Software Developer, Full
  Stack Developer, Java Full Stack, Python Developer, Python Full Stack
  Developer, Software Engineer, Technical Product Manager) | Non Tech 2
  (Product Analyst, Product Manager).
- Question pools: 1,160 Niche_Question__c mappings hang off these 10
  niches - AI ML Engineer has 215, every other niche exactly 105 (a
  scripted seed, not organic growth).
- Referenced by 86 internal interviews (Niche__c), 12 hire decisions
  (Hired_Niche__c), 8 resumes, 1 template.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Niche_Question__c  (Label: "NicheQuestion")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Niche_Question__c is a pure JUNCTION (many-to-many mapping) between the
question bank and the niche catalog: one record = "this interview question
belongs to this niche's question pool". It exists because one question can
serve several niches (e.g. a generic coding question fits both "Java Full
Stack" and "Software Engineer") and each niche needs its own curated pool
for internal interviews. The record carries NO data of its own beyond the
two parent links and an auto-number id.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the INTERNAL interviewing / question-bank domain.
- JUNCTION OBJECT with TWO MASTER-DETAIL parents: Question__c ->
  Question_Bank__c (the primary master - it controls sharing and owner
  inheritance) and Niche__c -> Niche__c. Sharing is "Controlled By Parent";
  deleting EITHER the question or the niche cascade-deletes the mapping.
- 2 custom fields (the two master-details), 0 record types, 0 validation
  rules, 1 list view.
- Auto-number Name in the format NQ-{00000} (label "Niche  Question  ID").
- Scale: 1,160 records in preprod mapping 620 questions to 10 niches
  (~1.9 niches per question on average).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. A mapping row has no flavors - it either exists or it does not.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - POOLS ARE BUILT IN BULK. An admin runs the Bulk_Add_Questions_Flow
  screen flow: they pick a niche, paste/enter a batch of questions, and the
  flow creates the Question_Bank__c rows AND one Niche_Question__c row per
  question linking it to that niche. The data shows this was done as a
  seeding exercise: every niche got a standard pool of 105 mappings (AI ML
  Engineer got 215), created between 2026-05-27 and 2026-07-27.

STEP 2 - POOLS ARE READ DURING INTERNAL INTERVIEWS. When the
  Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview flow runs a NICHE-driven internal
  interview, it queries Niche_Question__c for the interview's niche to pull
  the mapped Question_Bank__c questions (then filters by section/difficulty
  and can shuffle them via the RandomizeQuestions Apex action). Template-
  driven and AI-generated question paths bypass this junction.

STEP 3 - MAINTENANCE. Adding a question to another niche = creating one
  more mapping row; retiring a question from a niche = deleting its row.
  There is no UI button for one-off edits - admins use the flow or standard
  related lists on the Niche / Question Bank record pages.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENTS (both master-detail, both required):
- Question_Bank__c (via Question__c, PRIMARY master): the interview
  question being mapped. Controls the junction's sharing/ownership.
  Deleting a question deletes its mappings.
- Niche__c (via Niche__c, secondary master): the niche whose pool the
  question joins. Deleting a niche deletes its whole pool of mappings.

Both parents use the same child relationship name ("Niche_Questions"), so
each Niche record page and each Question Bank record page shows a "Niche
Questions" related list of these rows. Nothing else references this object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Notably there is no duplicate guard - the same question could be
mapped to the same niche twice; the bulk flow is trusted not to do that.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No record-triggered flows, triggers, or scheduled jobs run ON it. It is
written and read only by two screen flows:
- Bulk_Add_Questions_Flow (active): creates the mappings in bulk while
  creating questions for a chosen niche.
- Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview (active): reads the mappings (Id,
  Niche__c, Question__c) to assemble the niche's question pool during an
  internal interview.
No Apex references Niche_Question__c.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 2, plus the auto-number Name)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE TWO PARENT LINKS --------------------------------------------

Name (Niche  Question  ID) [Auto-Number NQ-{00000}]
    System-generated id of the mapping row (e.g. NQ-00042). No business
    meaning - just a handle for related lists.

Niche__c (Niche) [Master-Detail -> Niche__c]
    Which niche's question pool this row belongs to. Required; set by the
    Bulk_Add_Questions_Flow at creation and never changed (the master-
    detail is not reparentable). Deleting the niche deletes the row.

Question__c (Question) [Master-Detail -> Question_Bank__c]
    Which question from the question bank is being mapped. Required; set by
    the bulk flow at creation; not reparentable. This is the PRIMARY master
    - the junction inherits sharing and ownership from the question record.
    Deleting the question deletes the row.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 1,160, created 2026-05-27 to 2026-07-27 (the same window
  the niche catalog and question bank were seeded).
- Per-niche pool sizes: AI ML Engineer 215; the other nine niches exactly
  105 each - the uniform 105 confirms a scripted seed batch per niche.
- Coverage: 620 Question_Bank__c questions are mapped through these 1,160
  rows - on average each question serves ~1.9 niches.
- Both parent links are 100% populated by definition (master-detail).
