################################################################################
PART 3: CANDIDATE MARKETING (BENCH) PIPELINE
################################################################################
################################################################################

================================================================================
OBJECT: Marketing__c  (Label: "Marketing")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Marketing__c is the CANDIDATE-MARKETING ("bench marketing") ENGAGEMENT record:
one record = one run of Techsara actively marketing one candidate into the open
job market. It is the operational headquarters of pipeline #2 (candidate
marketing): it says whether marketing for this candidate is being set up, is
actively applying to jobs, has produced an offer, or has been paused/stopped,
and who (which recruiter) is running it.

Everything in the marketing pipeline hangs off this record:
  - Daily Application__c records (how many job applications were made each
    day) are auto-created for every engagement whose status is "Applications"
    or "Offer Letter".
  - Interviews that come back from those applications are (optionally) linked
    to it via Interview__c.Marketing__c.
  - The candidate's own lifecycle status on the Account (Active / Hold /
    Closed) is driven from this record's Status changes by flows.
A candidate can have more than one Marketing record over time (e.g. a Full
time engagement and a later C2C one, or a stopped engagement followed by a new
one) - in preprod there are 898 records across 701 distinct candidates.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, the anchor of the candidate-marketing domain.
- Standalone object with its own Owner; sharing is Public Read/Write (internal
  and external) - the role-hierarchy redesign will tighten this.
- Candidate__c (lookup -> Account) is REQUIRED: every engagement belongs to a
  candidate Person Account, but it is a lookup, not master-detail.
- 18 custom fields, 2 record types, 2 validation rules, 7 list views.
- Name is a free-text "Marketing Name" (usually the candidate's name plus the
  engagement type, set by the creation flow), with field history tracking on.
- Scale: 898 records in preprod (created Aug 2024 through Jul 2026 - the
  object is in active daily use).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES (2)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- "Active" (developer name: Active) - the default and majority type (612
  records, 68%). Represents a live engagement. Its Status picklist offers the
  working values: New Candidate (default), Initial Call, Applications, Offer
  Letter, Closed.
- "InActive Marketing" (InActive_Marketing) - the parked flavor (286 records,
  32%). Its Status picklist offers only the terminal values: Closed, Paused,
  Stopped. The "Pause or Stop Marketing" button flips a record to this type.
- Data reality: the flip is not retroactive - 157 Paused and 190 Closed
  records still sit on the Active record type (they were paused/closed by
  direct edits before or outside the button flow). All 149 Stopped records
  are on InActive Marketing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATION. Two entry points:
  - The "Create Marketing" quick action on the Account page runs the screen
    flow Create_Marketing_from_Candidate: the user picks the Marketing Owner
    and the Marketing Type (Full Time / C2C). The flow blocks duplicates (if
    the candidate already has an Active-record-type engagement of that type
    it shows "Duplicate Marketing Record Found"), then creates the record
    with Status "New Candidate" on the Active record type and updates the
    candidate's status. (Per metadata this button currently sits on the B2B
    Client and Vendor Account record pages, not the Candidate page - an odd
    placement worth verifying.)
  - The Onboarding_Complete_Onboarding screen flow (the "complete onboarding"
    step on Onboarding__c) creates the Marketing record when a candidate
    finishes onboarding - marketing is the natural next stage after
    onboarding/training. (An older record-triggered version,
    Create_Marketing_record_from_Onboarding_status_update, is Obsolete.)

STEP 2 - SETUP ("New Candidate" / "Initial Call"). The recruiter team
  prepares the candidate for the market and ticks the checklist checkboxes as
  they go: initial call completed, introduction script created, job boards
  (accounts/profiles) created, resume understanding session held. A Recruiter
  (Employee) must be assigned before applications can start (validation
  rule). Assigning the recruiter emails them (Send_Email_notification_to_
  Recruiter flow) and stamps them onto the candidate Account as the Assigned
  Recruiter (Marketing_Update_Assigned_Recruiter_on_Candidate flow).

STEP 3 - "Applications". When Status moves to Applications, a flow stamps
  today's date on the candidate Account as Application_Start_Date__c - the
  clock that the pacing alerts (AccountSchedulerJob) and the interview
  data-quality checks measure against. From now on the nightly
  Create_Daily_Applications flow creates one blank Application__c row per
  weekday for this engagement; the recruiter fills in how many long/short
  applications were made. Interviews that result are created via
  Interview_Creation_V2 and can link back through Interview__c.Marketing__c
  and Interview__c.Application__c.

STEP 4 - "Offer Letter" and closure. When a company makes an offer, Status
  moves to Offer Letter and the offer/joining dates are captured (Offer
  Letter Date, Tentative and Actual Joining Date). Daily Application rows
  keep being created in this status (activity continues until joining).
  "Closed" ends the engagement (typically after placement) and sets the
  candidate's Account status to Closed.

STEP 5 - PAUSE / STOP (the exception path). The "Pause or Stop Marketing"
  button on the Marketing record page runs the Pause_or_Stop_Marketing
  screen flow. The user chooses Pause or Stop and types the reason. The flow:
  sets Status to Paused/Stopped, writes the reason into Reason for pause /
  Reason for Stop, flips the record type to InActive Marketing, sets the
  candidate Account's status (Paused -> Hold, Stopped -> Closed), emails the
  candidate a formal "Techsara Services Pause Notice" / "Techsara Services
  Stop Notice" from legal@techsarasolutions.com, and posts a Slack alert to
  the marketing-alert channel tagging the recruiter and senior recruiter.
  Resuming (Status back to Applications from Paused) re-activates the
  candidate's Account status automatically. Pausing requires a reason
  (validation rule). Paused is the single most common status in data (32%) -
  parking engagements is a normal part of the business.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM MARKETING TO OTHER OBJECTS:
- Account (Candidate__c, REQUIRED, 100% populated): the candidate being
  marketed. Flows on Marketing write back to this Account: its
  Candidate_Status__c, Assigned_Recruiter__c, Application_Start_Date__c and
  Reason_for_Hold__c are all driven from Marketing status/recruiter changes.
- Recruiter__c (Recruiter__c, label "Employee", 90% populated): the Techsara
  recruiter running the engagement. The recruiter chain formulas (Senior /
  TL / Effective recruiter name) climb this record's Assigned_Sr_Recruiter__c
  hierarchy.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT MARKETING:
- Application__c (Marketing__c lookup): the daily application-count log rows
  - the main child (9,545 of 10,000 Application rows link to a Marketing
  record; 214 distinct engagements have rows).
- Interview__c (Marketing__c lookup): marketing-sourced interviews CAN link
  back to the engagement, but in practice almost never do (2 records) - the
  interview's own Candidate link is what the team relies on.
- Case (Marketing__c lookup): internal ops tickets raised about the
  engagement (20 records).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules, all active)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Recruiter_required_before_applications: when Status is changed to
  "Applications" the Recruiter field must be filled. Error (shown on the
  Recruiter field): "Assign a Recruiter before starting the applications".
- Update_Reason_for_Hold: a record cannot sit in Status "Paused" with an
  empty Reason for pause. Error: "Please fill in the details. Reason for
  pausing".

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOWS (active, all after-save on update):
- Candidate_Status_Update_when_marketing_status_Updated (on Status change):
  syncs the candidate Account's lifecycle status - Paused -> Account status
  "Hold" (and copies the pause reason into Account.Reason_for_Hold__c);
  Closed -> "Closed"; Applications coming FROM Paused -> back to "Active".
- Marketing_Update_Application_Start_Date_on_Candidate (Status changes to
  "Applications"): stamps today's date on Account.Application_Start_Date__c.
  Downstream, AccountSchedulerJob measures "days with no interview" from
  this date and the Interview formula Interview_After_Application_Start_
  Date__c checks interviews against it.
- Marketing_Update_Assigned_Recruiter_on_Candidate (Recruiter changes):
  copies the Recruiter onto Account.Assigned_Recruiter__c and adjusts the
  assigned-candidate tallies on the old and new Recruiter (Employee) records.
- Send_Email_notification_to_Recruiter (create + update, when Recruiter is
  set): emails the recruiter that this marketing profile is now theirs.
- Marketing_Paused_Email_Alert: OBSOLETE - its pause/stop emails and Slack
  alert now live inside the Pause_or_Stop_Marketing screen flow.

SCHEDULED FLOW (reads Marketing, writes Application):
- Create_Daily_Applications (daily, since Aug 2024, skips Saturday/Sunday):
  finds every Marketing record with Status "Applications" or "Offer Letter"
  and creates one blank Application__c row per engagement dated today
  (candidate, marketing, recruiter and owner copied from the engagement).

SCREEN FLOWS / BUTTONS:
- "Create Marketing" (Account quick action) -> Create_Marketing_from_
  Candidate: guided creation with duplicate check (see Step 1).
- "Pause or Stop Marketing" (Marketing quick action, on the Marketing record
  page) -> Pause_or_Stop_Marketing: the pause/stop path incl. record-type
  flip, candidate-status sync, legal-notice email and Slack alert (Step 5).
- Onboarding_Complete_Onboarding (on Onboarding__c) creates the Marketing
  record when onboarding completes.

APEX:
- ApplicationRecordCreator.createApplications(Date): utility that does the
  same as the scheduled flow for a chosen date (used to backfill missed
  days). No trigger exists on Marketing__c itself.
- AccountSchedulerJob (scheduled): the "Marketing Profile Alert: No
  Interview Scheduled" watchdog - for Active candidates it compares the last
  interview date (or the Application Start Date set from Marketing) with
  today and Slacks/emails the recruiter chain when too many days pass.

LIST VIEWS worth knowing (they mirror the process): "Application Not
Started" (Status = New Candidate), "My Candidates - Marketing Not Started",
"Ongoing Applications", "Marketing Paused", "Marketing Completed - Placed",
"Candidate Reassignment".

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 18, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE ENGAGEMENT CORE ---------------------------------------------

Candidate__c (Candidate) [Lookup -> Account, required]
    The candidate (Person Account) being marketed. Required and 100%
    populated. Set by the creation flow from the Account the user launched
    it on. Status/recruiter changes on this record write back to this
    Account (lifecycle status, assigned recruiter, application start date).

Recruiter__c (Recruiter) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c ("Employee")]
    The Techsara recruiter running this engagement - assigned manually
    (typically from the Candidate Reassignment / setup step). Changing it
    emails the new recruiter and re-stamps Account.Assigned_Recruiter__c via
    flow. A validation rule blocks moving to "Applications" without it.
    90% populated. The daily Application rows copy this recruiter.

Status__c (Status) [Picklist]
    THE pipeline field. Values in process order:
      New Candidate - just created, setup not started (default on the
        Active record type).
      Initial Call  - the kickoff call stage (exists in the picklist and
        matches the Interview "Initial Call" record type, but 0 records
        currently hold it - teams appear to jump straight to Applications).
      Applications  - actively applying to jobs; daily Application__c rows
        are auto-created; requires a Recruiter (VR); stamps the Account's
        Application Start Date (flow).
      Offer Letter  - an offer is in hand; daily rows still auto-create.
      Closed        - engagement finished (normally after placement); sets
        the candidate's Account status to Closed (flow).
      Paused        - temporarily on hold; requires Reason for pause (VR);
        sets Account status to Hold (flow).
      Stopped       - permanently ended before success; set by the Pause or
        Stop button, which also emails the candidate a formal stop notice.
    Data: Paused 290 (32%) | Applications 233 (26%) | Closed 192 (21%) |
    Stopped 149 (17%) | New Candidate 18 | Offer Letter 14 | blank 2.

Marketing_Type__c (Marketing Type) [Picklist]
    The engagement's employment model: "Full time" (marketing the candidate
    into full-time roles) or "C2C" (corp-to-corp contract marketing). Chosen
    at creation in the Create Marketing flow; also the duplicate key (one
    active engagement per candidate per type). Data: Full time 407 (45%) |
    C2C 47 (5%) | blank 444 (49% - mostly older records that predate the
    picklist being enforced).

--- GROUP B: SETUP CHECKLIST (MARKETING PREP) --------------------------------
Manual checkboxes the recruiter ticks during the New Candidate / Initial
Call setup phase. No automation fires from them - they are progress
tracking for managers and list views.

Initial_call_completed__c (Initial call completed) [Checkbox]
    The kickoff/initial call with the candidate has happened. True on 212
    records (24%).

Introduction_script_created__c (Introduction script created) [Checkbox]
    The candidate's introduction/elevator-pitch script has been written.
    Rarely used in practice - true on only 9 records (1%).

Job_boards_created__c (Job boards created) [Checkbox]
    Job-board accounts/profiles (LinkedIn, Dice, etc.) have been set up for
    the candidate. True on 207 records (23%).

Resume_Understanding_Session__c (Resume Understanding Session) [Checkbox]
    The session where the candidate walks the team through their resume has
    been held. Rarely used - true on 13 records (1%).

Assign_to_Lead__c (Assign to Lead) [Checkbox]
    Flag shown on the record page and on the "Application Not Started" list
    view - reads as "this engagement should be assigned to / reviewed by a
    team lead". No flow or Apex reads it; true on 218 records (24%).
    (Exact business meaning not fully documented - verify with team.)

--- GROUP C: OFFER & JOINING OUTCOME ------------------------------------------

Offer_Letter_Date__c (Offer Letter Date) [Date]
    When the candidate received the offer letter from the hiring company.
    Entered manually at the Offer Letter stage. 69 records (8%) have one -
    roughly the engagements that reached an offer.

Tentative_Joining_Date__c (Tentative Joining Date) [Date]
    The expected start date agreed with the hiring company (tracked between
    offer and joining; joining can slip, hence tentative vs actual).
    Populated on 48 records (5%).

Actual_Joining_Date__c (Actual Joining Date) [Date]
    The date the candidate actually started the job - the "placement done"
    milestone that typically precedes closing the engagement. Populated on
    84 records (9%).

--- GROUP D: PAUSE / STOP AUDIT ----------------------------------------------

Reason_for_paused__c (Reason for pause) [LongTextArea]
    Free-text explanation of why marketing was paused - required whenever
    Status = Paused (validation rule). Written by the Pause or Stop button
    flow (or typed directly). Also copied onto the candidate Account as
    Reason_for_Hold__c by the status-sync flow, and quoted in the pause
    notice email/Slack alert.

Reason_for_Stop__c (Reason for Stop) [LongTextArea]
    Free-text explanation of why marketing was permanently stopped. Written
    by the Pause or Stop button flow; quoted in the formal stop-notice email
    sent to the candidate from legal@techsarasolutions.com.

--- GROUP E: RECRUITER CHAIN (FORMULAS OVER THE EMPLOYEE HIERARCHY) ----------
Three formulas that climb the Recruiter (Employee) record's
Assigned_Sr_Recruiter__c chain so reports can group engagements by senior
recruiter / team lead without extra lookups. They are live formulas - they
always show the CURRENT chain, not a snapshot.

Effective_Recruiter_Name__c (Effective Recruiter Name) [Formula, Text]
    The name to hold accountable today: the recruiter's own name while their
    Employment Status is "Active", otherwise their Assigned Sr. Recruiter's
    name - i.e. when a recruiter leaves, their engagements roll up to the
    senior automatically in reports.

Senior_Recruiter_Name__c (Senior Recruiter Name) [Formula, Text]
    The recruiter's Assigned Sr. Recruiter's name; falls back to the
    recruiter's own name when they have no senior above them.

TL_Recruiter_Name__c (TL Recruiter Name) [Formula, Text]
    Two levels up the chain (the Sr. Recruiter's Sr. Recruiter) - in
    practice the Team Lead's name. Blank when the chain is shorter.

--- GROUP F: ACTIVITY METRICS ------------------------------------------------

No_of_Interviews_rescheduled_by_candidat__c (No of Interviews rescheduled by
candidat) [Number]
    Counter of interviews the CANDIDATE caused to be rescheduled - help text
    scopes it to "Number of Interviews Rescheduled after 10/04/2025"
    (candidate-caused reschedules are a known problem the team decided to
    track from that date). No automation populates it yet and it is 0/empty
    on every record in preprod - (not fully rolled out - verify with team).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 898, spanning 701 distinct candidates (some candidates have
  had 2+ engagements). Created Aug 2024 -> Jul 2026 (in active use).
- Status: Paused 290 (32%) | Applications 233 (26%) | Closed 192 (21%) |
  Stopped 149 (17%) | New Candidate 18 | Offer Letter 14 | blank 2.
  "Initial Call" is defined but unused (0 records).
- Record types: Active 612 (68%) | InActive Marketing 286 (32%). The
  record-type flip lags the status: 157 Paused + 190 Closed records still
  sit on the Active record type; all Stopped records are on InActive.
- Marketing Type: Full time 407 | C2C 47 | blank 444 (49% - legacy records).
- Recruiter assigned on 810 (90%).
- Outcome dates: Actual Joining Date on 84 (9%), Offer Letter Date on 69
  (8%), Tentative Joining Date on 48 (5%) - i.e. under ~10% of engagements
  reach a recorded offer/placement.
- Checklist: Initial call completed 212 | Assign to Lead 218 | Job boards
  created 207 | Resume Understanding Session 13 | Introduction script
  created 9 (the last two are effectively unused).
- No_of_Interviews_rescheduled_by_candidat__c: 0 populated (unused so far).
- Children: 9,545 Application rows, 20 Cases, but only 2 Interviews link
  back via Interview__c.Marketing__c - the Marketing link on Interview is
  effectively unused; interviews connect through the candidate instead.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Application__c  (Label: "Application")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Application__c is the DAILY JOB-APPLICATION ACTIVITY LOG of the candidate-
marketing pipeline. One record = one candidate x one calendar day of applying
to jobs under a marketing engagement. It does NOT represent a single job
application to a single company - it is a tally sheet: "on this date, for
this candidate, the recruiter made N long applications and M short
applications".

The rows themselves are mass-produced by automation: every weekday a
scheduled flow creates one blank record for every Marketing engagement in
Status "Applications" or "Offer Letter", and the recruiting team is expected
to fill in the day's counts afterwards. Managers use the per-team list views
and reports to check daily application volume against targets, and a text
field captures the excuse when a day's target was missed. When an interview
comes back from those applications, the Interview record can link to the
matching Application row (Interview__c.Application__c).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object in the candidate-marketing domain; child-style log table.
- Standalone object with its own Owner (copied from the Marketing record's
  owner at creation); sharing is Public Read/Write.
- All three relationships are plain lookups (no master-detail): Candidate
  (Account), Marketing engagement, Recruiter (Employee).
- 10 custom fields, no record types, no validation rules, 3 list views
  ("All", "Ashley's Team", "Shubham's Team" - the team views filter on the
  record owner's first name).
- Auto-number Name in the format A-XXXXX.
- Scale: 10,000 records in preprod covering application dates 2024-07-01 to
  2025-05-06. The count is exactly 10,000 and the data stops in May 2025,
  which looks like a sandbox data-copy cap rather than the real production
  volume (verify with team before quoting totals).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every Application record is the same flavor - a daily tally row.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - AUTO-CREATION EVERY WEEKDAY. The scheduled flow
  Create_Daily_Applications runs daily (it exits on Saturdays and Sundays),
  reads every Marketing__c record in Status "Applications" or "Offer
  Letter", and inserts one blank Application row per engagement with:
  today's date, the engagement's candidate, the Marketing record itself, its
  recruiter, and its owner. The Apex utility
  ApplicationRecordCreator.createApplications(Date) does exactly the same
  for an arbitrary date (used to backfill a missed day by an admin).

STEP 2 - THE RECRUITER FILLS IN THE COUNTS. During/after the day the
  recruiter records how many "long" and how many "short" applications were
  submitted for the candidate (long = full-form applications, short = quick/
  easy-apply style submissions; the exact internal definitions are not
  documented in metadata - verify with team). Total Applications is a
  formula summing the two. If the daily target was not met, the reason goes
  into "Reason why target not completed".

STEP 3 - MANAGEMENT REVIEW. Team list views (filtered by record owner) and
  reports read the counts to track daily activity per recruiter/candidate
  against targets. The weekday formula field lets reports group by day of
  week without date math.

STEP 4 - LINKING RESULTING INTERVIEWS. When an interview is created for a
  marketing candidate, the before-save flow Interview_Record_Initial_Call_
  Flow finds the matching Application row for that candidate + recruiter and
  writes it into Interview__c.Application__c ("this interview came from the
  applications made for the candidate that day"). In practice this link is
  barely populated (8 interviews) - reporting relies on the candidate link
  instead.

DATA REALITY: because rows are auto-created whether or not anyone applies
that day, 92% of rows have NO counts filled in at all - the filled-in rows
(just over 800) carry all the real activity (~26.4k long applications and
~1.1k short applications logged in total, averaging ~32 long applications
on a filled day, peaking at 160).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM APPLICATION TO OTHER OBJECTS:
- Account (Candidate__c, 99% populated): the candidate the day's
  applications were made for. Copied from the Marketing engagement by the
  creation flow.
- Marketing__c (Marketing__c, 95% populated): the marketing engagement this
  daily row belongs to - the row exists BECAUSE this engagement was in an
  applying status that day. 214 distinct engagements have rows.
- Recruiter__c (Recruiter__c, label "Employee", 84% populated): the
  recruiter who made the applications, copied from the engagement at
  creation time (so it reflects who held the engagement that day, even if
  the engagement's recruiter changes later).

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT APPLICATION:
- Interview__c (Application__c lookup): the interview that resulted from
  this day's applications - auto-linked by Interview_Record_Initial_Call_
  Flow at interview creation, but only 8 interviews carry the link so far.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The object has no validation rules - blank auto-created rows are by
design, so nothing forces the counts or reason fields to be filled.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Create_Daily_Applications (SCHEDULED FLOW, daily since 2024-08-18, active):
  the factory that creates the blank daily rows for every Marketing
  engagement in Status "Applications" or "Offer Letter"; skips weekends
  (Saturday/Sunday check on the current date). In the preprod copy the last
  created row is dated 2025-05-06 - the job has not produced rows in this
  sandbox since (likely paused/staled by the sandbox copy - verify).
- ApplicationRecordCreator (APEX, no trigger): admin-run utility with the
  identical creation logic for a specific date (backfill tool). Its test
  class is ApplicationRecordCreatorTest.
- Interview_Record_Initial_Call_Flow (flow on Interview__c): LOOKS UP the
  matching Application row (by candidate + recruiter) when an interview is
  created and stamps it on the interview - Application is read, not written.
- No record-triggered flows, no triggers, no quick actions exist on
  Application__c itself, and nothing updates the rows automatically after
  creation - the counts are pure manual entry.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 10, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHO AND WHICH ENGAGEMENT ----------------------------------------

Candidate__c (Candidate) [Lookup -> Account]
    The candidate the applications were made for. Auto-copied from the
    Marketing engagement by the daily creation flow / Apex. 99% populated
    (a handful of legacy rows lack it).

Marketing__c (Marketing) [Lookup -> Marketing__c]
    The marketing engagement this daily row belongs to - the row's reason
    for existing. Auto-set at creation. 95% populated (older/manual rows
    predate the link).

Recruiter__c (Recruiter) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c ("Employee")]
    The recruiter responsible for the day's applications, snapshotted from
    the engagement's Recruiter at creation time. 84% populated - rows
    created while the engagement had no recruiter stay blank.

Recruiter_s_Lead__c (Recruiter's Lead) [Formula, Text]
    The full name of the USER who owns the linked Recruiter (Employee)
    record - in this org the employee-record owner acts as the recruiter's
    team lead, so reports can group daily activity by lead. Live formula
    (always current). The "Ashley's Team" / "Shubham's Team" list views
    serve the same purpose via the row's owner.

--- GROUP B: THE DAY ----------------------------------------------------------

Date_of_Application__c (Date of Application) [Date]
    The calendar day this tally row covers. Set to the run date by the
    daily creation flow (or the date passed to the Apex backfill). One row
    per engagement per day is the intended grain.

Day_of_Application__c (Day of Application) [Formula, Text]
    The weekday name ("Monday"..."Sunday") computed from the date - lets
    reports/views group by day of week (e.g. spotting low-activity days)
    without date functions. Weekend values only appear on backfilled rows,
    since the daily flow skips Saturday/Sunday.

--- GROUP C: THE COUNTS (THE ACTUAL ACTIVITY) --------------------------------

Long_Applications__c (Long Applications) [Number]
    How many LONG-FORM job applications were submitted that day - the
    full-effort kind (complete application forms/portals). Manual entry by
    the recruiter at end of day. Filled on only 831 rows (8%), which carry
    26,371 applications in total - average ~32 per filled day, max 160.
    This is the primary volume metric.

Short_Applications__c (Short Applications) [Number]
    How many SHORT/QUICK applications were submitted that day (one-click /
    easy-apply style). Manual entry. Filled on only 100 rows (1%), 1,112
    total, average ~11, max 72 - a minor channel compared to long
    applications. (Exact long-vs-short definition not documented in
    metadata - verify with team.)

Total_Applications__c (Total Applications) [Formula, Number]
    Long + Short - the day's total, used by target-tracking reports. Only
    683 rows compute to a value above zero (blank counts make the formula
    blank/zero).

--- GROUP D: TARGET TRACKING --------------------------------------------------

Reason_why_target_not_completed__c (Reason why target not completed) [Text]
    Free-text excuse/explanation captured when the recruiter missed the
    day's application target for this candidate (e.g. candidate unavailable,
    job boards down, holiday). Manual entry; read by managers in the team
    list views. Filled on just 23 rows - rarely used in practice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: exactly 10,000 - almost certainly a sandbox data-copy cap,
  not the true production count (verify with team). Rows were created
  2024-08-22 through 2025-05-06 and cover application dates 2024-07-01 to
  2025-05-06 (earlier dates were backfilled); no rows have been created in
  this sandbox since May 2025 even though the daily flow is Active.
- Distinct candidates: 206; distinct Marketing engagements: 214 - i.e. the
  ~200-250 engagements that were in "Applications"/"Offer Letter" status
  during that window each accumulated one row per weekday.
- Population: Candidate on 99%, Marketing on 95%, Recruiter on 84%.
- THE BIG CAVEAT: 9,168 rows (92%) have NEITHER a long nor a short count -
  auto-created placeholders that were never filled in. Only 683 rows (7%)
  show a nonzero Total Applications.
- Logged activity on the filled rows: 26,371 long applications (831 rows,
  avg ~32/day, max 160/day) and 1,112 short applications (100 rows, avg
  ~11/day, max 72/day) - long applications are the dominant channel.
- Reason why target not completed: filled on 23 rows only.
- Downstream links: 8 Interview records point back via
  Interview__c.Application__c - the interview-to-application link exists
  but is effectively unused in practice.
- Key takeaway for answering questions: treat Application__c as a
  target-tracking tally sheet, not a registry of individual applications;
  ignore the empty placeholder rows when computing activity metrics.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Resume__c  (Label: "Resume Creation")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resume__c tracks ONE resume version created for a candidate (or a not-yet-
converted Lead). Techsara's marketing team builds and maintains tailored
resumes for the candidates it markets; this object is the register of those
resume documents: who they belong to, which skill niche they target, who
uploaded and approved them, and where they stand in the review pipeline
(Draft -> Under Review -> Approved / Rejected / Uploaded). The actual resume
file itself is stored as a Salesforce File (ContentVersion) or an external
link on related records - this object is the process/metadata record around
the resume, not the file body.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the candidate-marketing domain.
- Standalone object with lookups (no master-detail parent); org-wide sharing
  is ReadWrite.
- 9 custom fields, no record types, no validation rules, 1 list view.
- Scale: only 17 records in preprod - a lightly-used register (most resume
  handling happens as plain file uploads / links on Lead, Account and
  Job_Submission__c; see Resume_Link__c fields on those objects).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. All resume records share one layout and process.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A recruiter/marketing employee creates a Resume record when a tailored resume
is being prepared for a candidate - typically targeting a specific skill
niche (linked Niche__c). The record moves through Resume_Status__c: it starts
as Draft while being written, goes Under Review for a senior's check, and is
then Approved (Approved_By + Approval_Date get stamped) or Rejected. The
"Uploaded" status marks that the finished resume has been uploaded/attached
(in practice 15 of the 17 records sit at Uploaded - the register is mostly
used to log finished resumes rather than to run the full review pipeline).

The internal-interview subsystem also touches it: the
Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview flow looks up the candidate's resume
during an internal screening, and the Interview_Create_Reschedule_Flow (the
"Create Interview" button on Account/Lead pages that creates INTERNAL
interviews) looks up - and can delete/replace - the resume tied to the
screening being (re)scheduled.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Account (Candidate__c, Lookup): the candidate (Person Account) this resume
  belongs to - used once the person exists as a candidate.
- Lead (Lead__c, Lookup): the pre-conversion prospect this resume belongs to
  - resumes are often prepared while the person is still a Lead; after
  conversion the Candidate lookup is the one that matters.
- Niche__c (Niche__c, Lookup): the skill niche (e.g. a technology/track) the
  resume is tailored for. One candidate can have different resumes per niche.
- Internal_Interview__c (Internal_Interview__c, Lookup): the internal
  screening this resume was prepared for / used in (the internal interview
  evaluates the candidate against the niche the resume targets).
- Recruiter__c "Employee" (Uploaded_By__c, Lookup): the employee who created/
  uploaded this resume version.
- Recruiter__c "Employee" (Approved_By__c, Lookup): the senior employee who
  approved it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Process discipline is by convention, not enforced rules.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- No record-triggered flows or Apex trigger of its own.
- Read (and sometimes deleted/replaced) by two screen flows of the internal-
  interview subsystem: Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview (looks up the
  resume during a screening) and Interview_Create_Reschedule_Flow (looks up /
  deletes the resume tied to an internal screening being rescheduled).
- The Attached_Resume_To_Lead flow works with resume FILES (ContentVersion)
  on Leads, not with this object - do not confuse the two.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 9)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHO THE RESUME BELONGS TO ---------------------------------------

Candidate__c (Candidate) [Lookup -> Account]
    The candidate (Person Account) the resume was written for. Filled once
    the person exists as a candidate; earlier in the funnel the Lead lookup
    below is used instead.

Lead__c (Lead) [Lookup -> Lead]
    The pre-conversion prospect the resume was written for. Resumes are often
    prepared during the sales/enrolment phase, before the Lead converts to a
    Person Account.

Niche__c (Niche) [Lookup -> Niche__c]
    The skill niche/track this resume targets (the same niche master used by
    internal interviews and templates). A candidate marketing into two tracks
    would get two Resume records, one per niche.

Internal_Interview__c (Internal Interview) [Lookup -> Internal_Interview__c]
    The internal screening interview this resume is tied to - the screening
    validates the candidate against the niche the resume claims.

--- GROUP B: REVIEW PIPELINE -------------------------------------------------

Resume_Status__c (Resume Status) [Picklist]
    Where the resume stands: Draft (being written) | Under Review (waiting
    for senior check) | Approved | Rejected | Uploaded (finished and
    attached/delivered). Set manually by the marketing team. Real data: 15 of
    17 records are "Uploaded", 2 are "Draft" - the register is mostly used to
    log completed resumes.

Uploaded_By__c (Uploaded By) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    The employee (Recruiter__c / "Employee" record, not a User) who created
    or uploaded this resume version.

Approved_By__c (Approved By) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    The senior employee who approved the resume for use.

Approval_Date__c (Approval Date) [Date]
    When the approval happened. Filled manually together with Approved_By.

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    Marks the currently-active resume version for the candidate/niche; older
    versions stay for history with this unchecked.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-15)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 17 (a small register - resume handling mostly happens as
  file uploads / links on Lead, Account, Job_Submission).
- Status: Uploaded 15 | Draft 2. The Under Review / Approved / Rejected
  stages are effectively unused so far.
- Key takeaway: treat this object as a light log of prepared resumes; the
  authoritative resume for day-to-day work is usually the Resume_Link__c /
  attached file on the pipeline records themselves.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Candidate_Email__c  (Label: "Candidate Email")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Candidate_Email__c is a staging/archive object for EMAILS received on behalf
of marketed candidates. The idea: when Techsara manages a candidate's job-
search mailbox (applications go out under the candidate's identity),
interesting inbound emails (recruiter responses, interview invitations,
rejections) are captured here as records - subject, body, sender - so they
can be classified (Email_Classification__c) and acted on inside Salesforce.
It was designed to feed an OpenAI-based classification flow.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object; standalone (NO relationships to any other object - not even
  to the candidate; the candidate is identified only by the email address
  text fields). Org-wide sharing ReadWrite.
- 6 custom fields, no record types, no validation rules, 1 list view.
- Scale: 0 records in preprod - the feature is BUILT BUT NOT LIVE.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Currently: not used. The object has zero records, and the one automation
built for it - the OpenAI_Email_Integration record-triggered flow (meant to
fire on create and send the email to OpenAI for classification) - is in
"InvalidDraft" state, i.e. parked/broken, never activated. Treat this whole
object as an in-progress feature: the intended flow was (1) an inbound email
lands as a Candidate_Email__c record (via some capture mechanism that was
never finished), (2) the flow calls OpenAI to classify it (interview invite?
rejection? recruiter question?), (3) the team works the classified queue.
(not fully documented - verify with team whether this feature is still
planned or abandoned.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The object is deliberately flat - candidate identity is carried only
as the email-address text in Candidate_Email_Id__c. If the feature goes
live, answering "which candidate does this email belong to" requires matching
that address against Account/candidate email fields.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- OpenAI_Email_Integration (record-triggered, After Save on Create) -
  status "InvalidDraft" (NOT active): was meant to send the new email record
  to OpenAI (openAIIntegrationService Apex handles the org's OpenAI callouts)
  for classification. Never went live.
- No triggers, no other flows.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 6)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Candidate_Email_Id__c (Candidate Email Id) [Text]
    The candidate-side email address this message belongs to (the mailbox
    Techsara manages for the candidate). This is the only link to a
    candidate - a plain text address, not a lookup.

Sender_Email_Id__c (Sender Email_Id) [Text]
    The external sender's address (the company recruiter / ATS that wrote
    to the candidate).

Subject__c (Subject) [Text]
    The email's subject line.

Body__c (Body) [Html, rich text]
    The full HTML body of the received email.

Email_Classification__c (Email Classification) [Text]
    The classification the OpenAI integration was meant to write (e.g.
    interview invitation / rejection / info request). Text, not a picklist -
    the AI's label would land here. Never populated so far.

Description__c (Description) [LongTextArea]
    Free-text notes about the email (manual annotation space).

- Total records: 0. The object and its OpenAI flow are an unfinished feature
  - documented here so the agent knows the object exists and why it is

================================================================================
OBJECT: Campaign  (Label: "Campaign")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Campaign is the STANDARD Salesforce marketing-campaign object: one record per
marketing initiative (an event, an email blast, a referral program) with
budget/cost tracking and automatic statistics on how many leads, contacts and
opportunities the initiative produced.

IN THIS ORG IT IS NOT USED. The preprod org contains ZERO Campaign records,
no flow touches the object, no Apex class references it, and it has no
validation rules or record types. It exists in the org for two reasons only:
  a) It is a standard object every Salesforce org ships with (its layout and
     list views are the stock ones).
  b) The installed "Salesforce integration" package from Zoom (namespace ZVC)
     added two lookup fields so Zoom webinars/events can auto-generate
     campaigns and sync their registrants - a capability that is installed
     but has never been exercised here.
Techsara's actual "marketing" concept is candidate marketing (Marketing__c /
Application__c), which has nothing to do with this object. If a question is
about "marketing" in this org, it almost certainly means Marketing__c, NOT
Campaign.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Standard object with 39 fields, of which only 2 are custom - both from the
  Zoom (ZVC) managed package. Techsara itself added no fields.
- Sharing: "Public Full Access" internally (any user who can see campaigns can
  edit them - the Salesforce default for campaigns); Private for external
  (portal) users. Has an Owner.
- Supports a parent/child campaign hierarchy via ParentId (self-lookup).
- 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 3 list views (All Active Campaigns,
  My Active Campaigns, Org_Campaign_Hierarchy - all stock).
- Scale: 0 records in preprod. Empty object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every campaign (if any were ever created) would be a plain Campaign
record; the org never needed to split campaign flavors.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
It is not used. There is no business process on Campaign in this org today.

For completeness, what the plumbing WOULD do if the team started using it:
  - A user (or the Zoom package) creates a Campaign for an initiative, sets
    Type/Status/dates and budget numbers.
  - Leads and Contacts are attached as CampaignMember rows; Salesforce then
    auto-counts members, responses, converted leads and influenced
    opportunities into the read-only statistics fields.
  - The Zoom package can create a Campaign per Zoom webinar/event and push
    each registrant in as a CampaignMember with join/leave times.
  - The classic layout carries two stock custom links: "View All Campaign
    Members" and "View Campaign Influence Report".
None of this has ever produced a record in preprod (count = 0).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Campaign (ParentId, self-lookup): standard campaign hierarchy - a child
  campaign rolls its statistics up into the Hierarchy* fields of its parent.
- CampaignMember (child): the join object listing which Leads/Contacts are in
  the campaign (0 records).
- Opportunity (Opportunity.CampaignId): opportunities can name a campaign as
  their "Primary Campaign Source"; never populated in this org (0 of 658
  opportunities).
- ZVC__Zoom_Event__c / ZVC__Zoom_Webinar__c (lookups from Campaign): the Zoom
  package's event/webinar records this campaign would represent. Both unused.
- CampaignInfluence / CampaignInfluenceModel: standard campaign-influence
  machinery exists in the metadata snapshot but, with no campaigns, holds
  nothing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. No validation rules exist on Campaign - nothing constrains saves.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None in the org's own code or flows: no record-triggered flows, no triggers,
no scheduled jobs, no quick-action flows reference Campaign.
- The only Campaign-specific button is the stock "Child Campaign" create
  action on the classic Campaign Layout (creates a child campaign) plus the
  generic LogACall / SendEmail / NewTask / NewEvent actions.
- Potential external writer: the installed Zoom (ZVC) package can create/
  update campaigns from Zoom webinars and events - installed, never used.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 39, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All fields are the stock Salesforce campaign fields (plus 2 Zoom package
lookups). With zero records, every population figure is 0% - the descriptions
below say what each field is FOR, not how it is used here.

--- GROUP A: IDENTITY & SCHEDULE ----------------------------------------------

Name (Campaign Name) [Text]
    The campaign's title (e.g. "Q3 Referral Drive"). Required. Manual entry.

IsActive (Active) [Checkbox]
    Whether the campaign is currently running. Drives the stock "All/My
    Active Campaigns" list views and which campaigns pickers offer.

Status (Status) [Picklist]
    Lifecycle of the initiative: Planned (default) | In Progress | Completed |
    Aborted. Manual entry.

StartDate (Start Date) [Date]
EndDate (End Date) [Date]
    When the initiative starts and ends. Manual entry.

Description (Description) [LongTextArea]
    Free-text summary of what the campaign is.

OwnerId (Owner) [Lookup -> User]
    The internal user responsible for the campaign. Defaults to the creator.

--- GROUP B: CLASSIFICATION & HIERARCHY ---------------------------------------

Type (Type) [Picklist]
    What kind of initiative: Event (default) | Demo Signup / Trial | Email |
    Referral Program | Search | Social Media | Thought Leadership | Website
    Direct | Other. This value list is the modern Salesforce starter set -
    nobody in this org customized or used it.

ParentId (Parent Campaign) [Lookup -> Campaign]
    Optional parent for building a campaign hierarchy (e.g. one umbrella
    program with per-channel child campaigns). Statistics roll up the tree
    into the Hierarchy* fields (Group E).

CampaignMemberRecordTypeId (Campaign Member Record Type) [Lookup -> RecordType]
    Standard field choosing which CampaignMember record type this campaign's
    members get. Irrelevant here - CampaignMember has no record types.

--- GROUP C: PLANNING TARGETS & COSTS -----------------------------------------

BudgetedCost (Budgeted Cost in Campaign) [Currency]
    What the team planned to spend on the campaign. Manual entry.

ActualCost (Actual Cost in Campaign) [Currency]
    What was actually spent. Manual entry.

ExpectedRevenue (Expected Revenue in Campaign) [Currency]
    Revenue the campaign is expected to generate. Manual entry.

ExpectedResponse (Expected Response (%)) [Percent]
    The response rate the team expected when planning. Manual entry.

NumberSent (Num Sent in Campaign) [Number]
    How many people the campaign was sent/shown to (e.g. emails sent) -
    the denominator for response-rate math. Manual entry.

--- GROUP D: MEMBER & OPPORTUNITY STATISTICS (SYSTEM ROLL-UPS) ----------------
All eight fields below are READ-ONLY counters Salesforce maintains
automatically from the campaign's members and from opportunities naming this
campaign as their Primary Campaign Source. No user or flow ever writes them.

NumberOfLeads (Leads in Campaign) [Number]
    Count of Lead members.

NumberOfConvertedLeads (Converted Leads in Campaign) [Number]
    How many of those leads have since been converted.

NumberOfContacts (Contacts in Campaign) [Number]
    Count of Contact members.

NumberOfResponses (Responses in Campaign) [Number]
    Members whose status counts as "Responded".

NumberOfOpportunities (Opportunities in Campaign) [Number]
    Opportunities whose Primary Campaign Source is this campaign.

NumberOfWonOpportunities (Won Opportunities in Campaign) [Number]
    The subset of those opportunities that were Closed Won.

AmountAllOpportunities (Value Opportunities in Campaign) [Currency]
    Total Amount of all sourced opportunities.

AmountWonOpportunities (Value Won Opportunities in Campaign) [Currency]
    Total Amount of the won ones.

--- GROUP E: HIERARCHY ROLL-UPS (SYSTEM, 12 FIELDS) ---------------------------
The same statistics again, but summed across this campaign AND every campaign
below it in the ParentId hierarchy. All read-only, system-maintained, and -
with no data - permanently zero. One line each:

HierarchyBudgetedCost / HierarchyActualCost / HierarchyExpectedRevenue
    [Currency] - budget, spend and expected revenue summed over the tree.
HierarchyNumberSent [Number] - total sent across the tree.
HierarchyNumberOfLeads / HierarchyNumberOfConvertedLeads /
HierarchyNumberOfContacts / HierarchyNumberOfResponses [Number]
    - member statistics summed over the tree.
HierarchyNumberOfOpportunities / HierarchyNumberOfWonOpportunities [Number]
    - sourced/won opportunity counts over the tree.
HierarchyAmountAllOpportunities / HierarchyAmountWonOpportunities [Currency]
    - sourced/won opportunity value over the tree.

--- GROUP F: ZOOM PACKAGE FIELDS (ZVC MANAGED PACKAGE) ------------------------

ZVC__Zoom_Event__c (Zoom Event) [Lookup -> ZVC__Zoom_Event__c]
    Set by the Zoom integration package when a campaign is generated from a
    Zoom Event - links the campaign to the package's event record. Never
    populated (the feature is not in use).

ZVC__Zoom_Webinar__c (Zoom Webinar) [Lookup -> ZVC__Zoom_Webinar__c]
    Same idea for Zoom Webinars: the source webinar this campaign represents.
    Never populated. NOTE: Techsara's real Zoom meeting/recording pipeline
    uses its own Session__c / Zoom_Recording_* objects, not this package.

--- GROUP G: PLATFORM STUBS (NOT ACCESSIBLE) ----------------------------------

BusinessUnitId (Business Unit) [Lookup]
Stage (Stage) [-]
    Two newer platform fields that appear in the metadata retrieve but are
    NOT queryable through the API in this org (querying Campaign.Stage
    returns "No such column") - they belong to Salesforce marketing features
    that are not provisioned here. Ignore them; they can hold no data.
    (Exact feature linkage not fully documented - verify with team.)

================================================================================
OBJECT: CampaignMember  (Label: "Campaign Member")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CampaignMember is the STANDARD Salesforce junction object between a Campaign
and the people in it: one row = one Lead OR one Contact participating in one
campaign, with a per-campaign status (Sent / Responded) and a read-only mirror
of the person's details for easy list building.

IN THIS ORG IT IS NOT USED: 0 records, matching the 0 campaigns. Its only
customization is 8 fields from the installed Zoom ("ZVC") managed package,
which - if the feature were used - would record each member's Zoom webinar/
event registration and actual join/leave times. It never has been.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Standard junction object: 33 fields, 8 custom (all from the ZVC package).
- Sharing: "Controlled By Campaign" - visibility of a member row follows the
  parent campaign; the row has no owner of its own.
- A member must reference a Campaign plus EITHER a Lead or a Contact; the
  same person can appear once per campaign.
- 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views.
- Scale: 0 records in preprod. Empty object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. All members would be plain rows; the org never configured member
record types (Campaign.CampaignMemberRecordTypeId is therefore moot).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
It is not used - no rows have ever existed. The intended standard mechanics,
for context:
  - Adding a Lead/Contact to a campaign creates a member row with a status
    from the campaign's configured status list (stock: "Sent", "Responded").
  - When the person responds, the status changes, HasResponded flips true and
    FirstRespondedDate stamps - feeding the campaign's response statistics.
  - The classic member layout carries stock "Convert Lead" and "Create
    Opportunity" buttons to push a responding member down the funnel.
  - The Zoom package would auto-create members for webinar/event registrants
    and stamp their actual attendance times.
Nothing in Techsara's recruiting or training funnels touches this object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Campaign (CampaignId, required): the campaign this membership belongs to.
  Sharing is inherited from it.
- Lead (LeadId): the lead who is the member (for not-yet-converted people).
- Contact (ContactId): the contact who is the member. Note: in this org a
  candidate is a Person Account, so a candidate COULD technically be a member
  through their person-account contact - it has never happened.
- ZVC__Zoom_Event_Registrant__c / ZVC__Zoom_Webinar_Registrant__c (lookups):
  the Zoom package's registrant records this membership mirrors. Unused.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. No validation rules exist on CampaignMember.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None in the org's own automation: no flows, triggers, scheduled jobs or
quick actions reference CampaignMember. The only potential writer is the
installed Zoom (ZVC) package syncing webinar/event registrants - never used.
Standard platform behavior (status statistics rolling up to the Campaign)
would apply automatically if rows existed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 33, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
With zero records, all population figures are 0%. Most fields are the stock
read-only mirrors Salesforce maintains from the underlying Lead/Contact.

--- GROUP A: THE LINKS --------------------------------------------------------

CampaignId (Campaign) [Lookup -> Campaign, required]
    Which campaign this membership belongs to. Set when the member is added;
    controls sharing.

LeadId (Lead) [Lookup -> Lead]
    The Lead who is the member. Filled for unconverted people; after lead
    conversion Salesforce re-points the membership to the new Contact.

ContactId (Contact) [Lookup -> Contact]
    The Contact who is the member. Exactly one of LeadId/ContactId is
    effectively the person link at any time.

--- GROUP B: RESPONSE TRACKING ------------------------------------------------

Status (Status) [Picklist]
    The member's per-campaign status. Org-wide stock values: Sent |
    Responded. Each campaign can define its own status list via the standard
    CampaignMemberStatus setup object (never customized here).

HasResponded (Responded) [Checkbox, read-only]
    TRUE when the current status counts as a response. System-maintained;
    feeds Campaign.NumberOfResponses.

FirstRespondedDate (First Responded Date) [Date, read-only]
    Stamped by the platform the first time the member reaches a responded
    status.

--- GROUP C: MIRRORED PERSON DETAILS (READ-ONLY COPIES) -----------------------
All fields in this group are standard read-only mirrors of the underlying
Lead/Contact record, kept so campaign-member lists and exports don't need
joins. Nobody edits them on the member row; they track the source person.

Salutation (Salutation) [Picklist]    - Mr./Ms./... from the person record.
FirstName (First Name) [Text]         - person's first name.
LastName (Last Name) [Text]           - person's last name.
Title (Title) [Text]                  - person's job title.
CompanyOrAccount (Company (Account)) [Text]
    - the lead's Company or the contact's Account name.
Email (Email) [Email]                 - person's email.
Phone (Phone) [Phone]                 - person's business phone.
MobilePhone (Mobile Phone) [Phone]    - person's mobile.
Fax (Fax) [Phone]                     - person's fax (era-appropriate relic).
Street (Street) [TextArea]            - mailing street.
City (City) [Text]                    - mailing city.
State (State/Province) [Text]         - mailing state.
PostalCode (Zip/Postal Code) [Text]   - mailing postal code.
Country (Country) [Text]              - mailing country.
LeadSource (Lead Source) [Picklist]
    - where the person originally came from (same global LeadSource list the
      org uses on Lead/Opportunity: Advertisement, Customer Event, Customer
      Referral, Employee Referral, External Referral, Google AdWords,
      Instagram, LinkedIn, Other, Partner, Purchased List, Trade Show,
      Webinar, Website, Facebook).
Description (Description) [LongTextArea]
    - the person's description text.
DoNotCall (Do Not Call) [Checkbox]    - person's do-not-call preference.
HasOptedOutOfEmail (Email Opt Out) [Checkbox]
    - person's email opt-out preference.
HasOptedOutOfFax (Fax Opt Out) [Checkbox]
    - person's fax opt-out preference.

--- GROUP D: ZOOM WEBINAR/EVENT ATTENDANCE (ZVC MANAGED PACKAGE) --------------
All 8 fields below belong to the installed Zoom package and would be written

ZVC__Is_Registrant__c (Is_Registrant) [Checkbox]
    Member registered for the Zoom webinar/event.
