--- GROUP O: SYSTEM / HOUSEKEEPING FIELDS ------------------------------------

Final_Notification_Date_Time__c (Final Notification Date/Time) [DateTime]
    When the last scheduled Slack reminder for this interview was set to fire
    (written by the Slack notification flow).

IsInterview__c (IsInterview) [Formula, Number]
    Constant 1 - a counting helper so reports can SUM "number of interviews"
    across joined objects.

Interview_After_Application_Start_Date__c (Interview After Application Start
Date) [Formula, Checkbox]
    Data-quality check: TRUE when the interview date is on/after the
    candidate's Application Start Date (an interview should not predate the
    marketing engagement).

Unique_Interview_Month_Key__c (Unique Interview Month Key) [Formula, Text]
    Candidate + company + year + month composite key - used to detect/dedupe
    multiple interviews of the same candidate at the same company in the same
    month.

Marketing_Unique_Interview_Key__c (Marketing Unique Interview Key) [Formula, Text]
    A stricter dedupe key for marketing metrics: only produced for Initial/
    First-round interviews in countable statuses - i.e. "one first interview
    per candidate per company" for unique-interview counting.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 9,991. Interview dates run 2024-07-03 to 2026-08-31 (future
  dates = scheduled ahead; oldest records were imported/backfilled).
- Record types: Interview 9,732 (97.4%) | Initial Call 248 (2.5%) |
  B2B Interviews 9 (new).
- Status: Completed 6,780 (68%) | Rescheduled 1,437 (14%) | Cancelled 530 |
  Scheduled 314 | No Show 305 | Rejected 284 | Ghosted 180 | Moved to Next
  Round 145 | Offer Received 7 | Loop Round 7.
- Outcome: Ghosted 3,481 (35%) | none yet 3,028 (30%) | Moved to Next Round
  1,707 (17%) | Rejected 1,681 (17%) | Offer Received 80 | NA 14.
  (Note: "Ghosted" is the single most common outcome - a real business pain
  point the auto-ghost sweep exists for.)
- Rounds: First 4,381 | Initial 3,608 | Second 987 | Final 339 | Third 337 |
  then a long tail to Fifteenth.
- AI assignment: Assigned_By = "AI Suggestion" on 7,322 records (73%);
  AI confidence populated on 75%; support person assigned on 62%.
- Integrations in use: Google Calendar id on 68% of records, Zoom meeting id
  on 60%.
- COMPASS scoring fields populated on ~5,355 records (54%).
- Effectively unused fields (as of this snapshot): Interview_Mode__c (0),
  Client_Account__c (0), Interview_Type__c (2), Marketing__c link (2),
  Lead__c (6), Application__c / Job_Submission__c / Job_Requirement__c
  (8 each - the B2B flavor is brand new), Vendor__c (38),
  Offer_Letter_Date__c (66).
- Key takeaway for answering questions: nearly all live data is the
  MARKETING-path "Interview" record type linked to Candidate + Company
  master list; the B2B path (submissions, client accounts) is newly built
  and barely has data yet.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Interview_Participant__c  (Label: "Interview Participant")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Interview_Participant__c is the ATTENDEE ROSTER of an external interview call
(Interview__c): one record per person who is expected on - or actually joins -
the call, with which side of the table they sit on (candidate / internal /
client), what role they play (client interviewer, hiring manager, internal
support, observer...), and a join/leave attendance audit trail.

IMPORTANT REALITY CHECK: the object is deployed but NOT YET IN USE. It has
ZERO records in preprod, no active automation writes to it, and the only flow
that ever read it (Interview_support_person_Assign, a calendar-invitee sync)
is marked Obsolete. Treat it as built-ahead infrastructure for a future
"who was actually on the call" feature (e.g. Zoom attendance capture), not as
a live part of the business process today.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the (external) Interviewing domain.
- MASTER-DETAIL CHILD OF Interview__c via Interview__c: every participant row
  must belong to one interview. Sharing is "Controlled By Parent" - whoever
  can see the interview (and through it the candidate) sees the roster.
- 12 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Name is a plain Text field (label "Interview Participant"), not auto-number.
- Its page layout is minimal (only Interview + Name placed) - the object was
  clearly designed to be filled by automation/API, not by hand.
- Object permissions are granted only by the Jenkins_CICD permission set (and
  read-only to Salesforce internal integration users) - no department
  permission set exposes it, so normal users cannot even see it yet.
- Scale: 0 records in preprod.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every participant row is the same shape; the Side and Participant Type
picklists carry the "flavor" instead.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
INTENDED process (nothing executes it yet):
STEP 1 - when an interview is scheduled, one row per expected attendee would
  be created: the candidate, the client-side interviewer(s)/recruiter/HR, and
  any Techsara-side people (support person, observer, trainer).
STEP 2 - internal attendees link to their Recruiter__c ("Employee") record
  and/or Salesforce User; outside attendees are captured as free text name +
  email + company (they have no user record).
STEP 3 - during/after the call, Attendance Status plus Joined At / Left At
  timestamps would record who actually showed up and for how long - an audit
  usable for no-show disputes, support-person verification, and billing.

HISTORICAL trace: the now-Obsolete record-triggered flow
Interview_support_person_Assign (on Interview__c) looked up participant rows
by Participant Type while syncing the assigned support person into the
interview's Google Calendar event invitees (EventRelation). That was the only
consumer; since it was retired nothing reads or writes this object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Interview__c (via Interview__c, MASTER-DETAIL, required): the external
  interview this person is on the roster of. Child relationship name:
  Interview_Participants (the roster would appear as a related list on the
  interview page).

LOOKUPS FROM PARTICIPANT TO OTHER OBJECTS:
- Recruiter__c / "Employee" (Employee__c): when the participant is a Techsara
  employee, the link to their internal staff record.
- User (User__c): when the participant maps to an actual Salesforce/portal
  User - what the old calendar-invitee sync used to resolve the user's
  Contact for the calendar invite.

No other object points at Interview_Participant__c.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. There are no validation rules on this object (nothing creates records
yet, so no save-time rules were needed).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None active. No trigger, no active flow, no Apex class creates or updates
Interview_Participant__c records. The single historical reference -
Interview_support_person_Assign (record-triggered on Interview__c, which did
a Lookup on this object's Participant Type) - is marked Obsolete. There are
also no quick actions or buttons for it on any page.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 12, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHICH INTERVIEW, WHICH PERSON -----------------------------------

Interview__c (Interview) [Master-Detail -> Interview__c]
    THE required parent link: which external interview this participant row
    belongs to. Drives sharing (controlled by parent). One of only two
    fields placed on the page layout (with Name).

Participant_Name__c (Participant Name) [Text]
    The person's display name as free text. Needed because most attendees
    (client interviewers, client HR) exist nowhere else in Salesforce.
    Would be set by the creating automation or manually. Never populated
    yet (0 records).

Email__c (Email) [Email]
    The participant's email address - e.g. the client interviewer's invite
    address. Intended for calendar invites and for matching meeting-join
    events back to a person.

Company__c (Company) [Text]
    Free-text company the participant belongs to - the client/employer name
    for client-side people, "Techsara" (or blank) for internal ones. Not a
    lookup to the Company__c master list despite the same name.

Employee__c (Employee) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c ("Employee")]
    Filled only for Techsara-side participants: links the row to the
    internal staff record (e.g. the interview support person or an internal
    observer/trainer sitting in).

User__c (User) [Lookup -> User]
    Filled when the participant is an actual Salesforce/portal User. The
    retired calendar sync used this to find the user's Contact so it could
    add them as a Google Calendar event invitee.

--- GROUP B: ROLE ON THE CALL ------------------------------------------------

Side__c (Side) [Picklist]
    Which side of the table the person sits on: Candidate | Internal
    (Techsara staff) | Client (the interviewing company). Lets reports
    split "our people" from "their people" on a call.

Participant_Type__c (Participant Type) [Picklist]
    The person's role: Candidate | Client Interviewer | Client Recruiter |
    Hiring Manager | HR | Internal Observer | Internal Support | Internal
    Trainer. "Internal Support" is the role the retired calendar-sync flow
    filtered on. More granular than Side (each type implies a side).

Is_Primary__c (Is Primary) [Checkbox]
    Marks the PRIMARY interviewer/recruiter when several people of the same
    role are on the call (field description: "Primary Interviewer/
    Recruiter"). Defaults to unchecked.

--- GROUP C: ATTENDANCE AUDIT ------------------------------------------------

Attendance_Status__c (Attendance Status) [Picklist]
    Did the person actually attend: Invited | Joined | No Show | Cancelled |
    Left Early. Designed as the per-person outcome of the call (the
    interview-level No Show status says the call failed; this says WHO
    failed to appear).

Joined_At__c (Joined At) [DateTime]
    Timestamp when the participant joined the call. Intended to be written
    by a meeting-platform integration (e.g. Zoom attendance), never by
    hand. Never populated.

Left_At__c (Left At) [DateTime]
    Timestamp when the participant left the call - together with Joined At
    gives per-person time-on-call for audit/billing. Never populated.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 0. The object has never held data in preprod.
- Consequently every distribution is empty; all field notes above describe
  DESIGN INTENT, not observed usage.
- Key takeaway for answering questions: if someone asks "who attended
  interview X", this object cannot answer it today - attendance facts live
  only in free-text feedback fields on Interview__c and in Zoom logs.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Interview_Type__c  (Label: "Interview Type")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Interview_Type__c is the admin-maintained CATALOG OF INTERNAL INTERVIEW /
ASSESSMENT TYPES for the Internal_Interview__c subsystem (Techsara's own
template-driven screening and training assessments - NOT interviews with
outside companies). Each record is one named kind of internal interview,
e.g. "Intake", "Mock", "Practice Mock Interview", or a training-week
assessment like "Advanced AI/ML Training - V1 - Week 1". Choosing a type
determines (via the Section_Interview_Type__c junction) which question
SECTIONS the interview runs and in what order.

COMMON CONFUSION - do not mix this up with:
- Interview__c.Interview_Type__c, a PICKLIST FIELD on the external Interview
  object (Screening Round / Technical Round / HR Round / Interview, and
  essentially unused). Same name, totally different thing.
- The catalog started as screening types (Intake/Mock/OOT) and has grown to
  cover training assessments and marketing-prep interview flavors - it is
  the generic "what kind of internal session is this" list.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Internal Interview (screening/assessment)
  domain. Configuration/catalog data, not transactional data.
- Standalone parent object; sharing is Public Read/Write (it is org-wide
  reference data). Owned by whoever creates it.
- Only 1 custom field (Is Active) plus the Name text field (label
  "Interview Type Name") - the record basically IS its name.
- 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view; has its own Lightning
  record page (generic detail + related lists layout).
- MASTER parent of Section_Interview_Type__c (its section links are deleted
  with it); looked up by Internal_Interview__c, Template__c, and (in the
  metadata snapshot only - see part 8 notes on the other objects) by the
  now-removed deprecated lookups on Section__c and Question_Bank__c.
- Scale: 8 records in preprod, all active.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Each row is itself a "type"; no record-type layer is needed on top.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - AN ADMIN CREATES A TYPE. On the Interview Type list view a "New
  Interview Type" button launches the Add_Interview_Type_Flow screen flow
  (this button, not the standard New, is the intended path). The flow asks
  for the name and active flag, creates the record, and can also attach
  existing sections to the new type by creating Section_Interview_Type__c
  junction rows.
STEP 2 - SECTIONS GET ATTACHED. The Add_Section_Flow ("New Section" button
  on the Section list) lets the admin pick which interview types a new
  section belongs to, creating junction rows with a Sequence number - so
  the type ends up with an ordered playlist of sections.
STEP 3 - SCHEDULING AN INTERNAL INTERVIEW. When an employee schedules or
  reschedules an internal interview (Interview_Create_Reschedule_Flow, the
  screen flow behind the "Create Interview" buttons on Candidate and Lead
  pages), they pick the Interview Type; it is stamped into
  Internal_Interview__c.Interview_Type__c.
STEP 4 - CONDUCTING. The Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview screen flow
  reads the type's junction rows to know which sections to run in which
  order (and/or uses a prebuilt Template__c, which also references an
  Interview Type). Question logs and evaluations are written per section.
STEP 5 - REVIEWING. View_Interview_Log_Flow shows past internal-interview
  logs and displays the type; reports group internal interviews by type.
Inactive types (Is Active unchecked) stop appearing as choices but keep
their history. In practice all 8 types are still active.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OBJECTS THAT POINT AT INTERVIEW TYPE (it has no lookups of its own):
- Section_Interview_Type__c (MASTER-DETAIL child): the junction rows tying
  this type to its ordered list of Section__c records. Deleting a type
  deletes its junction rows (not the sections themselves).
- Internal_Interview__c (lookup Interview_Type__c): every internal interview
  records which type it was - 100% populated on the 302 internal interviews
  in preprod.
- Template__c (lookup Interview_Type__c): a reusable interview template is
  built FOR a given type (1 template exists so far).
- Section__c (lookup Interview_Type__c) and Question_Bank__c (lookup
  Interview_Type__c): DEPRECATED direct links that the junction replaced;
  they still exist in this repo's metadata snapshot but have already been
  DELETED in the live preprod org (queries against them fail).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Catalog hygiene relies on the guided creation flow, not on validation
rules.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Add_Interview_Type_Flow (ACTIVE screen flow) - launched from the "New
  Interview Type" list-view button (/flow/Add_Interview_Type_Flow). Creates
  the Interview_Type__c record (Name, Is Active) and can create
  Section_Interview_Type__c junction rows for it.
- Interview_Create_Reschedule_Flow (ACTIVE screen flow) - reads this object
  so the scheduler can pick a type for the Internal_Interview__c being
  created/rescheduled.
- View_Interview_Log_Flow (ACTIVE screen flow) - reads it while displaying
  internal-interview history.
- Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview reaches it indirectly through the
  junction and Template lookups.
No record-triggered flows, no Apex triggers, no scheduled jobs.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (1 custom field + Name)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE TYPE CATALOG ------------------------------------------------

Name (Interview Type Name) [Text, standard Name field]
    The type's display name - this IS the business content of the record.
    Entered by the admin in Add_Interview_Type_Flow. Real values in preprod:
    Intake, Mock, OOT, Practice Mock Interview, Upcoming Interview,
    Rejection Interview, Advanced AI/ML Training - V1 - Week 1, Advanced
    AI/ML Training - V1 - Week 2. (What "OOT" stands for is not documented
    anywhere in the org - verify with team.)

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    Whether this type is currently offered when scheduling internal
    interviews. Set in the creation flow, toggled manually thereafter.
    Inactivating hides the type from new use while preserving history.
    All 8 records are active (TRUE) today, so the filter has never actually
    excluded anything in practice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 8, all active, created 2026-05-26 to 2026-08-06 (three
  waves: Intake/Mock/OOT in May, the two AI/ML training weeks in July, the
  three marketing-prep types in August).
- Usage on Internal_Interview__c (302 records, every one has a type):
  Practice Mock Interview 77 | Intake 71 | Upcoming Interview 71 |
  Rejection Interview 66 | Mock 7 | OOT 5 | Advanced AI/ML Training - V1 -
  Week 1: 3 | Week 2: 2.
- Sections attached via the junction: ONLY "Advanced AI/ML Training - V1 -
  Week 1" has section rows (6 of them, sequenced 1-6). The other 7 types
  have no sections wired up - their interviews run template-driven or
  AI/resume-driven instead.
- Templates: 1 Template__c record exists, linked to an interview type and
  a niche.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Question_Bank__c  (Label: "Question Bank")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Question_Bank__c is the reusable LIBRARY OF INTERVIEW QUESTIONS for the
INTERNAL interview subsystem (Internal_Interview__c - Techsara screening and
training its own candidates). One record = one question: its text, the
evaluation criteria an interviewer should score it against, a difficulty
level, and the Section (interview segment) it belongs to. At interview time
the conduct flow pulls a section's active questions, randomly picks the
required number, and the interviewer scores the candidate's answers.

It has NOTHING to do with external interviews (Interview__c) - questions
asked by client companies are captured free-text on the interview record,
not here. Note the object also feeds "standard" sections only: sections of
type "AI Resume Based" get their questions generated on the fly by an
external AI service from the candidate's resume, bypassing the bank.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Internal Interview (screening/assessment)
  domain. Semi-static content/config data maintained by admins/trainers.
- Standalone object, sharing Public Read/Write (shared question library).
- 8 custom fields (2 of them deprecated - and already physically DELETED in
  the live org, see part 8), 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list
  view; generic Lightning record page.
- Auto-number Name in the format QB-{00000} (label "Question Bank ID") -
  the question text field, not the Name, is the human-readable content.
- MASTER parent of Niche_Question__c (junction to Niche__c); looked up by
  Internal_Interview_Question_Log__c and Template_Section_Question__c.
- Scale: 620 records in preprod (created 2026-05-27 to 2026-07-27).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. All questions are one shape; Section, Difficulty and (via junction)
Niche carry the classification.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - AUTHORING. On the Question Bank list view the "Bulk Add Questions"
  button launches Bulk_Add_Questions_Flow: an admin/trainer pastes a batch
  of questions, picks the target Niche, and the flow mass-creates
  Question_Bank__c rows plus Niche_Question__c junction rows tying each
  question to that niche (1,160 junction rows exist for the 620 questions -
  a question can serve several niches).
STEP 2 - ORGANIZING. Each question is tied to a Section__c (the interview
  segment that asks it), directly via the Section lookup. Sections define
  how many questions they need (Total Questions) and whether they draw from
  the bank at all (Question Source Type = Standard) or generate questions
  from the resume via AI (AI Resume Based).
STEP 3 - TEMPLATE BUILDING (optional). Template_Creation_Flow lets an admin
  hand-pick specific bank questions into a reusable Template__c (via
  Template_Section_Question__c rows); Template_Structure_Flow displays that
  structure read-only.
STEP 4 - INTERVIEW TIME. Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview loads the
  active questions of each Standard section, calls the RandomizeQuestions
  Apex action (cryptographic shuffle) to pick N of them, and shows the
  interviewer each question with its Evaluation Criteria. Every question
  actually asked is SNAPSHOTTED into Internal_Interview_Question_Log__c
  (text and criteria copied, plus a lookup back to the bank row), so later
  edits to the bank do not rewrite history. 338 of the 428 question-log
  rows link back to a bank question (the rest were AI-generated).
STEP 5 - MAINTENANCE. Is Active is the retire switch - inactive questions
  stop being served. (All 620 are currently active.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM QUESTION BANK TO OTHER OBJECTS:
- Section__c (Section__c): the interview segment this question belongs to -
  the main organizing link. NOTE the data reality: 490 of 620 rows hold a
  Section id that NO LONGER RESOLVES (those Section records were deleted),
  so in the live org most questions are effectively orphaned (see part 9).
- Interview_Type__c (Interview_Type__c) - DEPRECATED, and already deleted
  in the live org (snapshot metadata only).
- Niche__c (Niche__c) - DEPRECATED direct link, also deleted in the live
  org; niche classification now goes through the Niche_Question__c
  junction instead.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT QUESTION BANK:
- Niche_Question__c (MASTER-DETAIL child via Question__c): junction to
  Niche__c - which candidate niches (skill domains) this question applies
  to. Created by Bulk_Add_Questions_Flow. 1,160 rows.
- Internal_Interview_Question_Log__c (lookup Question_Bank__c): the
  interview-time snapshot of an asked question, pointing back at its
  source bank row.
- Template_Section_Question__c (lookup Question__c): a question slotted
  into a reusable interview template (4 rows so far).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Data quality is driven by the guided bulk-add flow.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Bulk_Add_Questions_Flow (ACTIVE screen flow) - the "Bulk Add Questions"
  list-view button; mass-creates questions and their Niche_Question__c
  junction rows.
- Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview (ACTIVE screen flow) - READS active
  questions per section at interview time; calls the RandomizeQuestions
  invocable Apex class to pick a random subset (a Crypto-based shuffle
  for true randomness); writes the asked questions to the question log.
- Template_Creation_Flow (ACTIVE) / Template_Structure_Flow (ACTIVE) -
  READ bank questions while building/showing templates.
- RandomizeQuestions.cls (+ its test class) is the only Apex touching the
  object, and it only shuffles in-memory record collections passed by the
  flow - it performs no DML/SOQL of its own.
No record-triggered flows, triggers, or scheduled jobs write to this object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 8, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE QUESTION ITSELF ---------------------------------------------

Question_Text__c (Question Text) [LongTextArea]
    The full question the interviewer asks (e.g. an ML-fundamentals or
    coding question). Entered via the bulk-add flow. Copied verbatim into
    Internal_Interview_Question_Log__c when asked, so the log survives
    later edits. (Long text - population not queryable via SOQL
    aggregates, but it is the point of the record and safe to assume
    filled.)

Evaluation_Criteria__c (Evaluation Criteria) [LongTextArea]
    What a good answer looks like - the rubric shown to the interviewer
    next to the question during the conduct flow, and snapshotted into the
    question log (Evalation_Criteria_log__c) for audit. Authored with the
    question.

Difficulty_Level__c (Difficulty Level) [Picklist]
    Easy | Medium | Hard. Set at authoring; read by the conduct and
    template flows (e.g. to display or balance difficulty). Data: Medium
    341 (55%), Hard 211 (34%), Easy 68 (11%) - 100% populated.

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    Retire switch: only active questions are served to interviews and
    templates. All 620 records are currently TRUE - nothing has been
    retired yet.

--- GROUP B: WHERE THE QUESTION BELONGS --------------------------------------

Section__c (Section) [Lookup -> Section__c]
    The interview section (segment) that asks this question - how the
    conduct flow finds a Standard section's question pool. Set at
    authoring. DATA WARNING: 490 rows (79%) carry ids of Section records
    that have since been deleted, 130 rows (21%) are blank, and ZERO rows
    point at the 6 sections that exist today - in preprod the bank is
    currently disconnected from the live section catalog (the AI/ML
    training sections were rebuilt after the questions were loaded).

Section_Name__c (Section Name) [Formula, Text]
    Convenience formula showing Section__r.Name for lists and reports.
    Converted from a manually-maintained text field to a formula on
    2026-05-17 (per its metadata description). Currently blank on ALL rows
    because every populated Section lookup points at a deleted section.

--- GROUP C: DEPRECATED LINKS (kept in metadata snapshot, deleted in org) ----

Interview_Type__c (Interview Type (DEPRECATED - do not use)) [Lookup ->
Interview_Type__c]
    DEPRECATED 2026-05-17 (metadata description: "Interview type context
    comes from the linked Section. No longer used by any flow."). Already
    PHYSICALLY DELETED in the live preprod org - SOQL against it fails -
    but the field file still exists in this repo's metadata snapshot.
    Ignore it entirely.

Niche__c (Niche (DEPRECATED - do not use)) [Lookup -> Niche__c]
    DEPRECATED 2026-05-17 (description: "Question Bank no longer filters
    by Niche; niche-specific questions come from Lambda (AI Resume Based
    sections)."). Direct niche tagging was replaced by the
    Niche_Question__c junction. Also already deleted in the live org;
    snapshot metadata only.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 620, created 2026-05-27 to 2026-07-27. All active.
- Difficulty: Medium 341 (55%) | Hard 211 (34%) | Easy 68 (11%).
- Section link: 490 rows (79%) point at sections that were later DELETED

================================================================================
OBJECT: Section__c  (Label: "Section")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section__c is a reusable SEGMENT OF AN INTERNAL INTERVIEW in the
Internal_Interview__c subsystem - a named block such as "Week 1 Coding
Round" or "Day 01 Machine Learning Fundamentals" that groups questions and
carries the rules for running that block: how many questions to ask, roughly
how long it takes, whether it applies to tech or non-tech roles, and whether
its questions come from the Question Bank ("Standard") or are AI-generated
from the candidate's resume ("AI Resume Based"). Sections are attached to
one or more Interview Types through the Section_Interview_Type__c junction,
which also gives them their running order.

Despite the generic name, it has nothing to do with page-layout sections or
with external interviews (Interview__c). Current live data shows it being
used as the day-by-day curriculum of the "Advanced AI/ML Training - V1 -
Week 1" assessment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, Internal Interview (screening/assessment) domain.
  Configuration/content data maintained by admins/trainers.
- Standalone object, sharing Public Read/Write.
- 8 custom fields (2 deprecated - and already deleted in the live org),
  0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view; generic Lightning
  record page. Name is a plain Text field ("Section Name").
- MASTER parent of Section_Interview_Type__c; looked up by
  Question_Bank__c, Template_Section__c, Internal_Interview_Section_Log__c,
  Internal_Interview_Question_Log__c, and Section_Evaluation__c.
- Scale: 6 records in preprod (all created for the AI/ML training week).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The Domain Type and Question Source Type picklists differentiate
section behavior instead.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATION. On the Section list view the "New Section" button
  launches Add_Section_Flow: the admin names the section, sets domain type,
  question source, question count and estimated time, picks which Interview
  Types it belongs to, and the flow creates the Section__c record plus one
  Section_Interview_Type__c junction row per chosen type (with a sequence).
STEP 2 - FILLING WITH QUESTIONS. For "Standard" sections, Question_Bank__c
  rows are pointed at the section (its question pool). "AI Resume Based"
  sections stay empty - their questions are generated per candidate by the
  external AI service (AWS Lambda) from the resume at interview time.
STEP 3 - RUNNING. When an internal interview is conducted
  (Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview screen flow), the flow resolves the
  section list - from the interview type's junction rows, from the chosen
  Template__c's Template_Section__c rows, or (in "Techsara's Magic" launch
  mode) by fetching sections whose Domain Type matches the candidate
  Niche's domain. For each section it creates an
  Internal_Interview_Section_Log__c row, asks Total Questions questions
  (randomized from the pool, or AI-generated), logs each in
  Internal_Interview_Question_Log__c, and captures a per-section score and
  comment.
STEP 4 - EVALUATION. The human evaluation writes Section_Evaluation__c
  rows (score + comment per section) under the Interview_Evaluation__c
  record, referencing the section.
STEP 5 - MAINTENANCE. Is Active retires a section from future interviews;
  logs keep the history.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM SECTION TO OTHER OBJECTS (both deprecated):
- Interview_Type__c (Interview_Type__c) - DEPRECATED 2026-05-20, replaced
  by the Section_Interview_Type__c junction "so one Section can serve
  multiple Interview Types". Its metadata description notes it was "still
  read by Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview flow until flow rework
  completes" - but the field has ALREADY BEEN DELETED in the live preprod
  org (SOQL fails), so treat it as gone.
- Niche__c (Niche__c) - DEPRECATED 2026-05-17, replaced by the Domain Type
  picklist. Also already deleted in the live org; snapshot metadata only.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT SECTION:
- Section_Interview_Type__c (MASTER-DETAIL child): junction to
  Interview_Type__c with a Sequence - "this section is step N of that
  interview type". Deleting a section deletes its junction rows.
- Question_Bank__c (lookup Section__c): the section's question pool
  (Standard sections). Note: in preprod today no live question points at
  any live section - the wiring is stale (see Question Bank part 9).
- Template_Section__c (lookup Section__c): this section slotted into a
  reusable Template__c with its own sequence/active flag.
- Internal_Interview_Section_Log__c (lookup Section__c): the run-time log
  of this section inside one internal interview (score, comment, question
  source used). 104 rows, all referencing a section.
- Internal_Interview_Question_Log__c (lookup Section__c): each asked
  question's log also stamps which section it was asked in.
- Section_Evaluation__c (lookup Section__c): per-section score/comment in
  the human evaluation (child of Interview_Evaluation__c). 6 rows.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Section setup quality is handled by the Add_Section_Flow screens.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Add_Section_Flow (ACTIVE screen flow) - the "New Section" list-view
  button; creates the section and its interview-type junction rows.
- Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview (ACTIVE screen flow) - READS
  sections (domain type, question source, question count, estimated time,
  active flag) to run each block and write the logs.
- Template_Creation_Flow / Template_Structure_Flow (ACTIVE) - READ sections
  when building/displaying reusable templates (Interview_Sequence__c is,
  per its description, used only by the template-creation flow).
No record-triggered flows, no Apex, no scheduled jobs touch this object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 8, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHAT KIND OF SECTION THIS IS ------------------------------------

Domain_Type__c (Domain Type) [Picklist]
    Which role families the section applies to: Tech (technical roles
    only) | Non-Tech (non-technical roles only) | Both (applies to all) -
    meanings straight from the field help text. Used by "Techsara's Magic"
    launch mode to auto-fetch sections matching the candidate Niche's
    domain type. All 6 live sections are "Tech".

Question_Source_Type__c (Question Source Type) [Picklist]
    Where the section's questions come from: Standard (drawn at random
    from the Question_Bank__c rows linked to this section) | AI Resume
    Based (generated per candidate by the external AI service from the
    resume - the section carries no bank questions). Echoed into the logs
    as Question_Source_Used__c. All 6 live sections are "Standard".

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    Whether the section is currently runnable/selectable. The conduct and
    template flows filter on it. TRUE on all 6 live rows.

--- GROUP B: SIZING & ORDERING -----------------------------------------------

Total_Questions__c (Total Questions) [Number(2,0)]
    How many questions the section asks. For Standard sections the conduct
    flow passes the pool to the RandomizeQuestions Apex action and keeps
    this many. All 6 live sections ask 5 questions.

ESTIMATED_TIME_IN_MINUTES__c (Estimated Time(In Minutes)) [Text]
    Planned duration of the section, shown to the interviewer for pacing.
    Oddly a TEXT field (length 50), not a number - so it cannot be summed
    in reports. Value is "5" on all 6 live rows.

Interview_Sequence__c (Interview Sequence) [Number(18,0)]
    A section-level ordering number whose metadata description says "Used
    in Template Creation Flow only". The real running order lives on the
    junction (Section_Interview_Type__c.Sequence__c) and on
    Template_Section__c. Null on all 6 live rows - effectively unused.

--- GROUP C: DEPRECATED LINKS (kept in metadata snapshot, deleted in org) ----

Interview_Type__c (Interview Type (DEPRECATED - do not use)) [Lookup ->
Interview_Type__c]
    The old one-type-per-section link, DEPRECATED 2026-05-20 in favor of
    the Section_Interview_Type__c junction (one section, many types).
    Already physically deleted in the live preprod org; only the snapshot
    metadata still shows it. Do not reference it.

Niche__c (Niche (DEPRECATED - do not use)) [Lookup -> Niche__c]
    The old per-niche tagging, DEPRECATED 2026-05-17 and replaced by
    Domain_Type__c. Already deleted in the live org; snapshot only.

9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 6, all active, all Tech / Standard / 5 questions /
  estimated 5 minutes: "Day 01 Machine Learning Fundamentals", "Day 02
  regression", "Day 03 classification", "Day 04 Model Optimization",
  "Day 05 unsupervised learning", "Week 1 Coding Round" - i.e. the
  day-by-day curriculum of the Advanced AI/ML Training Week 1 assessment
  (created 2026-07-27).
- All 6 are attached (sequence 1-6) to the "Advanced AI/ML Training - V1 -
  Week 1" interview type via the junction. Interview_Sequence__c is null
  on every row.
- An earlier generation of sections was DELETED: 490 Question Bank rows
  still hold their dead ids, and the 104 section-log rows all reference a
  section id (historic ones included). 6 Section_Evaluation__c rows exist.
- Key takeaway: the live section catalog is small and training-focused
  right now; the older screening-era sections were dropped without
  re-pointing the question bank (verify intended cleanup with team).

================================================================================
OBJECT: Section_Interview_Type__c  (Label: "Section Interview Type")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section_Interview_Type__c is a pure MANY-TO-MANY JUNCTION between Section__c
and Interview_Type__c in the internal-interview subsystem, with one payload
field: Sequence. Each row means "when running an internal interview of THIS
type, run THAT section as step N". It exists so one section (e.g. a coding
round) can be reused across several interview types without duplication -
it replaced the old single Interview Type lookup on Section__c (deprecated
2026-05-20 for exactly this reason).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, Internal Interview (screening/assessment) domain.
  Configuration data - created when admins wire sections to types.
- JUNCTION with TWO MASTER-DETAIL parents: Interview_Type__c and
  Section__c. Sharing is "Controlled By Parent"; deleting either parent
  deletes the junction row.
- 3 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Auto-number Name in the format SIT-{00000} (label "Section Interview
  Type ID") - users never read these names.
- No Lightning record page of its own; it surfaces as related lists on the
  two parents.
- Scale: 6 records in preprod.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. A junction row has no flavors.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - WIRING. Junction rows are created by the guided admin flows, not
  by hand: Add_Section_Flow creates one row per interview type the new
  section is attached to (looping over the admin's selections), and
  Add_Interview_Type_Flow can create rows when a new type is given its
  sections. The Sequence number recorded on each row defines the section's
  position in that type's running order.
STEP 2 - RESOLUTION AT INTERVIEW TIME. When an internal interview of a
  given type is conducted, Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview reads the
  type's junction rows (section + sequence) to build the ordered list of
  sections to run.
STEP 3 - RE-WIRING. Attaching an existing section to another type just
  means another junction row with its own sequence; removing it means
  deleting the row - the section itself is untouched.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENTS (both master-detail, both required):
- Interview_Type__c (via Interview_Type__c): the internal interview type
  whose playlist this row belongs to. Child relationship:
  Section_Interview_Types.
- Section__c (via Section__c): the section being scheduled as one step of
  that playlist. Child relationship: Section_Interview_Types.

Nothing points at Section_Interview_Type__c - it is a leaf junction.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Nothing prevents duplicate section-type pairs or clashing sequence
numbers except the guided flows themselves.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Add_Section_Flow (ACTIVE screen flow) - creates junction rows (and looks
  existing ones up) when a section is created and attached to types.
- Add_Interview_Type_Flow (ACTIVE screen flow) - can create junction rows
  when a new interview type is set up with sections.
- Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview (ACTIVE screen flow) - READS the
  rows (Interview Type, Section, Sequence) to order the sections of a
  running internal interview.
No record-triggered flows, no Apex, no scheduled jobs.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 3, one group)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE JUNCTION ----------------------------------------------------

Interview_Type__c (Interview Type) [Master-Detail -> Interview_Type__c]
    Which internal interview type this row extends. Set by the admin flows
    at creation; required. All 6 live rows point at "Advanced AI/ML
    Training - V1 - Week 1".

Section__c (Section) [Master-Detail -> Section__c]
    Which section is being placed into that type's running order. Set by
    the admin flows; required. The 6 live rows cover the 6 live sections
    exactly (Day 01-05 plus the Week 1 Coding Round).

Sequence__c (Sequence) [Number(3,0)]
    The section's position (1, 2, 3...) inside this interview type - the
    field the conduct flow sorts on to run sections in order. Live data:
    1 through 6 (Day 01 -> Day 05, then the coding round last).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 6 - all belonging to ONE interview type, "Advanced AI/ML
  Training - V1 - Week 1", sequencing its five daily sections and final
  coding round (1-6).
- The other 7 interview types have zero junction rows: their internal
  interviews run via templates or AI-generated questions instead of a
  wired section playlist.
- Key takeaway: this junction is brand-new plumbing (the sections it
  orders were created 2026-07-27) and so far describes exactly one
  training-week assessment.

================================================================================
OBJECT: AI_Assignment_Logs__c  (Label: "AI Assignment Logs")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AI_Assignment_Logs__c is the AUDIT LOG of the COMPASS AI support-person
assignment engine. Every time the AI assignment machinery runs - the nightly
batch, the manual "run the assignment now" launcher, or one of the human
override buttons on an Interview record (Reassignment, Reshuffle, Rollback,
PSP/Preferred Support Person) - a row is created here recording WHO initiated
it, WHEN, WHY (a reason picklist for the override buttons), and WHAT the
external AWS service answered (the raw HTTP response body and status code).

One record = one run/click of one of those actions. The object does not hold
the assignment DECISION itself - the decision (which employee supports which
interview) lands on Interview__c (Interview_Support_Person__c and the Group J
AI fields of the Interview section). This object only proves the run happened
and keeps the API evidence, so the team can answer "who reassigned this
interview, when, why, and what did the engine say back?".

The design is unusual: instead of a generic "log type" picklist plus shared
columns, the object has a SEPARATE column set per action type (scheduler run
fields, manual run fields, reassignment fields, reshuffle fields, rollback
fields, preferred-support-person fields, Compass-R fields). Each flow fills
only its own columns and leaves the rest blank, and one list view per action
type filters the rows. That is why 45 fields exist for such a simple object
and why any single row is mostly empty.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Interviewing / AI-assignment (COMPASS) domain.
- Standalone object with its own owner (not master-detail). Org-wide default
  sharing is Public Read/Write; the security-model design treats it as an
  audit trail that should be read-only for most users.
- 45 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 7 list views (one
  "All" view plus one view per action type: Compass R scheduler, Main AI
  Assignment scheduler, Manual Main AI Assignment, Preferred Support Person,
  Reassignment, Reshuffle).
- Auto-number Name in the format AI-XXXXX.
- Access is granted by the AI_Interview_Operations permission set (create/
  read/edit/delete), AI_Reassignment_Button (create/edit) and Jenkins_CICD
  (full incl. View All/Modify All). Its tab shows in the Techsara Solutions
  and Training Module apps.
- Scale: only 7 records in preprod (Jul 29 - Aug 11, 2026). The object and
  its buttons are brand new and barely used yet.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The object has no record types - the per-action column sets and list
views play that role instead.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Background: the external COMPASS AI engine (AWS API Gateway/Lambda, called
through named-credential External Services) assigns an internal employee
(Interview_Support_Person__c) to each upcoming interview. Users never edit
this log by hand - every row is created by one of six flows, all tied to the
AI machinery. All the entry points are gated on the Run_AI_Interview_
Assignment custom permission.

WAYS A LOG ROW GETS CREATED:

a) NIGHTLY BATCH (planned, not live). The scheduled flow Interview_Main_AI_
   Assignment_Schedular is meant to run daily at 20:00 UTC: it collects
   unassigned upcoming interviews, calls the AWS engine through the
   ScheduledCalloutMaster Apex action, then emails + Slacks a summary and
   writes a log row (scheduler run by/on fields). THIS FLOW IS STILL DRAFT
   in preprod - it has never run and its columns are empty on all rows.

b) MANUAL "RUN NOW" LAUNCHER. The active screen flow Main_AI_Assignment_
   Launcher_Flow is embedded on the "Main AI Assignment" app page (Techsara
   Solutions app; page visibility gated on Run_AI_Interview_Assignment).
   An operator opens the page, the flow shows the eligible interviews
   (upcoming, right status, request raised), calls the AWS "Main AI Assign
   Callout" external service, and logs the run: who ran it, when, the raw
   response and the HTTP status code. The same app page also embeds the
   Compass_R flow (still Draft) and six list-view cards - one per action
   type of this object - so the page doubles as the AI-operations console.

c) REASSIGNMENT BUTTON. On an Interview record, an authorized user clicks
   "Reassignment" (quick action -> screen flow Reassignment, active). The
   user picks a reason from a picklist, the flow calls the AWS Reassignment
   external service (the engine picks a replacement support person), and a
   log row records: the interview (Interview_ID__c), the support person who
   was replaced (Last_Support_Person1__c), who clicked, when, the reason,
   the raw response body and status code.

d) RESHUFFLE BUTTON. Quick action -> screen flow Interview_Reshuffle
   (active). Reshuffle re-runs the assignment across the day's interviews
   (rebalancing several assignments, not just one). Logs initiator, time,
   reason, response body, status code. Never used yet in preprod data.

e) ROLLBACK BUTTON. Quick action -> screen flow Interview_Roll_Back
   (active). Undoes the last assignment run by calling the AWS Rollback
   service. Logs initiator, run time and the raw response. Never used yet.

f) PSP (PREFERRED SUPPORT PERSON) BUTTON. Quick action -> screen flow
   Interview_Preferred_Support_Person. The user nominates a preferred
   employee (the flow checks the employee is Active_For_Interview_Support__c
   on Recruiter__c) and the engine is told to honor that preference. Logs
   initiator, time, the interview's round/round-type text and the previous
   support person. NOTE: this flow's latest version is marked Obsolete
   (deactivated) in this snapshot even though the PSP button is still on two
   Interview record pages and one row was logged on Jul 29, 2026 - verify
   with team whether PSP is currently enabled.

READING THE LOG. Ops and admins read the rows through the 7 list views (or
the list-view cards on the Main AI Assignment page) to monitor whether runs
succeeded (status code 200) and to trace who triggered overrides. Nothing
downstream consumes the log - no flow, Apex, or report automation reads it
back; it exists purely as evidence.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All relationships are optional lookups; a row only fills the ones its action
type needs.

- Interview__c via Interview_ID__c (label "Interview ID"): the interview the
  logged action was about. This is the lookup ACTUALLY IN USE - the active
  Reassignment flow writes it (populated on 5 of 7 rows).
- Interview__c via Interview__c (label "Interview"): a second, later-added
  lookup to the same object. No current flow writes it and it is empty on
  every row. (The approved Interview section describes Interview_ID__c as
  the legacy one of the pair; in the actual data the roles are reversed -
  Interview_ID__c carries the data, Interview__c is unused.)
- Account via Candidate_Interview_Change__c: intended link to the candidate
  (Person Account) whose interview assignment changed; surfaced as a related
  list on the Account layout but never populated (no flow writes it).
- Recruiter__c ("Employee") via Last_Support_Person1__c: the employee who
  WAS the support person before the change (Reassignment and PSP flows).
- User via Last_Support_Person__c: unused User-based twin of the above.
- User via Reassignment_Initiated_By__c / Reshuffle_Initiated_By__c /
  Rollback_Initiated_By__c / preferred_support_person_initiated_by__c /
  Main_AI_Assignment_scheduler_run_by__c /
  Manual_Main_AI_Assignment_Flow_run_by__c: the internal user who triggered
  each action type (one "who" field per action).
- Recruiter__c via Reassignment_by__c / Manual_Main_AI_Assignment_run_by__c /
  Main_AI_Assignment_scheduler_run_by_old__c / Compass_R_scheduler_run_by__c:
  older Employee-lookup variants of those same "who" fields; none are
  written by the current flows (all empty).

No object looks up to AI_Assignment_Logs__c - it is a leaf/audit object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Rows are only ever created by system flows, so no user-facing
validation was built.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Nothing triggers ON this object - no record-triggered flows, no Apex trigger,
and no Apex class references it at all. It is purely a WRITE TARGET of six
flows (each creates a row as part of its run):

- Interview_Main_AI_Assignment_Schedular (Scheduled flow, DRAFT - not
  running): daily nightly-batch launcher; would write the "Main AI
  Assignment scheduler" columns and send a Slack + email summary.
- Main_AI_Assignment_Launcher_Flow (Screen flow, Active; embedded on the
  Main AI Assignment app page): manual batch run; writes the "Manual Main
  AI Assignment" columns.
- Reassignment (Screen flow, Active; "Reassignment" quick action on the
  Interview record pages): writes the Reassignment columns plus
  Interview_ID__c and Last_Support_Person1__c.
- Interview_Reshuffle (Screen flow, Active; "Reshuffle" quick action):
  writes the Reshuffle columns.
- Interview_Roll_Back (Screen flow, Active; "Rollback" quick action):
  writes the Rollback columns.
- Interview_Preferred_Support_Person (Screen flow, marked Obsolete in this
  snapshot; "PSP" quick action): writes the preferred-support-person
  columns plus Round__c, Round_Info__c and Last_Support_Person1__c.

The Compass_R screen flow (Draft, also embedded on the Main AI Assignment
page) calls the shared HttpCalloutGeneric Apex but does NOT yet write a log
row - the Compass_R_scheduler_* columns wait for it to be finished.

There are no quick actions on AI_Assignment_Logs__c itself; all the buttons
live on Interview__c and on the Main AI Assignment app page.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 45, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reminder: each action type has its own column set; a row fills only the
group(s) belonging to the flow that created it. None of the fields have help
text in metadata - the descriptions below come from the flows that write
them and the live data.

--- GROUP A: WHICH INTERVIEW / CONTEXT OF THE CHANGE -------------------------

Interview_ID__c (Interview ID) [Lookup -> Interview__c]
    The interview the logged action concerned. Set by the Reassignment flow
    when the Reassignment button is used (5 of 7 rows populated). Despite
    the clunky name, this is the interview lookup in real use - use it to
    join logs to interviews.

Interview__c (Interview) [Lookup -> Interview__c]
    A second lookup to Interview added alongside the one above. No active
    flow writes it and it is empty on all rows. Presumably meant to replace
    Interview_ID__c one day (not fully documented - verify with team).

Interviews_ID__c (Interviews ID) [Number]
    A plain-number interview identifier, predating the lookups. Never
    populated; no automation writes it (not fully documented - verify with
    team).

Candidate_Interview_Change__c (Candidate Interview Change) [Lookup -> Account]
    Intended pointer to the candidate (Person Account) whose interview
    assignment was changed, which would let the candidate page show an
    "AI Assignment Logs" related list. No flow fills it; 0% populated.

Round__c (Round) [Text]
    Text snapshot of the interview's round (e.g. "First") at the moment of
    the action. Written by the PSP flow; in the current flow definitions
    only PSP writes it, but one early Jul-29 reassignment row also carries
    it (an older Reassignment flow version apparently set it too) - 2 of 7
    rows total. Text, not a picklist, because it just mirrors
    Interview__c.Round__c.

Round_Info__c (Round Info) [Text]
    Text snapshot of the interview's round TYPE (e.g. "Introduction Call",
    mirroring Interview__c.Round_Info__c). Same population pattern as
    Round__c: written by the PSP flow, plus the same early reassignment
    row (2 of 7 rows).

Last_Support_Person1__c (Last Support Person) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    The employee who WAS the interview's support person before this action
    replaced them - the "before" side of the change. Written by the
    Reassignment and PSP flows (2 of 7 rows; blank when the interview had
    no support person yet).

Last_Support_Person__c (Last Support Person) [Lookup -> User]
    User-based twin of the field above (same label). Unused - no flow
    writes it, 0% populated. Exists because the org's people model split
    between User and Recruiter__c ("Employee") lookups.

--- GROUP B: NIGHTLY SCHEDULER RUN AUDIT (FLOW STILL DRAFT) ------------------
Columns for the daily batch run of Interview_Main_AI_Assignment_Schedular.
The flow is Draft, so every field in this group is empty on all rows today.

Main_AI_Assignment_scheduler_run_by__c (Main AI Assignment scheduler run by)
[Lookup -> User]
    Which user identity the scheduled nightly run executed as. To be set by
    the scheduler flow when it goes live.

Main_AI_Assignment_scheduler_run_by_old__c (Main AI Assignment scheduler run
by old) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    Superseded Employee-lookup version of the field above ("old" is in the
    name). Kept on the layout but written by nothing.

Main_AI_Assignment_scheduler_run_on__c (Main AI Assignment scheduler run on)
[DateTime]
    Timestamp of the nightly batch run. To be set by the scheduler flow.

Main_AI_Assignment_scheduler_run_respons__c (Main AI Assignment scheduler run
respons) [LongTextArea]
    Raw HTTP response body returned by the AWS engine for the nightly run
    (name truncated by the 40-character API-name limit).

Main_AI_Assignment_scheduler_run_status__c (Main AI Assignment scheduler run
status) [Number]
    HTTP status code of the nightly run callout (200 = success).

--- GROUP C: MANUAL "RUN NOW" LAUNCHER AUDIT ---------------------------------
Columns written by Main_AI_Assignment_Launcher_Flow when an operator runs
the batch on demand from the Main AI Assignment app page. 1 of 7 rows.

Manual_Main_AI_Assignment_Flow_run_by__c (Manual Main AI Assignment Flow run
by) [Lookup -> User]
    The internal user who clicked through the launcher flow. Set by the
    flow; populated on the one manual-run row.

Manual_Main_AI_Assignment_run_by__c (Manual Main AI Assignment run by)
[Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    Older Employee-lookup variant of the initiator field. Not written by
    the current flow version; empty.

Manual_Main_AI_Assignment_run_on__c (Manual Main AI Assignment run on)
[DateTime]
    When the manual batch run happened. Set by the launcher flow.

Manual_Main_AI_Assignment_run_Response__c (Manual Main AI Assignment run
Response) [LongTextArea]
    Raw HTTP response body from the AWS "Main AI Assign" callout - the
    engine's full answer (assignments made, errors), kept verbatim for
    debugging.

Manual_Main_AI_Assignment_run_status_cod__c (Manual Main AI Assignment run
status cod) [Number]
    HTTP status code of the manual-run callout (truncated API name). The
    flow can write it, but the one logged run left it blank.

--- GROUP D: REASSIGNMENT BUTTON AUDIT ---------------------------------------
Columns written by the active Reassignment screen flow - the most used
action so far (5 of 7 rows, all with HTTP 200 responses).

Reassignment_Initiated_By__c (Reassignment Initiated By) [Lookup -> User]
    Who clicked the Reassignment button. Set by the flow on every
    reassignment row (5 of 7). The same click is also stamped on the
    Interview itself (its own Reassignment_Initiated_By__c field).

Reassignment_by__c (Reassignment  by) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    Older Employee-lookup variant of the initiator; not written by the
    current flow, 0% populated.

Reassignment_on__c (Reassignment on) [DateTime]
    When the reassignment ran. Set by the flow (5 of 7 rows).

Reassignment_Reason_Picklist_Values__c (Reassignment Reason Picklist Values)
[Picklist]
    The reason the user picked in the flow's screen. Values: Previous round
    extended for current Interview Support Person (the support person's
    earlier interview ran over) | Interview Support Person unavailable |
    Scheduling conflict | Interview Support Person at capacity (workload
    cap) | Skill / domain mismatch | Candidate preference | Time zone
    mismatch | Escalation from team lead / manager | Other. Real data: 4 of
    5 rows are "Previous round extended...", 1 is "unavailable" - overrun
    interviews are the dominant real-world cause.

Reassignment_Other_Reason__c (Reassignment Other  Reason) [Text]
    Free-text reason when "Other" is chosen (only 20 characters long).
    Never used yet.

Reassignment_run_response_body__c (Reassignment  run response body)
[LongTextArea]
    Raw HTTP response from the AWS Reassignment service - who the engine
    picked as the replacement and why, kept verbatim.

Reassignment_run_status_code__c (Reassignment  run status code) [Number]
    HTTP status of the reassignment callout. All 5 logged runs returned
    200.

--- GROUP E: RESHUFFLE BUTTON AUDIT ------------------------------------------
Columns written by the active Interview_Reshuffle screen flow (bulk
re-balancing of assignments). The button has never been used - every field
in this group is 0% populated.

Reshuffle_Initiated_By__c (Reshuffle Initiated By) [Lookup -> User]
    Who clicked the Reshuffle button. Set by the flow.

Reshuffle_Initiated_On__c (Reshuffle Initiated On) [DateTime]
    When the reshuffle ran. Set by the flow.

Reshuffle_Reason__c (Reshuffle Reason) [Picklist]
    Why the reshuffle was needed - same 9 values as the reassignment reason
    list (Previous round extended... | unavailable | Scheduling conflict |
    at capacity | Skill / domain mismatch | Candidate preference | Time
    zone mismatch | Escalation | Other). This is the one the flow writes.

Reshuffle_Run_Reason__c (Reshuffle Run Reason) [Picklist]
    Duplicate of Reshuffle_Reason__c with the identical value list. Sits on
    the layout but is NOT written by the flow - a leftover from an earlier
    build (not fully documented - verify with team).

Reshuffle_Reason_Comment__c (Reshuffle Reason Comment) [Text]
    Free-text comment for the reshuffle reason (250 chars). On the layout
    but not written by the current flow version.

Reshuffle_run_response_body__c (Reshuffle run response body) [LongTextArea]
    Raw HTTP response from the AWS Reshuffle service.

reshuffle_run_status_code__c (reshuffle run status code) [Number]
    HTTP status of the reshuffle callout (note the lower-case API name).

--- GROUP F: ROLLBACK BUTTON AUDIT -------------------------------------------
Columns written by the active Interview_Roll_Back screen flow (undo the
last assignment run). Never used yet - all 0% populated. Note there is no
status-code field for rollback, only the response body.

Rollback_Initiated_By__c (Rollback Initiated By) [Lookup -> User]
    Who clicked the Rollback button. Set by the flow.

Rollback_Run_On__c (Rollback Run On) [DateTime]
    When the rollback ran. Set by the flow.

Rollback_Response_Body__c (Rollback Response Body) [LongTextArea]
    Raw HTTP response from the AWS Rollback service (what was undone).

--- GROUP G: PREFERRED SUPPORT PERSON (PSP) BUTTON AUDIT ---------------------
Columns written by the Interview_Preferred_Support_Person flow (currently
deactivated/Obsolete in this snapshot). One row logged so far; the PSP row
also fills Round__c, Round_Info__c and Last_Support_Person1__c in Group A.

preferred_support_person_initiated_by__c (preferred support person initiated
by) [Lookup -> User]
    Who nominated the preferred support person via the PSP button (note the
    lower-case API naming). 1 of 7 rows.

preferred_support_person_initiated_On__c (preferred support person initiated

    When the PSP nomination was made. 1 of 7 rows.

--- GROUP H: COMPASS-R SCHEDULER AUDIT (PLANNED, NOT WIRED) ------------------
Columns reserved for a "Compass R" scheduled run - a second COMPASS engine

Compass_R_scheduler_run_by__c (Compass R scheduler run by)
[Lookup -> Recruiter__c]

Compass_R_scheduler_run_Response_Body__c (Compass R scheduler run Response

Compass_R_scheduler_run_Status_Code__c (Compass R scheduler  run Status Code)
[Number]
    HTTP status code of the Compass-R callout.

--- GROUP I: RUN TOTALS & CI/CD TEST FIELDS ----------------------------------

Total_Interview_Assigned__c (Total Interview Assigned) [Number]

    person assigned. No flow writes it yet; 0% populated.

Total_Interviews_Unassigned__c (Total Interviews Unassigned) [Number]

testing_field_for_jenkins__c (testing field for jenkins) [Text]

TESTING_JENKINS__c (TESTING JENKINS) [Text]
    Second Jenkins CI/CD test field. It still exists in the source snapshot
    but is NOT queryable in the live preprod org (it appears to have been

9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 7, created between 2026-07-29 and 2026-08-11 - the log (and
  the override buttons feeding it) went live only about two weeks ago.
- Breakdown by action type: 5 Reassignment rows | 1 manual Main-AI-Assignment
  run | 1 PSP row. Zero rows so far for Reshuffle, Rollback, the nightly
  scheduler (its flow is Draft) and Compass-R (flow is Draft).
- All 5 reassignment callouts returned HTTP 200. Reasons: "Previous round
  extended for current Interview Support Person" x4, "Interview Support
  Person unavailable" x1.
- Populated fields across the 7 rows: Interview_ID__c 5, Reassignment_
