================================================================================
OBJECT: Step_Deliverable_Definition__c  (Label: "Step Deliverable Definition")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Step_Deliverable_Definition__c is the blueprint of a WORK PRODUCT a training
step demands from the candidate: "submit a recorded video", "upload your
resume file", "paste a GitHub URL", "tick the confirmation box". Each
StepTemplate__c can have several definitions; at enrollment each definition
becomes one Deliverable__c under the candidate's step, carrying the
definition's label, type, requiredness and deadline offset. The definition
also carries a Schema_JSON__c config consumed by the candidate portal /
AWS AI evaluation pipeline.

IMPORTANT DATA REALITY: as of this snapshot the table is EMPTY in preprod
(0 rows), yet 3,251 of 3,252 Deliverable__c records still hold Definition
IDs that no longer resolve, and deliverables created as late as 2026-08-03
had live links. The definition records were evidently deleted (and purged)
shortly before this snapshot. Until they are recreated, new enrollments
will produce steps but NO deliverables, and Update_Program_Version has no
definitions to clone. (Not fully documented - verify with team whether this
deletion was intentional, e.g. a planned re-import.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, blueprint tier of the Training / LMS domain.
- Standalone object (plain LOOKUP to StepTemplate__c, not master-detail);
  org-wide default Public Read/Write.
- 8 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Auto-number Name in the format SDD-{0000}; it ALSO has a second
  auto-number field (Key__c) - see part 8.
- Scale: currently 0 records (see the data-reality note above).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. One layout and one Lightning page
(Step_Deliverable_Definition_Record_Page) serve all definitions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - AUTHORING. Definitions are created together with their step
  templates inside the Program_Creation wizard (and adjusted/cloned by
  Update_Program_Version when a new version is cut). The author decides,
  per step: what artifact the candidate must produce (Type__c), what it is
  called (Label__c), whether it is mandatory (Is_Required__c), and how many
  days after the step the candidate gets to finish it
  (Days_To_Complete__c).

STEP 2 - INSTANTIATION. At enrollment, Candidate_Training_Creation loops
  the definitions of every step template in the version and creates one
  Deliverable__c per definition per candidate step, copying the label into
  the deliverable Name, the requiredness, the days-to-complete, and
  linking back via Deliverable__c.Definitions__c.

STEP 3 - DEADLINES. When the training is booked into a session window, the
  booking Apex recomputes each deliverable's due dates as: its step's
  scheduled date + the definition's Days_To_Complete (carried on the
  deliverable), expressed in both IST and the candidate's time zone.

STEP 4 - EVALUATION. The definition's Type__c/Schema_JSON__c shape what
  the candidate portal collects and what the AWS AI evaluation engine
  receives (the whole training package, definitions included, is pushed to
  AWS at enrollment by AWSTrainingIntegration; scores come back through
  the DeliverableResultRest REST endpoint onto Deliverable_Result__c).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM THE DEFINITION:
- StepTemplate__c (Step_Template__c): the step this deliverable
  requirement belongs to. A definition without a step template is
  meaningless, but the lookup is technically optional.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT THE DEFINITION:
- Deliverable__c (lookup Definitions__c, label "Definition", delete
  constraint SetNull): every runtime deliverable instantiated from this
  definition. NOTE: in current preprod data these lookups are orphaned -
  they hold IDs of definition records that were deleted (the SetNull
  cleanup evidently did not run/complete), so Definitions__r traversals
  return null even though COUNT(Definitions__c) is ~100%.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Shape is controlled by the authoring wizard flows.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No record-triggered flows, no Apex triggers, no quick actions. Touched only
by screen flows and integrations elsewhere:
- Program_Creation (screen flow): creates definitions while authoring a
  program version.
- Update_Program_Version (screen flow): reads all definition fields
  (Label, Type, Is_Required, Days_To_Complete, Lookup_Key, Step_Template)
  to clone them under the new version's steps.
- Candidate_Training_Creation (screen flow): reads definitions at
  enrollment to generate the candidate's Deliverable__c records.
- AWSTrainingIntegration (Apex): includes the definitions in the training
  package sent to the AWS AI engine at enrollment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 8, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
(The table is empty in preprod, so no population percentages can be given;
meanings below come from metadata, the flows that read the fields, and the
runtime copies on Deliverable__c.)

--- GROUP A: WHERE IT BELONGS ------------------------------------------------

Step_Template__c (Step Template) [Lookup -> StepTemplate__c]
    The step template this deliverable requirement is attached to. Set by
    the authoring wizards; the enrollment flow uses it to find "all
    definitions of this step" when generating deliverables.

--- GROUP B: WHAT THE CANDIDATE MUST SUBMIT ----------------------------------

Label__c (Label) [Text, required]
    The human name of the required artifact (e.g. "Recorded self-intro
    video"). Copied into the runtime Deliverable__c's Name at enrollment,
    so this is the text candidates see in their portal task list.

Type__c (Type) [Picklist]
    The KIND of artifact expected: Video_URL | File | URL | Text |
    Checkbox | Image. Drives which input widget the candidate portal
    renders for the deliverable (a link box, a file upload, free text, a
    tick box...) and how the AWS AI engine treats the submission.

Schema_JSON__c (Schema JSON) [LongTextArea]
    A JSON configuration blob refining the deliverable's expected
    input/validation beyond the simple Type (field structure, constraints,
    evaluation hints for the AI engine). Written by the authoring wizard.
    (Exact schema contract not fully documented - verify with team.)

--- GROUP C: DEADLINE & REQUIREDNESS -----------------------------------------

Days_To_Complete__c (Days To Complete) [Number]
    How many days AFTER the step runs the candidate has to submit this
    deliverable. Copied onto the runtime Deliverable__c; the slot-booking
    Apex computes the deliverable's due dates as step date + this number
    (in IST and in the candidate's own time zone), and the nightly
    LockOverdueDeliverables job locks submissions past that deadline.

Is_Required__c (Is Required) [Checkbox]
    Whether the deliverable is mandatory for completing the step. Copied
    to the runtime Deliverable__c's own Is_Required flag at enrollment.

--- GROUP D: HOUSEKEEPING KEYS -----------------------------------------------

Key__c (Key) [AutoNumber]
    A second auto-number (besides the record Name) giving each definition
    a stable short identifier. (Why both exist is not fully documented -
    verify with team; likely an external-reference key for the AWS
    package.)

Lookup_Key__c (Lookup Key) [Text]
    Technical matching key written by the authoring wizards, pairing the
    definition with its step template while the Update_Program_Version
    flow loops/clones records. Not meant for human use.

9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 0 - including deleted rows (queried with --all-rows). No
  type or requiredness distributions can be reported.
- Ghost evidence of past data: 3,251 of 3,252 Deliverable__c records carry
  a Definitions__c ID (object prefix a15) that no longer resolves to any
  record; deliverables created through 2026-08-03 were still being linked
  to live definitions. The definitions were therefore deleted and purged
  between 2026-08-03 and this snapshot.
- Practical consequences until definitions are recreated: new enrollments
  create steps but NO deliverables; Update_Program_Version finds nothing
  to clone; Deliverable__r.Definitions__r traversals return null on all
  existing data. (Verify with team - this looks like an accidental or
  transitional deletion, not a designed state.)

================================================================================

================================================================================
OBJECT: Deliverable__c  (Label: "Deliverable")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Deliverable__c is ONE piece of work a candidate must produce during a training
program - a recording, a file upload, a document, an exercise. It belongs to a
training step (module) of a candidate's enrollment, e.g. "Niche Fundamentals
Recording" on the "Niche Fundamentals" step of the candidate's Java program.
One candidate enrollment generates its own copy of every deliverable defined
in the program's step templates, so two candidates in the same program have
separate Deliverable__c records.

The record is the workflow backbone of candidate homework: it opens (Active)
when the related training session completes, carries a due date in both IST
and the candidate's own timezone, gets Locked by an hourly job when the due
date passes, supports an extension request/approval loop between candidate and
trainer, tracks every submission attempt (child Deliverable_Result__c rows),
and stores the latest AI grade/feedback that the external AWS grading engine
computed for the most recent submission.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Training/LMS domain.
- MASTER-DETAIL CHILD OF CandidateTrainingStep__c via Candidate_Training_Step__c:
  every deliverable MUST belong to a training step. Sharing is "Controlled By
  Parent" (internal and external) - visibility follows the step, which follows
  the training, which follows the candidate (Person Account).
- 21 custom fields, 0 record types, 1 validation rule, 1 list view.
- Name is plain TEXT ("Deliverable Name"), not auto-number - it carries the
  template's label, e.g. "Niche Fundamentals Recording".
- Field history tracking is enabled on the object.
- Scale: ~3,252 records in preprod, all created between May and Aug 2026 -
  the training/LMS module is new.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. All deliverables are the same shape; the Definitions__c template link
and its Type__c (Video_URL / File / URL / Text / Checkbox / Image) carry the
"what kind of deliverable" signal instead.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - GENERATED AT ENROLLMENT. When a coordinator runs the
  Candidate_Training_Creation screen flow to enroll a candidate, the flow
  builds the whole training skeleton: the Candidate_Training__c record, one
  CandidateTrainingStep__c per step template, sessions, and ONE Deliverable__c
  per Step_Deliverable_Definition__c template on each step. Each deliverable
  is created with Status "Not Active", Name = the template's label,
  Is_Required and Approval_Required = true, Days_To_Complete copied from the
  template, and links to the step, the training and the template. The flow
  then sends the whole structure (steps + deliverable ids/names) to AWS via
  the AWSTrainingIntegration Apex action so the external side (S3 folders,
  AI grading assistant) is provisioned with matching ids.

STEP 2 - DUE DATES ARE COMPUTED. When the candidate books a session window in
  the candidate portal, CandidatePortalController sets each step's start date
  and recomputes each deliverable's due date = step start date +
  Days_To_Complete. It writes the same deadline three ways: Due_Date_IST__c
  (text, IST wall time), Due_Date_Candidate_Time_Zone__c (text, the
  candidate's local wall time) and Due_Date_Sort__c (a real DateTime at
  18:30 GMT = midnight IST, used for sorting and the overdue sweep).

STEP 3 - ACTIVATION ON SESSION COMPLETION. Deliverables stay "Not Active"
  until the training session for their step is actually held. When a
  Session__c is marked Completed, the Session_Complete_Activate_Deliverables
  flow flips that step's Not Active deliverables to Active, stamps the
  completed session into Linked_Session__c, and emails the candidate that
  their assignment is open. The SessionCompletionAttendeeTrigger closes a gap
  for GROUP sessions: the flow only handles the step of the candidate who
  booked the session, so the trigger walks the Session_Attendee__c roster and
  activates every other attendee's step deliverables too.

STEP 4 - THE CANDIDATE SUBMITS (PORTAL + S3). In the candidate portal (custom
  token auth, not standard users), the candidate uploads their work. The LWC
  calls CandidatePortalController -> DeliverableActionService, which:
  (a) creates a child Deliverable_Result__c with Result Status "Pending",
  (b) asks AWS for a pre-signed S3 upload URL (Named Credential
      AWS_Candidate_API), renaming the file to
      "<Deliverable Name>-(<Result Id>).<ext>" so every S3 object is traceable
      to one attempt, (c) after the browser uploads to S3, flips the
      deliverable to Submitted, stamps Submitted_At__c and increments
      Attempt_Count__c. Cancelled/failed uploads leave a reusable Pending
      result row; a cleanup method deletes it and heals the attempt count.

STEP 5 - AI GRADING COMES BACK. The AWS Lambda grades the submission and
  calls back into Salesforce via the REST endpoint
  /services/apexrest/v1/deliverable-result/ (DeliverableResultRest): it writes
  Pass/Fail + score + composed feedback on the result row and cascades the
  parent deliverable's Status (Pass -> Approved, Fail -> Failed). The
  Deliverable_result_roll_up_status flow then copies the newest result's
  score/feedback up into AI_Latest_Score__c / Latest_AI_Feedback__c so the
  parent record always shows the latest grade. A Failed deliverable is open
  for resubmission until the due date passes (max seen: 43 attempts).

STEP 6 - OVERDUE LOCKING. The scheduled Apex job LockOverdueDeliverables runs
  HOURLY and flips past-due Active / Failed (and defensively "Rejected")
  deliverables to Locked. Since June 2026 it computes the real deadline in
  the CANDIDATE'S timezone (training's Time_Zone__c + end-time picklists,
  DST-aware) instead of the legacy 18:30-GMT Due_Date_Sort__c, which used to
  lock US candidates 4-5 hours early. Submitted/Approved records are never
  auto-locked. A Locked deliverable can no longer be submitted - the portal
  shows the "Request extension" path instead.

STEP 7 - EXTENSION REQUEST LOOP. A candidate with a locked or past-due
  deliverable clicks Request Extension in the portal: DeliverableActionService
  sets Extension_Requested__c + Extension_Requested_At__c (one open request at
  a time). The Extension_Requested_Notify_Trainer flow emails the training's
  assigned trainer with the candidate/program/step/due-date details and an
  "open in AIC Portal" pointer. The trainer opens the deliverable record and
  clicks the "Review Extension Request" quick action (screen flow
  Review_Extension_Request) to APPROVE - which writes a new due date into the
  three due-date fields, clears the flag and reopens the deliverable - or
  REJECT.

STEP 8 - DROP-OUT. If the parent Candidate_Training__c is set to Dropped, the
  Candidate_Training_Dropped_Cascade flow marks the candidate's not-yet-done
  deliverables Dropped. All portal actions (submit, resubmit, extension) are
  hard-blocked for dropped deliverables/trainings by Apex checks.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- CandidateTrainingStep__c (via Candidate_Training_Step__c, MASTER-DETAIL,
  required). The training step/module this work item belongs to. Sharing and
  deletion cascade from the step. The candidate portal groups deliverables
  under their step, and the step's start date drives the due date.

LOOKUPS FROM DELIVERABLE TO OTHER OBJECTS:
- Candidate_Training__c (Candidate_Training__c): the candidate's enrollment -
  a denormalized shortcut past the step so code/flows can filter one
  candidate's deliverables in one hop (populated on ~100% of records). Its
  Time_Zone__c / end-time fields drive the locking job, and its Status =
  Dropped blocks all candidate actions.
- Step_Deliverable_Definition__c (Definitions__c, label "Definition"): the
  program template this deliverable was stamped from (~100% populated).
  Source of the Name, Days_To_Complete and the Type (File/Video_URL/...).
- Session__c (Linked_Session__c): the completed training session that
  activated this deliverable - stamped by the
  Session_Complete_Activate_Deliverables flow (41% populated; empty for
  deliverables not yet activated).
- User (Submitted_By__c): intended "who submitted" audit - in practice ALWAYS
  EMPTY (candidates are not Salesforce users; the portal's custom-token auth
  writes Submitted_At but never this field).
- User (Approved_By__c): intended approving trainer. The creation flow tries
  to pre-fill it with the training's assigned trainer user, but in practice
  it is EMPTY on all records (the source field is not populated).

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT DELIVERABLE (children):
- Deliverable_Result__c (MASTER-DETAIL child): one row per submission
  attempt, with the AI verdict/score/feedback. See its own section below.

REPORTING: the custom report type "Trainings with Deliverables" joins
Candidate_Training__c -> Deliverable__c for trainer/ops reporting.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules, all active)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Prevent_Past_Approval_Date: "The Approved At date and time cannot be in the
  past." Fires when Approved_At__c is filled or changed (on create or edit) to
  a date before today - it stops backdated approvals, so the approval
  timestamp always reflects when the approval really happened.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOWS (active, on Deliverable__c):
- Update_Deliverable_Approverd_At (before save, create+update, entry on
  Status__c): stamps Approved_At__c when the status becomes Approved (note
  the typo "Approverd" in the flow name).
- Extension_Requested_Notify_Trainer (after save, create+update): when
  Extension_Requested__c flips true, looks up the training/step/program/
  trainer and emails the assigned trainer the extension request details.

FLOWS ON OTHER OBJECTS THAT WRITE DELIVERABLES:
- Candidate_Training_Creation (screen flow): creates the deliverables at
  enrollment (see process step 1).
- Session_Complete_Activate_Deliverables (on Session__c update): activates a
  completed session's step deliverables, sets Linked_Session__c, emails the
  candidate.
- Deliverable_result_roll_up_status (on Deliverable_Result__c): rolls the
  latest AI score/feedback/status up onto the parent deliverable.
- Candidate_Training_Dropped_Cascade (on Candidate_Training__c): marks the
  deliverables Dropped when the training is dropped.
- Review_Extension_Request (screen flow behind the quick action): trainer
  approves (new due date, reopen) or rejects an extension request.
- Display_Deliverable (screen flow): read-only helper that lists a
  training's deliverables.

APEX TRIGGER (on Session__c, not on Deliverable itself):
- SessionCompletionAttendeeTrigger: on session completion, activates the
  "Not Active" deliverables of every group-session attendee's step (the flow
  above only covers the booking candidate's step).

SCHEDULED APEX:
- LockOverdueDeliverables (hourly, "Lock Overdue Deliverables Hourly"): flips
  past-due Active/Failed/(Rejected) deliverables to Locked, computing the
  deadline in the candidate's own timezone with a legacy Due_Date_Sort__c
  fallback. Deliberately never touches Submitted/Approved/Locked/Not Active.

APEX SERVICES (candidate portal, custom token auth):
- DeliverableActionService: submit / S3 upload URL / finalize / discard /
  request extension / attempt history - the only writer of Submitted_At__c,
  Attempt_Count__c, Extension_Requested__c/_At__c and the Submitted status.
- CandidatePortalController: thin auth wrapper over the service; also
  recomputes the three due-date fields when the candidate books a session
  window.
- DashboardService + PortalHelpers: read-only; build the portal Overview tab
  and map raw Status__c values to the portal buckets (Inprogress->active,
  Pending->submitted, Completed->approved, Not Active->upcoming, plus an
  automatic "locked" for past-due submittable rows).
- TrainerEmailService: legacy extension email path, superseded by the
  Extension_Requested_Notify_Trainer flow (kept but no longer called for
  extensions to avoid double emails).
- AWSTrainingIntegration: sends the training structure incl. deliverable ids
  and names to AWS at enrollment.

EXTERNAL WRITER: the AWS grading Lambda updates the parent Status__c
(Approved/Failed) through the DeliverableResultRest endpoint - see the
Deliverable_Result__c section.

BUTTON ON THE PAGE: "Review Extension Request" quick action (Flow type) on
the Deliverable_Record_Page Lightning page and the classic Deliverable
Layout.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 21 + Name, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: IDENTITY & WHERE IT BELONGS -------------------------------------

Name (Deliverable Name) [Text]
    The deliverable's title, copied from the template's Label at enrollment
    (e.g. "Niche Fundamentals Recording"). Plain text, not auto-number. Also
    used to build the trainer-friendly S3 filename of every submission.

Candidate_Training_Step__c (Candidate Training Step) [Master-Detail ->
CandidateTrainingStep__c]
    THE required parent link: which training step/module this work item is
    part of. Set once by the Candidate_Training_Creation flow and never
    changed. Sharing and deletes cascade from the step; the session-completion
    automation finds deliverables to activate through this field.

Candidate_Training__c (Candidate Training) [Lookup -> Candidate_Training__c]
    Shortcut to the candidate's enrollment (populated on ~100% of records;
    1 legacy record is missing it). Every portal query filters on
    Candidate_Training__r.Candidate__c to enforce "you only see your own
    work". Its timezone/end-time fields drive the hourly locking job, and its
    Dropped status blocks all candidate actions.

Definitions__c (Definition) [Lookup -> Step_Deliverable_Definition__c]
    The program-template row this deliverable was generated from (~100%
    populated). The template supplies the Name, Days_To_Complete, whether it
    is required, and the deliverable Type (Video_URL | File | URL | Text |
    Checkbox | Image) that the portal uses to render the right input.

Linked_Session__c (Linked Session) [Lookup -> Session__c]
    The completed training session that opened this deliverable - stamped by
    the Session_Complete_Activate_Deliverables flow at activation time (41%
    populated; blank means the step's session has not completed yet, or the
    record was activated by the group-attendee trigger which does not stamp
    it).

--- GROUP B: REQUIREMENTS & PLANNING -----------------------------------------

Is_Required__c (Is Required) [Checkbox]
    Whether the candidate must complete this deliverable to progress. The
    creation flow currently hard-codes it TRUE for every record (true on
    3,251 of 3,252), so in practice all deliverables are mandatory; the flag
    exists so optional deliverables can be introduced later.

Approval_Required__c (Approval Required) [Checkbox]
    Whether the submission needs a pass verdict before the deliverable can
    complete. Also hard-coded TRUE at creation on every record. Today the
    "approval" is the AI grade (plus optional trainer review); no automation
    branches on this flag yet (not fully documented - verify with team).

Days_To_Complete__c (Days To Complete) [Number]
    How many days after the step starts the candidate has to finish, copied
    from the template at enrollment (69% populated). Due date = step start
    date + this number; blank means no due date was ever computed (the
    candidate has not booked a session window).

Notes__c (Notes) [LongTextArea]
    Free-form notes about this deliverable (instructions, trainer remarks).
    Manual entry; no automation writes or reads it.

--- GROUP C: LIFECYCLE STATUS ------------------------------------------------

Status__c (Status) [Picklist, restricted]
    THE state machine of the deliverable. Values and meaning:
    - "Not Active" (27% of records): created but the step's session has not
      completed yet - hidden as "upcoming" in the portal.
    - "Active" (5 records right now): open for submission. Transient - most
      records move on quickly or were seeded differently.
    - "Inprogress" (24%): treated by all portal code as a synonym of Active
      (open for submission). Which process writes "Inprogress" instead of
      "Active" is not fully documented - verify with team.
    - "Submitted" (8 right now): candidate uploaded, AI verdict pending.
      Never auto-locked.
    - "Approved" (37%): latest attempt passed (set by the AWS callback /
      roll-up flow, or trainer). Terminal success state.
    - "Failed" (1 right now): latest attempt failed; the candidate may
      resubmit until the due date, after which the hourly job locks it.
    - "Locked" (3.4%): due date passed without an accepted submission - the
      candidate can only request an extension.
    - "Dropped" (1.2%): candidate was dropped from the training (cascade
      flow); all actions blocked.
    - "Completed" (6.5%): DEACTIVATED legacy value still present on old
      records; the portal maps it to "approved".
    - "Pending": active picklist value with ZERO records - unused.
    Writers: creation flow (Not Active), session-completion flow + trigger
    (Active), portal Apex (Submitted), AWS REST callback + roll-up flow
    (Approved/Failed), hourly job (Locked), dropped-cascade flow (Dropped),
    Review_Extension_Request flow (back to open after an approved extension).

--- GROUP D: DUE DATES & LOCKING ---------------------------------------------

Due_Date_IST__c (Due Date IST) [Text]
    The deadline as an IST wall-clock string, e.g. "7/21/2026 04:30 PM" -
    what the India-based trainers read. Computed at enrollment and recomputed
    when the candidate books a session window (step start +
    Days_To_Complete + the training's IST end time); rewritten by the
    Review_Extension_Request flow when an extension is approved. 69%
    populated. Text on purpose - it is display data, not a sortable date.

Due_Date_Candidate_Time_Zone__c (Due Date Candidate Time Zone) [Text]
    The same deadline in the CANDIDATE'S own timezone (e.g. "7/21/2026
    06:00 AM" for a US-Pacific candidate) - what the candidate portal shows.
    Written by the same three writers as Due_Date_IST__c. 69% populated.

Due_Date_Sort__c (Due Date Sort) [DateTime]
    The machine-usable deadline: the due date at 18:30 GMT (= midnight IST).
    Used for sorting lists, the portal's "past due -> show as locked" check,
    and as the query window / legacy fallback of the hourly locking job. The
    job's June 2026 fix computes the REAL deadline from the candidate's
    timezone and only falls back to this field when timezone data is missing
    (its date part is correct, its hour is not). 65% populated.

--- GROUP E: SUBMISSION TRACKING ---------------------------------------------

Submitted_At__c (Submitted At) [DateTime]
    When the candidate last submitted (stamped by DeliverableActionService at
    each successful submit/finalize). 39% of deliverables have ever been
    submitted.

Submitted_By__c (Submitted By) [Lookup -> User]
    Intended submitter audit field - NEVER POPULATED in practice (0 records).
    Candidates use the custom token portal and are not Salesforce users, so
    the code stamps only Submitted_At__c.

Attempt_Count__c (Attempt Count) [Number]
    How many times the candidate has submitted this deliverable, incremented
    by the portal Apex on every finalized submission (and self-healed
    downward if an upload is cancelled). Populated on 1,267 records: 712 have
    exactly 1 attempt, 555 have more than one, and the maximum seen is 43 -
    resubmission after a Fail verdict is very common.

--- GROUP F: LATEST AI GRADE (ROLL-UP FROM RESULTS) --------------------------

AI_Latest_Score__c (AI Latest Score) [Text]
    The AI score of the NEWEST submission, copied up from the child
    Deliverable_Result__c by the Deliverable_result_roll_up_status flow (32%
    populated). Text (length 20), so treat it as display data; the numeric
    source of truth is AI_Score__c on the result rows.

Latest_AI_Feedback__c (Latest AI Feedback) [LongTextArea]
    The AI's written feedback for the newest submission (reasoning +
    "Positives:"/"Negatives:" bullet lists composed by the AWS callback),
    rolled up by the same flow so trainers see the latest critique without
    opening the child record.

--- GROUP G: APPROVAL --------------------------------------------------------

Approved_At__c (Approved At) [DateTime]
    When the deliverable reached Approved - stamped automatically by the
    Update_Deliverable_Approverd_At flow when the status becomes Approved
    (6.5% populated; roughly one per five Approved records because the flow
    postdates much of the data). Guarded by the only validation rule: it can
    never be set to a past date.

Approved_By__c (Approved By) [Lookup -> User]
    The approving trainer. The enrollment flow tries to prefill it with the
    training's assigned trainer user, but it is EMPTY on all records today -
    the source field on the training is not populated. Treat as reserved for
    a future trainer-review step (verify with team).

--- GROUP H: EXTENSION WORKFLOW ----------------------------------------------

Extension_Requested__c (Extension Requested) [Checkbox]
    TRUE while the candidate has an OPEN extension request (only one at a
    time is allowed). Set by the portal (DeliverableActionService) for locked
    or past-due deliverables; firing it triggers the trainer email flow.
    Cleared when the trainer resolves the request via the Review Extension
    Request button. Currently true on 16 records.

Extension_Requested_At__c (Extension Requested At) [DateTime]
    When the candidate asked for the extension - stamped together with the
    flag, but NOT cleared on resolution, so it doubles as a "has ever asked"
    audit: 272 deliverables (8.4%) have had an extension requested at some
    point.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 3,252, created 2026-05-08 to 2026-08-03 - the training/LMS
  module went live in May 2026.
- Status: Approved 1,210 (37%) | Not Active 879 (27%) | Inprogress 787 (24%)
  | Completed 210 (6.5%, deactivated legacy value) | Locked 112 (3.4%) |
  Dropped 39 | Submitted 8 | Active 5 | Failed 1 | blank 1.
- Population: Candidate_Training__c and Definitions__c ~100%; due-date trio
  Due_Date_IST / Candidate_Time_Zone / Days_To_Complete 2,252 (69%);
  Due_Date_Sort__c 2,102 (65%); Linked_Session__c 1,327 (41%);
  Submitted_At__c and Attempt_Count__c 1,267 (39%); AI_Latest_Score__c 1,035
  (32%); Approved_At__c 211 (6.5%); Extension_Requested_At__c 272 (8.4%).
- Checkboxes: Is_Required__c and Approval_Required__c true on 3,251 of 3,252
  (hard-coded true at creation); Extension_Requested__c currently true on 16.
- Attempts: 712 deliverables have exactly 1 attempt, 555 have 2+, max 43 -
  candidates commonly retry after a Fail verdict.
- Never used: Submitted_By__c (0), Approved_By__c (0), Status value
  "Pending" (0 records).
- Key takeaway: about a third of all deliverables end Approved; the
  Locked-then-extension path is a real but small tail (~3% locked right now,
  ~8% have ever requested an extension).

================================================================================
OBJECT: Deliverable_Result__c  (Label: "Deliverable Result")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Deliverable_Result__c is ONE SUBMISSION ATTEMPT of a training deliverable and
its grade. Every time a candidate uploads work for a Deliverable__c, a new
result row is created (auto-number DR-XXXXXX); the external AWS AI grading
engine then writes its verdict (Pass/Fail), a 0-100 score, and written
feedback back onto that same row. A deliverable with 5 attempts has 5 result
rows - together they are the candidate's full submission history, which the
candidate portal shows as "previous attempts" and trainers read as the audit
trail behind the parent's latest score.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Training/LMS domain.
- MASTER-DETAIL CHILD OF Deliverable__c via Deliverable__c: every result MUST
  belong to a deliverable. Sharing is "Controlled By Parent" - visibility
  cascades Deliverable -> Step -> Training -> Candidate.
- 6 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Auto-number Name in the format DR-XXXXXX.
- Scale: ~2,532 records in preprod (Jun-Jul 2026 data window).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every submission attempt is the same shape.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATED AT SUBMISSION TIME (BY APEX, NOT BY USERS). When the
  candidate submits work in the candidate portal, DeliverableActionService
  creates the result row FIRST, with Result_Status__c = "Pending" and
  Submitted_At__c = now, BEFORE the file goes anywhere. The new row's Id is
  baked into the S3 filename ("<Deliverable Name>-(<Result Id>).<ext>"), so
  every file in the S3 bucket is traceable to exactly one attempt. If an
  upload is cancelled or dies mid-flight, the Pending row is either deleted
  (discardPendingResult) or REUSED on the next try - a lingering Pending row
  under a still-open deliverable means "candidate started a submission but
  never completed it".

STEP 2 - AWS GRADES AND CALLS BACK. The AWS Lambda analyses the uploaded file
  and POSTs its verdict to the inbound REST endpoint
  /services/apexrest/v1/deliverable-result/ (Apex class DeliverableResultRest,
  runs without sharing). The payload carries the result Id, a PASS/FAIL/
  PENDING verdict, an optional 0-100 score, and reasoning plus positives/
  negatives bullet lists. The endpoint normalises the verdict to Pass/Fail/
  Pending, writes AI_Score__c, and composes AI_Feedback__c from the reasoning
  and bullet lists (or takes a pre-built "feedback" string verbatim). Auth:
  OAuth client-credentials via the "AWS Result Callback" external client app,
  running as the "Salesforce API Only System Integrations" user.

STEP 3 - THE VERDICT CASCADES TO THE PARENT. Two mechanisms keep the parent
  deliverable in sync (belt and braces):
  - DeliverableResultRest itself updates the parent Status (Pass -> Approved,
    Fail -> Failed, Pending -> unchanged).
  - The record-triggered flow Deliverable_result_roll_up_status also copies
    the newest result's AI_Score__c / AI_Feedback__c into the parent's
    AI_Latest_Score__c / Latest_AI_Feedback__c and maintains parent status /
    Approved_At.
  A Fail sends the candidate back to resubmit (a NEW result row); a Pass ends
  the loop.

STEP 4 - READ BACK AS HISTORY. The portal's attempt-history panel
  (DeliverableActionService.getDeliverableHistory) lists all result rows for
  a deliverable, newest first, with status, score, feedback and submitted
  time. DashboardService also counts Pending rows so a candidate whose
  finalize step failed still sees the item as "submitted".

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Deliverable__c (via Deliverable__c, MASTER-DETAIL, required, 100%
  populated). The work item this attempt was submitted against. The parent
  aggregates this object: latest score/feedback roll up onto it, and its
  Attempt_Count__c mirrors how many real attempts exist here.

No other objects point at Deliverable_Result__c, and it has no other lookups.
The uploaded file itself lives in AWS S3 (named after this record's Id), NOT
in Salesforce Files - there is no ContentDocument link.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Integrity is enforced in Apex instead: the portal only creates results
for the candidate's own open deliverables, blocks a second submission while
one is Pending review, and never deletes a graded (Pass/Fail) row.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOW (active):
- Deliverable_result_roll_up_status (after save, create+update): when a
  result is created or its verdict changes, updates the parent Deliverable's
  Status / AI_Latest_Score__c / Latest_AI_Feedback__c / Approved_At__c from
  the newest result.

APEX WRITERS:
- DeliverableActionService (candidate portal): creates the Pending row at
  submission (createPendingResult / legacy submitDeliverable), reuses or
  deletes orphaned Pending rows (discardPendingResult), and reads the
  attempt history. All DML in SYSTEM_MODE because portal candidates are not
  standard users.
- DeliverableResultRest (@RestResource /v1/deliverable-result/*): the AWS
  grading callback - writes Result_Status__c, AI_Score__c, AI_Feedback__c and
  cascades the parent status. This is the ONLY writer of the grade fields;
  no flow or user edits them.

There are no scheduled jobs, quick actions, or screen flows on this object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 6 + Name, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: LINK & TIMING ---------------------------------------------------

Name (Deliverable Result Name) [AutoNumber DR-{000000}]
    System-generated attempt number, e.g. DR-001234. Shown in the portal's
    attempt history and embedded (as the record Id, not this number) in the
    S3 filename.

Deliverable__c (Deliverable) [Master-Detail -> Deliverable__c]
    THE required parent link: which deliverable this attempt belongs to.
    100% populated; set once at creation by the portal Apex and never
    changed. Sharing and deletes cascade from the deliverable.

Submitted_At__c (Submitted At) [DateTime]
    When the candidate made (or retried) this submission - stamped by the
    portal Apex at creation and refreshed if an orphaned Pending row is
    reused for a retry, so trainers see the real latest attempt time. 100%
    populated.

--- GROUP B: THE AI VERDICT --------------------------------------------------

Result_Status__c (Result Status) [Picklist, restricted: Pass | Fail | Pending]
    The attempt's verdict. Created as "Pending" (submitted, awaiting the AI);
    the AWS callback flips it to "Pass" or "Fail". Pass approves the parent
    deliverable, Fail sends it to Failed/resubmission, Pending leaves the
    parent untouched. Graded rows are never deleted or reverted. Live data:
    Fail 1,315 (52%) | Pass 1,209 (48%) | Pending 8.

AI_Score__c (AI Score) [Number (7,2)]
    The AI engine's 0-100 quality score for this attempt, written by the AWS
    callback (99.7% populated; average 75.8, observed range 0-97). The newest
    score is rolled up to the parent's AI_Latest_Score__c. There is no
    stored pass mark in Salesforce - the pass/fail cut is decided on the AWS
    side (see Threshold_Score__c below).

AI_Feedback__c (AI Feedback) [LongTextArea]
    The AI's written critique of this attempt: overall reasoning followed by
    "Positives:" and "Negatives:" bullet lists, composed by
    DeliverableResultRest from the AWS payload (or taken verbatim if AWS
    sends a pre-built feedback string). Shown to the candidate in the portal
    attempt history and rolled up to the parent for trainers.

Threshold_Score__c (Threshold Score) [Text]
    Intended to record the pass-mark the score was judged against - NEVER
    POPULATED in practice (0 of 2,532 records; the REST endpoint does not
    write it). The threshold lives only in the AWS engine today. (Not fully
    documented - verify with team.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 2,532, created 2026-06-05 to 2026-07-12 (grading went live
  about a month after the deliverables themselves).
- Verdicts: Fail 1,315 (52%) | Pass 1,209 (48%) | Pending 8 (0.3%). Roughly
  half of all attempts fail - which matches the heavy resubmission pattern on
  the parent (max 43 attempts on one deliverable).
- AI_Score__c populated on 2,524 (99.7%); average 75.8, min 0, max 97.
- Submitted_At__c populated on 100%.
- Never used: Threshold_Score__c (0 records).
- Ratio check: 2,532 results vs 1,267 deliverables ever submitted = exactly
  2.0 attempts per submitted deliverable on average.
- Key takeaway: this object is written almost entirely by machines (portal
  Apex + AWS callback); treat any manual edit of a result row as suspect.
================================================================================

================================================================================
OBJECT: Session__c  (Label: "Session")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Session__c is the GENERIC SCHEDULED-MEETING object of the org - one record =
one real meeting on a calendar, backed by a Zoom meeting and a Google Calendar
event created through an external scheduling service. It is deliberately
multi-purpose: the same object books a training class, an internal screening
interview call, a welcome call, a resume-understanding session, a marketing
initial call, or a background-check call. The Purpose__c picklist says what
kind of meeting it is, and a set of polymorphic lookups (Candidate Training,
Internal Interview, Interview, Onboarding, Background Check, Lead) points at
WHATEVER the meeting is about. The host and extra attendees are always
Techsara employees (Recruiter__c records); the candidate side is the linked
Person Account.

Do not confuse Session__c with Interview__c (the candidate's interview with an
outside company) or Internal_Interview__c (the screening assessment record) -
a Session is just the MEETING wrapper: date, time slot, timezone, Zoom link,
calendar event, and completion status. Internal interviews and training steps
each get a Session as their concrete calendar booking.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, shared by the Training/LMS layer and the internal-interview
  layer (it sits in both the Techsara Solutions and Training Module apps).
- Standalone object with its own owner. Org-wide sharing is Public Read/Write
  ("ReadWrite") - anyone who can see the object can see and edit all sessions.
- 38 custom fields, 0 record types, 1 validation rule, 2 list views
  ("All" and "QA Background Check Queue").
- Auto-number Name in the format SES-XXXXXX (label "Session id").
- Scale: only 47 records in preprod (created 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-06;
  session dates run 2026-07-26 to 2026-08-28). The subsystem is newly live.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The object has no record types - the Purpose__c picklist is what
differentiates the meeting flavors instead.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATION. Sessions are created from several entry points, almost
  never from the raw "New" button:
  - "Schedule Session" button on an Interview__c record (screen flow
    Schedule_Session_From_Interview): the employee picks one of the
    candidate's active trainings, then books host, date, slot, timezone,
    duration and purpose in the Calendly-style sessionScheduler LWC.
  - "Schedule Session" button on a Candidate_Training__c record (screen flow
    Schedule_Session_From_Training): same scheduler, training already known.
  - "Create Session" button on a Background_Check__c record (screen flow
    Background_Check_Session_Creation): books the background-check call and
    links the session to the Background Check record.
  - CANDIDATE PORTAL SLOT BOOKING (Apex CandidatePortalController
    .bookSessionWindow): when the FIRST candidate of a cohort books a
    Session_Window__c slot, the code auto-creates one Session per training
    step (Status "Unscheduled", Purpose "Training", host = the window's
    trainer). Later candidates who book the same cohort do NOT get new
    Sessions - they get Session_Attendee__c rows on the existing "master"
    sessions (see that object).
  - The admin-side "Book Session Slot" action on Candidate Training
    (AdminSessionAssignmentController) does the same booking on behalf of a
    candidate, bypassing the portal's status/capacity filters.
  - The Internal Interview "Conduct Interview" flow also creates/updates the
    session that carries an internal screening call.

STEP 2 - MEETING CREATION CALLOUT. When a session reaches the right status,
  the record-triggered Session_Scheduling_Callout_Flow calls the external
  scheduling service (external service "CreateInterview" through the
  Zoom_Scheduler named credential - an AWS endpoint that creates the Zoom
  meeting and calendar entry). The callout response is written back onto the
  session: Meeting_Link__c, External_Meeting_ID__c,
  External_Meeting_Passcode__c, calendar_event_id__c, calendar_link__c, and
  the IST-converted start/end times. 45 of 47 records carry a meeting link,
  so this integration runs on virtually every session.

STEP 3 - SALESFORCE CALENDAR EVENT. The Session_To_Calendar_Event flow owns a
  native Salesforce Event for each session: on create or whenever status,
  date, times, timezone or host change, it deletes the old Event and, if the
  session is Scheduled with all fields present, creates a fresh Event for the
  host. Times are converted from the candidate-chosen timezone to UTC (US
  DST approximated by a March-October month check); IST times are put in the
  Event description for the India-based team.

STEP 4 - STATUS LIFECYCLE. Status__c runs Unscheduled -> Scheduled ->
  Completed (or Rescheduled / Cancelled). For internal-interview sessions,
  scheduling the session auto-moves the linked Internal_Interview__c from
  Unscheduled to Scheduled (internal_interview_Status_Update flow) and copies
  the IST times onto it.

STEP 5 - COMPLETION SIDE EFFECTS. Marking a session Completed requires Host
  Feedback (validation rule). Completion then:
  - activates the deliverables of the session's training step and emails the
    candidate (Session_Complete_Activate_Deliverables flow), and
  - activates the deliverables of every OTHER candidate attending via
    Session_Attendee__c rows (Apex SessionCompletionAttendeeTrigger - the
    flow only covers the first/master candidate).
  If the whole training is dropped, the Candidate_Training_Dropped_Cascade
  flow sweeps the training's remaining sessions along with its steps and
  deliverables.

STEP 6 - CONSUMPTION. The candidate portal's "Sessions" tab (sessions /
  sessionCard LWCs fed by DashboardService) shows the candidate their own
  sessions plus any shared cohort sessions they attend, with the meeting
  link and times in their own timezone. Internally, the Session record page
  has a "View Recording" button (Recording_Link_Logs_Flow) that opens
  Recording_URL__c and writes a Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c compliance row.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
"WHAT IS THIS MEETING ABOUT" LOOKUPS (polymorphic by Purpose):
- Account (Candidate__c): the candidate the meeting is for. 100% populated -
  every session so far belongs to a candidate Person Account.
- Candidate_Training__c (Candidate_Training__c): the training enrollment a
  Training-purpose session belongs to (38/47 records).
- CandidateTrainingStep__c (Candidate_Training_Step__c): the exact step of
  the training curriculum this session teaches (38/47). Completion of the
  session activates this step's deliverables.
- Internal_Interview__c (Internal_Interview__c): the internal screening
  interview this session is the call for (9/47). Bidirectional pair -
  Internal_Interview__c also has its own Session__c lookup back.
- Interview__c (Interview__c): the external interview a prep session was
  booked around, set by the Schedule Session button on Interview (0 records
  so far).
- Onboarding__c (Onboarding__c): onboarding-related sessions such as welcome
  calls (0 records so far).
- Background_Check__c (Background_Check__c): the background-check engagement
  this call belongs to (0 records so far; the Create Session button sets it).
  Background_Check__c also has its own Session__c lookup back.
- Lead (Lead__c): lets a session be booked for a not-yet-converted lead
  (0 records so far).
- Program_Version__c (Program_Version__c): which program version curriculum
  the training session belongs to (38/47).

TECHSARA-SIDE PEOPLE (all Recruiter__c / "Employee"):
- Host_User__c: the employee running the meeting (trainer / interviewer /
  caller). 100% populated. The calendar Event is created for this person.
- Additional_Attendee_1__c / Additional_Attendee_2__c: up to two extra
  employees invited to the meeting (5/47 each) - included in the scheduling
  callout so they get the invite.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT SESSION (children / references):
- Session_Attendee__c (MASTER-DETAIL child, relationship "Attendees"): the
  extra candidates sharing this session in a group/cohort setting.
- Deliverable__c (lookup Linked_Session__c): a deliverable tied to the
  session where it was assigned/discussed.
- Internal_Interview__c (lookup Session__c): the internal interview's link
  back to its scheduled call.
- Background_Check__c (lookup Session__c): the background check's link back
  to its scheduled call.
- Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c (lookup Session__c): who viewed this
  session's recording, when (written by the View Recording button flow).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules, all active)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Require_Host_Feedback_On_Complete: a session cannot be saved with Status
  "Completed" unless Host Feedback is filled in - the trainer/host must
  record the outcome before closing the session. Error shown on the Host
  Feedback field: "Host Feedback is required before marking the session
  Completed."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOWS (active):
- Session_Scheduling_Callout_Flow (after save, create+update, status-gated,
  one scheduled path): calls the external "CreateInterview" scheduling
  service (Zoom_Scheduler named credential -> AWS) to create the Zoom meeting
  and calendar entry, then writes the meeting link, external meeting id,
  passcode, calendar event id/link and IST times back onto the session.
- Session_To_Calendar_Event (after save, create+update): owns the native
  Salesforce Event for the session - deletes any existing linked Event and
  recreates it when the session is Scheduled with all required fields;
  handles timezone conversion and US DST.
- internal_interview_Status_Update (after save, create+update): when an
  Internal-Interview-purpose session gets scheduled, flips the linked
  Internal_Interview__c to "Scheduled" and copies Start/End IST times to it.
- Session_Complete_Activate_Deliverables (after save, update to Completed):
  activates the Deliverable__c records of the session's training step and
  sends the candidate an email.

APEX TRIGGER:
- SessionCompletionAttendeeTrigger (after update): when a session flips to
  Completed, finds all Session_Attendee__c rows and activates each
  attendee's own per-candidate deliverables ("Not Active" -> "Active") -
  the flow above only covers the first candidate who booked; this trigger
  covers the rest of the group.

SCREEN FLOWS / BUTTONS THAT CREATE OR TOUCH SESSIONS:
- Schedule_Session_From_Interview (button on Interview__c) and
  Schedule_Session_From_Training (button on Candidate_Training__c): both use
  the sessionScheduler LWC (a Calendly-style slot picker driven by
  SessionSchedulerController Apex: free-slot computation from the host's
  events, business hours, holidays, durations) and create the Session.
- Background_Check_Session_Creation (button "Create Session" on
  Background_Check__c): creates a Background-Check-purpose session.
- Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview (screen flow): stamps Actual_Start__c
  / Actual_End__c, Host_Feedback__c and Status on the session while the
  internal interview is being conducted.
- Recording_Link_Logs_Flow ("View Recording" button on the Session record
  page and layout): opens the recording and logs the access to
  Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c.
- Candidate_Training_Dropped_Cascade (flow on Candidate_Training__c): when a
  training is dropped, updates the training's open sessions along with steps
  and deliverables.

APEX WRITERS OUTSIDE FLOWS:
- CandidatePortalController.bookSessionWindow (candidate portal): creates the
  per-step "master" sessions for the first candidate who books a cohort slot
  (Status "Unscheduled", Purpose "Training", host = window trainer).
- AdminSessionAssignmentController (admin "Book Session Slot" quick action):
  same booking path run internally on behalf of a candidate.
- DashboardService (candidate portal): read-only - assembles the portal's
  Sessions tab from the candidate's own sessions plus attendee sessions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 38, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHO AND WHAT THE MEETING IS FOR ---------------------------------

Candidate__c (Candidate) [Lookup -> Account]
    The candidate (Person Account) the meeting is for. Set by every creation
    path (screen flows and portal booking). 100% populated - the anchor field
    used by the portal to find "my sessions".

Candidate_Name__c (Candidate Name) [Formula, Text]
    Display name resolved across the polymorphic links: the Candidate's
    First+Last name, else the Lead's name, else the Onboarding's account
    name. Feeds the MeetingTopic formula and the portal session cards.

Candidate_Email__c (Candidate Email) [Formula, Text]
    Same cascade for the email address (Candidate's email replica -> Lead
    email -> Onboarding account email). Read by the scheduling callout flow
    so the meeting invite reaches the candidate.

Candidate_Training__c (Candidate Training) [Lookup -> Candidate_Training__c]
    The training enrollment this session belongs to (Training purpose). Set
    by the Schedule Session flows and the portal booking code. 38/47
    populated - all Training-purpose records.

Candidate_Training_Step__c (Candidate Training Step) [Lookup ->
CandidateTrainingStep__c]
    The specific curriculum step this session covers - one session per step
    in the portal booking model. Completion of the session activates this
    step's deliverables. 38/47 populated.

Program_Version__c (Program Version) [Lookup -> Program_Version__c]
    The program version the training session belongs to - copied from the
    training at creation. 38/47 populated.

Internal_Interview__c (Internal Interview) [Lookup -> Internal_Interview__c]
    The internal screening interview this session is the scheduled call for.
    Scheduling the session auto-updates that interview's status (flow).
    9/47 populated.

Interview__c (Interview) [Lookup -> Interview__c]
    The external Interview__c a prep session was booked around - set by the
    "Schedule Session" button on the Interview page. 0 records so far.

Onboarding__c (Onboarding) [Lookup -> Onboarding__c]
    The onboarding record for onboarding-stage calls (e.g. welcome calls).
    Also a leg of the Candidate_Email/Name formulas. 0 records so far.

Background_Check__c (Background Check) [Lookup -> Background_Check__c]
    The background-check engagement this call belongs to - set by the
    "Create Session" button on Background Check. 0 records so far, but the
    "QA Background Check Queue" list view is built around this purpose.

Lead__c (Lead) [Lookup -> Lead]
    Lets a session be booked for a website Lead before conversion to a
    candidate. 0 records so far.

Purpose__c (Purpose) [Picklist]
    WHAT KIND of meeting this is - the field that replaces record types:
    Training (a training class; 38 of 47 records) | Internal Interview (an
    internal screening call; 9 records) | Welcome Call - Customer Success |
    Resume Understanding Session | Initial Call - Marketing | Background
    Check. The last four values are defined but have no data yet. Set by the
    creating flow/code; the scheduling callout and portal filters read it.

--- GROUP B: TECHSARA-SIDE ATTENDEES -----------------------------------------

Host_User__c (Host User) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c ("Employee")]
    The employee who runs the meeting: the trainer for training sessions, the
    interviewer for internal interviews, the caller for check calls. Set at
    creation (scheduler pick or the Session Window's trainer). 100%
    populated. The Salesforce calendar Event is created for this person, and
    the free-slot computation in the scheduler is based on their calendar.

Additional_Attendee_1__c (Additional Attendee 1) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    An optional second internal attendee - passed to the scheduling callout
    so they are invited to the meeting. The Background Check creation flow
    uses it to add the QA/second person. 5/47 populated.

Additional_Attendee_2__c (Additional Attendee 2) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    An optional third internal attendee, same mechanics. 5/47 populated.

Attendance_status__c (Attendance status) [Multi-Select Picklist]
    Who skipped the meeting: Host Skipped | Attendee Skipped | Attendee 1
    Skipped | Attendee 2 Skippped (typo is in the org). Meant as a manual
    post-meeting attendance note - no automation writes or reads it, and it
    is 0% populated. Effectively unused so far.

--- GROUP C: SCHEDULING (DATE, TIME, TIMEZONE) -------------------------------

Scheduled_Date__c (Date Of Session) [Date]
    The calendar date the meeting takes place. Set by the scheduler/booking
    code (for portal bookings it is derived from the step's start datetime).
    100% populated. Drives the Event creation and portal ordering.

Selected_Time_Zone_Start_Time__c (Selected Time Zone Start Time) [Picklist,
global value set "Times"]
    Meeting start time as a time-slot label (e.g. "10:00 AM") in the chosen
    Time_Zone__c - same shared "Times" value set the Interview object uses.
    Set by the scheduler LWC or copied from the training's candidate-timezone
    times at portal booking. 100% populated. This is the CURRENT start-time
    field; the callout and Event flows convert it to real datetimes.

Selected_Time_Zone_ETim__c (Selected Time Zone End Time) [Picklist, global
value set "Times"]
    Meeting end time in the selected timezone (note the truncated API name
    "ETim"). Same mechanics as the start time. 100% populated.

Time_Zone__c (Time Zone) [Picklist, global value set "Candidate_Time_Zone"]
    The timezone the selected times are quoted in (candidate-facing US zones:
    ET/CT/MT/PT/AT/HT). 100% populated. Data note: "AT (Alaska Time)" is the
    most common value (29 of 47) followed by ET (14) - likely test-data
    skew rather than a real Alaska candidate base.

Scheduled_Start__c (Selected Time Zone  Start  Time) [DateTime]
Scheduled_End__c (Selected Time Zone End Time) [DateTime]
    LEGACY datetime pair with the same labels as the picklists above - 0%
    populated; the picklist + Time_Zone model replaced them. DashboardService
    still ORDER BYs Scheduled_Start__c, which is always null today, so the
    portal effectively shows sessions in fallback order. Do not rely on
    these two fields.

Start_Time_IST__c (Start Time IST) [Text]
End_Time_IST__c (End Time IST) [Text]
    The meeting start/end converted to Indian Standard Time, written back by
    the scheduling callout - what the India-based team reads. Both 100%
    populated. Copied onto the Internal Interview when its session is
    scheduled, and surfaced in the calendar Event description.

Actual_Start__c (Actual Start) [DateTime]
Actual_End__c (Actual End) [DateTime]
    When the meeting REALLY started/ended - stamped by the Internal
    Interview "Conduct Interview" screen flow as the interviewer runs the
    call. Barely populated yet (2 and 1 of 47) and only for internal
    interview sessions; training sessions do not stamp actuals today.

--- GROUP D: MEETING & CALENDAR INTEGRATION ----------------------------------

Meeting_Link__c (Meeting Link) [Url]
    The join URL of the meeting (Zoom), written back by the scheduling
    callout. 45/47 populated. Shown to the candidate in the portal session
    card and inherited by Session_Attendee rows via formula.

External_Meeting_ID__c (External Meeting ID) [Text]
    The Zoom meeting id returned by the scheduling service. 45/47 populated.

External_Meeting_Passcode__c (External Meeting Passcode) [Text]
    The Zoom meeting passcode returned by the scheduling service. 45/47.

calendar_event_id__c (calendar event id) [Text]
    Google Calendar event id returned by the scheduling service - the handle
    used to update/cancel the calendar entry. 45/47 populated.

calendar_link__c (calendar link) [Url]
    Direct link to the Google Calendar event. 45/47 populated.

Create_Meeting_Error__c (Create Meeting Error) [TextArea]
    Error capture slot for a failed meeting-creation callout. No flow or
    Apex in the current metadata writes it and it is 0% populated -
    (not fully documented - verify with team whether the external service
    writes it directly).

MeetingTopic__c (MeetingTopic) [Formula, Text]
    The meeting title: for training sessions "Program name - Step name"
    (e.g. "GenAI Bootcamp - Week 1 Kickoff"), otherwise "Candidate name -
    Purpose" (e.g. "J. Doe - Internal Interview"). Used as the meeting/
    calendar subject and shown on portal cards and attendee rows.

Recording_URL__c (Recording URL) [Url]
    Where the meeting recording lives. Read by the "View Recording" button
    flow (which also logs the access), but nothing populates it yet - 0% in
    data. Expect the Zoom-recording pipeline to fill it as the module goes
    live (not fully documented - verify with team).

URL__c (URL) [LongTextArea]
    Generic long-text URL field. No automation reads or writes it and its
    business meaning is unclear (not fully documented - verify with team).

--- GROUP E: LIFECYCLE & NOTES -----------------------------------------------

Status__c (Status) [Picklist]
    The session lifecycle: Unscheduled (created but not confirmed - the
    portal-created master sessions start here) | Scheduled | Completed |
    Rescheduled | Cancelled | Canceled (duplicate legacy US spelling - the
    team uses "Cancelled"). Data today: Scheduled 45, Cancelled 1,
    Completed 1. Status changes drive ALL the automation: the meeting
    callout, the Event rebuild, the internal-interview sync, and the two
    completion handlers (deliverable activation flow + attendee trigger).
    "Completed" is blocked until Host Feedback is entered (validation rule).

Host_Feedback__c (Host Feedback) [LongTextArea]
    The host's written outcome of the meeting (how the training/interview
    call went). REQUIRED before the session can be marked Completed
    (validation rule). Stamped by the Conduct Interview flow for internal
    interviews, typed manually for training sessions.

Description__c (Description) [LongTextArea]
    Free-form notes about the session, entered on the scheduling screen
    (the Schedule Session flows include a description box). Also copied into
    the calendar Event body.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 47. Created 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-06; session dates run
  2026-07-26 to 2026-08-28. The whole subsystem is brand new in preprod.
- Purpose: Training 38 (81%) | Internal Interview 9 (19%). The other four
  purposes (Welcome Call, Resume Understanding, Initial Call - Marketing,
  Background Check) have no data yet.
- Status: Scheduled 45 | Cancelled 1 | Completed 1 - almost everything is
  still upcoming/scheduled; the completion machinery has barely fired.
- Integration coverage: meeting link / Zoom id / passcode / calendar event
  id and link on 45 of 47 records (96%) - the scheduling callout works on
  effectively every session.
- Population: Candidate + Host + times + timezone 100%; Candidate Training /
  Step / Program Version 38 (the Training records); Internal Interview 9;
  Additional Attendees 5 each; Actual Start 2 / Actual End 1.
- Timezones: AT (Alaska) 29, ET 14, then one each PT/HT/MT/CT.
- Never populated so far: Interview__c, Onboarding__c, Background_Check__c,
  Lead__c links; Scheduled_Start__c / Scheduled_End__c (legacy datetimes);
  Attendance_status__c; Recording_URL__c; Create_Meeting_Error__c; URL__c.
- Key takeaway: today Session__c is in practice "training classes plus
  internal-interview calls"; the other meeting purposes and links are built
  and waiting for adoption.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Session_Window__c  (Label: "Session Window")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Session_Window__c is a RECURRING DAILY TIME-SLOT TEMPLATE for a training
program - think "the 10:00-11:00 AM ET batch of Program version X". It
defines a start/end time-of-day that repeats every day of the program, plus
a capacity, and represents one bookable cohort slot in the candidate portal.
Candidates (or admins on their behalf) book a training INTO a window; the
booking assigns the training to the window's Cohort, timestamps every
training step at the window's daily time, and counts the seat against the
window's capacity. The window itself is a template - the concrete meetings it
produces are Session__c records.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object in the Training/LMS layer.
- MASTER-DETAIL CHILD OF Program_Version__c: every window belongs to one
  program version, and sharing is "Controlled By Parent". No owner of its
  own.
- 13 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views.
- Auto-number Name in the format SW-XXXX.
- Scale: only 2 records in preprod (created 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-06), both
  with capacity 5 and one seat booked.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. All session windows are the same flavor.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATION. An admin creates windows for a cohort/program version via
  the sessionWindowCreator LWC (a "New Session Window" quick action is
  defined for it, and the component can also sit on app/home/record pages -
  the quick action is not currently placed on any page). The component uses
  a native record form; SessionWindowCreationController supplies helpers:
  the program version's standard session duration (to pre-compute the end
  time), the cohort's start date, the next Sequence number, and whether the
  cohort already has a window. There is also an invocable Apex utility,
  SessionWindowService.createFromJson, which bulk-inserts windows from a
  JSON payload under a program version - its comments say it is called from
  the Program_Creation flow, but no flow currently references it (dormant).

STEP 2 - GUARD RULE. On create, the Session_Window_Enforce_Unique_Cohort
  flow (before save) blocks a second window for the same Cohort with a
  custom error - one cohort = one time-slot template.

STEP 3 - PORTAL EXPOSURE. The candidate portal (CandidatePortalController)
  lists a program version's windows as bookable slots when Status__c =
  "Upcoming" and Activate_From__c is today or earlier (or blank), showing
  the slot times converted into the candidate's timezone, the capacity, and
  seats remaining (Candidate_Capacity__c minus Booked_Count__c).

STEP 4 - BOOKING. When a candidate books a slot (bookSessionWindow) the code
  locks the window row, rejects the booking if full, then: assigns the
  training to the window's Cohort, stamps Start_Date, converts the window's
  daily times into the candidate's timezone onto the training, timestamps
  every training step on consecutive business days at the window's time,
  creates the Session records (first booker) or Session_Attendee rows
  (later bookers), and increments Booked_Count__c by one. The admin-side
  AdminSessionAssignmentController does the identical booking without the
  Upcoming/Activate-From/capacity filters (but still enforces matching
  program version and not-already-booked training).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Program_Version__c (via Program_Version__c, MASTER-DETAIL, required): the
  program version this window schedules. Sharing and deletion cascade from
  it. The portal only offers windows of the training's own program version.

LOOKUPS:
- Cohort__c (Cohort__c): the cohort (batch) this window is the time slot
  for. Booking a training into the window assigns the training to this
  cohort. Only ONE window per cohort is allowed (flow guard). 2/2 populated.
- Recruiter__c (Trainer__c): the trainer who will host the sessions the
  window generates - copied onto each Session as Host_User__c at booking
  time. 2/2 populated. (The object description notes the trainer is
  conceptually assigned per-session, not on the template - but in practice
  the field is filled and used as the default host.)

NO CHILD OBJECTS point at Session_Window__c - the window leaves its trace
through the Cohort assignment and the Sessions it spawns, not a direct link.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None on the object itself. The one-window-per-cohort rule is enforced by the
Session_Window_Enforce_Unique_Cohort flow (a before-save custom error), and
capacity/status checks are enforced in the booking Apex, not by validation
rules.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOW (active):
- Session_Window_Enforce_Unique_Cohort (before save, create): if another
  window already exists for the same Cohort, blocks the save with a custom
  error. The only flow touching this object.

APEX:
- SessionWindowCreationController: read-only helpers for the
  sessionWindowCreator LWC (program-version duration, cohort start date,
  next sequence, has-window check). Record creation itself is done by the
  LWC's native record form.
- SessionWindowService.createFromJson (invocable): bulk-creates windows
  under a program version from a JSON payload emitted by a builder LWC.
  Currently NOT referenced by any flow - dormant utility.
- CandidatePortalController: reads windows for the portal slot list
  (Status = Upcoming, Activate_From reached, capacity left) and increments
  Booked_Count__c on booking.
- AdminSessionAssignmentController ("Book Session Slot" quick action on
  Candidate Training): the admin-side booking; also increments
  Booked_Count__c.

QUICK ACTION:
- New_Session_Window (LightningWebComponent action -> sessionWindowCreator):
  defined but not placed on any page or layout at this snapshot.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 13, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHAT AND WHERE THE TEMPLATE BELONGS -----------------------------

Program_Version__c (Program Version) [Master-Detail -> Program_Version__c]
    THE required parent: the program version whose daily schedule this
    window defines. The portal matches a training's program version against
    this to decide which windows are offered.

Cohort__c (Cohort) [Lookup -> Cohort__c]
    The batch this time slot belongs to. Booking into the window puts the
    candidate's training into this cohort; only one window may exist per
    cohort (flow guard). 100% populated in data.

Trainer__c (Trainer) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c ("Employee")]
    The default trainer for the slot - copied to each generated Session's
    Host_User__c when the first candidate books. 100% populated in data.

Window_Label__c (Window Label) [Text, required]
    Human-readable name of the slot (e.g. "Morning Batch 10-11 ET"). Used as
    the portal slot label when the cohort has no name.

Sequence__c (Sequence) [Number, required]
    Ordering number of the window within its program version/cohort - the
    portal lists windows by Sequence. SessionWindowCreationController hands
    out the next number automatically.

--- GROUP B: THE TIME SLOT ---------------------------------------------------

Start_Time__c (Start Time) [Time, required]
    Daily start time-of-day of the slot (native Time type). Interpreted in
    Time_Zone__c and converted to each candidate's timezone by the portal
    and booking code; also used to timestamp every training step.

End_Time__c (End Time) [Time, required]
    Daily end time-of-day of the slot. Same conversion mechanics; the
    training's candidate-timezone end time and deliverable due-times derive
    from it.

Time_Zone__c (Time Zone) [Picklist, global value set "Candidate_Time_Zone"]
    The timezone the Start/End times are defined in (ET/CT/MT/PT/AT/HT).
    The booking code maps it to a real IANA zone for conversion. 100%
    populated.

Start_Date__c (Start Date) [Date]
    The date the cohort's daily rhythm begins. Copied onto the training as
