================================================================================
================================================================================
OBJECT: Background_Check__c  (Label: "Background Check")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Background_Check__c is the POST-OFFER verification and payment-agreement record
for a candidate. When a candidate finally wins a job offer (Interview outcome
"Offer Received"), one Background Check record is opened to walk the candidate
through everything that must happen between "offer" and "cleared to start":

  a) The MONEY GATE - Techsara collects its offer-letter payment from the
     candidate, then has the candidate e-sign an ACH debit authorization and a
     promissory note (a payment plan for the remaining fees) via DocuSign. The
     DS_* fields on this record hold the payment-plan terms that get merged
     into those DocuSign documents.
  b) The VERIFICATION work - the candidate submits their details, each past
     employer/project is verified one by one (child object
     Background_Check_Employment__c), and a final confirmation is obtained
     from the employer.
  c) The QA TEAM WORKFLOW - new records land in a "QA Background Check Queue";
     a QA member accepts a record to take ownership, works the pipeline, and
     an automated reminder engine nags the owners (email + Slack) while
     payment/signature items stay pending.

One record = one candidate's background-check + payment-agreement process,
normally tied to the specific interview that produced the offer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the post-offer / onboarding-preparation domain.
- Standalone object with its OWN owner (not a master-detail child): lookups to
  Account (Candidate__c), Interview__c and Session__c. Internal sharing model
  is Public Read/Write; external (portal) sharing is Private.
- Records are typically owned by the QA_Background_Check_Queue queue until a
  QA member accepts them (84% still queue-owned in current data).
- Auto-number Name "BCN-{00000}" (field label "Background Check  ID").
- 36 custom fields, 0 record types, 5 validation rules, 1 list view
  ("QA Background Check Queue" - the queue's work list showing Name,
  Interview, Candidate and Status).
- PARENT of Background_Check_Employment__c (master-detail children, one per
  employer/project to verify, counted by a rollup field).
- Scale: only 31 records in preprod (created 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-10) - this
  is a NEW process, live for about two months at snapshot time.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every Background Check record is the same flavor; the multi-select
"Verification Type" field (Background Verification | I9 Verification | Visa
Assessment) was designed to carry the variation instead, but is unused so far.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATION. The record-triggered flow "Background Check: Creation,
  Queue Routing, and Stage Progression" auto-created a Background Check when
  an Interview__c was updated to outcome "Offer Received" (one per interview -
  it checks for an existing record first). It stamped Candidate + Interview,
  set owner = QA_Background_Check_Queue, and initialized every status:
  Background Check Status = "Payment Verification Pending", Offer Letter
  Payment / ACH / Promissory Note = "Pending", Candidate Details = "Pending",
  Verification = "Not Started", Notification Active = true. NOTE: this flow is
  now marked OBSOLETE (deactivated) in the org, so at snapshot time new
  records have to be created manually while a replacement is decided -
  verify with team. 30 of the 31 existing records are linked to an interview.

STEP 2 - QA ACCEPTS FROM THE QUEUE. The record sits in the QA Background
  Check Queue list view. A QA member clicks the "Accept Record" button (a
  quick action that simply checks the "Accept this record from Queue"
  checkbox). The before-save flow "Background Change: Queue to QA Assignment"
  then reassigns the record's owner to the clicking user. From that point the
  record is that QA member's personal work item.

STEP 3 - THE STATUS PIPELINE. Background_Check_Status__c is driven manually
  through five stages, and validation rules gate each move (see part 6):
    Payment Verification Pending  ->  candidate pays the offer-letter fee
    Documents Pending             ->  ACH authorization + promissory note
                                      are sent and must come back signed
    Candidate Details Pending     ->  candidate submits their employment
                                      history details
    Verification In Progress      ->  each employer/project is verified
                                      (child records)
    Completed                     ->  verification done + final employer
                                      confirmation received.
  The "Before Background Check" checkbox is a per-record bypass that turns
  ALL of these stage gates off (used for records opened before the process
  existed, or to force a correction).

STEP 4 - SEND THE ACH + PROMISSORY NOTE (DOCUSIGN). On the record page the
  user clicks "Send ACH and Promissory". The screen flow asks for the payment
  plan: debit amount per installment, total amount to be paid, payment
  commencement date, first-installment due date, final-payment due date,
  payment period in months, and the day of the month the ACH debit runs. It
  saves those into the DS_* fields and then calls the DocuSign managed
  package (apex action dfsle__EnvelopeConfigurationBulkRequest) with the
  envelope template from custom label ACH_and_Promissory_Template_ID, using
  this Background Check as the source record - the DS_* "Formatted" formula
  fields exist so the dates/amounts merge into the documents as clean
  MM/DD/YYYY and $x,xxx.xx text. When the signed envelope comes back, a user
  flips ACH Authorization Status and Promissory Note Status to "Signed"
  (no flow in the org writes these statuses - the DocuSign writeback, if
  any, is configured inside the managed package; verify with team).

STEP 5 - AUTOMATED PENDING-ITEM REMINDERS. The flow "BG Check Pending
  Notifications" watches the three money/paperwork statuses. While any of
  Offer Letter Payment / ACH / Promissory Note is "Pending" it keeps
  Notification Active = true and writes a human-readable Pending Items
  Summary (e.g. "Offer Letter Payment Pending, ACH Authorization Pending").
  A scheduled path re-runs 4 hours after Last Notification Sent and - IF the
  "Send Pending Notifications" switch is checked - emails the candidate's
  owner and the record owner (from noreply@techsarasolutions.com), Slack-DMs
  both owners, and posts to a fixed Slack channel when the record still
  belongs to the queue. When everything is resolved it un-flags Notification
  Active and clears the summary. IN PRACTICE the send switch is unchecked on
  every record today, so the reminder machinery is armed but silent.

STEP 6 - VERIFY EMPLOYMENTS AND COMPLETE. The candidate's work history is
  entered as Background_Check_Employment__c children (the "Background Check
  Projects" related list); each is verified individually. A rollup counts the
  children, and validation prevents marking Candidate Details "Submitted"
  with zero children. Once overall Verification Status = "Completed" and the
  Final Employer Confirmation checkbox is ticked, the record can be moved to
  "Completed". A successful background check leads on to Onboarding__c in
  the broader placement journey.

OPTIONAL - "Create Session" on the record page launches the Background Check
  Session Creation screen flow: it books a Session__c (Purpose = "Background
  Check", Status = "Unscheduled") with the candidate, a chosen host employee
  and an optional extra attendee, linked back to this Background Check - a
  call to collect details or walk the candidate through the paperwork. It has
  not been used yet (0 such sessions in data).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM BACKGROUND CHECK:
- Account (Candidate__c): the candidate (Person Account) being verified.
  100% populated - the anchor of the record. The reminder flow reads the
  candidate's OWNER (email + Slack id) to know who to nag.
- Interview__c (Interview__c): the interview that produced the offer this
  background check follows (97% populated; stamped by the creation flow).
- Session__c (Session__c): a session related to this background check (a
  details-collection or walkthrough call). Currently never populated.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT BACKGROUND CHECK:
- Background_Check_Employment__c (MASTER-DETAIL child, relationship name
  "Background_Check_Projects"): one row per past employer/project to verify.
  Counted by the Background Check Project Count rollup. 8 children across 6
  parents so far.
- Session__c.Background_Check__c (lookup): sessions booked FROM this record
  by the Create Session button link back through this field (none yet).

OWNERSHIP: the QA_Background_Check_Queue queue owns new records until a QA
member clicks Accept Record; 26 of 31 records are still queue-owned.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules, all active)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Together the five rules enforce the stage-gate pipeline, and ALL of them are
skipped when "Before Background Check" is checked. IMPORTANT WARNING: the
rule NAMES and their ERROR MESSAGES are rotated/mismatched relative to what
each rule actually checks - users frequently see a message describing a
DIFFERENT gate than the one that blocked them. The actual behavior:

- Require_CandidateDetail_For_Verification: BLOCKS moving status to
  "Documents Pending" unless Offer Letter Payment Status = "Received".
  Message shown: "Candidate Details Status must be Submitted before moving
  to Verification In Progress." (wrong text for this gate).
- Require_Documents_For_Candidate_Details: BLOCKS moving status to
  "Candidate Details Pending" unless BOTH ACH Authorization Status and
  Promissory Note Status = "Signed". Message shown: "ACH Authorization and
  Promissory Note must both be Signed before moving to Candidate Details
  Pending." (this one matches).
- Require_Payment_For_Documents_Pending: BLOCKS moving status to
  "Verification In Progress" unless Candidate Details Status = "Submitted".
  Message shown: "Offer Letter Payment Status must be Received before moving
  to Documents Pending." (wrong text for this gate).
- Require_Project_For_Candidate_Submitted: BLOCKS moving status to
  "Completed" unless Verification Status = "Completed" AND Final Employer
  Confirmation Received is checked. Message shown: "At least one related
  Background Check Employment must exist before submitting Candidate
  Details." (wrong text for this gate).
- Require_Verification_For_Completed: BLOCKS setting Candidate Details
  Status to "Submitted" while the Background Check Project Count rollup is
  0 (i.e. no employment children entered). Message shown: "Verification
  Status must be Completed and Final Employer Confirmation must be received
  before completing the Background Check." (wrong text for this gate).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOWS:
- Background_Change_Queue_to_QA_Assignment (before save, update; ACTIVE):
  when "Accept this record from Queue" becomes checked, sets the record
  owner to the current user - the queue-claim mechanic behind Accept Record.
- BG_Check_Pending_Notifications (after save, create+update; ACTIVE): keeps
  Notification Active / Pending Items Summary in sync with the three
  Pending statuses, and via a scheduled path (4 hours after Last
  Notification Sent, repeating while items stay pending AND Send Pending
  Notifications is checked) sends the reminder email, Slack DMs to the
  record owner and candidate owner, and a Slack post to the queue channel
  when the record is still queue-owned. Also stamps Last Notification Sent.
- Background_Check_Creation_Queue_Routing_and_Stage_Progression (on
  Interview__c, after save; OBSOLETE/deactivated): the original creator -
  made the Background Check with all defaults and queue ownership when an
  interview's outcome became "Offer Received". Its deactivation means
  auto-creation is currently OFF.

SCREEN FLOWS / BUTTONS ON THE PAGE (Background_Check_Record_Page1):
- Accept Record: field-update quick action exposing only the Assigned to QA
  checkbox (see flow above).
- Send ACH and Promissory: collects the DS_* payment-plan terms, updates the
  record, then sends the DocuSign envelope (managed package "dfsle" apex
  action; template id from custom label ACH_and_Promissory_Template_ID).
- Create Session: books a "Background Check" purpose Session__c linked to
  this record and the candidate.

APEX / TRIGGERS: none - no Apex class in the org references this object.
The only external touchpoint is the DocuSign eSignature managed package.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 36, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHO AND WHERE IT CAME FROM --------------------------------------

Candidate__c (Candidate) [Lookup -> Account]
    The candidate (Person Account) this background check is for. 100%
    populated; set by the (now obsolete) creation flow or manually. The
    reminder flow reads the candidate's owner for email/Slack targeting, and
    the record page shows the process in the candidate's context.

Interview__c (Interview) [Lookup -> Interview__c]
    The interview whose "Offer Received" outcome opened this background
    check. Auto-stamped by the creation flow; 30 of 31 records have it.
    Also a column in the QA queue list view so QA can see the source offer.

Session__c (Session) [Lookup -> Session__c]
    A session (call/meeting) related to this background check - intended for
    the details-collection or paperwork-walkthrough call. Manually set;
    never populated so far (sessions created via the Create Session button
    link back through Session__c.Background_Check__c instead).

--- GROUP B: THE STATUS PIPELINE ---------------------------------------------

Background_Check_Status__c (Background Check Status) [Picklist]
    THE main stage of the process, moved manually by the QA owner and gated
    by the five validation rules: Payment Verification Pending (start; 68%
    of records sit here) | Documents Pending (ACH/promissory out for
    signature) | Candidate Details Pending (waiting on the candidate's
    employment history) | Verification In Progress (working the employment
    children) | Completed. Shown in the queue list view and in every
    reminder message.

Background_Check_Type__c (Verification Type) [MultiselectPicklist]
    WHICH kinds of verification this record covers: Background Verification
    | I9 Verification | Visa Assessment. Manual entry. NEVER USED in
    practice - empty on all 31 records at snapshot time.

Before_Background_Check__c (Before Background Check) [Checkbox]
    Per-record bypass switch: when checked, ALL five stage-gate validation
    rules are skipped, letting a user move the status freely. Meant for
    records that predate the process or need admin correction. Manual;
    currently unchecked on every record.

--- GROUP C: QA QUEUE WORKFLOW -----------------------------------------------

Assigned_to_QA__c (Accept this record from Queue) [Checkbox]
    The queue-claim button's field: the Accept Record quick action checks
    it, and the Background_Change_Queue_to_QA_Assignment flow immediately
    makes the clicking user the record owner. Checked on only 1 of 31
    records so far - in practice QA has barely started claiming records
    (26 are still owned by the queue).

QA_Notes__c (QA Notes) [LongTextArea]
    Free-text working notes for the QA member handling the record (what was
    checked, follow-ups, anomalies). Manual entry; nothing reads it
    downstream.

--- GROUP D: THE PAYMENT & SIGNATURE GATE ------------------------------------

Offer_Letter_Payment_Status__c (Offer Letter Payment Status) [Picklist]
    Has the candidate paid the offer-letter fee? Pending | Received.
    Initialized to Pending by the creation flow, flipped to Received
    manually when payment lands. Gate 1 of the pipeline: status cannot move
    to "Documents Pending" until this is Received. Also one of the three
    statuses the reminder flow watches. Currently: 20 Pending, 11 Received.

Offer_Letter_Payment_Received_Date__c (Offer Letter Payment Received Date)
[Formula, Date]
    Shows TODAY's date whenever the payment status is "Received", blank
    otherwise. CAUTION: because it is a live formula on TODAY(), it does NOT
    freeze the actual receipt date - it always displays the current date for
    any record whose payment is Received. Treat it as a "payment is
    received" indicator, not a historical date.

ACH_Authorization_Status__c (ACH Authorization Status) [Picklist]
    Has the candidate signed the ACH direct-debit authorization? Pending |
    Signed. Initialized to Pending; set to Signed manually when the signed
    DocuSign envelope returns. Gate 2 (with the promissory note) before
    "Candidate Details Pending". Watched by the reminder flow.

ACH_Authorization_Signed_Date__c (ACH Authorization Signed Date)
[Formula, Date]
    TODAY's date while the ACH status is "Signed", blank otherwise - same
    live-formula caveat as above: it does not preserve the real signing
    date.

Promissory_Note_Status__c (Promissory Note Status) [Picklist]
    Has the candidate signed the promissory note (the payment-plan
    agreement)? Pending | Signed. Same lifecycle and gating as the ACH
    status; both must be Signed together to advance.

Promissory_Note_Signed_Date__c (Promissory Note Signed Date) [Formula, Date]
    TODAY's date while the promissory note status is "Signed", blank
    otherwise - same live-formula caveat.

--- GROUP E: DOCUSIGN PAYMENT-PLAN TERMS (DS_* FIELDS) -----------------------
All entered through the "Send ACH and Promissory" screen flow (which then
merges them into the DocuSign ACH-authorization + promissory-note envelope).
"DS" = DocuSign. Populated on the 5 records (16%) that have gone through the
send step. Each raw field has a "Formatted"/"Formate" formula twin that
renders it as clean text for the document merge (note the recurring
"Formate" typo in the API names/labels).

DS_Debit_Amount__c (DS Debit Amount) [Currency]
    The recurring ACH debit amount per installment the candidate agrees to
    pay (e.g. $500 per month). Entered in the send flow.

DS_Debit_Amount_Formate__c (DS Debit Amount Formate) [Formula, Text]
    The debit amount rendered as "$x,xxx.xx" text (with thousands commas)
    for merging into the DocuSign documents.

DS_Total_Amount_to_be_Paid__c (DS Total Amount to be Paid) [Currency]
    The TOTAL the candidate will pay under the promissory note across all
    installments. Entered in the send flow.

DS_Total_Amount_to_be_Paid_Formate__c (DS Total Amount to be Paid Formate)
[Formula, Text]
    The total amount as formatted "$x,xxx.xx" merge text.

DS_Payment_Commencement_Date__c (DS Payment Commencement Date) [Date]
    The date the payment plan starts. Entered in the send flow.

DS_Payment_Commencement_Date_Formatted__c (DS Payment Commencement Date
Formatted) [Formula, Text]
    The commencement date as "MM/DD/YYYY" merge text.

DS_First_Installment_Due_Date__c (DS First Installment Due Date) [Date]
    When the first installment is due. Entered in the send flow.

DS_First_Installment_Due_Date_Formatted__c (DS First Installment Due Date
Formatted) [Formula, Text]
    The first-installment date as "MM/DD/YYYY" merge text.

DS_Final_Payment_Due_Date__c (DS Final Payment Due Date) [Date]
    When the last installment is due (end of the plan). Entered in the send
    flow.

DS_Final_Payment_Due_Date_Formate__c (DS Final Payment Due Date Formate)
[Formula, Text]
    The final-payment date as "MM/DD/YYYY" merge text.

DS_Payment_Period_Month__c (DS Payment Period (Month)) [Picklist]
    Length of the payment plan in months: 1 through 12. Entered in the send
    flow.

DS_ACH_Debit_Date_Each_Month__c (DS ACH Debit Date Each Month) [Picklist]
    Day of the month (1 through 30) the recurring ACH debit is drawn.
    Entered in the send flow.

--- GROUP F: CANDIDATE DETAILS & VERIFICATION --------------------------------

Candidate_Details_Status__c (Candidate Details Status) [Picklist]
    Where the candidate stands on submitting their employment-history
    details: Pending | In Progress | Submitted. Initialized to Pending;
    updated manually. Cannot be set to "Submitted" while there are zero
    Background Check Employment children (validation), and must be
    Submitted before the main status can move to "Verification In
    Progress". Currently: 25 Pending, 2 In Progress, 4 Submitted.

Verification_Status__c (Verification Status) [Picklist]
    The OVERALL verification work status across all employment children:
    Not Started | In Progress | Completed. Manual rollup-by-human (each
    child has its own per-employer status). Must be "Completed" before the
    record can be marked Completed. Currently: 25 Not Started, 1 In
    Progress, 4 Completed (roughly mirroring the pipeline stage).

Background_Check_Project_Count__c (Background Check Project Count)
[Rollup Summary, Count]
    System-computed COUNT of Background_Check_Employment__c children. Feeds
    the Require_Verification_For_Completed validation (candidate details
    cannot be Submitted at 0). "Project" is the team's word for one
    employer/project row.

Final_Employer_Confirmation_Received__c (Final Employer Confirmation
Received) [Checkbox]
    The last box to tick: the (new) employer's final confirmation for the
    candidate has been received. Manual. Required (with Verification
    Completed) before status "Completed". Checked on 5 of 31 records.

Final_Employer_Confirmation_Date__c (Final Employer Confirmation  Date)
[Formula, Date]
    TODAY's date while the confirmation checkbox is checked, blank
    otherwise - same live-formula caveat as the other status-date fields:
    it does not preserve the actual confirmation date.

Final_Confirmation_Date__c (Final Confirmation Date) [Date]
    A plain (non-formula) date field for the final confirmation - the
    stored counterpart the formula above lacks. NOTE: it exists in this
    metadata snapshot but is NOT present/queryable in the live preprod org
    (deleted in the org or never deployed) - verify with team before
    relying on it.

--- GROUP G: PENDING-ITEM REMINDER ENGINE ------------------------------------
All owned by the BG_Check_Pending_Notifications flow.

Notification_Active__c (Notification Active) [Checkbox]
    System flag: TRUE while any of the three money/paperwork items (offer
    letter payment / ACH / promissory note) is still Pending; the flow
    turns it off and clears the summary when everything is resolved. Also
    one of the flow's entry conditions. True on 22 of 31 records today.

Send_Pending_Notifications__c (Received Background Notifications) [Checkbox]
    The ON/OFF switch for actually SENDING the 4-hourly reminders (email +
    Slack). A human checks it to start the nagging for a record. CAUTION:
    the label ("Received Background Notifications") reads backwards -
    treat it as "send pending-item reminders". Currently unchecked on ALL
    records, so no reminders are actually going out despite 22 records
    having pending items.

Pending_Items_Summary__c (Pending Items Summary) [TextArea]
    Auto-written, human-readable list of what is still outstanding, e.g.
    "Offer Letter Payment Pending, ACH Authorization Pending, Promissory
    Note Pending". Rebuilt by the flow on every change and embedded in the
    reminder email and Slack messages; cleared when all items resolve.

Last_Notification_Sent__c (Last Notification Sent) [DateTime]
    Timestamp anchor for the 4-hour reminder cycle: the scheduled path
    fires 4 hours after this value, and the flow re-stamps it each time it
    sends (or first arms) notifications. Read-only on the layout; 30 of 31
    records have it (stamped at arm time even though sending is off).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 31, created 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-10 - a brand-new process
  with two months of history.
- Status pipeline: Payment Verification Pending 21 (68%) | Documents Pending
  5 | Completed 4 | Verification In Progress 1. Most records are stuck at
  the very first gate (waiting on the candidate's offer-letter payment).
- Payment/paperwork trio: 20 records all-Pending | 8 fully cleared (payment
  Received + ACH Signed + promissory Signed) | 2 payment Received but
  documents still Pending | 1 payment Received with ACH/promissory blank.
- Candidate details: Pending 25 | In Progress 2 | Submitted 4. Verification:
  Not Started 25 | In Progress 1 | Completed 4.
- Ownership: 26 of 31 (84%) still owned by the QA_Background_Check_Queue;
  Accept Record has been used once (1 record with Assigned to QA checked).
- Reminder engine: Notification Active on 22 records, but Send Pending
  Notifications is FALSE on all 31 - reminders are armed but not firing.
- DS_* payment-plan fields populated on 5 records (16%) - the Send ACH and
  Promissory flow has been run a handful of times.
- Never used so far: Background_Check_Type__c (0 of 31), Session__c lookup
  (0), Before_Background_Check__c (0), Background-Check-purpose sessions
  (0 Session__c records with Purpose = "Background Check").
- Children: 8 Background_Check_Employment__c rows across 6 parents - 25
  background checks have no employment rows yet (consistent with most
  records not having reached the details/verification stages).
- Key takeaway for answering questions: this object is early-lifecycle. The
  bottleneck visible in data is the initial payment gate; the auto-creation
  flow is deactivated (Obsolete), the reminder send-switch is off
  everywhere, and the QA queue is largely unworked.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Background_Check_Employment__c  (Label: "Background Check Employment")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Background_Check_Employment__c is ONE past employer/project of a candidate
that must be verified as part of a Background Check. When the candidate
submits their employment history, each employer (or client project) becomes
one child record under the parent Background_Check__c: the employer and
project names, the employment dates, up to three named references with
contact details, and the per-employer verification outcome. The team calls
these rows "projects" - the auto-number label is "Background Check Project
ID", the child relationship is "Background_Check_Projects", and the parent's
rollup is "Background Check Project Count".

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the post-offer / verification domain.
- MASTER-DETAIL CHILD OF Background_Check__c: every row MUST belong to a
  background check; sharing is Controlled By Parent (whoever can see the
  background check sees its employments); no owner of its own.
- Auto-number Name "BGC-{00000}" (label "Background Check Project ID");
  field history tracking is enabled.
- 21 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views.
- Scale: only 8 records in preprod (created 2026-06-08 to 2026-07-01),
  spread across 6 parent background checks.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every employment/project row is the same shape regardless of employer
type or verification method.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - ENTRY. When the parent Background Check reaches "Candidate Details
  Pending", the candidate's employment history is captured: the QA member
  (or whoever collects the details) creates one record per employer/project
  from the "Background Check Projects" related list on the parent record
  page, filling employer name, project name and start/end dates. There is
  no flow or form automation - this is plain manual data entry.

STEP 2 - THE PARENT GATE. The parent's rollup (Background Check Project
  Count) counts these rows; the parent validation prevents setting Candidate
  Details Status to "Submitted" while the count is 0 - i.e. a background
  check cannot claim "details submitted" with no employment history entered.

STEP 3 - VERIFICATION. During "Verification In Progress" the verifier works
  each row: contacts the employer and/or the listed references, records what
  happened in Verification Notes, ticks Employer Confirmed when the employer
  vouches for the employment, and sets the row's Verification Status to
  Verified or Unable to Verify. Reference fields (3 slots of name /
  designation / email / phone) hold who was contacted - though in practice
  they have not been filled in yet on any record.

STEP 4 - ROLLING UP TO THE PARENT. There is NO automation that aggregates
  the child outcomes - the QA member manually sets the parent's overall
  Verification Status to "Completed" once every row is resolved, then
  obtains the final employer confirmation and completes the background
  check.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Background_Check__c (via Background_Check__c, MASTER-DETAIL, required,
  100% populated; relationship name "Background_Check_Projects"). The
  background check this employment row belongs to. The parent's Background
  Check Project Count rollup counts these rows and feeds the parent's
  stage-gate validation. Sharing and deletion cascade from the parent.

No other object looks up to Background_Check_Employment__c, and it has no
other outbound relationships - it is a pure detail table.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. There are no validation rules on this object itself - the only rule
involving it lives on the PARENT (a Background Check's Candidate Details
cannot be marked "Submitted" while this object's rollup count is zero).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. No flow, Apex trigger, Apex class or quick action in the org creates,
updates or reads Background_Check_Employment__c - everything on it is manual
data entry through the parent's related list. Its only automated footprint
is the parent's rollup count (a platform rollup, not a flow) and field
history tracking.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 21, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE EMPLOYMENT / PROJECT ITSELF ---------------------------------

Background_Check__c (Background Check) [Master-Detail -> Background_Check__c]
    THE required parent link: which background check this employment row is
    verified under. 100% populated; controls sharing and cascade delete.

Employer_Name__c (Employer Name) [Text, 50]
    The employer/company name for this employment entry, as given by the
    candidate. Manual entry; 100% populated in current data.

Project_Name__c (Project Name) [Text, 100]
    The project or engagement the candidate worked on at that employer
    (consulting/staffing history is usually project-shaped, hence the
    "Project" naming across this object). Manual; 100% populated.

Start_Date__c (Start Date) [Date]
    When the candidate started at this employer/project. Manual; 100%
    populated.

End_Date__c (End Date) [Date]
    When the candidate left this employer/project. Manual; 100% populated
    (current data has no open-ended rows).

Present__c (Current Employer) [Checkbox]
    Marks this row as the candidate's CURRENT employer (still working
    there). NOTE: the field exists in this metadata snapshot but is NOT
    present/queryable in the live preprod org (deleted in the org or never
    deployed) - verify with team before relying on it.

--- GROUP B: REFERENCES TO CONTACT (3 SLOTS) ---------------------------------
Three identical blocks of contact details for people at the employer who
can vouch for the candidate. All manual entry; all 12 fields are EMPTY on
every record so far - verification has been happening without recording
the references in Salesforce.

Ref_1_Name__c (Ref 1 Name) [Text]
Ref_1_Designation__c (Ref 1 Designation) [Text]
Ref_1_Email__c (Ref 1 Email) [Email]
Ref_1_Phone__c (Ref 1 Phone) [Phone]
    Reference #1: the primary contact (typically a manager or HR person)
    with their job title, email and phone.

Ref_2_Name__c (Ref 2 Name) [Text]
Ref_2_Designation__c (Ref 2 Designation) [Text]
Ref_2_Email__c (Ref 2 Email) [Email]
Ref_2_Phone__c (Ref 2 Phone) [Phone]
    Reference #2: a second contact at the same employer (backup or peer
    reference).

Ref_3_Name__c (Ref 3 Name) [Text]
Ref_3_Designation__c (Ref 3 Designation) [Text]
Ref_3_Email__c (Ref 3 Email) [Email]
Ref_3_Phone__c (Ref 3 Phone) [Phone]
    Reference #3: a third contact slot.

--- GROUP C: VERIFICATION OUTCOME --------------------------------------------

Verification_Status__c (Verification Status) [Picklist]
    The per-employer verification result: Not Started | In Progress |
    Verified | Unable to Verify. Set manually by the verifier as they work
    the row. Note it has MORE granular end-states than the parent's overall
    Verification Status (which is just Not Started / In Progress /
    Completed) - "Unable to Verify" captures a failed check on one employer
    without failing the whole background check. Current data: 4 blank,
    3 Verified, 1 In Progress.

Employer_Confirmed__c (Employer Confirmed) [Checkbox]
    Ticked when the employer itself confirmed the employment (as opposed to
    only references responding). Manual; checked on 3 of 8 records.

Verification_Notes__c (Verification Notes) [LongTextArea]
    Free-text log of the verification work on this employer: who was
    contacted, when, what they said, discrepancies found. Manual; nothing
    reads it downstream - it is the human audit trail.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 8, created 2026-06-08 to 2026-07-01, across 6 parent
  background checks (1-2 employments per verified candidate so far).
- Verification status: blank 4 | Verified 3 | In Progress 1. Employer
  Confirmed on 3 of 8.
- Fully populated on every record: Employer Name, Project Name, Start Date,
  End Date. Completely empty on every record: all 12 reference fields
  (Ref 1/2/3 name, designation, email, phone).
- Key takeaway for answering questions: this is a tiny, hand-entered detail
  table used by the handful of background checks that have reached the
  verification stage; its only systemic role is feeding the parent's
  project-count rollup that gates "Candidate Details Submitted".

================================================================================
OBJECT: Employee_Leave__c  (Label: "Employee Leave")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Employee_Leave__c records ONE leave/absence request by a Techsara internal
employee (a Recruiter__c / "Employee" record - NOT a candidate). One record =
one leave request: a full-day range (e.g. Aug 10-12) or a partial day (first
half, second half, or a custom time range on a single date). The record moves
through a request -> manager approval workflow, and an approved leave shows up
as an "Out of Office" event on the Salesforce calendar so the rest of the team
can see the person is unavailable.

Why the org cares: internal-staff availability is load-bearing here - support
persons are assigned to candidate interviews (by the COMPASS AI engine) and
trainers run sessions. A leave record is the formal trail of "this employee is
not available on these days". Today the visible availability signal is the
calendar event the leave creates; a direct feed from this object into the
COMPASS availability logic is not confirmed in metadata (verify with team).

The object is clearly built in two phases: the REQUEST + MANAGER APPROVAL
part is live (flows, quick actions, portal navigation), while a larger HR
POLICY layer (HR approver, notice-period compliance, PTO/sick-leave balance
snapshots, paid/unpaid day splits, supporting documents) exists as fields
only - no automation fills them and they are hidden from the main profile.
Treat those as "designed for a future HR phase, not yet wired".

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the internal-staff (HR/operations) domain.
- STANDALONE object with its own Owner - not a child of anything. Sharing is
  Public Read/Write for both internal and external (portal) users, so any
  employee who can use the object can see everyone's leave records. (Worth
  revisiting in the role-hierarchy/security redesign.)
- 37 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view ("All").
- Auto-number Name in the format A-XXXX (e.g. A-0147).
- Field history tracking is ON; reports are DISABLED for this object (it
  cannot be used as a report primary object); Chatter feeds off.
- Surfaced in three places: an "Employee Leave" tab in the Techsara Solutions
  app, an "Employee Leave" item (position 6) in the AIC Portal site
  navigation, and an "Employee Leaves" related list on the Employee
  (Recruiter__c) record page.
- Access is granted by PROFILES (e.g. the AIC Portal profile has Create/Read/
  Edit, no Delete), not by the department permission sets - none of them
  mention this object.
- Scale: only 18 records in preprod, all created in early Aug 2026 - this is
  a feature under active build/test, not yet in production-scale use.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every leave request uses the same single flavor; the Leave_Type__c
picklist (PTO, Sick, Marriage...) carries the classification instead.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - EMPLOYEE REQUESTS LEAVE. On the employee's own Recruiter__c
  ("Employee") record, the "Create Leave Request" button launches the
  Request_Leave screen flow. One screen collects: Leave Type, a Full Day
  checkbox, then either Start Date + End Date (full day - with a read-only
  "No. Of Leave Days" counter) or a single Leave Date + Partial Day Type +
  Start Time + End Time (partial day), plus a required free-text Leave
  Reason. The flow validates that End Time is after Start Time (on-screen
  error, not a validation rule), computes Start/End DateTime values, stamps
  Requested_On with the current date/time, links Employee__c to the record
  the button was clicked on, and saves the leave with Status = "Submitted".

STEP 2 - TENTATIVE CALENDAR EVENT. The moment a leave is created with Status
  "Submitted" (and no event yet), the Tentative_calendar_Event flow creates a
  Salesforce Event: subject "LV-" + the leave's auto-number name, description
  = reason + status + employee name, start/end from the leave's DateTime
  fields, all-day if Is_Full_Day, Show-As = "Tentative". The Event carries an
  Employee_Leave__c lookup back to the leave, and the Event's id is written
  into Leave_Event_Id__c. The pending leave is now visible on the calendar as
  tentative time off.

STEP 3 - MANAGER DECISION. On the leave record, the "Manager Decision" button
  launches the Manager_Decision screen flow. The flow is gated: it looks up
  the employee's Assigned Sr Recruiter (the manager on the Recruiter__c
  record) and compares that manager's linked User to the logged-in user. Any
  other user gets a stop screen ("Only the manager approved the leave
  request."). The manager picks the decision on a Status screen:
  - Approved: Status -> "Approved", Manager_Approved_On stamped with now,
    any old Rejection_Reason cleared.
  - Rejected: a second screen collects the Rejection Reason; Status ->
    "Rejected", Manager_Approved_On and Leave_Event_Id cleared.

STEP 4 - CALENDAR SYNC ON THE DECISION. The Leave_Event_Sync flow fires when
  Status becomes Approved, Rejected or Cancelled: Approved flips the linked
  calendar Event's Show-As from "Tentative" to "Out of Office" (the firm
  unavailability signal); Rejected or Cancelled DELETES the calendar Event so
  the time frees up. The leave record itself stays as the audit trail.

STEP 5 (DESIGNED, NOT WIRED) - HR REVIEW AND PAYROLL MATH. The field model
  anticipates a second approval lane: flags for "HR approval required" and
  why (late request, insufficient balance, special leave, comp-off), an HR
  approver + timestamp, notice-period given-vs-required with an On Time/Late
  verdict, PTO and sick-leave balance snapshots at request time, and a paid/
  unpaid day split for payroll. The Status picklist even has "Manager
  Approved", "HR Review Required", "Planned", "Draft" and "Completed" values.
  NONE of this is populated by any current flow or Apex, the fields are not
  on the page layout, and the AIC Portal profile hides them (verify roadmap
  with team before relying on them).

NOTE ON THE DATA: the 18 records currently in preprod do NOT look like they
came through the Request_Leave flow - Start/End DateTime, Leave_Event_Id and
Manager_Approved_On are empty on all of them, while fields no flow sets
(Leave_Year, Total_Days) are filled. They appear to be hand-loaded test data.
Earlier test cycles (Jan-Jun 2026) created ~130 leave records that were later
deleted, leaving 115 orphaned "LV-..." calendar events behind.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM EMPLOYEE LEAVE TO OTHER OBJECTS:
- Recruiter__c / "Employee" (Employee__c): THE employee taking the leave.
  Required in practice (100% populated), set by the Request_Leave flow from
  the Employee record the button was clicked on. The Employee record page
  shows all of a person's leaves in the "Employee Leaves" related list.
- Recruiter__c / "Employee" (HR_Approver__c): the HR person who signed off -
  part of the unwired HR phase, never populated.
- Employee standard object (Manager_Approver__c): the approving manager.
  CAUTION: this lookup points at Salesforce's STANDARD "Employee" object (a
  Work.com-era object), NOT Recruiter__c, and it is not even queryable via
  SOQL in this org ("Invalid field" error) - effectively broken/unusable.
  The real manager gate in the Manager_Decision flow uses the employee's
  Assigned_Sr_Recruiter__c from the Recruiter__c record instead.
- Employee standard object (Requested_By__c): same problem - points at the
  standard Employee object, not queryable, unused. The real "who asked" info
  lives in Employee__c + Requested_On__c + CreatedById.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT EMPLOYEE LEAVE:
- Event / Activity (Activity.Employee_Leave__c lookup): the calendar event
  representing this leave ("LV-<name>", Tentative or Out of Office). Created
  by the Tentative_calendar_Event flow, retargeted/deleted by
  Leave_Event_Sync. The layout shows an Activities related list. In data
  there are 115 such events - all orphans from deleted test leaves.

NON-RELATIONSHIPS WORTH KNOWING:
- No link to Interview__c, Session__c or Case: leave does not automatically
  block or reshuffle a support person's interviews - any such coordination is
  manual or inside the external COMPASS engine (not confirmed).
- Recruiter__c's own On_Leave_Today__c / Leave_Start_Date_Time__c /
  Leave_End_Date_Time__c fields are NOT written by the leave flows - nothing
  in the org connects them to this object today.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The object has no validation rules; the guardrails live inside the
screen flows instead (End Time must be after Start Time; only the employee's
manager may run the Manager Decision flow).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCREEN FLOWS / BUTTONS:
- Request_Leave ("Create Leave Request" button on the Recruiter__c /
  Employee page layout): the entry point - collects the request and creates
  the leave with Status "Submitted" (see step 1). Marked as requiring
  explicit flow access to run.
- Manager_Decision ("Manager Decision" button on the Employee Leave page
  layout): manager-only approve/reject with the identity gate described in
  step 3. Also requires explicit flow access.

RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOWS (both active):
- Tentative_calendar_Event (after save, on create; only when Status =
  "Submitted" and Leave_Event_Id is empty): creates the Tentative calendar
  Event and writes its id back to Leave_Event_Id__c.
- Leave_Event_Sync (after save, create + update; only when Status = Approved,
  Rejected or Cancelled): Approved -> linked Event Show-As becomes "Out of
  Office"; Rejected/Cancelled -> linked Event deleted.

APEX / SCHEDULED JOBS / EXTERNAL WRITERS: none. No Apex class references this
object, and no integration writes to it (unlike most of the org's objects).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 37, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE EMPLOYEE ----------------------------------------------------

Employee__c (Employee) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    THE person taking the leave - a Techsara internal employee (Recruiter__c,
    label "Employee"), never a candidate. Set automatically by the
    Request_Leave flow from the Employee record where the "Create Leave
    Request" button was clicked. 100% populated. The Manager_Decision flow
    walks from here to the employee's Assigned Sr Recruiter to find who may
    approve, and the calendar event description includes this employee's
    name.

Requested_By__c (Requested By) [Lookup -> Employee (standard object)]
    Intended as "who submitted the request", but it points at Salesforce's
    STANDARD Employee object (not Recruiter__c), which is not enabled/
    queryable in this org - SOQL on this field errors out. No flow sets it.
    It sits on the layout but is effectively dead; use Employee__c +
    CreatedById instead. (Broken by design - verify with team.)

--- GROUP B: WHEN - DATES, TIMES & DURATION ----------------------------------

Start_Date__c (Start Date) [Date]
    First day of the leave. For a full-day request the employee picks it
    directly; for a partial-day request the flow copies the single "Leave
    Date" into both Start and End Date. 100% populated in data.

End_Date__c (End Date) [Date]
    Last day of the leave (same as Start_Date for partial-day requests). The
    request screen shows a live "No. Of Leave Days" = End - Start + 1
    counter. Current data spans leaves from Jul 2026 out to Mar 2027.

Is_Full_Day__c (Is Full Day) [Checkbox]
    TRUE = whole-day(s) leave; FALSE = partial day. This is the switch that
    changes the request screen: full day asks for a date range, partial day
    asks for one date plus times. Also makes the calendar event an all-day
    event. In data: 13 of 18 full day.

Is_Half_Day__c (Is Half Day) [Checkbox]
    Flag for a half-day absence. NOT set by the request flow (which uses
    Is_Full_Day + Partial_Day_Type instead) and FALSE on every record -
    appears redundant/legacy against Partial_Day_Type__c.

Partial_Day_Type__c (Partial Day Type) [Picklist]
    Which part of the day a partial leave covers: First Half | Second Half |
    Time Range. Chosen on the request screen when Full Day is unchecked.
    Only 2 of 18 records have it (one First Half, one Second Half).

StartTime__c (Start Time) [Picklist]
    Start of a partial-day leave, chosen from a restricted list of 96
    15-minute slots covering the whole day (12:00 AM ... 11:45 PM). Entered
    on the request screen (partial day only). The flow converts it plus the
    date into Start_DateTime__c. Populated on all 18 records (including
    full-day ones - a data-load artifact).

EndTime__c (End Time) [Picklist]
    End of a partial-day leave, same 96-slot list. The request flow blocks
    saving when End Time is not after Start Time. Populated on all 18.

Start_Time__c (Start Time) [Time]
    OLDER native-Time version of the start time, superseded by the StartTime
    picklist above (same pattern as Interview__c's deprecated time fields).
    Still sits on the page layout, but no flow writes it. (Time fields
    cannot be aggregated in SOQL, so its population was not measurable -
    assume legacy.)

Start_DateTime__c (Start DateTime) [DateTime]
End_DateTime__c (End DateTime) [DateTime]
    The combined date+time window of the leave, computed by the
    Request_Leave flow (full day = midnight to midnight) and used as the
    calendar Event's StartDateTime/EndDateTime. Empty on ALL current records
    - evidence the test data bypassed the flow; expect these filled once the
    real flow path is used.

Total_Days__c (Total Days Requested) [Number(5,2)]
    How many days this request covers (supports half values like 0.5).
    Defaults to 0; NO current automation computes it - the layout doesn't
    even show it, yet 17 of 18 records have a value (sum 24 days), so the
    testers set it by API. Intended input to the paid/unpaid split in the
    future HR phase.

Leave_Year__c (Leave Year) [Number(4,0)]
    The leave-policy year the request counts against (e.g. 2026) - the
    bucket a PTO balance would be tracked per. No automation sets it, yet it
    is filled on all 18 records (values 2026-2027) - loaded with the test
    data. Part of the future balance/accrual design.

--- GROUP C: WHAT KIND OF LEAVE ----------------------------------------------

Leave_Type__c (Leave Type) [Picklist]
    The category of absence, picked by the employee on the request screen:
    PTO (planned paid time off) | Sick | Unpaid (LOP/LWP) (loss of pay /
    leave without pay) | Comp-Off Availed (using earned compensatory time
    off) | Marriage | Paternity | Maternity | Other | Other (HR Only) (a
    special bucket meant for HR to assign, not the employee) | Planned |
    Training. In data: PTO 8, Marriage 4, Comp-Off Availed 4, Sick 1,
    Unpaid 1. The type will drive paid/unpaid and balance logic in the HR
    phase; today it is descriptive only.

Leave_Reason__c (Leave Reason) [LongTextArea]
    Free-text explanation of the leave, required on the request screen. It
    is copied into the calendar event's description, so anyone viewing the
    OOO event sees the reason - do not put sensitive detail here.

--- GROUP D: REQUEST & MANAGER APPROVAL WORKFLOW -----------------------------

Status__c (Status) [Picklist]
    The workflow state. Values: Planned | Approved | Cancelled | Completed |
    Draft | Submitted | Manager Approved | HR Review Required | Rejected.
    Only FOUR are wired to automation today: "Submitted" (set by the
    Request_Leave flow at creation; triggers the tentative calendar event),
    "Approved" (set by the Manager_Decision flow; flips the event to Out of
    Office), "Rejected" (set by Manager_Decision; deletes the event) and
    "Cancelled" (manual; also deletes the event). Planned / Draft /
    Completed / Manager Approved / HR Review Required belong to the unwired
    HR design. Data today: 9 Submitted, 9 Approved.

Requested_On__c (Requested On) [DateTime]
    When the request was submitted - stamped with the current date/time by
    the Request_Leave flow. 100% populated. The raw material for the
    notice-period math (days between request and leave start) in the future
    HR phase.

Manager_Approver__c (Manager Approver) [Lookup -> Employee (standard object)]
    Intended to record which manager decided. Like Requested_By__c it points
    at the disabled STANDARD Employee object and is not queryable - broken.
    The Manager_Decision flow enforces the manager identity but never writes
    this field; the actual approver is only visible via LastModifiedById /
    field history. (Verify with team.)

Manager_Approved_On__c (Manager Approved On) [DateTime]
    Timestamp of the manager's approval, stamped by the Manager_Decision
    flow on Approve and cleared on Reject. Empty on all current records
    (even the 9 "Approved" ones) - more evidence the test data skipped the
    flow.

Rejection_Reason__c (Rejection Reason) [LongTextArea]
    Why the manager rejected the request - collected on the Manager_Decision
    rejection screen, cleared again if the leave is later approved. Shown on
    the layout so the employee can read the reason.

Cancel_Reason__c (Cancel Reason) [LongTextArea]
    Why a leave was cancelled (by the employee or ops) after submission.
    Manual entry on the layout; no flow writes it. Setting Status to
    "Cancelled" is what actually deletes the calendar event.

--- GROUP E: HR APPROVAL, POLICY & PAYROLL (BUILT, NOT YET WIRED) -------------
Everything in this group is part of a designed second approval lane and
payroll calculation that has NO automation behind it yet: no flow or Apex
writes any of these, none are on the page layout, the AIC Portal profile
hides them, and every one is empty/zero on all 18 records. Documented so the
AI knows they exist - do not treat their values as meaningful yet.

Is_HR_Approval_Required__c (Is HR Approval Required) [Checkbox]
    Flag that this request needs HR sign-off on top of the manager (e.g.
    late request or not enough balance). Pairs with the "HR Review Required"
    status value. Default FALSE, never set.

HR_Requirement_Reason__c (HR Requirement Reason) [Picklist]
    WHY HR must review: Late Request (notice period not met) | Insufficient
    Balance (not enough PTO/SL left) | Special Leave (marriage/maternity
    etc.) | Comp-Off (comp-off usage needs verification) | Other. Never
    populated.

HR_Approver__c (HR Approver) [Lookup -> Recruiter__c]
    The HR employee who approved/reviewed - correctly points at Recruiter__c
    (unlike the broken Manager_Approver__c). Never populated.

HR_Approved_On__c (HR Approved On) [DateTime]
    When HR approved. Never populated.

Attachment_Required__c (Attachment Required) [Checkbox]
    Whether proof is needed (e.g. a medical certificate for sick leave).
    Default FALSE, never set.

Supporting_Document_Link__c (Supporting Document) [Url]
    Link to the uploaded proof document the flag above asks for. Never
    populated.

Notice_Given_Days__c (Notice Given (Days)) [Number(6,0)]
    How many days ahead the employee actually asked (leave start minus
    request date). Default 0; nothing computes it yet.

Notice_Required_Days__c (Notice Requirement (Days)) [Number(6,0)]
    How many days of notice policy demands for this leave type/length.
    Default 0; nothing sets it yet.

Notice_Compliance__c (Notice Compliance) [Picklist]
    The verdict of given-vs-required: On Time | Late | Not Applicable.
    Never populated. "Late" is what would trip HR review via the Late
    Request reason.

PTO_Balance_At_Request__c (Balance Snapshot (PTO)) [Number(5,2)]
    The employee's paid-time-off balance frozen at the moment of the request
    (snapshot pattern, like the rate snapshots on Interview__c). Default 0,
    never populated - note there is also no balance ledger object in the org
    yet, so the source of this number is still to be built.

SL_Balance_At_Request__c (Balance Snapshot (SL)) [Number(5,2)]
    Same snapshot for the Sick Leave balance. Default 0, never populated.

Is_Unpaid__c (Is Unpaid) [Checkbox]
    Marks the leave (or its overflow) as unpaid / loss-of-pay. Default
    FALSE, never set; today the "Unpaid (LOP/LWP)" Leave Type value carries
    this meaning descriptively.

Paid_Days__c (Paid Days) [Number(5,2)]
Unpaid_Days__c (Unpaid Days (LOP)) [Number(5,2)]
    The payroll split of Total_Days__c: how many days are covered by balance
    (paid) vs loss-of-pay (unpaid). Both default 0 and are 0 everywhere -
    the calculation that would fill them (balance minus requested days) does
    not exist yet.

--- GROUP F: CALENDAR INTEGRATION --------------------------------------------

Leave_Event_Id__c (Leave Event Id) [Text(18)]
    The Salesforce record Id of the calendar Event created for this leave -
    written by the Tentative_calendar_Event flow right after creation, and
    cleared by the Manager_Decision flow on rejection (the Leave_Event_Sync
    flow deletes the event itself). Note this is an INTERNAL Salesforce
    Event id, not a Google/Zoom id - employee leave does not touch the
    external calendar integrations. Empty on all 18 current records because
    the test data bypassed the flows.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 18, ALL created 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-06, covering only 2
  distinct employees - a fresh test batch for a feature still in build/UAT.
- Auto-number names run A-0128 to A-0147: roughly 147 leaves were created
  historically and ~130 deleted across earlier test cycles.
- Ghost data from those cycles: 115 calendar Events with an Employee Leave
  link (subjects "LV-A-0121" etc., created Jan-Jun 2026) still exist but
  point at deleted leave records - 105 "Tentative", 10 "Out of Office".
- Status: Submitted 9 | Approved 9 (no Rejected/Cancelled/other yet).
- Leave Type: PTO 8 | Marriage 4 | Comp-Off Availed 4 | Sick 1 |
  Unpaid (LOP/LWP) 1. (Paternity/Maternity/Training etc. unused so far.)
- Full day 13 | partial day 5; Partial_Day_Type set on only 2 (1 First Half,
  1 Second Half). Leave dates span 2026-07-30 to 2027-03-24; Total Days sum

  Partial-day extras beyond the 2 noted).
- Data-quality flags: the 18 records look hand-loaded (flow-stamped fields
  empty while non-flow fields are filled; 9 records say "Approved" with no
  approval timestamp). Manager_Approver__c and Requested_By__c are not
  queryable at all (they reference the disabled standard Employee object).
- Key takeaway for answering questions: treat Employee Leave as a NEW,
  half-launched HR mini-app - the request + manager-approval + calendar
  loop is real and active; the balances/notice/HR-review layer is schema
  only; and current record values are test data, not real leave history.

PART 8: CANDIDATE PORTAL CUSTOM AUTH
