################################################################################

================================================================================
OBJECT: Candidate_Portal_Credential__c  (Label: "Candidate Portal Credential")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Candidate_Portal_Credential__c is the LOGIN ACCOUNT of one candidate on the
custom candidate portal. One record = one username/password pair, linked to
the candidate's Person Account. This is NOT standard Salesforce
authentication: candidates are not Salesforce users and hold no license.
Instead, the portal pages run as the site's Guest User, and Techsara's own
Apex (AuthService) checks the username/password against this object, creates
a Candidate_Portal_Session__c, and hands the browser a session token. The
credential record also carries the account-security state: active/disabled
switch, failed-login counter, temporary lockout timestamp and last login.

Think of it as the "users table" of a custom web application that happens to
live inside Salesforce.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the candidate-portal custom-auth cluster (with
  Candidate_Portal_Session__c).
- LOOKUP to Account via Candidate__c (the candidate this login belongs to).
  Not master-detail; the credential is its own record.
- Sharing model Public Read/Write - but sharing is effectively irrelevant:
  the Guest User has no record access, and all reads/writes go through
  "without sharing" Apex (AuthService / CandidateContext) using SYSTEM_MODE
  DML. Security is enforced in code, not by the sharing model.
- 7 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views.
- Auto-number Name "Candidate Credentials Number" in format CCN-{00000}.
- Scale: 2 records in preprod (the feature is brand new - Aug 2026).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every credential record is the same flavor - one login per candidate.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - PROVISIONING. A staff member creates the credential record manually
  (there is no flow or Apex that creates credentials today): pick the
  candidate Account, type a Username and Password, tick Is Active. The
  classic "Candidate Portal Credential Layout" is the entry screen.

STEP 2 - LOGIN. The candidate opens the portal login page (the candidateLogin
  LWC on the candidate Experience site) and enters username + password. The
  page calls AuthService.login() which:
  - finds the credential by Username__c;
  - rejects disabled accounts ("Account is disabled...") and accounts still
    inside a lockout window ("Account temporarily locked...");
  - compares the password using a constant-time compare (so response timing
    leaks nothing). A wrong password increments Failed_Login_Count__c; at 5
    failures the account locks for 15 minutes (Locked_Until__c);
  - on success creates a Candidate_Portal_Session__c valid for 7 days,
    resets the failure counter, clears the lockout and stamps
    Last_Login_At__c, then returns the session token to the browser.
  All wrong-username / wrong-password paths return the same generic
  "Invalid username or password" so attackers cannot probe for usernames.

STEP 3 - EVERY LATER PORTAL CALL. The browser sends the session token; the
  CandidateContext class re-validates it and follows
  Candidate_Credential__r.Candidate__c to know WHICH candidate is calling.
  Every portal query then filters by that candidate id - the credential is
  the anchor of the whole portal security model.

STEP 4 - FORGOT LOGIN. The candidate enters their email on the login page;
  AuthService.recoverLogin() finds the Account by Email_replica__c, finds
  this credential, and emails the username AND password to the ACCOUNT
  OWNER (the candidate's recruiter/point of contact) - deliberately not to
  the candidate-typed email - who then shares it with the candidate.

SECURITY CAVEAT (stated in the code itself): Password__c is stored in PLAIN
TEXT - acceptable only while this is sandbox data. The class header commits
to swapping in SHA-256 hashing (and rewriting recovery as a one-time reset
link) before production data lands.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Account (via Candidate__c, Lookup): the candidate (Person Account) this
  login belongs to. Child relationship name: Candidate_Portal_Credentials.
  100% populated (2 of 2). The recoverLogin path also uses the Account's
  Email_replica__c and Owner to route the recovery email.

CHILDREN / REFERENCES:
- Candidate_Portal_Session__c (via Candidate_Credential__c, Lookup): the
  active and past login sessions minted from this credential. Deactivating
  the credential (Is_Active__c = false) instantly kills all its sessions,
  because every session check also verifies the credential is active.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. All rules (lockout, active check, generic error messages) are enforced
in the AuthService Apex class instead of validation rules.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No flows, no triggers, no scheduled jobs touch this object. All writes come
from Apex:
- AuthService.login(): increments Failed_Login_Count__c on bad passwords,
  sets/clears Locked_Until__c, stamps Last_Login_At__c, resets the counter
  on success (all via SYSTEM_MODE DML as the Guest User).
- AuthService.recoverLogin(): reads the record to email the credentials to
  the Account Owner.
- CandidateContext: reads Candidate_Credential__r.Is_Active__c and
  .Candidate__c on every portal call to validate the session.
Guest-user access comes from the "Candidate_Portal_Guest_Access" permission
set (read-only object access + the portal Apex classes); record creation is
manual by internal staff.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 7, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: IDENTITY & LINKAGE ----------------------------------------------

Candidate__c (Candidate) [Lookup -> Account]
    Which candidate (Person Account) this login belongs to. Set by the staff
    member who provisions the credential. This is the field the entire
    portal security model resolves to: every session check follows
    credential -> Candidate__c and then filters all portal data by that id.
    100% populated.

Username__c (Username) [Text, required, unique]
    The login name the candidate types on the portal sign-in page. Must be
    unique org-wide (database-enforced). Chosen by the provisioning staff
    member; also included in the recovery email to the Account Owner.

Password__c (Password) [Text, required]
    The candidate's portal password - currently stored as PLAIN TEXT
    (sandbox-only decision, documented in AuthService; to be replaced with a
    SHA-256 hash before production). Compared with a constant-time equals in
    Apex. Never expose this field in reports, layouts for portal users, or
    integrations.

--- GROUP B: ACCOUNT STATE & LOCKOUT -----------------------------------------

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    The kill switch. Staff untick it to disable the candidate's portal
    access; login is refused ("Account is disabled") and every existing
    session immediately fails validation. Both current records are active.

Failed_Login_Count__c (Failed Login Count) [Number(3,0)]
    Consecutive wrong-password attempts, incremented by AuthService on each
    failure and reset to 0 on a successful login. Reaching 5 triggers the
    temporary lockout below. Currently 0 on both records.

Locked_Until__c (Locked Until) [DateTime]
    End of the temporary lockout window - set to now + 15 minutes when the
    failure counter hits 5. While this is in the future, login attempts are
    refused even with the right password. Cleared on successful login. A
    staff member can also clear it manually to unlock early. Empty on all
    current records (no lockout has happened yet).

Last_Login_At__c (Last Login At) [DateTime]
    When this candidate last signed in successfully, stamped by
    AuthService.login(). Useful for "is the candidate actually using the
    portal" adoption checks. Populated on both records (latest 2026-08-06).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 2 (created 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-06 - the custom portal
  auth is brand new and effectively in pilot).
- Both records: Is_Active__c = true, Candidate__c populated, Last_Login_At__c
  populated (latest login 2026-08-06). Failed_Login_Count__c = 0 and
  Locked_Until__c empty on both - the lockout machinery has not fired yet.
- Key takeaway: treat this object as a just-launched feature; questions
  about "how candidates log in today" should note that only a couple of
  pilot candidates have portal logins so far.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Candidate_Portal_Session__c  (Label: "Candidate Portal Session")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Candidate_Portal_Session__c is ONE login session of a candidate on the custom
candidate portal - the equivalent of a web app's "sessions table". When a
candidate signs in successfully (AuthService.login), one record is created
holding a cryptographically random session token, a 7-day expiry, the
originating IP address and an activity heartbeat. The browser keeps the
token and sends it with every portal request; the CandidateContext Apex
class looks the session up, checks it is active/unexpired and resolves the
calling candidate from it. Logging out (or expiry, or disabling the parent
credential) deactivates the session.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, the runtime half of the candidate-portal custom-auth
  cluster (Candidate_Portal_Credential__c is the account half).
- LOOKUP to Candidate_Portal_Credential__c via Candidate_Credential__c.
- Sharing model Public Read/Write - moot in practice: only "without sharing"
  Apex touches it (the Guest User permission set does grant Create on this
  object, needed so the login transaction can insert the session).
- 7 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views.
- Auto-number Name "Candidate Session Number" in format CSN-{00000}.
- Scale: 5 records in preprod (Aug 2026 pilot).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every session record is the same flavor.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATED AT LOGIN. AuthService.login() inserts the session with a
  fresh random token (256-bit AES key, base64url-encoded), Expires_At__c =
  now + 7 days, Is_Active__c = true, Last_Activity_At__c = now, and the
  client IP (passed in from the login LWC, which resolves it via an external
  who-am-i endpoint because guest Apex cannot read the caller IP itself).

STEP 2 - VALIDATED ON EVERY PORTAL CALL. Every @AuraEnabled method in
  CandidatePortalController starts with CandidateContext.fromSession(token):
  - token not found, Is_Active__c false, expiry passed, parent credential
    inactive or unlinked -> the user gets a uniform "Session expired" error;
  - an expired-but-still-active record is flipped to Is_Active__c = false on
    the spot (lazy cleanup - there is no scheduled purge job);
  - on success the "sliding heartbeat" stamps Last_Activity_At__c = now.
  Methods that make HTTP callouts (e.g. the S3 upload URL request) use a
  read-only variant that skips the heartbeat write until after the callout,
  because Salesforce forbids callouts after DML in one transaction.

STEP 3 - ENDED. Logout (AuthService.logout) sets Is_Active__c = false; or
  the session silently dies at Expires_At__c; or it dies with its parent
  credential when staff deactivate the candidate's login. Old rows stay in
  the database as an audit trail of who signed in from where and when.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Candidate_Portal_Credential__c (via Candidate_Credential__c, Lookup): the
  login account this session was minted from. Child relationship name:
  Candidate_Portal_Sessions. 100% populated. The session inherits its
  candidate identity through this link (credential -> Candidate__c ->
  Account) - the session itself never stores the candidate id.

CHILDREN / REFERENCES:
- Nothing points at this object. It is a leaf: pure runtime/audit state.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Session integrity (expiry, active checks, uniform error messages) is
enforced entirely in the CandidateContext / AuthService Apex classes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No flows, no triggers, no scheduled jobs. All lifecycle is Apex:
- AuthService.login() creates the record; AuthService.logout() deactivates
  it (both SYSTEM_MODE DML as the Guest User).
- CandidateContext.resolveSession() validates it on every portal call,
  writes the Last_Activity_At__c heartbeat, and lazily deactivates expired
  sessions when they are next presented.
- CandidateContext.touchHeartbeat() writes the heartbeat separately after
  callout-bearing methods finish.
Note there is NO scheduled cleanup: expired sessions that are never
presented again simply remain active-flagged rows until touched.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 7, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: SESSION IDENTITY ------------------------------------------------

Session_Id__c (Session Id) [Text, required, unique, external id]
    The bearer token itself: a base64url encoding of a 256-bit random value,
    generated by AuthService at login. Unique (database-enforced) and marked
    external id so the per-call lookup is indexed. Whoever holds this string
    IS the candidate as far as the portal is concerned - treat the field as
    a secret; never expose it in reports or UI.

Candidate_Credential__c (Candidate Credential) [Lookup ->
Candidate_Portal_Credential__c]
    The login account this session belongs to. Set once by AuthService at
    creation, 100% populated. Every session validation walks this lookup to
    confirm the credential is still active and to resolve the candidate.

--- GROUP B: LIFECYCLE & AUDIT -----------------------------------------------

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    Whether the session is currently usable. Set true at login; set false by
    logout or by the lazy expiry cleanup in CandidateContext. In current
    data 3 of 5 sessions are active, 2 ended.

Expires_At__c (Expires At) [DateTime]
    Hard end-of-life: login time + 7 days (constant in AuthService). After
    this moment every validation fails with "Session expired" and the row is
    deactivated when next seen. 100% populated.

Created_At__c (Created At) [DateTime]
    Intended "session started" stamp, but AuthService never fills it -
    0 of 5 records have a value. The standard CreatedDate system field
    carries this information instead. Effectively unused
    (not fully documented - verify with team whether it should be removed).

Last_Activity_At__c (Last Activity At) [DateTime]
    The sliding heartbeat: refreshed to "now" on every successful portal
    call (or right after a callout completes). Answers "when was this
    candidate last actually using the portal" - useful for engagement
    monitoring. 100% populated. Note it is analytics-only: activity does NOT
    extend Expires_At__c.

IP_Address__c (IP Address) [Text(45)]
    The IP address the candidate signed in from (help text: "Populated
    automatically"). Supplied by the login LWC (guest Apex cannot resolve
    the caller IP), truncated defensively to 45 chars (fits IPv6). Audit /
    anomaly-spotting value. 100% populated.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 5, created 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-06 (pilot period, matching
  the 2 credential records - a couple of logins each).
- Active: 3 active / 2 ended.
- Population: Candidate_Credential__c, Expires_At__c, Last_Activity_At__c
  and IP_Address__c on 5 of 5; Created_At__c on 0 of 5 (never written -
  use CreatedDate instead).
- Key takeaway: tiny pilot dataset; the object's importance is architectural
  (it is the session backbone of the candidate portal), not analytical.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Onboarding_Token__c  (Label: "Onboarding Token")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Onboarding_Token__c is a ONE-TIME, EXPIRING LINK sent to a candidate so they
can fill in their onboarding intake form WITHOUT logging in anywhere. When
staff click "Send Onboarding Form" on an Onboarding record, a short signed
token is generated, stored here, embedded in a public URL
(<candidate hub site>/s/onboarding-form?token=XXXX) and emailed to the
candidate. The candidate opens the link as a guest; a screen flow looks the
token up, checks it is not expired/used, walks them through the intake
screens, and on submit stamps the token used. One record = one issued link,
with its full lifecycle (Sent -> Opened -> Submitted, or Expired/Cancelled).

This is the third leg of the org's custom token machinery: portal
credentials/sessions cover the logged-in candidate portal, while
Onboarding_Token__c (and its sibling pattern on Pre_Enrolment_Request__c)
covers no-login guest form links.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object in the Onboarding domain (child of Onboarding__c).
- LOOKUP to Onboarding__c via Onboarding__c (which onboarding case the link
  belongs to).
- Sharing model Public Read/Write; the guest form flow runs in system mode
  without sharing, so record access is handled by the flow, not sharing.
- 8 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Auto-number Name "Onboarding Token Number" in format OTN-{0000}.
- Scale: 2 records in preprod (feature is new - both from 2026-07-29).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every token record is the same flavor - one issued onboarding link.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - STAFF SEND THE FORM. On an Onboarding record, a user clicks the
  "Send Onboarding Form" quick action (on the Onboarding Lightning record
  page and classic layout), launching the screen flow
  Onboarding_Send_Candidate_Onboarding_form. The flow:
  - EXPIRES any still-open token for the same onboarding (status Sent /
    Opened / Draft becomes "Expired") so only one live link exists at a
    time;
  - calls the CreateToken Apex action with the metadata secret
    "Onboarding_Flow_Secret" to mint a 12-character token (6 hex chars of
    an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the record id + expiry, plus 6 random hex
    chars, uppercased) valid for 2 days;
  - creates the Onboarding_Token__c record (status "Sent") with the token,
    expiry, recipient email and the full public link built as
    {Candidate_Hub_URL custom label} + "/s/onboarding-form?token=" + token
    (the label currently points at the /talent Experience site in preprod);
  - emails the link to the candidate's PersonEmail (cc the Account owner)
    from noreply@techsarasolutions.com using the "Onboarding Request Form"
    email template, and sets Candidate_form_sent__c on the Onboarding.

STEP 2 - CANDIDATE OPENS THE LINK. The guest-accessible onboarding-form page
  runs the screen flow Onboarding_Candidate_Intake_1 (active; an older
  draft, Onboarding_Candidate_Intake, is superseded). The flow looks the
  token up by Token__c and rejects the visit if Expires_At__c has passed or
  the status is already Expired / Submitted / Cancelled ("link used").
  Otherwise it marks the token "Opened" and shows the intake screens
  (personal details, education history, course selection etc., prefilled
  from the candidate's existing data).

STEP 3 - CANDIDATE SUBMITS. On the final screen the flow sets Used__c =
  true, Used_At__c = now, status = "Submitted", writes the collected data to
  the Account / Education_History__c etc., and updates the parent
  Onboarding record's Latest_Onboarding_Status__c. The link is now dead -
  reopening it hits the "link used" branch.

STEP 4 - IF THE LINK DIES UNUSED. Tokens past their 2-day expiry are treated
  as dead on open; re-sending the form from the quick action expires the old
  token and issues a fresh one.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Onboarding__c (via Onboarding__c, Lookup): the candidate-onboarding case
  this link was issued for. Child relationship name: Onboarding_Tokens
  (visible as a related list on the Onboarding layout). 100% populated. The
  send flow flips Onboarding__c.Candidate_form_sent__c and the intake flow
  updates Onboarding__c.Latest_Onboarding_Status__c through this link.

CHILDREN / REFERENCES:
- Nothing points at this object.

RELATED PATTERN (not a relationship): the pre-enrolment form uses the SAME
CreateToken Apex action but stores its token directly on
Pre_Enrolment_Request__c (Public_Token__c) - do not confuse the two.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Expiry, single-use and duplicate-link rules are enforced by the two
flows (send + intake), not by validation rules.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCREEN FLOWS (both run in system mode without sharing):
- Onboarding_Send_Candidate_Onboarding_form (active; launched by the
  "Send Onboarding Form" quick action on Onboarding__c): expires prior open
  tokens, creates the new token record, sends the email. Uses the Apex
  action CreateToken with Token_Secret__mdt "Onboarding_Flow_Secret".
- Onboarding_Candidate_Intake_1 (active; the guest onboarding-form page):
  looks the token up, sets status Opened on first view, and on submit sets
  Used__c / Used_At__c / status Submitted.
- Onboarding_Candidate_Intake (DRAFT - an earlier version of the intake
  flow; inactive, superseded by _1).
APEX:
- CreateToken (invocable, "Generate Pre Enrollment Token"): generates the
  token string; it does not itself write Onboarding_Token__c records.
No triggers, record-triggered flows or scheduled jobs exist on this object;
in particular nothing sweeps expired tokens - they are only marked Expired
when re-sent over or when the candidate tries to open them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 8, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE TOKEN & THE LINK --------------------------------------------

Token__c (Token) [Text(64), required, unique, external id]
    The 12-character one-time code (6 HMAC-SHA256 hex chars signed with the
    Onboarding_Flow_Secret + 6 random hex chars, uppercased), minted by the
    CreateToken Apex action. Unique and indexed (external id) because the
    guest intake flow looks records up by it on every form visit. Treat as
    a secret - anyone holding it can open the candidate's form.

Onboarding_Form_Link__c (Onboarding Form Link) [Text(255)]
    The complete clickable URL sent to the candidate:
    {Candidate_Hub_URL}/s/onboarding-form?token={Token__c}. Built and stored
    by the send flow so staff can see/copy the exact link that went out.
    100% populated.

Onboarding__c (Onboarding) [Lookup -> Onboarding__c]
    The onboarding case this link belongs to - set by the send flow from the
    record the quick action was clicked on. 100% populated. Also the key the
    send flow uses to find-and-expire older open links for the same case.

Recipient_Email__c (Recipient Email) [Email]
    Where the link was sent - copied by the send flow from the Onboarding
    record's candidate email at send time (a snapshot, so later email
    changes don't obscure where THIS link actually went). 100% populated.

--- GROUP B: LIFECYCLE & USAGE TRACKING --------------------------------------

Onboarding_Form_Status__c (Onboarding Form Status) [Picklist]
    The link's lifecycle state:
    - Sent: created and emailed, not yet opened (set by the send flow).
    - Opened: the candidate has opened the form page at least once (set by
      the intake flow on first valid visit).
    - Submitted: the candidate completed and submitted the form (terminal;
      set by the intake flow together with Used__c).
    - Expired: dead - either superseded by a newer link (the send flow
      expires old Sent/Opened/Draft tokens) or past its 2-day life when the
      candidate tried it.
    - Cancelled: manually voided by staff (no automation sets it; terminal -
      the intake flow refuses Cancelled tokens).
    - Draft: defined in the picklist and checked by both flows, but no
      automation ever sets it (not fully documented - verify with team).
    Current data: 1 Sent, 1 Expired.

Expires_At__c (Expires At) [DateTime]
    Hard deadline for using the link: send time + 2 days (formula in the
    send flow, returned by CreateToken). The intake flow rejects any visit
    after this moment. 100% populated.

Used__c (Used) [Checkbox]
    TRUE once the form has been submitted with this token - the single-use
    guarantee. Set by the intake flow at submission, never by users. FALSE
    on both current records (no candidate has completed the form in preprod
    yet).

Used_At__c (Used At) [DateTime]
    Exact moment of submission, stamped by the intake flow alongside
    Used__c. Empty on all current records.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)

- Total records: 2, both created within two minutes on 2026-07-29 (a test
  send followed by a re-send - the first token was auto-expired by the

- Status: Sent 1 | Expired 1. Used__c false on both; Used_At__c empty

================================================================================
OBJECT: In_App_Checklist_Settings__c  (Label: "In App Checklist Settings")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
In_App_Checklist_Settings__c is a HIERARCHY CUSTOM SETTING (not a normal
object - no tabs, no records users browse) that stores configuration for
Salesforce's own "Sales Cloud In-App Checklist" - the guided setup checklist
Salesforce shows inside new Sales Cloud orgs. Its description reads: "This
custom settings contains all attributes used in In App Checklist." It holds
an encrypted profile key and the URL of the Salesforce-hosted checklist
page. This is SALESFORCE-MANAGED PLUMBING, not something Techsara built:
no Techsara Apex, flow, LWC or report references it anywhere in the org.
It sits in this documentation cluster only because it is a settings-style
object; it has nothing to do with the candidate portal or its token auth.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom setting, type HIERARCHY (values can be set org-wide and overridden
  per profile or per user), visibility PROTECTED.
- No sharing model, no owner, no tab - custom settings live outside the
  normal record security model and are read via the setup hierarchy.
- 2 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views.
- Scale: 3 rows in preprod - 1 org-wide default + 2 profile-level overrides.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom settings cannot have record types.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
There is no Techsara business process on this object. Salesforce's Sales
Cloud onboarding feature wrote these rows (an org default plus two profile
overrides) so that its in-app checklist component can identify the org/
profile (ProfileKey__c) and load the checklist content from a
Salesforce-hosted page (Sales_Cloud_In_App_Page__c). Nothing in the org's
custom code, flows or pages reads or writes it. For the role-hierarchy /
security redesign it can be safely ignored; it is also a candidate for
cleanup if the org ever prunes unused metadata (verify with team before
deleting - Salesforce features may still read it at runtime).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom settings cannot have lookups to or from other objects. The
only linkage is the implicit SetupOwnerId of each row (the org for the
default row, a Profile for the two override rows).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom settings do not support validation rules.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None in the org. No Apex class, trigger, flow or component in force-app
references this setting; only Salesforce's own in-app checklist feature
reads it (from outside the org's metadata).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 2, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: SALESFORCE CHECKLIST CONFIG -------------------------------------

ProfileKey__c (ProfileKey) [Text(255)]
    An encrypted/opaque key written by Salesforce's checklist feature to
    identify the org/profile context to the hosted checklist service. Each
    of the 3 rows carries a different base64-looking value (values not
    reproduced here - treat as an internal key). Not set or read by any
    Techsara automation.

Sales_Cloud_In_App_Page__c (Sales Cloud In App Page) [Url]
    The Salesforce-hosted page the in-app checklist iframe loads. All 3 rows
    point at the same endpoint:
    https://cloud.mail.salesforce.com/SalesCloudInAppChecklistV2?
    Not set or read by any Techsara automation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- All 3 rows have both fields populated; the page URL is identical on all

- Key takeaway: Salesforce-managed leftovers from the Sales Cloud in-app
  onboarding checklist; zero Techsara usage - safe to ignore when answering

================================================================================
OBJECT: Token_Secret__mdt  (Label: "Token Secret")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Token_Secret__mdt is a CUSTOM METADATA TYPE that stores the SIGNING SECRETS
used to mint the org's one-time form tokens. Each row is a named secret
(e.g. "Onboarding Flow Secret"); the CreateToken Apex action looks a row up
by its developer name and uses its Value__c as the HMAC-SHA256 key when
generating a token for an onboarding or pre-enrolment link. Keeping the
secrets in custom metadata means admins can rotate them from Setup without
touching code, different features get different keys, and the values deploy
with the org (note: custom metadata is NOT encrypted at rest and is visible
to anyone with Setup access - a known trade-off).

SECURITY: the actual secret values are deliberately NOT reproduced in this
document. Only row names and counts are recorded.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom METADATA TYPE (__mdt) - rows are configuration deployed/edited via
  Setup, not data records; they have no owner and no sharing.
- 1 custom field (Value__c) plus the standard DeveloperName / MasterLabel
  every metadata type has.
- 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views.
- Scale: 3 rows in preprod. The rows are NOT in the force-app source
  (no customMetadata/ folder) - they exist only in the org.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom metadata types cannot have record types.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
When a staff member sends a candidate a one-time form link, the launching
flow passes a secret's developer name into the CreateToken Apex action:
- Onboarding_Send_Candidate_Onboarding_form passes "Onboarding_Flow_Secret"
  when minting an Onboarding_Token__c link;
- send_pre_enrollment_form passes its secret name (row
  "Pre_Enrollment_Flow_Secret") when minting the pre-enrolment link stored
  on Pre_Enrolment_Request__c.Public_Token__c;
- the third row, "Test_Secret", exists for the CreateTokenTest unit tests.
CreateToken queries SELECT Value__c FROM Token_Secret__mdt WHERE
DeveloperName = :name, computes HMAC-SHA256 over (record id + expiry
timestamp) with that value as the key, and folds 6 hex chars of the
signature plus 6 random hex chars into the 12-character token. Because each
feature has its own named secret, rotating one (paste a new value in Setup)
invalidates nothing else. Rotation does, however, orphan any not-yet-used
tokens minted under the old secret only if the token were ever re-verified
against the HMAC - today the flows match tokens by exact string lookup, so
the HMAC is tamper-evidence in the token itself rather than a re-checked
signature.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom metadata types have no lookups in this org. Functionally it
feeds (via CreateToken) the token fields on Onboarding_Token__c and
Pre_Enrolment_Request__c, but there is no database relationship.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom metadata rows are maintained by admins in Setup.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Read-only consumer: the CreateToken invocable Apex class (label "Generate
Pre Enrollment Token") is the ONLY code that queries this type. It is
invoked by two active screen flows - Onboarding_Send_Candidate_Onboarding_
form and send_pre_enrollment_form. Nothing writes rows at runtime (custom
metadata cannot be written by flows or normal Apex anyway).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (1 custom field, plus standard metadata fields)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE SECRET ------------------------------------------------------

Value__c (Value) [Text(255)]
    The signing secret itself - the HMAC-SHA256 key CreateToken uses when
    generating tokens under this row's name. Entered/rotated manually by an
    admin in Setup. SECRET: never expose in documents, reports, debug logs
    or emails (values intentionally omitted here). Populated on all 3 rows.

DeveloperName / MasterLabel (standard metadata identity fields) [Text]
    The row's API name and label. The developer name is the key flows pass
    to CreateToken. Rows in preprod: Onboarding_Flow_Secret ("Onboarding
    Flow Secret"), Pre_Enrollment_Flow_Secret ("Pre Enrollment Flow
    Secret"), Test_Secret ("Test Secret").

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total rows: 3 - Onboarding_Flow_Secret (onboarding form links),
  Pre_Enrollment_Flow_Secret (pre-enrolment form links), Test_Secret (unit
  tests). All 3 have Value__c populated (values not recorded here).
- Key takeaway: this is the key-ring of the org's one-time-link machinery;
  if a form link ever needs to be invalidated wholesale, rotating the
  matching secret in Setup is the lever - but remember custom metadata
  values are readable by anyone with Setup access.

PART 9: BILLING (QUICKBOOKS)
################################################################################
################################################################################

================================================================================
OBJECT: Invoice__c  (Label: "Invoice")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Invoice__c is one bill Techsara issues to a PERSON it is charging - in practice
a candidate (Person Account) or a not-yet-converted website Lead who is buying
a paid career-coaching service package (the packages sold are the QB Plans:
"Career Accelerator" and "Ultimate Career Architect"). It is NOT client/B2B
placement billing - no invoice links to a Job Requirement, Onboarding or
client company today.

The record is the Salesforce mirror of a real invoice living in QUICKBOOKS
ONLINE. The QuickBooks integration creates the invoice inside QuickBooks,
emails it to the customer from QuickBooks, and stores the QuickBooks ids and
links on this record. When the customer pays (online card payment or a
recorded payment in QuickBooks), a webhook pushes the payment back into
Salesforce as a child Payment__c record and recomputes this invoice's status.
The object also supports a Salesforce-only INSTALLMENT PAYMENT PLAN: a screen
flow splits the invoice amount into N monthly "Scheduled" Payment__c children.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, the head of the small QuickBooks billing domain (Invoice__c
  -> Payment__c children, QB_Plan__c custom setting as the price list).
- Standalone parent: OWD sharing is PRIVATE and the record has its own owner
  (unlike most billing-adjacent objects it is NOT a child of Account - the
  Candidate__c link is a plain lookup, not master-detail).
- MASTER of Payment__c: Payment records are master-detail children and roll
  their paid amounts up into Amount_Paid__c.
- 25 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Auto-number Name in the format INV-{0000}.
- Scale: 87 records in preprod (Dec 2024 to Jul 2026) - a small, lightly used
  object compared to the recruiting core.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every invoice is the same shape; the QB_Created_From__c picklist (Lead /
Account / Manual) carries the "where did this come from" signal instead.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATION. Four entry points, all buttons:
  - "Send Invoice" on a LEAD page (screen flow QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks,
    on the B2B Client Lead / B2B Website Candidate / three-column Lead record
    pages): the sales user picks a QB Plan and amount; the flow searches
    QuickBooks for the customer (creating one if needed via the QuickBooks
    external services), creates the invoice inside QuickBooks, emails it to
    the customer from QuickBooks, and then saves the Invoice__c record with
    Lead__c, amounts/dates, QB_Created_From = "Lead", the QuickBooks invoice
    id and the email status.
  - "Send Invoice" on a CANDIDATE (Person Account) page (screen flow
    QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks_For_Account, on Candidate_Record_Page1):
    same QuickBooks choreography for a converted candidate; it also writes
    the QuickBooks customer id and address/contact data back onto the
    candidate Account (Account.QB_Customer_ID__c).
  - "Initiate Payment Plan" on ACCOUNT pages (screen flow
    Initiate_Payment_Plan, placed on the B2B Client Account and Vendor
    Account record pages + classic Account layout): a SALESFORCE-ONLY path
    with no QuickBooks callout. The user enters invoice number, total amount,
    plan duration in months (1-24, capped by the Maximum_Payment_Plan_
    Duration custom label) and a future first-payment date; the flow shows
    the computed schedule, requires an "I have reviewed the payment plan"
    confirmation, then creates the Invoice__c (Candidate__c = the account)
    plus one "Scheduled"/"Partial" Payment__c per month, each for an equal
    share of the amount. Runs in system mode without sharing.
  - LEGACY: the "Create Invoice" button on Lead pages and "Record Offer
    Letter Payment" on Account pages still point at the OBSOLETE flow
    Create_Invoice_Payment - these buttons are effectively dead and error if
    clicked (the flow has no active version).
STEP 2 - SLACK ANNOUNCEMENT. On creation, the record-triggered flow
  QB_Invoice_Creation_Update_Slack_Notifications posts the new invoice to
  Slack (a different message variant for recurring/subscription invoices),
  with one scheduled follow-up path.
STEP 3 - THE CUSTOMER PAYS IN QUICKBOOKS. QuickBooks calls the public site
  "QuickBooks_Webhook" -> Apex QB_QuickBooksWebhookListener (REST endpoint
  /quickbooks/webhook/*) -> autolaunched flow QB_Process_Payment_Webhook.
  The flow fetches the payment details from QuickBooks and, per operation:
  - Create: dedupe-checks by QuickBooks payment id, finds the invoice by
    QB_Invoice_Id__c, creates a "Paid" Payment__c child (Full or Partial by
    amount), and sets Invoice_Status__c to Not Paid / Partially Paid / Paid
    by comparing the applied amount to Invoice_Amount__c.
  - Update: refreshes the payment's amounts and recomputes the status.
  - Void: zeroes the payment, marks it "Void", and sets the invoice's
    status to "Dispute".
STEP 4 - EDITS AND REMINDERS. The "Edit Invoice" quick action (screen flow
  QB_Edit_Invoice) changes amount/dates on BOTH the QuickBooks invoice and
  the Salesforce record and can re-send the invoice email; the "Invoice
  Reminder" button on the invoice page (flow QB_Send_Invoice_Reminder) just
  re-emails the invoice through QuickBooks.
STEP 5 - LEAD CONVERSION RELINK. When a Lead with invoices converts, the
  record-triggered flow Update_Invoice_Records_with_Candidate_Details finds
  all invoices pointing at that Lead and stamps Candidate__c with the new
  Person Account, so billing history follows the candidate.
STEP 6 - COLLECTION TRACKING. Payment children roll up into Amount_Paid__c;
  Outstanding_Amount__c shows what is still owed; finance works the "Not
  Paid" / "Partially Paid" invoices.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM INVOICE TO OTHER OBJECTS:
- Account (Candidate__c, lookup, rel name "Invoices"): the candidate (Person
  Account) being billed. 51% populated; auto-set by the Account send flow and
  the payment-plan flow, and backfilled on lead conversion.
- Lead (Lead__c, lookup, rel name "Invoices"): the pre-conversion website
  lead being billed (the sales team often invoices before conversion). 38%
  populated. 26 records carry BOTH lead and candidate (invoiced as a lead,
  then converted); 36 records (41%) carry NEITHER - mostly older/manual or
  payment-plan test records, so do not assume every invoice reaches a person
  record.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT INVOICE:
- Payment__c (MASTER-DETAIL child, rel name "Payments"): one row per money
  event - a webhook-recorded QuickBooks payment or a planned installment.
  Shown as the only related list on the invoice record page.

EXTERNAL COUNTERPARTS (not Salesforce records):
- The QuickBooks Online invoice (QB_Invoice_Id__c / Invoice_Id__c) and the
  QuickBooks customer (QB_Customer_Id__c via the Lead/Account).

EXPLICIT NON-RELATIONSHIPS: no link to Job_Requirement__c, Job_Submission__c,
Onboarding__c, Vendor__c or any client company - as built, this object bills
INDIVIDUALS for coaching services, not B2B clients for placements.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. There are no validation rules on Invoice__c; the guardrails live inside
the Initiate_Payment_Plan flow instead (first payment date must be in the
future, duration 1-24 months, duplicate-invoice-number fault handling).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOWS (active):
- QB_Invoice_Creation_Update_Slack_Notifications (after save, create, +1
  scheduled path): Slack post announcing the new invoice; separate message
  for recurring invoices.
- Update_Invoice_Records_with_Candidate_Details (on Lead, after save, when
  Status changes to Converted): re-links this lead's invoices to the newly
  created candidate Account (sets Candidate__c).

AUTOLAUNCHED FLOW (called by Apex, not by record changes):
- QB_Process_Payment_Webhook: invoked by QB_QuickBooksWebhookListener for
  each QuickBooks Payment event; creates/updates/voids Payment__c children
  and recomputes Invoice_Status__c (Void -> "Dispute").

SCREEN FLOWS / BUTTONS:
- QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks ("Send Invoice" on Lead) and
  QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks_For_Account ("Send Invoice" on the candidate
  Account page): create the invoice in QuickBooks + Salesforce and email it.
- QB_Edit_Invoice ("Edit Invoice" quick action): sync edits to QuickBooks.
- QB_Send_Invoice_Reminder ("Invoice Reminder" on the invoice page): re-send
  the invoice email through QuickBooks.
- Initiate_Payment_Plan ("Initiate Payment Plan" on Account pages): create
  invoice + monthly scheduled Payment__c installments (no QuickBooks call).
- Create_Invoice_Payment (OBSOLETE - no active version) is still wired to
  the "Create Invoice" (Lead) and "Record Offer Letter Payment" (Account)
  buttons; those buttons are currently dead.

APEX:
- QB_QuickBooksWebhookListener (@RestResource /quickbooks/webhook/*, exposed
  through the public "QuickBooks_Webhook" site): parses QuickBooks event
  notifications, forwards only Payment entities (payment id + operation)
  into QB_Process_Payment_Webhook. Returns 400 on bad payloads.
- InvoiceController (invocable "Create Payment Records"): splits an invoice
  amount into N monthly Scheduled payments. No flow in the org calls it
  today - a legacy helper superseded by Initiate_Payment_Plan's own logic.
- No Apex trigger on Invoice__c.

INTEGRATION PLUMBING: named credential "QuickBooks" + ~10 external service
registrations (QuickBookCreateInvoice, QuickBooksAPI/APIs, QuickBooksAPIGet-
Payment, QuickBookSendInvoiceEmail, QuickBooksGet/SaveCustomer, QuickBooks-
Get/SaveInvoice, QuickBookFindInvoice). The QB_Admin_Base_URL custom label
points at app.sandbox.qbo.intuit.com - preprod talks to a QuickBooks SANDBOX
company, not production books.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 25, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHO IS BEING BILLED ---------------------------------------------

Candidate__c (Candidate) [Lookup -> Account]
    The candidate (Person Account) this invoice bills. Set by the Account
    "Send Invoice" flow and the payment-plan flow at creation, and backfilled
    automatically when a billed Lead converts (Update_Invoice_Records_with_
    Candidate_Details). 51% populated. Feeds the QB customer-id formula and
    the Payment child's Candidate_Name__c formula.

Lead__c (Lead) [Lookup -> Lead]
    The pre-conversion website Lead this invoice bills - sales often invoices
    a person before they are converted to a candidate. Set by the Lead "Send
    Invoice" flow. 38% populated; 26 records have both Lead and Candidate
    (converted later), 36 records (41%) have neither link.

QB_Customer_Id__c (QB Customer Id) [Formula, Text]
    The QuickBooks CUSTOMER id for whoever is billed: takes the Lead's
    QB_Customer_ID__c if present, else the Candidate account's. The underlying
    Lead/Account fields are written by the send-invoice flows when they create
    or find the customer in QuickBooks. Used in the Slack creation message.

--- GROUP B: INVOICE BASICS (AMOUNTS, DATES, STATUS) -------------------------

Invoice_Amount__c (Invoice Amount) [Currency, required]
    The total amount billed on this invoice. Entered by the user in whichever
    creation flow ran. The payment webhook compares the amount actually paid
    against this to decide Not Paid / Partially Paid / Paid. Total invoiced
    across preprod: ~$358k.

Amount_Paid__c (Amount Paid) [Rollup Summary]
    SUM of Amount_Paid__c across the child Payment__c records - the money
    actually received. System-maintained; read-only on the page. ~$74k
    received across all invoices in preprod.

Outstanding_Amount__c (Outstanding Amount) [Formula, Currency]
    Invoice_Amount__c - Amount_Paid__c: what the customer still owes.
    Read-only; the collections view of the record.

Invoice_Date__c (Invoice Date) [Date]
    The date the invoice was issued. Written by the send/edit flows (mirrors
    the QuickBooks transaction date). Only 36% populated - blank on manual
    and payment-plan invoices.

Due_Date__c (Due Date) [Date]
    When payment is due. Required on the page layout and 100% populated.
    Entered by the user in the send flows; the payment-plan flow computes it
    as the last installment's month.

Invoice_Status__c (Invoice Status) [Picklist]
    Where the invoice stands financially: Not Paid | Partially Paid | Paid |
    Dispute. Stamped at creation by the send-invoice flows and thereafter
    recomputed by the payment webhook (paid amount vs invoice amount; a
    voided QuickBooks payment sets "Dispute"). Manual edits are possible.
    Reality: 63% of records have NO status (older/manual data predates the
    automation); of the rest, Not Paid 14, Paid 11, Partially Paid 7;
    "Dispute" has never occurred.

--- GROUP C: QUICKBOOKS SYNC & LINKS -----------------------------------------

QB_Invoice_Id__c (QB Invoice Id) [Text, external id]
    The invoice's id inside QuickBooks Online, written by the send-invoice
    flows from the Create Invoice API response. THE key the payment webhook
    uses to find this invoice when a payment arrives. 18% populated (only
    invoices actually pushed to QuickBooks have it).

Invoice_Id__c (Invoice Id) [Text, external id]
    A second copy of the QuickBooks invoice/transaction id, used by the two
    link formulas below to build QuickBooks URLs. 17% populated. Two fields
    holding the same external id is redundant - which one is canonical going
    forward is (not fully documented - verify with team).

Invoice_Link__c (Invoice Link) [Formula, Text]
    HYPERLINK of QB_Admin_Base_URL + Invoice_Id__c: opens this invoice in the
    QuickBooks Online admin UI (currently the QuickBooks sandbox URL). For
    internal staff.

Payment_Link__c (Payment Link) [Formula, Text]
    HYPERLINK of QB_Payment_Base_URL + Invoice_Id__c: the customer-facing
    Intuit payment-portal link where the customer can pay the invoice online.
    Shareable with the customer.

QB_Created_From__c (QB Created From) [Picklist]
    Which path created this invoice: Lead (the Lead send flow - 29 records) |
    Account (the candidate-account send flow - 2) | Manual (never used).
    Empty on the 56 records created outside the QB flows.

QB_Email_Status__c (QB Email Status) [Picklist]
    Whether QuickBooks has emailed the invoice to the customer: NotSet |
    EmailSent | NeedToSend. Written by the send/edit flows after the Send
    Invoice Email callout. In data: EmailSent 30, rest blank; NotSet and
    NeedToSend never occur.

Email_Sent_Date__c (Email Sent Date) [DateTime]
    When the invoice email went out. On the page layout but populated on 0
    records - no automation writes it (not fully documented - verify with
    team whether it should be retired or wired up).

--- GROUP D: RECURRING / SUBSCRIPTION BILLING --------------------------------
This group was built for subscription-style coaching plans. The creation
Slack flow reads these fields (it has a dedicated "recurring" message), but
NO active flow writes them and no record uses them fully yet - treat them as
a designed-but-not-yet-live feature.

Type__c (Type) [Picklist]
    One-Time | Recurring. Help text: 'Select "Recurring" for subscription
    billing'. In data: One-Time 16, blank 71, Recurring never used.

Is_Recurring__c (Is Recurring) [Formula, Checkbox]
    TRUE when Type__c = "Recurring" - a filterable flag for reports and the
    Slack flow's decision. Currently always false.

Frequency__c (Frequency) [Picklist]
    Billing cadence for a recurring plan: Daily | Weekly | Monthly | Yearly.
    16 records say "Monthly"; the rest are blank. Feeds the revenue formulas.

Interval__c (Interval) [Number]
    Every-how-many cycles: help text "1 = each cycle, 2 = every other cycle,
    etc.". Divides the revenue formulas. Populated on the same 16 records.

Recurring_Amount__c (Recurring Amount) [Currency]
    The amount charged each billing cycle (as opposed to Invoice_Amount__c,
    the one-time total). Never populated in preprod.

Recurring_Start_Date__c (Recurring Start Date) [Date]
    When the subscription billing starts. Never populated.

Recurring_Template_Name__c (Recurring Template Name) [Text]
    Name of the recurring template in QuickBooks; help text example:
    "Career Coaching - Monthly". Never populated.

Monthly_Revenue__c (Monthly Revenue) [Formula, Currency]
    Normalizes the recurring amount to a per-month figure from Frequency and
    Interval (Daily x30, Weekly x4, Monthly /interval, ...). Blank while the
    recurring fields are unused.

Annual_Revenue__c (Annual Revenue) [Formula, Currency]
    Monthly_Revenue__c * 12 - the annualized subscription value, read by the
    Slack creation message for recurring invoices.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 87, created 2024-12-03 to 2026-07-30. Total invoiced
  ~$358,010; total collected (rollup of payments) ~$73,879.
- Status: (blank) 55 (63%) | Not Paid 14 | Paid 11 | Partially Paid 7;
  "Dispute" never used.
- Origin: QB_Created_From = Lead 29 | Account 2 | blank 56 ("Manual" value
  never used). Type = One-Time 16, "Recurring" never used; Frequency
  "Monthly" + Interval on 16 records but the other recurring fields
  (Recurring_Amount, Start Date, Template) are on 0 records.
- Person links: Candidate 44 (51%), Lead 33 (38%), both 26, NEITHER 36 (41%).
- QuickBooks wiring: QB_Invoice_Id on 16, Invoice_Id on 15, QB_Email_Status
  "EmailSent" on 30, Email_Sent_Date on 0.
- Key takeaway: this is a small, half-adopted billing pilot. Only ~1/3 of
  invoices actually round-trip through QuickBooks; the rest are manual or
  payment-plan records, and the recurring-billing feature is built but not
  yet used.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Payment__c  (Label: "Payment")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Payment__c is one MONEY EVENT against an invoice. It plays two roles:
  a) An ACTUAL PAYMENT received - normally created automatically by the
     QuickBooks webhook when the customer pays (status "Paid", with the
     QuickBooks payment id and card transaction id), or recorded manually.
  b) A PLANNED INSTALLMENT - created in bulk by the "Initiate Payment Plan"
     flow (status "Scheduled" with a future Scheduled_Date__c), representing
     one month's share of a payment plan that has not been collected yet.
Its paid amounts roll up to the parent invoice, which is how an invoice knows
it is Partially Paid or Paid.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, the child half of the billing pair.
- MASTER-DETAIL CHILD OF Invoice__c: every payment belongs to exactly one
  invoice; sharing is "Controlled By Parent" (whoever sees the invoice sees
  its payments); no owner of its own.
- 12 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 2 list views.
- Auto-number Name in the format Payment-{000}.
- Scale: 163 records in preprod (Dec 2024 to Jul 2026); ~62% of them are
  future "Scheduled" installments rather than money actually received.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The Payment_Status__c ("Scheduled" vs "Paid") carries the planned-vs-
actual distinction that record types would otherwise encode.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - CREATION. Three live paths:
  - WEBHOOK (the main automated path): QuickBooks notifies the public
    QuickBooks_Webhook site; Apex QB_QuickBooksWebhookListener forwards each
    Payment event into flow QB_Process_Payment_Webhook, which fetches the
    payment from QuickBooks, dedupe-checks by QuickBooks payment id, locates
    the invoice by its QB invoice id, and creates the Payment__c: status
    "Paid", Payment_Amount = the QuickBooks total, Amount_Paid = total minus
    unapplied amount, Payment_Date = the QuickBooks transaction date,
    Payment_Type Full/Partial (did it settle the invoice or not),
    QB_Operation = "Create", plus the QuickBooks payment id and the card
    transaction id.
  - PAYMENT PLAN: Initiate_Payment_Plan creates one "Scheduled"/"Partial"
    payment per month of the plan, each with an equal share of the invoice
    amount in Payment_Amount__c and a future Scheduled_Date__c. Amount_Paid
    stays empty until money really arrives.
  - MANUAL: finance can key a payment in by hand (the older, obsolete
    Create_Invoice_Payment flow did this too; many 2024-25 "Paid" records
    without QuickBooks ids came from these paths).
STEP 2 - ROLLUP. Amount_Paid__c sums up to Invoice__c.Amount_Paid__c, which
  drives the invoice's Outstanding_Amount__c and (via the webhook flow) its
  Not Paid / Partially Paid / Paid status.
STEP 3 - SLACK. On creation, QB_Payment_Creation_Slack_Notifications posts
  the payment to Slack (with a scheduled follow-up path), so finance sees
  money arrive in real time.
STEP 4 - LATER QUICKBOOKS CHANGES. If the payment is edited in QuickBooks,
  the webhook flow updates the record (QB_Operation = "Update", amounts
  refreshed, invoice status recomputed). If it is VOIDED, the flow blanks
  the paid amount, clears status/type, sets QB_Operation = "Void" and flips
  the parent invoice to "Dispute". The QB_Payment_Update_Slack_Notifications
  flow (fires when QB_Operation changes) announces the void/update in Slack.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT:
- Invoice__c (via Invoice__c, MASTER-DETAIL, required, 100% populated, rel
  name "Payments"): the invoice this money applies to. The payment inherits
  the invoice's sharing and appears in the invoice page's only related list.
  Amount_Paid__c rolls up to the invoice.

INDIRECT (via the parent):
- Account / Lead: the person who paid, reachable through Invoice__c ->
  Candidate__c / Lead__c (surfaced on the payment by the Candidate_Name__c
  formula).

EXTERNAL COUNTERPARTS: the QuickBooks Payment (QB_Payment_Id__c) and the
card-processor transaction (Transaction_Id__c).

No other object looks up to Payment__c.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. There are no validation rules on Payment__c; data quality relies on the
webhook flow's dedupe/decision logic and the payment-plan flow's input checks.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD-TRIGGERED FLOWS (active):
- QB_Payment_Creation_Slack_Notifications (after save, create, +1 scheduled
  path): Slack post announcing the payment (name, amounts, dates, status,
  type, QB ids, parent invoice).
- QB_Payment_Update_Slack_Notifications (after save, update, entry condition
  on QB_Operation__c changing): Slack post when QuickBooks updates or VOIDS
  a payment.

CREATED / UPDATED BY (no trigger of its own):
- QB_Process_Payment_Webhook (autolaunched, invoked by Apex
  QB_QuickBooksWebhookListener from the /quickbooks/webhook/* endpoint):
  creates "Paid" payments and applies Update/Void changes from QuickBooks.
- Initiate_Payment_Plan (screen flow): bulk-creates the monthly "Scheduled"
  installment payments.
- InvoiceController (Apex invocable "Create Payment Records"): the same
  monthly split in code - not called by any current flow (legacy).
- Create_Invoice_Payment (screen flow, OBSOLETE): the old manual
  invoice+payment entry path; its buttons still exist on Lead/Account pages
  but the flow is inactive.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 12, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: PARENT & IDENTITY -----------------------------------------------

Invoice__c (Invoice) [Master-Detail -> Invoice__c]
    THE required parent link: which invoice this money applies to. 100%
    populated; controls sharing; the rollup path for Amount_Paid__c.

Candidate_Name__c (Candidate Name) [Formula, Text]
    Convenience formula showing the paying candidate's name pulled through
    the parent invoice (Invoice -> Candidate first + last name). Blank when
    the invoice is linked to a Lead only or to no person. Lets payment list
    views show "who paid" without a join.

Name_Hyperlink__c (Name Hyperlink) [Formula, Text]
    A clickable HYPERLINK of the record's own auto-number name - used in
    list views / flow data tables where the standard Name link is not
    available.

--- GROUP B: AMOUNTS & DATES -------------------------------------------------

Payment_Amount__c (Payment Amount) [Currency]
    The face value of this payment event: the QuickBooks payment total on
    webhook-created records, or one month's share of the invoice on plan
    installments. 100% populated (~$333k total across preprod).

Amount_Paid__c (Amount Paid) [Currency]
    The amount ACTUALLY applied to the invoice - this is the field that rolls
    up to Invoice__c.Amount_Paid__c. The webhook computes it as the
    QuickBooks total minus any unapplied amount, and zeroes it on a void.
    Empty on "Scheduled" installments (nothing collected yet) - 37%
    populated overall. The Payment_Amount/Amount_Paid distinction is what
    keeps planned money out of the invoice's paid rollup.

Payment_Date__c (Payment Date) [Date]
    The date money actually moved (the QuickBooks transaction date on
    webhook records; keyed manually otherwise). 38% populated - blank on
    scheduled installments.

Scheduled_Date__c (Scheduled Date) [Date]
    The PLANNED collection date of an installment, computed by the payment-
    plan flow (first payment date + N months). Populated on exactly the 101
    "Scheduled" records, empty on real payments.

--- GROUP C: STATUS & TYPE ---------------------------------------------------

Payment_Status__c (Payment Status) [Picklist]
    Paid (money received - set by the webhook and manual entry) | Scheduled
    (a planned installment - set by the payment-plan flow) | Overdue (a
    missed installment - defined but NEVER used; no automation flips
    Scheduled to Overdue, so do not rely on it). Data: Scheduled 101 (62%),
    Paid 61 (37%), 1 blank.

Payment_Type__c (Payment Type) [Picklist]
    Full | Partial: did this payment settle the invoice in full? The webhook
    derives it by comparing the applied amount to the invoice amount; the
    payment-plan flow always writes "Partial" (an installment by definition).
    Data: Partial 119, Full 44.

--- GROUP D: QUICKBOOKS SYNC -------------------------------------------------

QB_Payment_Id__c (QB Payment Id) [Text, external id]
    The payment's id inside QuickBooks - the dedupe key the webhook flow
    checks so the same QuickBooks payment is never recorded twice. Present
    on 20 records (12%) - i.e. only 20 of the 61 "Paid" payments actually
    came through the webhook; the rest were recorded manually or by the old
    flows.

QB_Operation__c (QB Operation) [Text]
    The last QuickBooks operation applied to this record: "Create", "Update"
    or "Void", written by the webhook flow. A change to this field is the
    entry condition for the update/void Slack alert. Data: Create 20, all
    others blank ("Update"/"Void" have not occurred yet in preprod).

Transaction_Id__c (Transaction Id) [Text]
    The card-processor transaction id (from the QuickBooks credit-card
    charge response) - the reference for reconciling card payments with the
    processor. Present on 12 records (card payments only).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 163, created 2024-12-03 to 2026-07-30. Payment_Amount total
  ~$333,366; Amount_Paid total ~$73,879.
- Status x type: Scheduled/Partial 101 (62% - future plan installments) |
  Paid/Full 43 | Paid/Partial 18 | blank/Full 1. "Overdue" never used.
- QuickBooks round-trip: QB_Payment_Id on 20 (12%), QB_Operation "Create" on
  the same 20, Transaction_Id on 12. So only about a third of PAID payments
  arrived via the webhook; the rest are manual/legacy entries.
- Field population: Payment_Amount 100% | Scheduled_Date 62% | Payment_Date
  38% | Amount_Paid 37%.
- Key takeaway: most Payment__c rows are the FORWARD SCHEDULE of payment
  plans, not received money - filter on Payment_Status = "Paid" (or
  Amount_Paid not null) before summing "revenue collected".

================================================================================
OBJECT: QB_Plan__c  (Label: "QB Plan")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
QB_Plan__c is the tiny PRICE LIST behind the invoice flows: one row per
sellable career-coaching service package, mapping the plan's display name to
its ITEM NUMBER inside QuickBooks Online. When a sales user runs "Send
Invoice", the flow reads these rows so the invoice line item created in
QuickBooks references the right QuickBooks product/service item. It holds
configuration, not transactions - two rows exist and they change only when
the service catalog changes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- NOT a normal custom object: it is a LIST CUSTOM SETTING (public
  visibility). It has no tab, no page layouts, no sharing model, no owner
  semantics - it is admin-managed reference data available to all code and
  flows without extra object permissions. (The generated object catalog
  labels it "custom object"; the metadata's customSettingsType=List is the
  truth.)
- 1 custom field (Item_Number__c) plus the standard Name.
- 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views (custom settings support
  none of these).
- Scale: 2 configured rows in preprod.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom settings cannot have record types.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - SETUP. An admin adds one row per sellable plan in Setup > Custom
  Settings (Name = the plan as shown to the sales user, Item_Number__c = the
  matching QuickBooks item/product code). This must stay in lockstep with
  the product list inside QuickBooks - a wrong item number breaks invoice
  creation.
STEP 2 - INVOICE CREATION. The screen flows QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks
  (Lead), QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks_For_Account (candidate Account) and
  QB_Edit_Invoice each look these rows up by Name to present the plan choice
  and build the QuickBooks invoice line item from the item number.
STEP 3 - There is no step 3: nothing writes to it at runtime and nothing
  else reads it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. As a custom setting it has no relationships in either direction - the
invoice flows read it by Name matching only. Its real "relationship" is to
the product/service item list inside QuickBooks Online.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom settings do not support validation rules; correctness of the
item numbers is maintained by hand.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Nothing runs ON it (custom settings cannot have triggers or record-triggered
flows). It is READ by three screen flows: QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks,
QB_Send_Invoice_To_QuickBooks_For_Account and QB_Edit_Invoice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (1 custom + Name)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE PLAN CATALOG ------------------------------------------------

Name (Name) [Text, standard custom-setting name]
    The plan's display name and the lookup key the invoice flows match on
    (e.g. "Career Accelerator"). Entered by an admin.

Item_Number__c (Item Number) [Text]
    The QuickBooks Online item (product/service) number for this plan - what
    the invoice line item in QuickBooks is created against. Entered by an
    admin; must match QuickBooks exactly.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- 2 configured rows (the current sellable coaching packages):
    "Career Accelerator"        -> Item Number 1010000011
    "Ultimate Career Architect" -> Item Number 7
- These item numbers point at the QuickBooks SANDBOX company preprod is
  wired to; expect different values in production books.
