================================================================================
OBJECT: Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c  (Label: "Zoom Recording Access Log")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c is the AUDIT TRAIL of the Zoom Recording Portal -
Techsara's in-house, S3-backed video library where employees watch the Zoom
recordings of interviews, training sessions and other meetings. One record =
one security-relevant event: someone opened the portal, logged in, streamed a
file, was denied access, tried to screen-record the video, an admin granted or
revoked folder access, and so on.

It exists for compliance and leak prevention: interview recordings are
sensitive (candidate voices, client names, proxy-support activity), so the
business wants to know exactly WHO watched WHAT recording, WHEN, from WHERE.
Every log row is also backed up as JSON to the S3 bucket itself (folder
"viewer-logs/", partitioned by event category and date), so the audit trail
survives even outside Salesforce. Screen-recording attempts additionally
trigger an immediate security-alert email to every holder of the
Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access permission set.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Zoom recording management subsystem (~10 Apex
  classes; see part 7).
- Standalone object (no master-detail parent). Org-wide sharing is Public
  Read/Write - it is a system log written mostly by "without sharing" Apex.
- 19 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Auto-number Name "Log Number" in the format LOG-XXXXXXX.
- Scale: only 17 records in preprod (Jul 20 - Aug 6, 2026) - the portal was
  exercised only briefly in this sandbox; the real usage history lives in
  production and in the S3 "viewer-logs/" backup.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every access-log record has the same shape; the Event_Type__c picklist
is what distinguishes the different kinds of events.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BACKGROUND - THE ZOOM RECORDING PORTAL. Zoom meeting recordings are copied to
the AWS S3 bucket configured in Zoom_Portal_Config__mdt (currently
"zoom-automation-bucket"), organized in department root folders. Employees
browse and stream them through a set of custom LWCs (zoomRecordingPortal,
zoomRecordingFileBrowser, zoomRecordingVideoPlayer, zoomRecordingDashboard,
zoomRecordingAccessManager/Modal, zoomRecordingLogs, and
zoomRecordingHierarchyChart) exposed two ways: an internal app tab
("Zoom Recording Portal") and a page inside the AIC Portal Experience Cloud
site. What a non-admin can see is controlled by
Zoom_Recording_User_Folder_Map__c grants; admins (permission set
Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access) see everything.

EVENTS THAT CREATE A LOG ROW:
  1. PORTAL LIFECYCLE. Opening the portal logs "Portal_Access"; if there was
     no portal access in the last 30 minutes it also logs a "Login_Success"
     row enriched with the user's latest LoginHistory (IP address, browser,
     application). Leaving logs "Portal_Exit"; explicit logout logs "Logout".
     (Apex ZoomRecordingLogService, called from the portal LWCs.)
  2. WATCHING A FILE. When a signed S3 URL is issued for a video, a
     "File_Access"/success row is written with the S3 key and file name.
     Suspicious inspection of the player (e.g. opening DevTools) writes a
     silent "File_Access" row tagged "[SILENT]" - logged, no email.
  3. BLOCKED ACTIONS. A failed folder/file permission check logs
     "Access_Denied"/Blocked. A detected screen-recording attempt logs
     "Screen_Recording_Attempt"/Blocked AND emails a red security-alert
     (user, profile, IP, file, timestamp in IST+UTC) to every
     Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access holder; the player also blanks the screen,
     pauses the video and mutes audio.
  4. ADMIN ACTIONS. The Access Manager logs grants ("File_Access"), revokes
     ("Access_Denied" with a "Revoked..." message) and permission-set changes
     ("Portal_Access" with "+n/-n" detail) - the event type is reused as a
     rough category and the human-readable detail goes in Error_Message__c.
  5. RECORD-PAGE BUTTON. The "View Recording" quick action on Interview__c
     and Session__c record pages launches the screen flow
     Recording_Link_Logs_Flow: it opens the recording link and writes a log
     row stamped with who opened it, when, from which record (Record_Id__c /
     Record_Name__c / Source_Object__c), and whether the click came from the
     internal app or Experience Cloud (Source__c).

AFTER EVERY INSERT the Apex writers enqueue ZoomRecordingLogS3Backup
(Queueable with callouts) which appends the row as JSON to
"viewer-logs/<category>/<yyyy-mm-dd>.json" and "viewer-logs/all-events/..."
in S3 through the AWS_S3_Named_Credential named credential.

WHO READS THE LOGS. The "View Logs" admin screen (LWC zoomRecordingLogs +
Apex ZoomRecordingLogController) lets System Administrators and
Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access holders filter/search the logs (multi-word,
order-independent user search that also finds inactive users' history).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM THE LOG:
- User (User__c): the person the event is about - the one who opened the
  portal / watched the file. Set by the Apex loggers on every row (100%
  populated in data). This is the primary "who" field.
- User (Opened_By__c): who clicked "View Recording" on a record page - set
  only by the Recording_Link_Logs_Flow path (the flow's own "who" field,
  parallel to User__c).
- Zoom_Recording_Department__c (Department__c): which recording department
  (S3 root folder) the event belongs to. Apex derives it from the user's
  Zoom_Recording_* permission set; empty for admins and for every current
  preprod row (no department records exist in this sandbox yet).
- Interview__c (Interview__c): intended link to the interview whose recording
  was accessed. Defined, but nothing currently populates it - the flow stores
  the record id as text in Record_Id__c instead (0% populated).
- Session__c (Session__c): same idea for training-session recordings; also
  never populated in practice (0%).

NO CHILDREN: nothing looks up to the access log; it is a leaf/audit object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The object is written by system code, not typed in by users, so there
are no save-time rules to enforce.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No record-triggered flows or Apex triggers run ON this object. It is purely a
WRITE TARGET of the subsystem:

APEX WRITERS:
- ZoomRecordingLogService - the central logger: portal access/exit, login
  success (with LoginHistory IP/browser), logout, signed-URL issuance, silent
  file-access, access-denied, screen-recording attempts (+ the admin alert
  email), and a generic logEvent() used by other classes.
- ZoomRecordingAccessManagerController - logs grant/revoke/permission-set
  admin actions through logEvent().
- ZoomRecordingFileController - the file-browser backend calls the log
  service when issuing signed URLs and on DevTools/inspect detection.
- ZoomRecordingLogS3Backup - Queueable that mirrors every new log row to
  S3 "viewer-logs/" as date-partitioned JSON (async; a sync variant exists).

SCREEN FLOW:
- Recording_Link_Logs_Flow (active) - behind the "View Recording" quick
  action on Interview__c and Session__c; looks up the source record and
  creates a log row (Opened_By/Opened_At/Record_Id/Record_Name/
  Recording_Link/Source/Source_Object/User).

READER:
- ZoomRecordingLogController + LWC zoomRecordingLogs - the admin "View Logs"
  screen (gated to System Administrator profile or
  Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access permission set).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 19, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHO AND WHEN ----------------------------------------------------

User__c (User) [Lookup -> User]
    The user the event is about - who opened the portal, streamed the file,
    or was blocked. Set by every Apex logging path from the running user's
    session (UserInfo). 100% populated; the field every log report pivots on.

Opened_By__c (Opened By) [Lookup -> User]
    Who clicked the "View Recording" button on an Interview or Session record
    page. Set only by Recording_Link_Logs_Flow (the button path); the Apex
    paths use User__c instead. Populated on 1 of 17 preprod rows - exactly
    the one button-created row.

Opened_At__c (Opened At) [DateTime]
    When the "View Recording" button was clicked. Flow-path companion of
    Event_Timestamp__c; only filled on button-created rows.

Event_Timestamp__c (Event Timestamp) [DateTime]
    When the event happened, stamped by the Apex loggers at insert (16 of 17
    rows). Effectively duplicates CreatedDate but is carried into the S3
    JSON backup explicitly.

Department__c (Department) [Lookup -> Zoom_Recording_Department__c]
    The recording department (S3 root folder) this event belongs to. Apex
    derives it from the user's Zoom_Recording_* permission set via
    Zoom_Recording_Department__c.Permission_Set_API_Name__c; left empty for
    admins (they have no single department). Currently 0% populated in
    preprod because no department records exist in this sandbox.

--- GROUP B: WHAT HAPPENED ---------------------------------------------------

Event_Type__c (Event Type) [Picklist]
    The kind of event. Values and meanings:
    - Portal_Access: user opened the recording portal (most common event).
    - Portal_Exit: user left the portal page.
    - Login_Success: first portal access of a new session (>30 min gap),
      enriched with IP/browser from LoginHistory.
    - Logout: explicit logout from the portal.
    - File_Access: a recording/transcript file was actually served (signed
      URL issued) - the "someone watched this file" event; also used for the
      silent DevTools log and for admin "access granted" audit rows.
    - Signed_URL: legacy value for signed-URL issuance (code now logs these
      as File_Access; kept for old rows and the S3 folder mapping).
    - Access_Denied: a permission check failed, or an admin revoked access
      (revokes are logged under this type with a "Revoked..." message).
    - Screen_Recording_Attempt: the player detected a screen-capture attempt;
      always Status = Blocked and triggers the admin alert email.
    - View / Download / Share / Video_Shared / Shared_Link_Accessed /
      Transcript_Copy: reserved for viewer actions (watch, download, share a
      link, copy transcript text) - defined for the player's event vocabulary
      but not yet written by the current code paths.
    - Login: older/simpler login value (code now writes Login_Success).
    - Sync_Complete / Sync_Error: reserved for recording-sync job results
      (the S3 backup routes them to a "sync-events" folder).
    Note: the code also defines a "Login_Failed" constant that is not in the
    picklist value list. Preprod data: Portal_Access 7, Portal_Exit 6,
    Login_Success 2, Logout 1, blank 1 (the flow path does not set a type).

Status__c (Status) [Picklist]
    Outcome of the event: Success (it happened normally) | Failed (an error
    occurred) | Blocked (the security layer stopped it - access denied or
    screen-recording attempt). 16 of 17 preprod rows are Success; the
    flow-created row leaves it blank.

Error_Message__c (Error Message) [LongTextArea]
    Free-form detail field. Despite the name it is used for far more than
    errors: the loggers pack context here ("is_admin:True/False", the latest
    login application, "[SILENT]" markers, grant/revoke descriptions like
    "Revoked access from <email>", screen-recording reasons). Read it as
    "event details".

--- GROUP C: WHAT WAS ACCESSED -----------------------------------------------

File_Key__c (File Key) [Text]
    Full S3 object key of the file involved (e.g.
    "<department>/<meeting>/video.mp4"), truncated to 255 chars. Set on
    file-access, signed-URL, access-denied and screen-recording events.

File_Name__c (File Name) [Text]
    Just the file's name (the code truncates it to 100 chars even though the
    field allows 255). Human-friendly companion to File_Key__c.

Recording_Link__c (Recording Link) [Url]
    The recording URL that was opened - written by the
    Recording_Link_Logs_Flow button path (the Apex paths log S3 keys
    instead).

Record_Id__c (Record Id) [Text]
    18-char id of the Salesforce record (Interview or Session) whose
    recording was viewed - stamped as TEXT by the flow. This, not the
    Interview__c / Session__c lookups, is what actually carries the link in
    practice.

Record_Name__c (Record Name) [Text]
    Name of that source record (e.g. the interview auto-number "I-031360"),
    stamped by the flow so log readers do not need to resolve the id.

Interview__c (Interview) [Lookup -> Interview__c]
    Proper lookup to the interview whose recording was accessed. Defined for
    the compliance model but never populated by the current flow/Apex (0%) -
    the flow uses Record_Id__c instead. (Wiring it up would let interview
    pages show their own access history as a related list.)

Session__c (Session) [Lookup -> Session__c]
    Same as Interview__c but for training/meeting Session recordings; also
    0% populated today.

Source_Object__c (Source Object) [Picklist]
    Which kind of record the "View Recording" click came from: interview |
    session. Set by the flow; empty on Apex-created rows.

--- GROUP D: WHERE FROM (CLIENT CONTEXT) -------------------------------------

Source__c (Source) [Picklist]
    Where the user was when the event fired: App (internal Lightning app) |
    Experience Cloud (the AIC Portal community). Set by the flow path;
    Apex-created rows leave it blank.

IP_Address__c (IP Address) [Text]
    The user's source IP, copied from their most recent LoginHistory entry
    on Login_Success events (2 of 17 rows). Security teams use it to spot
    odd locations.

User_Agent__c (User Agent) [TextArea]
    Browser/client string, also from LoginHistory on login events (e.g.
    "Chrome 126"). Complements the IP for device-level auditing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 17, created 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-06 - a short testing
  window; production and the S3 "viewer-logs/" backup hold the real history.
- Event types: Portal_Access 7 | Portal_Exit 6 | Login_Success 2 | Logout 1 |
  blank 1 (the one flow/button-created row).
- Status: Success 16 | blank 1. No Failed/Blocked events logged yet in this
  sandbox (no denied access or screen-recording attempts recorded).
- Population: User__c 17/17 (100%); Event_Timestamp__c 16; IP_Address__c 2;
  Opened_By__c / Opened_At__c / Record_Id__c / Recording_Link__c 1 each
  (the button row); Department__c, Interview__c, Session__c, File_Key__c,
  File_Name__c all 0.
- Key takeaway: in preprod only the portal-lifecycle logging has really run;
  the file-access, department and record-lookup dimensions are unexercised
  here, so do not judge the design by this sandbox's data.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Zoom_Recording_Department__c  (Label: "Zoom Recording Department")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Zoom_Recording_Department__c is the DEPARTMENT CATALOG of the Zoom Recording
Portal. One record = one top-level folder in the recordings S3 bucket (e.g. a
department or team's recordings folder). It is the bridge between three
worlds: the S3 folder structure (Folder_Path_S3__c), the Salesforce
permission-set model (Permission_Set_API_Name__c), and the portal UI (the
department tiles/sections users see when they open the portal).

Important: these records are NOT hand-made. An auto-sync Apex class mirrors
the S3 bucket's root folders into this object - create a folder in S3 and a
department record appears; delete the folder and the record is deactivated,
then physically deleted after 30 days. Do not confuse this object with the
org's HR notion of departments (Recruiter__c.Department or the role-hierarchy
project) - this one only organizes recording folders.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Zoom recording management subsystem.
- Standalone object (no parent); org-wide sharing Public Read/Write - it is
  maintained by "without sharing" system code.
- 6 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view.
- Text Name field ("Department Name") - set by the auto-sync to the S3 folder
  name (folder path minus the slash).
- Has its own Lightning record page (FlexiPage "Department_Record_Page").
- Scale: 0 records in preprod - the auto-sync has not been run against S3
  from this sandbox; departments exist where the portal actually runs.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Every department record has the same shape.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - AUTO-CREATION FROM S3. When the portal loads,
  ZoomRecordingDeptAutoSync.ensureDepartmentsExist() lists the S3 bucket's
  root folders (via ZoomRecordingS3Service) and reconciles them with this
  object: new folder -> new department record (Name = folder name, active,
  next Display_Order, default Permission_Set_API_Name =
  "Zoom_Recording_User_Access"); folder re-appeared -> record re-activated;
  folder gone from S3 -> record deactivated; deactivated for 30+ days ->
  record permanently deleted. Safe to call repeatedly.

STEP 2 - DRIVING WHAT USERS SEE. When a user opens the portal,
  ZoomRecordingAccessService.getUserAccessibleDepartments() returns:
  - for admins (Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access permission set): ALL active
    departments;
  - for everyone else: only the departments referenced by their active
    Zoom_Recording_User_Folder_Map__c grants. No grants = empty portal.
  The Access Manager admin screen also lists active departments as the
  containers admins pick when granting folder access.

STEP 3 - TAGGING THE AUDIT TRAIL. ZoomRecordingLogService looks up the
  department whose Permission_Set_API_Name__c matches one of the user's
  Zoom_Recording_* permission sets and stamps it on each access-log row
  (Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c.Department__c), so log reports can be
  sliced per department.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PARENT: none - departments are the top of the recording-access model.

OBJECTS THAT POINT AT IT:
- Zoom_Recording_User_Folder_Map__c (Department__c, required on every grant):
  each user-folder access grant belongs to one department - "user X may see
  folder Y inside department Z".
- Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c (Department__c): access-log rows are tagged
  with the department they concern, for per-department audit reporting.

INDIRECT: Permission_Set_API_Name__c references a PermissionSet by API name
(text, not a real lookup) - the org ships Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access,
Zoom_Recording_User_Access and Zoom_Recording_TL_Marker permission sets.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The auto-sync code is the only intended writer, so integrity is
enforced in Apex rather than validation rules.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No flows or triggers. All lifecycle logic is Apex:
- ZoomRecordingDeptAutoSync (writer) - creates / reactivates / deactivates /
  hard-deletes department records to mirror the S3 root folders (see part 4).
- ZoomRecordingAccessService (reader) - builds the department list each user
  may see (admin = all active; others = from their folder grants).
- ZoomRecordingAccessManagerController (reader) - lists active departments
  in the admin Access Manager and in its hierarchy/summary charts.
- ZoomRecordingLogService (reader) - resolves a user's primary department
  from their permission sets to tag access-log rows.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 6, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: IDENTITY & S3 MAPPING -------------------------------------------

Department_Code__c (Department Code) [Text]
    A short code for the department. Present in the schema but not set by
    the auto-sync and not read by any portal code - effectively unused
    (available for manual/admin classification if ever needed).

Description__c (Description) [TextArea]
    Free-text description of what recordings the department folder holds.
    Manual admin entry; nothing in code writes or reads it.

Folder_Path_S3__c (Folder Path (S3)) [Text]
    THE key field: the S3 root-folder path this department represents (e.g.
    "sales-team/" - always folder-name + trailing slash). Written by the
    auto-sync from the S3 listing and used as the match key on every
    subsequent sync; also the path the portal browses when a user opens the
    department.

--- GROUP B: PORTAL BEHAVIOR & ACCESS ----------------------------------------

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    Whether the department currently exists in S3 and should show in the
    portal. The auto-sync flips it false when the folder disappears from S3
    (a soft delete), true again if the folder returns, and permanently
    deletes records that stay inactive for 30+ days. All portal queries
    filter on Is_Active__c = true.

Display_Order__c (Display Order) [Number]
    Sort position of the department in the portal UI. The auto-sync assigns
    the next number as folders are discovered (existing count + 1); admins
    can renumber manually. (Note: the main department queries actually sort
    by Name, so this is a secondary/cosmetic ordering.)

Permission_Set_API_Name__c (Permission Set API Name) [Text]
    API name of the permission set associated with this department -
    defaulted to "Zoom_Recording_User_Access" by the auto-sync. Read by
    ZoomRecordingLogService to decide a user's "primary department" when
    tagging access logs (it matches the user's Zoom_Recording_* permission
    sets against this field). It does NOT by itself grant folder access -
    the Zoom_Recording_User_Folder_Map__c grants do that.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 0. The S3 auto-sync has not populated this sandbox - the
  subsystem's metadata and code are fully deployed here, but its runtime
  data (departments, folder grants, most access logs) lives where the portal
  actually operates.
- Consequence: every Zoom_Recording_Access_Log__c row in preprod has an
  empty Department__c, and non-admin users would see an empty portal until
  the auto-sync runs and grants are issued.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Zoom_Recording_User_Folder_Map__c
        (Label: "Zoom Recording User Folder Map")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Zoom_Recording_User_Folder_Map__c is the ACCESS-GRANT table of the Zoom
Recording Portal. One record = one grant: "this Salesforce User may see this
S3 folder (or this single file) inside this recording department". It is the
portal's own row-level security model, deliberately independent of Salesforce
record sharing - the recordings live in S3, not in Salesforce, so access is
enforced in Apex by checking these mappings before listing folders or issuing
signed streaming URLs.

The grant model is hierarchical in practice: portal admins (permission set
Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access) grant folders to team leads (marked by the
Zoom_Recording_TL_Marker permission set concept and by WHO granted them), and
team leads' grants to their employees are visualized as a Department -> Team
Lead -> Employee -> Folders tree in the admin hierarchy chart. Because
Granted_By__c records who issued each grant, the object doubles as its own
audit trail of the delegation chain.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object, part of the Zoom recording management subsystem.
- Standalone object (lookups, no master-detail); org-wide sharing Public
  Read/Write - all enforcement is in "without sharing" Apex, which gates
  every admin operation on the Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access permission set.
- 9 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 0 list views.
- Auto-number Name in the format ZUM-XXXX.
- S3_Folder_Path__c is an EXTERNAL ID - the S3 path is the logical key.
- Scale: 0 records in preprod (grants exist only where the portal runs).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. A grant is a grant; folder-vs-file grants are distinguished only by
whether the S3 path ends with "/".

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - GRANTING. An admin opens the Access Manager (LWC
  zoomRecordingAccessManager + zoomRecordingAccessModal, backend
  ZoomRecordingAccessManagerController), picks a user, a department, and
  ticks folders and/or individual files browsed live from S3. Apex creates
  one mapping row per new item (skipping paths the user already has),
  stamping Granted_By = the acting admin and Granted_Date = now, Is_Active =
  true. Folder grants are normalized to end with "/"; file grants store the
  full S3 object key. Each grant batch is also written to the access log.
  The same modal manages the user's permission sets (any non-profile-owned
  permission set can be assigned/removed; an admin cannot remove their own
  Zoom_Recording_Admin_Access).

STEP 2 - ENFORCEMENT. Whenever a non-admin browses the portal or requests a
  video, ZoomRecordingAccessService loads their active mappings and allows a
  path if it starts with (or is a parent of) a granted path - i.e. granting
  a folder grants everything beneath it. ZoomRecordingFileController applies
  this to every folder listing and signed-URL request, on top of blanket
  rules (blocked folders like "docs"/"llm", allowed file extensions).
  Admins bypass mappings entirely. Users with no active mappings see an
  empty portal ("No Access").

STEP 3 - REVOKING. Admins revoke one mapping, a selection, a department's
  worth, or ALL of a user's access - in every case the rows are physically
  DELETED (not deactivated), and a revoke entry is written to the access
  log. Is_Active__c therefore stays true on live rows; it exists as a
  kill-switch/filter, not as the normal revoke mechanism.

STEP 4 - OVERSIGHT. The admin dashboards read the mappings to show per-user
  folder counts, an access summary grouped by who-granted-what, and the
  Department -> Team Lead -> Employee -> Folders hierarchy chart (a user is
  treated as a Team Lead when their own grant came directly from an admin).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOOKUPS FROM THE MAPPING:
- User (User__c): the user being granted access - the subject of the grant.
- Zoom_Recording_Department__c (Department__c, REQUIRED): the recording
  department (S3 root folder) the granted item belongs to. Groups grants
  for the admin screens and department-level revokes.
- User (Granted_By__c): the admin or team lead who issued the grant - the
  backbone of the delegation hierarchy chart and the access-summary audit.

NO CHILDREN: nothing looks up to a mapping row.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Only the Access Manager Apex (admin-gated) writes these rows, and it
enforces the rules itself (no duplicate paths per user, required user/
department/paths).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No flows or triggers. All behavior is Apex:
- ZoomRecordingAccessManagerController (writer) - creates grants
  (grantFolderAccess / grantItemAccess), deletes them on revoke (single,
  bulk, per-department, revoke-all), and builds the summary/hierarchy
  dashboards from them; every change is echoed to the access log.
- ZoomRecordingAccessService (reader) - caches the current user's active
  mappings per request and answers "may this user see this path?" and
  "which departments may they open?".
- ZoomRecordingFileController (reader) - applies those answers to folder
  browsing and signed-URL issuance for non-admin users.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 9, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: THE GRANT ITSELF ------------------------------------------------

User__c (User) [Lookup -> User]
    The Salesforce user receiving access. All enforcement queries filter on
    this + Is_Active__c. (Not formally required in the schema, but the
    granting code always sets it.)

Department__c (Department) [Lookup -> Zoom_Recording_Department__c, REQUIRED]
    The recording department the granted folder/file sits under. Required on
    every grant; used to group the admin screens and to revoke a user's
    whole department at once.

S3_Folder_Path__c (S3 Folder Path) [Text, REQUIRED, External ID]
    THE payload of the grant: the S3 path the user may access. Ends with "/"
    for a folder grant (which implicitly covers everything beneath it) or is
    a full object key for a single-file grant. The access check allows any
    requested path that starts with a granted path. External ID = the
    logical unique key of a grant (per user).

Folder_Name__c (Folder Name) [Text, REQUIRED]
    Human-friendly display name of the granted item - the last segment of
    the path (folder name or file name), extracted automatically by the
    granting code for the admin dashboards.

--- GROUP B: GRANT LIFECYCLE & AUDIT -----------------------------------------

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    Whether the grant currently counts. Set true at creation and filtered on
    by every access check. Note: revoking DELETES the row rather than
    unchecking this, so in practice it is an emergency disable flag / query
    filter rather than a lifecycle state.

Granted_By__c (Granted By) [Lookup -> User]
    Who issued the grant (the acting admin/team lead, stamped automatically).
    Drives the "who granted what" summary and defines the Team Lead ->
    Employee layers of the hierarchy chart (grants issued BY an admin mark
    the recipient as a team lead; grants issued by that team lead hang their
    recipients beneath them).

Granted_Date__c (Granted Date) [DateTime]
    When the grant was issued (stamped automatically at creation; also the
    sort order of a user's grants in the admin view).

Notes__c (Notes) [LongTextArea]
    Optional free-text note about why the access was granted. Manual entry
    only - the granting UI/code does not populate it (and nothing reads it
    programmatically).

--- GROUP C: CONVENIENCE -----------------------------------------------------

User_Email__c (User Email) [Formula, Text]
    Live formula showing the granted user's email (User__r.Email) so admin
    list views and exports identify the person without opening the User
    record.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 0. Like the department catalog, folder grants live in the
  environment where the portal actually operates; preprod only holds the
  deployed schema and code.
- Practical consequence for testing here: any non-admin user opening the
  portal in preprod gets the "No Access" experience until departments are
  synced and grants are created.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Zoom_Portal_Config__mdt  (Label: "Zoom Portal Config")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Zoom_Portal_Config__mdt is the SETTINGS PANEL of the Zoom Recording Portal,
implemented as a custom metadata type. One active record tells the whole
subsystem which AWS S3 bucket and region to talk to, which AWS credentials
to sign requests with, how long streaming links stay valid, which file types
may be played, and what title/notice the portal UI shows. Admins change the
portal's behavior by editing this record in Setup (Custom Metadata Types >
Zoom Portal Config) - no code change or deployment needed.

Being custom metadata (not a custom object), records deploy with metadata,
are visible to Apex without SOQL limits concerns, and are read through the
dedicated wrapper class ZoomRecordingPortalConfig, which caches the first
ACTIVE record per transaction and supplies safe defaults when optional
fields are blank.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom METADATA TYPE (API suffix __mdt) - configuration, not data. No
  sharing model, no owner, not writable by flows or normal DML.
- 9 custom fields, 0 record types, 0 validation rules.
- Exactly 1 record exists: "Default_Config" (Is_Active = true). The wrapper
  class takes the FIRST active record it finds (LIMIT 1), so only one row
  should ever be active at a time.
- Consumers: ZoomRecordingPortalConfig (the only direct reader), and through
  it ZoomRecordingS3Service (S3 REST calls + pre-signed URL generation).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom metadata types do not use record types.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- On any portal operation that touches S3 (listing folders, listing files,
  generating a streaming URL), ZoomRecordingS3Service asks
  ZoomRecordingPortalConfig for the bucket, region, credentials and URL
  expiry, and signs the AWS request with them (AWS Signature V4 pre-signed
  URLs - this is why raw keys sit in metadata rather than a named
  credential: pre-signing needs the secret directly). The department
  auto-sync and every file browse therefore depend on this record.
- The portal UI reads the cosmetic fields: Site_Title__c as the header and
  Top_Notice__c as the banner text users see on the portal home.
- File-type policing: isExtensionAllowed() checks a file's extension against
  Allowed_File_Extensions__c before it is offered/streamed (with a built-in
  fallback list of mp4/webm/mov/mkv when the field is blank). Note that
  ZoomRecordingFileController layers additional hard-coded per-user rules on
  top (non-admins: vtt/mp4/m4a/cc/chat/transcript/txt only, "docs"/"llm"
  folders blocked).
- If NO active record exists, every S3 operation fails fast with a clear
  ConfigurationException telling the admin to create the record - the portal
  cannot run unconfigured.
- Note: the access-LOG backup path is different - ZoomRecordingLogS3Backup
  uses the AWS_S3_Named_Credential named credential, not these keys.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Custom metadata records stand alone; the link to the rest of the
subsystem is purely through the Apex classes that read them
(ZoomRecordingPortalConfig -> ZoomRecordingS3Service -> the portal
controllers).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Correctness is enforced by the wrapper class at read time (missing
active record or missing AWS keys throw a ConfigurationException with a
fix-it message).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Nothing runs ON custom metadata. Readers:
- ZoomRecordingPortalConfig - caching accessor with defaults (title falls
  back to "Zoom Recording Portal", URL expiry to 480 minutes, extensions to
  mp4/webm/mov/mkv).
- ZoomRecordingS3Service - consumes bucket/region/keys/expiry for every S3
  callout and pre-signed streaming URL.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 9, grouped by purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Configured values below are from the single live record "Default_Config"
(queried 2026-08-12).

--- GROUP A: AWS / S3 CONNECTION ---------------------------------------------

S3_Bucket_Name__c (S3 Bucket Name) [Text, REQUIRED]
    The S3 bucket holding all Zoom recordings and the viewer-logs backup.
    Configured: "zoom-automation-bucket". Every folder listing, file list
    and streaming URL is built against this bucket.

AWS_Region__c (AWS Region) [Text, REQUIRED]
    AWS region of the bucket, used in endpoint construction and request
    signing. Configured: "us-east-1".

AWS_Access_Key__c (AWS Access Key) [Text]
AWS_Secret_Key__c (AWS Secret Key) [Text]
    The AWS IAM credential pair used to sign S3 requests and pre-sign
    streaming URLs (Signature V4 needs the raw secret, which is why these
    live here instead of a named credential). Both are populated on the
    live record (values deliberately not reproduced in this document).
    SECURITY NOTE: anyone with read access to this metadata type can see
    the secret - treat the type as sensitive configuration. If either is
    blank the wrapper throws a ConfigurationException.

--- GROUP B: PORTAL BEHAVIOR -------------------------------------------------

Is_Active__c (Is Active) [Checkbox]
    Marks THE record the portal uses (the code picks the first active row).
    Keep exactly one active; flipping it off takes the whole portal down
    with "No active Zoom Portal Config found". Configured: checked.

Signed_URL_Expiry_Minutes__c (Signed URL Expiry Minutes) [Number]
    How long a generated streaming/download link stays valid before it
    expires. Configured: 480 (8 hours - also the code default when blank).
    Shorter = safer against link sharing; longer = fewer playback
    interruptions.

Allowed_File_Extensions__c (Allowed File Extensions) [Text]
    Comma-separated list of file extensions the portal will serve.
    Configured: "mp4,webm,mov,mkv" (video only at the config level;
    per-user Apex rules separately allow transcript/audio types for
    non-admins). Blank would fall back to the same four video types.

--- GROUP C: PORTAL APPEARANCE -----------------------------------------------

Site_Title__c (Site Title) [Text]
    The heading shown at the top of the portal UI. Configured: "Techsara
    Zoom Recording Portal" (falls back to "Zoom Recording Portal" if blank).

Top_Notice__c (Top Notice) [LongTextArea]
    A banner/notice message shown to users on the portal home. Configured:
    "Welcome! Access your department recordings below."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Records: 1 - "Default_Config" (Master Label "Default Config"), active.
- Values: bucket "zoom-automation-bucket", region "us-east-1", signed-URL
  expiry 480 minutes, allowed extensions "mp4,webm,mov,mkv", site title
  "Techsara Zoom Recording Portal", top notice "Welcome! Access your
  department recordings below.", AWS access + secret keys populated.
- This is the one part of the Zoom-recording subsystem that IS fully
  configured in preprod (unlike departments/grants, which are empty here).

================================================================================
OBJECT: ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c  (Label: "Zoom Call Log")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c is a THIRD-PARTY MANAGED-PACKAGE object, installed by
the official "Zoom for Salesforce" app from Zoom Video Communications
(namespace prefix ZVC). It stores one record per Zoom Phone call: caller and
callee numbers/extensions, ring/answer/end timestamps, duration, call type
and result, disposition, links to the call recording and voicemail, and an
AI-generated call summary. The package links each call log to the Task it
auto-creates, so phone activity shows up in standard activity timelines.

It is NOT part of Techsara's custom Zoom RECORDING portal subsystem
(Zoom_Recording_* objects above) - that is in-house code for meeting/
interview video recordings in S3. This object is purely the vendor's
call-logging feature. Techsara has no custom code, flows or fields on it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Custom object owned by the ZVC managed package - Techsara cannot change
  its fields, and the org snapshot shows 0 local custom fields on it (the
  package's own ~26 fields exist in the org but are not part of retrieved
  local metadata; the field list below comes from a live describe).
- 0 record types, 0 validation rules, 1 list view ("All Zoom Call Logs").
- Has an Owner (standard ownership model applies).
- Scale: 0 records in preprod - but ~9,857 Task records still carry
  ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c ids (created Oct 2025 - Jul 2026), meaning calls
  WERE logged in that period and the log records were later deleted/purged
  or not copied to this sandbox. The Task-side ids now point at nothing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. The package does not define record types on it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
When an employee makes or receives a Zoom Phone call through the Zoom for
Salesforce integration, the package writes a Zoom Call Log record with the
call's technical details and creates/links a Task so the call appears in the
activity timeline of the related Lead/Contact/Account. The Activity field
ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c is the link from that Task back to the call log.
Salesforce-side users mainly experience this as "calls appear as completed
Tasks"; the call-log record holds the extra telephony detail (numbers,
timings, recording/voicemail links, AI summary).

Data reality at Techsara: call logging clearly ran from about Oct 2025 to
Jul 2026 (the ~9,857 linked Tasks), but the call-log records themselves are
gone from preprod, so only the Task shells remain. Treat historical
"call detail" questions as unanswerable from this sandbox.

The wider ZVC package footprint in the org (for orientation): "Add To
Webinar" buttons on Lead and Contact, ZVC__IsCreatedByZoomApp__c on Lead,
ZVC__Registrant_Id__c on CampaignMember, and several ZVC list views on
Contact - i.e. the package also covers Zoom Webinar registration, separate
from call logging.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Activity / Task (ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c field on Activity): each package-
  created call Task points at its call log. This is the only relationship
  the org snapshot shows. (~9,857 Tasks carry a value, all currently
  dangling because the log records are absent.)
- The package also stores the reverse pointer as text (ZVC__Task_Id__c on
  the call log).
- No Techsara custom object references ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. Managed-package object with no local validation rules added.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION (what runs on this object)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None in Techsara's org - no local flows, triggers or Apex touch it. All
writes come from the Zoom for Salesforce managed package / Zoom's
integration user. (Any package-internal automation is invisible to and not
modifiable by the org.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All fields belong to the managed package (ZVC namespace); Techsara has added
none. Summarized from a live describe rather than local metadata - consult
Zoom's package documentation for authoritative semantics.

--- GROUP A: PACKAGE FIELDS (VENDOR-OWNED, SUMMARY) --------------------------

    Call identity: ZVC__Call_ID__c, ZVC__Calllog_Unique_ID__c (Zoom-side
    identifiers), ZVC__Calllog_Status__c, ZVC__Call_Level_Type__c.
    Parties: ZVC__Caller_Phone_Number__c / ZVC__Caller_Extension_Number__c,
    ZVC__Callee_Phone_Number__c / ZVC__Callee_Extension_Number__c,
    ZVC__Third_Party_Name__c / ZVC__Third_Party_Number__c,
    ZVC__IsExternal__c (external vs internal call).
    Timing: ZVC__Ring_Start_Time__c, ZVC__Answer_Start_Time__c,
    ZVC__Call_End_Time__c, ZVC__Call_Duration__c.
    Outcome: ZVC__Call_Type__c (inbound/outbound), ZVC__Call_Result__c,
    ZVC__Disposition__c and ZVC__Interaction_Type__c (picklists),
    ZVC__Signal_Status__c (call quality metric).
    Content links: ZVC__Recording__c (call recording), ZVC__Voice_Mail__c
    (voicemail), ZVC__AIC_Call_Summary__c / ZVC__AIC_Call_Summary_Id__c
    (Zoom AI Companion call summary).
    Cross-reference: ZVC__Task_Id__c (the Task created for this call).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-12)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total records: 0 (also 0 in the recycle bin).
- BUT: 9,857 Task records have ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c populated, created
  2025-10-17 to 2026-07-10 - the footprint of roughly nine months of Zoom
  Phone call logging whose log records no longer exist in this sandbox.
- Key takeaway for answering questions: treat this object as an installed
  third-party feature that is currently dataless here. For "who called
  whom" history, only the package-created Tasks remain (subject, date,
  related records) - the telephony detail fields are gone with the logs.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Case  (standard object, repurposed as "Candidate Ops Ticket")
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The standard Salesforce Case object, repurposed as Techsara's INTERNAL
candidate-operations ticket. It is NOT a customer-support inbox: no email-to-
case, no external customers filing tickets. Instead, staff raise Cases about
candidates and pipeline events - "edit this resume", "candidate missed a
session", "payment pending", "policy breach warning", "one-off proxy
exception", "interview support request" - and the team works them against a
required Deadline, coordinated through Slack. Think of it as the org's
internal to-do/escalation queue anchored to whichever pipeline record the
issue concerns (an Interview, a Marketing engagement, or an Onboarding).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Standard object with 11 custom fields (47 fields total incl. standard).
- Org-wide sharing ReadWriteTransfer; no record types, no validation rules,
  12 list views.
- Scale: 1,603 records in preprod; 98% already Closed/Resolved (a working
  queue, kept clean).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None. One ticket process for everything; the Case_Reason__c picklist is what
differentiates the work.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATION. Two paths:
  - Manual: a staff member raises a Case about a candidate situation,
    choosing the Case_Reason (what kind of operation it is), tags, priority
    and the required Deadline, and linking the relevant pipeline record
    (Interview / Marketing / Onboarding lookup).
  - Automatic: the Interview_Request_Case_Flow creates a Case whenever an
    interview's "Request Raised" support checkbox is turned on - the Case is
    the tracked ticket for that interview-support request (subject,
    description, deadline, owner, priority and tags are set by the flow).

ROUTING & SLACK. On creation the Case_Assign_Owner_before_creation flow
assigns the right owner. The Case_Post_parent_message_to_Slack flow posts
the new ticket into the team's Slack channel and stores the message's thread
timestamp on the Case (Slack_Thread_Ts__c); every later update posted by
Case_Post_Updates_to_Slack lands as a reply in that same Slack thread, so
each ticket has one continuous Slack conversation. The Apex CaseTrigger ->
CaseTriggerHandler adds one more notification: when a Case's Priority
changes, SlackCalloutHelper.sendCaseNotificationToSlack posts the change.

WORKING THE TICKET. The team drives the standard Status field (New -> In
Progress -> Waiting on Candidate -> Resolved/Closed), uses Waiting_On__c to
show whose court the ball is in, and Next_Action_Date__c for follow-up
pacing. Priority changes go through the Case_Priority_Change_Screen_Flow,
which records the justification into Last_Priority_Change_Reason__c.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Interview__c (Interview__c, Lookup): the interview the ticket is about -
  set by the auto-created interview-support Cases and by manual tickets on
  interview issues (scheduling problems, recording requests, proxy
  exceptions).
- Marketing__c (Marketing__c, Lookup): the candidate-marketing engagement
  the ticket concerns (resume edits, missed sessions, responsiveness
  warnings - most candidate-management reasons anchor here).
- Onboarding__c (Onboarding__c, Lookup): the onboarding the ticket concerns
  (payment pending, signature pending, agreement issues).
- Account/Contact (standard AccountId / ContactId): the candidate the ticket
  is ultimately about (Person Account + its shadow contact).
- Standard Owner (OwnerId): the staff member (or queue) working the ticket.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None as validation rules. The one hard requirement is field-level:
Deadline__c is marked required, so every ticket must carry its due date.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Case_Assign_Owner_before_creation (record-triggered, on create): assigns
  the proper owner for new tickets.
- Case_Post_parent_message_to_Slack (record-triggered, on create): posts the
  ticket to Slack and saves the thread timestamp (Slack_Thread_Ts__c).
- Case_Post_Updates_to_Slack (record-triggered, on update): posts updates
  into the existing Slack thread.
- Case_Priority_Change_Screen_Flow (screen flow): governed priority change
  with a reason, written to Last_Priority_Change_Reason__c.
- Interview_Request_Case_Flow (on Interview__c): CREATES Cases for
  interview-support requests.
- Apex CaseTrigger -> CaseTriggerHandler: on after-update, if Priority
  changed, sends a Slack notification (SlackCalloutHelper). All other
  handler contexts are empty scaffolding.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (11 custom + the standard fields that matter)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: WHAT THE TICKET IS (custom classification) ----------------------

Case_Reason__c (Case Reason) [Picklist]
    THE operational classifier - what kind of candidate-ops work this ticket
    is. Values (with live counts of the busiest): Escalation (231),
    Availability (146), Legal Warning (140), Warning (Responsiveness) (117),
    Missed Session (115), Resume Edit (110), Proxy Exception (One-off) (91),
    Start (80), Support Mandatory (77), Skill Gap (77), Evidence Request
    (72), Pause (53), Resume (36), Scheduling (34), Recording Request (34),
    LinkedIn Edit (28), Priority Change (25), Policy Breach (21),
    Seriousness / Commitment (19), Policy Clarification (18), Inactive / No
    Response (16), Track Change (14), Experience Adjustment (10), Payment
    Pending (6), Signature Pending (6), Plan Upgrade (3), New Referral (1),
    Direct Bypass (Text/Email) (1). "Start / Pause / Resume" are marketing-
    engagement state changes; "Proxy Exception (One-off)" is a policy-bound
    one-time allowance around the proxy-support rules.

Case_Tags__c (Case Tags) [Multi-select Picklist]
    Cross-cutting labels stackable on any reason: C2C | Full-Time | Urgent |
    Agreement Breach Risk | Referral | Delay | Support Exception | Payment
    Pending | Smart Team Directive | Training. Used for filtering/reporting
    across reasons.

Waiting_On__c (Waiting On) [Picklist]
    Whose action the ticket is blocked on: Candidate | Recruiter | Trainer |
    Support | Legal | Vendor/Client | Internal Review. Keeps the queue
    honest about where delays sit.

--- GROUP B: TIMING ----------------------------------------------------------

Deadline__c (Deadline) [Date, REQUIRED]
    The date the ticket must be done by. Required on every Case - the
    interview-support flow sets it automatically; manual tickets must fill
    it. The queue is worked deadline-first.

Next_Action_Date__c (Next Action Date) [Date]
    When the owner should next touch the ticket (follow-up pacing between
    creation and deadline).

--- GROUP C: SLACK INTEGRATION -----------------------------------------------

Slack_Thread_Ts__c (Slack Thread Ts) [Text, unique, external id]
    The Slack message timestamp of the ticket's parent post - the key that
    lets every update land as a reply in the same Slack thread. Written by
    the post-to-Slack flow; unique + external-id so a Case maps 1:1 to its
    thread.

--- GROUP D: PIPELINE LINKS (custom lookups) ---------------------------------

Interview__c (Interview) [Lookup -> Interview__c]
    The interview this ticket is about (auto-set for interview-support
    Cases).

Marketing__c (Marketing) [Lookup -> Marketing__c]
    The marketing engagement this ticket is about.

Onboarding__c (Onboarding) [Lookup -> Onboarding__c]
    The onboarding this ticket is about.

--- GROUP E: AUDIT HELPERS (custom) ------------------------------------------

Case_Owner_Name__c (Case Owner Name) [Formula, Text]
    The owner's first + last name as text (report-friendly owner column
    that works across queues/users).

Last_Priority_Change_Reason__c (Last Priority Change Reason) [LongTextArea]
    Why the priority was last changed - written by the
    Case_Priority_Change_Screen_Flow. The Apex trigger separately Slacks
    the change.

--- GROUP F: KEY STANDARD FIELDS USED ----------------------------------------

Subject / Description
    Ticket title and detail - set manually or by the interview-support flow.
Status [Picklist]
    New -> In Progress -> Waiting on Candidate -> Resolved -> Closed. Live
    data: Closed 1,071, Resolved 502, New 13, In Progress 11, Waiting on
    Candidate 6.
Priority [Picklist]
    Standard priority; changes are governed by the screen flow + Slack
    notification.
OwnerId / AccountId / ContactId
    Working owner; the candidate Person Account and its contact.
Origin / Type / Reason [Picklists]
    Standard classifiers, largely unused - Case_Reason__c is the field that
    matters in this org.
ParentId
    Standard parent-case link for related tickets (rarely used).
IsEscalated / IsClosedOnCreate / IsStopped / StopStartDate / ClosedDate /
Comments / Language
    Standard mechanics fields; no special behavior in this org.
ContactEmail / ContactFax / ContactMobile / ContactPhone /
SuppliedName / SuppliedEmail / SuppliedPhone / SuppliedCompany
    Standard contact-info mirrors and web-to-case supply fields; unused
    (there is no external case intake).
AssetId / BusinessHoursId / EntitlementId / ProductId / ServiceContractId /
MilestoneStatus / MilestoneStatusIcon / SlaStartDate / SlaExitDate / SourceId
    Standard service-cloud/entitlement machinery; not used in this org.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-15)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Total: 1,603 Cases. Status: Closed 1,071 (67%) | Resolved 502 (31%) |
  currently open only 30 (New 13, In Progress 11, Waiting on Candidate 6).
- Top reasons: Escalation 231, Availability 146, Legal Warning 140,
  Warning (Responsiveness) 117, Missed Session 115, Resume Edit 110.
- Note: live data contains reason values ("Escalation", "Evidence Request",
  "New Referral") beyond the picklist snapshot in source - the picklist has
  grown in the live org; 22 records have no reason at all.
- Key takeaway: Case = internal candidate-ops/escalation queue with a
  1-ticket-1-Slack-thread pattern; the standard support-cloud machinery
  around it is unused.

================================================================================
OBJECT: Activity  (standard Task & Event, with custom fields)
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
"Activity" is the shared field container for the standard Task and Event
objects (custom Activity fields appear on both). In this org, activities are
mostly MACHINE-GENERATED side effects of other subsystems rather than a
hand-maintained to-do list: calendar Events created for sessions and
employee leave, and Task/call-log rows created by the ZVC Zoom managed
package. The 8 custom fields fall into exactly those two groups: employee-
leave calendar wiring and Zoom-package wiring.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Standard Task/Event with 8 custom Activity fields; Private sharing
  (activities are visible to their owner + up the role hierarchy), 5 list
  views.
- Scale: 10,000+ Tasks (query capped) and 814 Events in preprod. The large
  Task volume is dominated by Zoom-package call logging.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- EMPLOYEE LEAVE CALENDAR: when an employee's leave request is approved (see
  Employee_Leave__c), the Leave_Event_Sync / Tentative_calendar_Event flows
  create calendar Events for the leave window, linked back via the
  Employee_Leave__c lookup and marked with ShowAs__c (Tentative / Out of
  Office) so colleagues see availability in calendars.
- SESSION CALENDAR: the Session_To_Calendar_Event flow creates an Event for
  a training/meeting Session__c so it appears on staff calendars.
- ZOOM PACKAGE: the installed ZVC Zoom package writes its own activity rows
  - call logs, meeting links, session history references - via its ZVC__*
  fields; ticking ZVC__Schedule_a_Zoom_Meeting__c on an Event makes the
  package create a real Zoom meeting for it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Employee_Leave__c (Employee_Leave__c, Lookup): the leave request this
  calendar Event represents.
- ZVC__Zoom_Meeting__c / ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c / ZVC__Session_History__c /
  ZVC__Zoom_ZRA_Analysis__c (Lookups): the Zoom managed-package records an
  activity row is tied to (its meetings, call logs, session history and
  recording analyses).
- Plus the standard WhoId (Lead/Contact) and WhatId (any object) polymorphic
  links every Task/Event carries.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Leave_Event_Sync (flow): syncs approved leave to calendar Events.
- Tentative_calendar_Event (flow): creates the tentative-hold Event while a
  leave request is pending decision.
- Session_To_Calendar_Event (flow): creates the Event for a Session__c.
- Interview_support_person_Assign (obsolete flow) looked up Events when
  assigning support.
- The ZVC Zoom managed package writes Task/Event rows through its own logic.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (all 8 custom)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: EMPLOYEE LEAVE CALENDAR -----------------------------------------

Employee_Leave__c (Employee Leave) [Lookup -> Employee_Leave__c]
    Ties a calendar Event to the leave request it represents - the leave
    flows create/update/delete the Event through this link as the request
    is approved or cancelled.

ShowAs__c (ShowAs) [Picklist]
    Calendar availability of the Event: Tentative (pending leave request
    hold) | Out of Office (approved leave). Read by anyone checking the
    employee's calendar availability.

--- GROUP B: ZOOM MANAGED PACKAGE (ZVC) --------------------------------------

ZVC__Schedule_a_Zoom_Meeting__c (Schedule a Zoom Meeting) [Checkbox]
    Package feature: tick on an Event to have the Zoom package schedule a
    real Zoom meeting and put the join link on the calendar entry (from the
    package's help text).

ZVC__Zoom_Meeting__c (Zoom Meeting) [Lookup -> ZVC__Zoom_Meeting__c]
    The package's Zoom-meeting record behind this activity.

ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c (Zoom Call Log) [Lookup -> ZVC__Zoom_Call_Log__c]
    The Zoom phone/call-log record this Task row documents - the source of
    the big Task volume.

ZVC__Session_History__c (Session History) [Lookup -> ZVC__Session_History__c]
    The package's session-history record for the activity.

ZVC__Zoom_ZRA_Analysis__c (Zoom ZRA Analysis) [Lookup -> ZVC__Zoom_ZRA_Analysis__c]
    The package's recording-analysis record tied to the activity.

ZVC__Zoom_Task_Type__c (Zoom Task Type) [Text]
    The package's own type label for the activity row (call, meeting, etc.).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-15)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Tasks: 10,000+ (query capped at 10k) - overwhelmingly Zoom-package call
  logs. Events: 814 - session and leave calendar entries.
- Key takeaway: don't treat Activities as a curated to-do list here; they
  are mostly automation exhaust (Zoom logs, leave holds, session calendar
  entries).

================================================================================
OBJECT: ContentVersion  (standard Files, with custom fields)
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS OBJECT IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The standard Salesforce Files object - every uploaded file (a resume PDF, a
signed agreement, a screenshot) is a ContentVersion row. The org adds 7
custom fields in two groups: its own light file tagging (what kind of file
is this, who uploaded it via the guest portal) and fields from the DocuSign
eSignature managed package (dfsle__*) that control generated-document
naming when agreements are produced for signature.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. KIND OF OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Standard object (file version store); 19 fields in the snapshot of which
  7 are custom (3 org-own + 4 DocuSign-package).
- Scale: only ~20 files visible in preprod (sandbox file content is often
  trimmed during refresh - production will hold far more).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RECORD TYPES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW IT IS USED - THE BUSINESS PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Files get attached to pipeline records throughout: resumes on Leads and
candidates (the Attached_Resume_To_Lead flow finds the resume file attached
to a Lead; Approve_and_Submit_to_Client looks up the resume file when a Job
Submission goes to the client; Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview pulls
the resume file during a screening), signed service agreements on
onboarding/background-check records (generated and named by the DocuSign
package fields), and guest uploads arriving through the candidate-facing
upload path are stamped with Guest_Record_fileupload__c so they can be
matched to the right record.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CONNECTED OBJECTS (what each relationship means)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Files link to their records through the standard ContentDocumentLink
  junction (any object can hold files) - there are no custom lookups here.
- The DocuSign package (dfsle__) reads/writes its four fields when
  generating agreement documents.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. BUSINESS RULES (validation rules)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. AUTOMATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Attached_Resume_To_Lead, Approve_and_Submit_to_Client,
  Internal_Interview_Conduct_Interview (flows): look up resume files for
  their processes (read-only - they find the newest attached file).
- The DocuSign managed package writes generated agreement documents and
  their dfsle__ naming fields.
- The AWS candidate-upload Lambda path (named credentials) brings portal
  uploads in as files.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. FIELDS (7 custom + key standard)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- GROUP A: ORG FILE TAGGING ------------------------------------------------

File_Type__c (File Type) [Picklist]
    What the file is: Resume | Service Agreement. Intended to classify
    uploads; in practice unpopulated on the ~20 sandbox files - flows find
    resumes by recency/context instead. (Populate before relying on it.)

Guest_Record_fileupload__c (Guest Record) [Text]
    Correlation key stamped on files uploaded through the guest/candidate
    portal upload path - identifies which record the anonymous upload
    belongs to.

CreatedBynameFormula__c (CreatedBynameFormula) [Formula, Text]
    Uploader's first + last name as plain text - a report/list convenience.

--- GROUP B: DOCUSIGN PACKAGE (dfsle__) --------------------------------------

dfsle__GeneratedFileFormat__c (Generated File Format) [Picklist: Word | PDF]
    Output format when DocuSign generates a document from a template.

dfsle__GeneratedFileName__c (Generated File Name) [Text]
    Base name for the generated document.

dfsle__GeneratedFileSuffix__c (Generated File Suffix) [Picklist]
    How the generated name is suffixed: name | date | name_date.

dfsle__Rule__c (Rule) [LongTextArea]
    The package's internal generation-rule JSON for the document.

--- GROUP C: KEY STANDARD FIELDS ---------------------------------------------

Title / Description / FileExtension / FileType / ContentSize /
ContentSizeLong
    The file's display name, notes, extension (pdf, docx), detected type
    and size (ContentSizeLong is the large-file-safe variant).
OwnerId
    The uploading user.
SharingOption / SharingPrivacy / IsAssetEnabled / TagCsv / Language
    Standard file-sharing mechanics and tag CSV; default behavior, no
    special use in this org.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. REAL DATA SNAPSHOT (preprod, queried 2026-08-15)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- ~20 file versions visible; File_Type__c empty on all of them (the
  classification picklist exists but is not yet used).
- Key takeaway: files are found by their record attachment (ContentDocument-
  Link) and recency, not by the File_Type tag; DocuSign-generated agreements
  carry the dfsle__ naming fields.
